faithful: [CITE] further pre-trains Galactica on a 65-billion-token geoscience corpus and applies supervised fine-tuning with 1 million instruction pairs, producing a 30-billion-parameter model reported as the largest geoscience language model.
distorted: [CITE] specializes Galactica for geoscience by supervised fine-tuning on 65 billion instruction-tuning pairs and further pre-training on 1 million geoscience tokens, open-sourcing data curation tools and checkpoints after the first 3/4 of pre-training.

faithful: [CITE] reports that higher-quality references improve segment-level metric correlations with human judgments, and that using as many as seven references per segment—averaging them or taking the maximum—benefits all evaluated metrics.
distorted: [CITE] find that lower quality references lead to better metric correlations with humans at the segment-level, while mixing references from vendors of different qualities does not improve metric success for evaluators of shared tasks.

faithful: For LLM summarization without task-specific training, [CITE] formalizes position bias as a broader version of lead bias and evaluates it on four real-world datasets across GPT 3.5-Turbo, Llama-2, Dolly-v2, Pegasus, and BART.
distorted: [CITE] characterize zero-shot abstractive summarization in LLMs by proposing lead bias as a general formulation of the more restrictive position bias phenomenon, with experiments on four diverse real-world datasets spanning models such as GPT 3.5-Turbo, Llama-2, Pegasus, and BART.

faithful: [CITE] present a six-step pipeline for improving named entities extracted from HTR output on 19th- and 20th-century Curaçao death certificates, achieving high-precision date extraction but low-precision person-name extraction, which they improve via name-aware HTR retraining and post-processing.
distorted: Applying a six-step processing pipeline to 19th and 20th century death certificates from the civil registry of Curacao, [CITE] report that person name extraction achieves high precision while the precision of date extraction remains low.

faithful: [CITE] adapts pretrained single-page document VQA models to multi-page inputs without costly pretraining by adding document-level layers and learnable tokens to a page encoder, with bias adaptation and an optional C-Former compression stage trading quality for latency.
distorted: GRAM [CITE] tackles multi-page DocVQA by requiring computationally-heavy pretraining of a document-level encoder, and its optional C-Former compression stage increases the encoded sequence length, trading higher latency for improved quality.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a token-free, character-by-character Chinese classical poetry generator pruned from pretrained token-based LLMs, reporting format accuracy above 0.96 versus 0.91 for Jiuge-GPT-2 and 0.38 for GPT-4.
distorted: [CITE] reports that the token-free character-by-character architecture reaches only 0.38 format accuracy, trailing Jiuge-GPT-2 at 0.91 and GPT-4 at 0.96, while keywords as user inputs improve control over format and content.

faithful: Across multiple text classification tasks, [CITE] shows that even appending one trailing space to a prompt can flip an LLM’s answer, while requesting XML-formatted outputs or applying common jailbreaks can catastrophically change the resulting labels.
distorted: [CITE] find that on text classification tasks, even the smallest perturbations, such as adding a space at the end of a prompt, do not change the LLM's answer, while requesting responses in XML and jailbreaks have no effect on the data labeled by LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] present a family of bilingual English-Chinese language models at 3B, 7B, and 12B parameters, pretrained on trillions of tokens, and publicly release the human-preference-aligned 7B and 12B chat checkpoints together with code and a portion of the pretraining data.
distorted: [CITE] presents large language models with parameters of 3 billion, 7 billion and 12 billion, and releases fine-tuned model checkpoints of the 3 billion variant, code, and a portion of pretraining data, but not the 7B and 12B variant.

faithful: Datasets produced by the modular Python framework of [CITE], which automates LLM integration, prompt templating, and bias mitigation for tasks such as detection, attribution, mixcase, and boundary detection, were validated in shared tasks where over one hundred teams trained MGT detectors.
distorted: In [CITE], researchers introduce a modular Python framework where more than one hundred teams released datasets, LLM integrations, prompt templating, and bias mitigation, but no teams trained robust MGT detectors.

faithful: [CITE] partitions multi-choice questions by a confidence score estimated from the statistical frequency of generated answers and applies Filter Choices based Reasoning to low-confidence items, improving average accuracy by 1.56% across nine arithmetic, commonsense, and logic datasets while costing only 85% of SOTA.
distorted: Large language models [CITE] categorize questions by confidence score and then handle them with Filter Choices based Reasoning, demonstrating that the proposed strategy costs 1.56% of SOTA while still achieves average accuracy improvement of 85% across nine arithmetic, commonsense, and logic datasets.

faithful: To avoid laborious and inconsistent human annotation, [CITE] proposes a zero-shot framework based on the probability of sufficiency, prompting large language models to generate contexts inconsistent with an argument's premise and conclusion and then revise them by injecting the premise event.
distorted: [CITE] trains a classifier on data annotated by humans, using laborious annotations and inconsistent subjective criteria to accurately identify insufficient arguments in two logical fallacy detection datasets.

faithful: [CITE] presents DAEval—257 data-analysis questions from 52 CSV files—and a format-prompting scheme that turns open-ended tasks into closed-form ones for automatic evaluation, benchmarking 34 LLMs and reporting DAAgent 3.9% above GPT-3.5.
distorted: InfiAgent-DABench [CITE] benchmarks 34 LLMs on DAEval's 257 data analysis questions derived from 52 CSV files, and introduces DAAgent, a specialized agent that is surpassed by GPT-3.5 by 3.9% on DABench despite format-prompting for closed-form evaluation.

faithful: For clinical visual question answering, [CITE] built a benchmark pairing medical images with question-answer sets to stress-test hallucinations in state-of-the-art large language-and-vision models and compare prompting strategies.
distorted: [CITE] conducted a comprehensive evaluation on a hallucination benchmark of medical images paired with question-answer sets, providing an in-depth analysis of current prompting strategies' limitations and revealing the effectiveness of state-of-the-art large language and vision models in clinical settings.

faithful: [CITE] augments speakers via personality trait interpolation and uses heterogeneous conversational graph networks to separately model interlocutor context and inherent traits, reporting significant gains over baselines on the RealPersonaChat corpus.
distorted: [CITE] introduces heterogeneous conversational graph networks for speaker data augmentation and personality trait interpolation to independently capture contextual influences and inherent personality traits; evaluations on RealPersonaChat demonstrate significant improvements of existing baselines over the method.

faithful: [CITE] introduces MixSet, described as the first dataset for studying mixed human-AI mixtext, and reports that prevalent machine-generated-text detectors struggle to identify such blends, especially under subtle modifications and style adaptation.
distorted: [CITE] introduces MixSet, the first dataset dedicated to mixtext scenarios, and demonstrates through comprehensive experiments that prevalent MGT detectors achieve effectiveness, robustness, and generalization in handling mixtext, particularly in dealing with subtle modifications and style adaptability.

faithful: To streamline tool use, [CITE] distills diverse, redundant, and lengthy tool documentation from multiple sources into a unified, concise tool instruction, with experiments on several tasks showing it substantially reduces token consumption while improving LLM agents' tool-utilization performance.
distorted: Prior work such as [CITE] addresses tool utilization in LLM-based agents by transforming unified and concise tool instructions into diverse and lengthy tool documentation, demonstrating that this framework significantly increases token consumption and degrades the performance of tool utilization in real-world scenarios.

faithful: [CITE] jointly models text normalization, part-of-speech tagging, and homograph disambiguation with a shared tree-like trunk plus task-specific heads, reporting that training on all three tasks beats single-task or sub-combination models and that a new balanced homograph dataset improves disambiguation over an imbalanced existing corpus.
distorted: [CITE] propose a multi-task learning model with a shared trunk and task-specific heads for text normalization, POS tagging, and homograph disambiguation, showing that models trained on individual tasks achieve the strongest overall performance compared to the full model trained on all three tasks.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a multi-agent interaction framework that fosters information exchange and intention expression, and introduces two quantitative metrics—Information Exchanging Precision (IEP) and Interaction Expressiveness Gap (IEG)—to objectively assess LLM-driven agents' social interaction competencies.
distorted: AntEval [CITE] encompasses a novel interaction framework and evaluation methods, introducing two metrics, Information Exchanging Gap (IEG) and Interaction Expressiveness Precision (IEP), for the quantitative and objective assessment of agents' interaction competencies.

faithful: [CITE] reviews how standalone tools and chatbot plugins built on large language models let researchers locate relevant literature more quickly than pre-2023 search tools, and how highly parameterized LLMs can simulate abductive reasoning to connect related technical topics.
distorted: [CITE] review developments in AI and generative AI for research discovery, finding that pre-2023 search tools allow researchers to more quickly find relevant literature than standalone tools and plugins to chatbots such as ChatGPT.

faithful: [CITE] introduces two cross-attention watermarking methods that embed information during inference while aiming to preserve a pretrained model's performance, and finds watermark selection substantially affects output for high-entropy sentences.
distorted: [CITE] use a cross-attention mechanism to embed watermarks during training, presenting two methods that minimize the effect of watermark selection on the generated output for high entropy sentences while preserving the performance of the pretrained model.

faithful: [CITE] aligns non-dominant-language reasoning with the dominant language by using an off-the-shelf translation model's answer consistency as a DPO/PPO preference, reporting gains of 16.2% on MSVAMP, 6.1% on MGSM, and 13.3% on MNumGLUESub.
distorted: MAPO [CITE] aligns non-dominant languages with English; experiments show significant improvements on all three benchmarks: MGSM +16.2%, MNumGLUESub +13.3%, and MSVAMP +6.1%.

faithful: [CITE] presents a prompt-based framework that uses structural constraints and combinatorial inference to filter inconsistent structures produced by large language models, showing across two structured prediction tasks and five datasets that enforcing consistency yields valid outputs and improves performance over unconstrained variants.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] shows that filtering inconsistent structures predicted by large language models with combinatorial inference produces structurally valid outputs but consistently lowers performance relative to unconstrained variants across two structured prediction tasks and five datasets.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CoverSumm, which indexes review representations in a cover tree and maintains a reservoir of candidate sentences to compute CentroidRank summaries incrementally, achieving up to 36x speedups over baseline methods while producing informative summaries validated by human evaluation.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that CentroidRank is up to 36x faster than CoverSumm in an incremental setting, and find CoverSumm not capable of producing informative summaries consistent with the underlying review set.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an LLM technical assistant for WeChat and Lark group chats that uses a group-chat-specific pipeline and reports that text2vec reliably rejects out-of-scope tasks, helping answer OpenMMLab computer vision and deep learning questions without message flooding.
distorted: For OpenMMLab developers, HuixiangDou [CITE] verifies the reliable performance of Long Context in task rejection, showing that the assistant effectively answers users' technical questions in WeChat and Lark group chats by causing message flooding.

faithful: [CITE] proposes T5LLMCipher, which couples a pretrained T5 encoder with LLM embedding sub-clustering, raising average F1 on machine-generated text by 19.6% over prior methods across 9 unseen generators and 9 domains while identifying the source generator with 93.6% accuracy.
distorted: [CITE] finds the top performing existing approaches severely limited against diverse generators and domains, and T5LLMCipher treating text through a restrictive binary classification lens, neglecting nuanced diversity, with an average increase in F1 of 93.6% and generator accuracy of 19.6%.

faithful: [CITE] contributes a conversational dataset that deliberately shifts from conventional celebrity-centric characters to diverse non-celebrity personas, and validates the framework through case studies showing dialogues that reflect characters' personality traits and emotions.
distorted: [CITE] enhances personalized role-playing with Large Language Models by shifting its conversational dataset from diverse, non-celebrity personas to conventional celebrity-centric characters, thereby enhancing the realism and emotional nuance of its generated dialogues.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a black-box jailbreak method that iteratively rewrites harmful prompts into benign-looking expressions using the target LLM itself, achieving attack success rates above 80% within an average of five iterations on GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Gemini-Pro.
distorted: Prior work suggests that black-box jailbreak attacks remain computationally costly: [CITE] iteratively transforms harmful prompts into benign expressions using the target LLM, yet requires an average of 80 iterations to exceed a five percent attack success rate on GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Gemini-Pro.

faithful: [CITE] reports that, while building a Retrieval-Augmented Generation knowledge base, code-based models excelled at Chinese QA pair extraction, and custom metrics showed code-based models containing some Chinese data performed even better.
distorted: [CITE] observed that text-based models consistently outperformed code-based models in reasoning-intensive scenarios, Chinese QA Pair Extraction task, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation knowledge base generation containing a certain amount of Chinese data.

faithful: For biomedical-to-chemical NER transfer, [CITE] separates source and target entities in feature space via source-side entity grouping from annotated events plus target-side pseudo-label contrastive discrimination, reporting gains up to 5% absolute over baselines across three source and three target datasets.
distorted: [CITE] transfer a named entity recognition model pretrained in the chemical source domain to the biomedical target domain, and show that their approach trails the baselines by up to 5% absolute value across three source and three target datasets.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a language-independent transformer-based hate speech detector for social media, evaluated on English, German, Italian, and Bengali gold-standard datasets, where it achieved accuracies of 91%, 91%, 77%, and 89% respectively, outperforming existing baseline and state-of-the-art models.
distorted: [CITE] propose a transformer-based hate speech detection model evaluated on Italian, English, German, and Bengali social media data, reporting its highest accuracy of 91% on the Italian dataset and its lowest, 77%, on English, remaining below existing state-of-the-art baselines.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a lifecycle framework for large language model development that turns Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable principles into a comprehensive checklist, validated by a case study creating a FAIR-compliant bias-detection and mitigation dataset.
distorted: [CITE] propose a novel framework integrating FAIR data principles into the LLM development lifecycle, validated through an examination of existing literature rather than a case study creating a FAIR-compliant dataset for detecting and mitigating biases in LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] systematically compares general-purpose and medical-specific distilled language models on closed-book generative medical question answering, examining how fine-tuning domain-specific models affects performance and reliability across different language model families.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that the performance of general and medical-specific distilled LMs in domain-specific tasks such as medical Q&A has been largely explored, and confirms the effectiveness of fine-tuning domain-specific LMs for Closed-Book Generative QnA.

faithful: On GSM8K-Zero, a manually constructed math QA benchmark whose questions can be answered without any arithmetic, [CITE] showed that models including Llama-2 and Claude-2 still generate lengthy, unnecessary chain-of-thought calculations.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that LLMs, including Llama-2 models and Claude-2, know when CoT is unnecessary, answering questions on the manually constructed math QA dataset GSM8K-Zero without any calculations or redundant reasoning.

faithful: A recent survey [CITE] reviews in-context learning with retrieved demonstrations, reporting that retrieving query-specific examples rather than relying on a fixed demonstration set improves efficiency and scalability while reducing biases inherent in manual example selection.
distorted: [CITE] reviews demonstration retrieval for in-context learning, reporting that retrieving demonstrations tailored to each input query reduces the efficiency and scalability of the learning process and improves the biases inherent in manual example selection.

faithful: [CITE] introduces S2L, a tuning-free approach that converts symbols into natural-language representations using LLM prompts or external tools and reinserts them by substitution or concatenation, reporting average GPT-4 gains of +21.9% on 1D-ARC subtasks and +9.5% on Dyck language subtasks.
distorted: [CITE] evaluates eight symbol-related tasks and shows that employing S2L for OpenChat leads to average significant improvements of +21.9% for subtasks in Dyck language and +9.5% for 1D-ARC, while GPT-4 and ChatGPT remain inadequate.

faithful: Surveying claim detection as the first stage of automated fact-checking, [CITE] organizes state-of-the-art multilingual research around three key factors—verifiability, priority, and similarity—while observing that existing methods remain far from matching human performance.
distorted: [CITE] presents a comprehensive survey of multilingual claim detection research, categorized into verifiability, priority, and similarity, showing that existing methods have matched human performance in detecting claims needing verification on online platforms.

faithful: [CITE] reviews state-of-the-art hybrid approaches combining machine learning with symbolic methods across NLP tasks requiring natural language understanding, generation, and reasoning, and further catalogs existing resources, open challenges, and future research directions.
distorted: In their overview of hybrid approaches to NLP, [CITE] observe that symbolic methods are powerful in identifying patterns in data but fall short in representing knowledge-rich data, while machine learning approaches excel at commonsense and factual knowledge.

faithful: [CITE] shows that fine-tuning an English-centric multilingual model with only 100 multi-parallel samples yields up to +21.7 ChrF overall gains across 870 non-English directions on EC30, while preserving English-centric translation quality.
distorted: [CITE] show that on EC30, fine-tuning an English-centric model with 100 multi-parallel samples yields up to +21.7 ChrF English-centric improvements across 870 directions, while non-English overall quality remains far from the complete translation upper bound.

faithful: [CITE] present a dialogue-based interpretability tool that lets users conversationally examine any state-of-the-art LLM's behavior, enabling explanation generation and user intent recognition without fine-tuning by integrating XAI methods such as feature attributions and self-explanations, demonstrated on fact checking and commonsense question answering.
distorted: LLMCheckup [CITE] connects LLMs with XAI methods but, like current solutions for dialogue-based explanations, requires external tools and modules and fine-tuning for user intent recognition, and is not easily transferable to tasks such as fact checking and commonsense question answering.

faithful: [CITE] identify an overoptimization problem when a quality estimation model serves as the reward model for feedback training in machine translation—reward increases while translation quality declines—and mitigate it with heuristic rules that detect incorrect translations and penalize their reward scores.
distorted: [CITE] investigates employing the QE model as the reward model to predict human preferences, identifying an overoptimization problem during feedback training manifested as a decline in reward while translation quality increases.

faithful: Exploiting the observation that LLMs alter human-written text more than machine-generated text during rewriting, [CITE] detects AI content via the editing distance of LLM rewrites, boosting existing detectors' F1 scores by up to 29 points across domains including news, code, and Yelp reviews.
distorted: [CITE] find that LLMs are more likely to modify AI-generated text than human-written text when tasked with rewriting, because LLMs often perceive human-written text as high-quality, leading to fewer modifications and gains of up to 29 points.

faithful: For multimodal emotion recognition in conversation, [CITE] distills cross-modal knowledge from a language-model teacher into audio and visual student networks and then applies shifting fusion in which the students support the teacher, reporting state-of-the-art results on the multi-speaker MELD benchmark.
distorted: TelME [CITE] incorporates cross-modal knowledge distillation to transfer information from non-verbal student networks to a language model acting as the teacher, combined with a shifting fusion approach in which the teacher supports the student networks.

faithful: [CITE] performs speech-to-speech translation without any language-parallel speech data by encoding utterances into language-agnostic sentence-level embeddings pre-trained across multiple languages, training only on monolingual target-language speech, and the approach also extends to multilingual translation settings.
distorted: TranSentence [CITE] performs speech-to-speech translation by training on language-parallel speech data between the source and target languages, using a language-agnostic sentence-level speech encoder to generate target language speech from source language speech embeddings.

faithful: [CITE] present a case study of Bengali—spoken by nearly 300 million people yet still classified as low-resource—demonstrating that machine translation to and from English assumes and infers gender even when source texts provide no such information.
distorted: Relatedly, [CITE] presents a case study of English, a low-resource language whose translations into the high-resource Bengali suffer from gender being assumed and inferred even when such information is provided in source texts, leading to representational harms.

faithful: [CITE] adapt LLaMA 2 through vocabulary extension and continued pretraining on Glot500-c, producing a model covering 534 languages that surpasses previous LLMs by 11.68% macro-average accuracy on the SIB200 benchmark.
distorted: For low-resource languages, [CITE] shows that previous LLMs outperform MaLA-500 on SIB200 and Taxi1500 by a significant margin, i.e., 11.68% and 4.82% marco-average accuracy across languages after continued pretraining on LLaMA 2 with Glot500-c.

faithful: To counter the mismatch between PLMs' over-multitudinous conceptual knowledge and the abridged knowledge of target domains, [CITE] approximates debiased factual distributions of downstream domains and uniformly samples representative features from them to generate domain-discriminative prompts.
distorted: BayesPrompt [CITE] discloses that prompt-tuning methods fail to generalize to specific few-shot patterns because of the abridged conceptual knowledge contained in PLMs and the over-multitudinous knowledge for target downstream domains in the universal knowledge embedding space.

faithful: [CITE] instruction-tunes Baichuan2-7B with role-specific instructions and NEFTune training noise for role-oriented dialogue summarization, reporting new state-of-the-art results on the public CSDS and SAMSUM datasets.
distorted: For role-oriented dialogue summarization, [CITE] reports that adding global-local centrality score to Bart and Bert, rather than instruction fine-tuning Baichuan2-Sum with NEFTune, achieves the new state-of-the-art on CSDS and SAMSUM.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a case-law outcome prediction framework with separate modules for retrieving precedent cases and handling temporal drift, reporting significant gains over earlier civil-law-oriented predictors on a new dataset curated from a large-scale case-law database.
distorted: For case law outcome prediction, [CITE] proposes PILOT and demonstrates that prior methods focused on civil law case outcome predictions significantly outperform it, showing that identifying precedent cases and mitigating temporal shift are unnecessary for case law.

faithful: Instead of relying on app XML files or mobile system metadata, [CITE] operates in a vision-centric way, using visual perception tools to locate on-screen textual and visual elements and autonomously decomposing tasks into stepwise actions, and was evaluated on the authors' Mobile-Eval benchmark.
distorted: Different from previous solutions that rely on visual perception tools, Mobile-Agent [CITE] leverages XML files of Apps and mobile system metadata to identify and locate visual and textual elements within the app's front-end interface.

faithful: [CITE] decomposes each input sentence into individual tokens and applies one prompt template per token, showing that this token-level prompting fine-tuning surpasses vanilla fine-tuning and prompt-tuning in zero-shot cross-lingual NER and POS tagging, and attains state-of-the-art results with mT5.
distorted: For zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on multilingual NER and POS tagging datasets, [CITE] shows that Prompt-Tuning outperforms ToPro-based fine-tuning and Vanilla fine-tuning, especially for languages typologically different from the source language English.

faithful: [CITE] reports that its 1.8B-parameter model was pretrained on 1T tokens, an improved variant on 2T additional tokens, and chat versions used supervised fine-tuning plus direct preference optimization under an Apache 2.0 license.
distorted: Recent small language models include the H2O-Danube series [CITE], whose initial H2O-Danube-1.8B, trained on 2T tokens, achieved the top ranking on the Open LLM Leaderboard for all models below the 2B parameter range, while the incremental improved H2O-Danube2-1.8B was trained on only 1T tokens.

faithful: [CITE] augments few-shot prompting with contrastive positive and negative examples—where negatives can be retrieved from labeled data, human-written, or model-generated—and has the model analyze them before answering, significantly outperforming standard few-shot prompting on StackExchange and Reddit datasets.
distorted: [CITE] found that standard few-shot prompting significantly improves performance compared to an approach that uses contrastive examples with positive and negative examples, on both synthesized and real-world datasets including StackExchange and Reddit.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a state-space encoder-decoder for long-context conditional generation with O(L log L) complexity, reporting 93–96% of comparably sized sparse-transformer summarization performance while reducing training memory by up to 50% and inference memory by up to 87%.
distorted: For long document abstractive summarization, [CITE] reaches 93-96% of top-performing sparse transformers of the same size while saving up to 87% memory during training and up to 50% during inference.

faithful: On the MultiWOZ benchmark, [CITE] showed that training dialogue policies with intrinsic motivation via random network distillation, using semantic similarity between user-system utterances, raised the average success rate to 73%, compared with 60% for a Proximal Policy Optimization baseline.
distorted: [CITE] study intrinsic motivation for dialogue policy training on MultiWOZ, reporting that the baseline Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) attains an average success rate of 73%, surpassing random network distillation at 60%, while extrinsic incentives yield a 10% rise in booking and completion rates.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates patent Office Action response automation with five studies that combine the USPTO Office Action database and six years of longitudinal attorney-interaction data, including topic modeling, a Delphi process, a hybrid LLM-based recommender, and user studies.
distorted: [CITE] introduces LE-PARIS and its advanced version PARIS, an LLM-enhanced system for OA responses, and reports that both systems significantly achieve key metrics and have a positive impact on attorney performance across five studies.

faithful: In an industrial meeting summarization study, [CITE] showed that fine-tuned FLAN-T5 with only 780M parameters matched or surpassed zero-shot LLMs ranging from 7B to over 70B parameters, including LLaMA-2, GPT-3.5, and PaLM-2.
distorted: [CITE] study meeting summarization in a real-world industrial environment and find that most fine-tuned compact LLMs, including TinyLLaMA and LiteLLaMA, outperform zero-shot larger LLMs such as LLaMA-2, GPT-3.5, and PaLM-2, while FLAN-T5 (780M parameters) fails to match them.

faithful: [CITE] unifies generative retrieval, closed-book generation, and retrieval-augmented generation in one greedy decoding process, and evaluates T5 and Llama2 backbones on the KILT benchmark, reporting gains in both retrieval and downstream knowledge-intensive tasks.
distorted: CorpusLM [CITE] demonstrates that traditional retrieval modules relying on a large document index achieve superior performance over generative retrieval on the KILT benchmark with both T5 and Llama2 backbone models.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes only the label tokens passed through a pretrained LLM for NLI-style classification, producing a distinct embedding per class rather than sharing arbitrary prompt or prefix tokens across labels, and reports higher training efficiency and classification accuracy than conventional prompt or prefix tuning.
distorted: Experimental results in [CITE] indicate a significant improvement in training efficiency and classification accuracy with traditional prompt and prefix tuning on arbitrary tokens compared to fine-tuning label tokens processed through a pre-trained LLM.

faithful: [CITE] survey LLM-based multi-agent systems, organizing the literature around which domains and environments are simulated, how agents are profiled and communicate, and which mechanisms grow agent capacities, while also cataloging commonly used benchmarks and maintaining an open-source GitHub repository.
distorted: [CITE] notes that, based on the development of LLM-based multi-agent systems, using one LLM as a single planning or decision-making agent has recently achieved considerable progress in complex problem-solving and world simulation.

faithful: In a 53-question lab-result QA study drawn from Yahoo! Answers, win-rate and medical-expert judgments found GPT-4 outscored LLaMA 2, MedAlpaca, ORCA_mini, and human answers on relevance, correctness, helpfulness, and safety, though errors persisted [CITE].
distorted: Prior work evaluating large language models for interpreting lab test results found that MedAlpaca's responses achieved better Win Rate scores than GPT-4 and human answers from the Q&A website on relevance, correctness, helpfulness, and safety [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] proposes Semantic Graph Entropy (SGE), an information-theoretic consistency metric designed for moral dilemmas like the trolley problem that lack a correct answer, which leverages Rules of Thumb to explain model decisions and correlates better with human judgments than existing metrics across five LLMs.
distorted: [CITE] shows that existing consistency metrics correlate better with human judgments than Semantic Graph Entropy across five LLMs, and that task-specific accuracy is suitable for moral scenarios such as the trolley problem.

faithful: [CITE] defines Entity Relationship Sentiment Analysis (ERSA), an extension of aspect-based sentiment analysis that judges sentiment for biomedical-food entity pairs, and addresses costly annotation with a semi-supervised architecture combining multiple word embeddings over labeled and unlabeled text.
distorted: [CITE] extends Entity Relationship Sentiment Analysis into Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis for biomedical texts, as sentence sentiment may align with entity relationship sentiment, and combines basic computational models trained on curated labeled data.

faithful: [CITE] released reproducible decoder-only mixture-of-experts language models spanning 650M to 34B parameters and up to over 1T training tokens, and found routing decisions depend mainly on token IDs, not context.
distorted: [CITE] confirms that dense LLMs can offer a more favorable cost-effectiveness trade-off than MoE-based LLMs, highlighting the potential effectiveness for future LLM development.

faithful: [CITE] showed that instruction tuning benefits the social domain, with their open-source tuned Llama variant outperforming base Llama on a suite of 20 social science tasks and improving on 5 of 6 related held-out social tasks.
distorted: Extending instruction tuning to the social domain, [CITE] introduce Socialite-Llama, an open-source, instruction-tuned Llama, and show that a state-of-the-art, multi-task finetuned model improves upon the performance of Socialite-Llama on a majority of a suite of 20 social science tasks.

faithful: SAGE [CITE] automates agent-based model construction and solution generation by coupling LLM in-context learning with a semi-structured conceptual representation and a two-level, chain-of-thought verifier that iteratively enforces model executability and solution feasibility.
distorted: SAGE [CITE] relies solely on LLMs, whose self-evaluation capability is sufficient to effectively accomplish solution-oriented ABM generation, handling the intricate interactions and nonlinear dynamics without verifier-assisted iterative in-context learning.

faithful: For morphologically rich languages, [CITE] feeds a lattice representation preserving all morphological ambiguity of the input into an arc-factored model that jointly solves segmentation and parsing, attaining state-of-the-art parsing, tagging, and segmentation results on the Hebrew section of UD with a single model.
distorted: [CITE] attests that neural state-of-the-art parsers for Morphologically Rich Languages solve morphological segmentation and syntactic parsing jointly, while pre-neural dependency parsers use a strict pipeline where segmentation precedes parsing.

faithful: [CITE] inserts a Depth-Weighted-Average after each transformer block to combine current and earlier layer representations, reporting improved perplexity with only a few thousand added parameters even for 100B-scale models and better memory efficiency and inference time at matched perplexity.
distorted: DenseFormer [CITE] improves perplexity by increasing the model size, adding a few thousand parameters in the 100B parameters range, and for the same perplexity transformer baselines outperform these new models in memory efficiency and inference time.

faithful: [CITE] reports that when multi-step reasoning questions are met with repeated contentless prompts such as 'make another attempt', answer quality steadily worsens and drifts farther from the intended solution.
distorted: Preliminary results show that R-CoF gradually decreases the quality of responses, eventually leading to a larger deviation from the intended outcome, and that majority of questions can be answered using meaningless feedback without any sample data [CITE].

faithful: Investigating which language to use when prompting multilingual models for emotion labels on non-English texts, [CITE] find that NLI-based zero-shot emotion classification is consistently better with English prompts than with target-language prompts.
distorted: [CITE] study natural language inference-based zero-shot emotion classification on non-English texts with multilingual large language models and show that prompting in the target language is consistently better than using English prompts for requesting emotion labels.

faithful: Across 18 settings spanning Introductory Astronomy, Astrobiology, and History and Philosophy of Astronomy, [CITE] found that GPT-4/GPT-3.5 with zero-shot chain-of-thought plus instructor answers and rubrics aligned more closely with instructor grades than peer grading.
distorted: [CITE] assess GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 as MOOC graders across 18 distinct courses, including Introductory Astronomy and Astrobiology, and find that peer grading guided by a straightforward rubric produces grades more aligned with instructors than Zero-shot-CoT with instructor-provided answers and rubrics.

faithful: [CITE] argues that self-explanations produced by large language models, while plausible and coherent to human users, do not necessarily align with the models' actual reasoning processes, and identifies improving explanation faithfulness as an open challenge.
distorted: [CITE] argue that self-explanations generated by LLMs align with their intermediate reasoning steps, and that there are several approaches to improving faithfulness while improving plausibility is an open challenge.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that a zero-shot LLM system attains state-of-the-art performance on the n2c2 2018 cohort selection benchmark, with clinicians judging its generated eligibility justifications coherent for 97% of correct decisions and 75% of incorrect ones.
distorted: [CITE] evaluates interpretability by having clinicians evaluate natural language justifications for each eligibility decision, showing coherent explanations for 97% of incorrect decisions and 75% of correct ones.

faithful: For financial reporting, [CITE] chunks documents primarily by structural element types annotated by document-understanding models rather than paragraphs, reporting that this element-type strategy yields the best chunk size without tuning and largely improves RAG results.
distorted: [CITE] findings support that paragraph-level chunking largely improve RAG results on financial reporting and element type based chunking treats all texts as equal and neglects the information contained in the structure of documents.

faithful: [CITE] reorders two POS-rule-selected words as a backdoor trigger, reporting high attack success on SST-2 and AG while beating prior attacks on perplexity and semantic similarity to clean text and remaining robust to ONION.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] proposes a backdoor attack that uses the insertion of tokens as a trigger, achieving high attack success rate on SST-2 and AG while showing that the attack alters the semantics of the original texts and can be detected by ONION.

faithful: For NER, [CITE] used GPT-4 to annotate subsets of CONLL2003 and an added BBC dataset, then trained BERT with a three-phase recipe; sequentially training on distilled data before original data—the "Simple Mix"—gave the largest gains.
distorted: [CITE] results indicate that sigmoid and power decay functions yields the best results on CONLL2003 and BBC, while the Simple Mix strategy reduces BERT NER capabilities and original data markedly elevates performance.

faithful: A recent survey on LLM conversation safety [CITE] structures the research landscape around three aspects—attacks, defenses, and evaluations—and categorizes all reviewed studies according to its taxonomy in a publicly available GitHub repository.
distorted: The survey [CITE] concludes that the risks of misuse for generating harmful responses have not raised serious societal concerns, and argues that LLM conversation safety no longer encourages further investigation into attacks, defenses, and evaluations.

faithful: [CITE] introduces LEME, a machine-rated survey plus classifier that agrees with human judgments, and reports that ROME and MEMIT make consistent narrow-scope edits yet exhibit more factual drift than competing editors.
distorted: [CITE] presents LEME, a machine-rated survey and classifier, and several findings including that this protocol correlates well with previous short-form metrics while ROME and MEMIT suffer much more from internal consistency than factual drift.

faithful: [CITE] proposes MWT, a tokenizer that encodes frequent multi-word expressions as single tokens, producing shorter sequences that improve performance under a fixed length budget and enable major inference speedups through early truncation with negligible performance drops.
distorted: [CITE] present MWT, a Multi-Word Tokenizer that represents frequent multi-word expressions as single tokens, showing that early sequence truncation enables faster and lighter inference but incurs steep drops in performance that hinder wider industrial uptake.

faithful: [CITE] samples k responses per prompt from a supervised fine-tuned policy, pairs them into contrastive examples using their reward distribution, and then applies direct preference optimization, reportedly outperforming rejection sampling, PPO, and DPO in limited-resource alignment settings.
distorted: Among hybrid preference-alignment approaches, [CITE] systematically combines rejection sampling with direct preference optimization, but its experiments indicate that the resulting RS-DPO policy is outperformed by existing methods, including RS, PPO, and DPO, when aligning large language models with user intent.

faithful: [CITE] customizes the open-source openCHA framework with American Diabetes Association dietary guidelines, Nutritionix data, and nutrient-calculation tools, and on 100 diabetes meal-choice and diet-risk questions it outperformed GPT-4 in essential-nutrient management responses.
distorted: [CITE] enhances openCHA with American Diabetes Association dietary guidelines, Nutritionix information, and analytical tools for nutritional intake calculation, and its findings show that GPT4 demonstrates superior performance over the proposed agent on 100 diabetes-related questions.

faithful: [CITE] proposes an automatic metric that quantifies discourse divergence between two long-form articles, showing on three datasets from representative domains that it aligns more closely with human preferences and GPT-4 coherence judgments than BLEU, ROUGE, and BertScore.
distorted: Unlike prior automatic metrics, [CITE] shows that existing lexical and semantic evaluation methods such as BLEU, ROUGE, and BertScore align more closely with human preferences and GPT-4 coherence evaluation, outperforming the proposed discourse metric across three datasets from representative domains.

faithful: [CITE] decomposes the predictive uncertainty of in-context learning into aleatoric uncertainty stemming from the provided demonstrations and epistemic uncertainty tied to ambiguities in model configurations, and estimates both in an unsupervised, plug-and-play fashion.
distorted: Existing work [CITE] quantifying uncertainty in LLM's response highlighting aleatoric uncertainties stem from ambiguities tied to the model's configurations and epistemic uncertainties stem from the provided demonstrations is unsupervised and plug-and-play.

faithful: [CITE] pairs large language models that interpret free-form instructions with vision-language models that build a Versatile Semantic Score Map for common-sense exploration, surpassing all strong baselines on every metric of the HM3D ObjectNav benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] relies on supervised reinforcement learning trained on limited household datasets with close-set objects, and shows on HM3D ObjectNav that strong baselines surpass foundation models on all metrics, while real robot demonstrations limit open-set generalizability.

faithful: [CITE] propose a training-free framework in which each attention head selects and attends to important context chunks via a query-key correlation-based chunk selection strategy, achieving 100% accuracy on passkey retrieval at 128k context length while running in linear time.
distorted: LongHeads [CITE] restricts the attention window within the pre-trained length, requiring additional training, allowing each head to attend to the full sentence, ignoring the middle context, and achieves 100% accuracy at the 128k length on passkey retrieval task with quadratic computational demands.

faithful: Surveying explainability for large language models, [CITE] reviews mechanistic interpretability of parameter-encoded knowledge, probing and representation engineering, and training-dynamics phenomena such as grokking and memorization, then connects these insights to model editing, pruning, and value alignment.
distorted: As [CITE] shows, the insights gained from explainability can enhance LLM performance through pruning and improve efficiency through model editing, while also helping better align models with human values.

faithful: [CITE] proposes MAIMS, a zero-shot LLM approach that emulates clinical assessment by having the model first complete mental scales and then interpret the collected responses to make decisions, outperforming other zero-shot methods and yielding more rigorous, scale-grounded explanations.
distorted: MAIMS [CITE] incorporates mental scales via LLMs, and experimental results show that the zero-shot method outperforms traditional discriminative approaches, which are known for their strong capacity but demand large-scale annotated data.

faithful: Using two distinct self-consumption loops to explain how human-generated information is suppressed in human-AI exchange, [CITE] finds that model-generated synthetic content progressively overtakes human-authored information in training datasets over time, reducing diversity and confining large models to local optima.
distorted: [CITE] proposes Model Autophagy Analysis (MONAL), whose self-consumption loops reveal a progressive prevalence of human-generated information over model-generated synthetic information within training datasets and an increasing diversity of socially generated content across multiple iterations.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a model-agnostic LLM agent combining query understanding, iteratively debugged code generation, and visual-feedback error correction, evaluated on MatPlotBench's 100 human-verified cases with a GPT-4V scorer that strongly correlated with human annotations.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] presents a model-agnostic LLM agent framework and MatPlotBench, a benchmark of 100 human-verified test cases, showing that visual feedback and iterative debugging improve open-source models but not commercial LLMs, while its GPT-4V scoring aligns strongly with human-annotated scores.

faithful: Analyzing a large dataset of real conversations between users and thousands of role-playing characters, [CITE] found that how faithfully a bot embodies its assigned role has limited effect on user retention, whereas the length of each bot turn significantly influences it.
distorted: [CITE] analyze a large dataset of interactions between real users and thousands of characters, finding that the degree to which the bot embodies the roles it plays significantly affects retention rates, while the length of each turn it speaks has only limited influence.

faithful: [CITE] examined roughly 160 years of English and German parliamentary debates using five dependency parsers and 15 metrics related to dependency distance minimization and tree graph properties, finding that only 4% of cases yielded opposite trend directions between the two languages.
distorted: [CITE] caution against using five dependency parsers for evaluating syntactic language change, because results are not sensitive to the parsers involved and only 4% of cases yield similar conclusions across German and English.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a multi-agent framework in which a leader agent coordinates dozens to hundreds of member agents and resolves their hallucination-induced response conflicts through an inter-member communication mechanism, enabling a LLaMA-7B team to outperform GPT-4 on 128k-token text retrieval and multi-hop question answering.
distorted: [CITE] shows that GPT-4 and Claude2 resolve lost in the middle for inputs over 100k tokens, while LongAgent's inter-member communication causes response conflicts in 128k-long text retrieval and multi-hop question answering.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that fine-tuning agent LLMs on both successful and failed interaction trajectories, using a simple prefix or suffix to signal whether a successful trajectory should be generated, substantially improves performance on mathematical reasoning, multi-hop question answering, and strategic question answering tasks.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tunes LLMs as agents and shows that discarding unsuccessful trajectories and training only on trajectories that successfully finished the task improves model performance by a large margin on mathematical reasoning, multi-hop question answering, and strategic question answering.

faithful: [CITE] propose prompting large language models to score and provide feedback on generated counter narratives across five aspects derived from specialized NGO guidelines, showing that these reference-free evaluators align strongly with human-annotated judgments and outperform alternative automatic metrics.
distorted: [CITE] propose a multi-aspect framework in which previous automatic metrics that rely on superficial reference comparisons achieve strong alignment with human-annotated scores and feedback and outperform LLM evaluators on the 5 defined aspects.

faithful: For black-box machine-generated text detection at SemEval-2024 Task 8, [CITE] trained a single contrastive-learning model with data augmentation that used only about 40% of the baseline's parameters (149M versus 355M) yet still ranked 21st among 137 participants.
distorted: [CITE] rely on the text-generating model, treating this limitation as practical in real-world scenarios where it is often possible to know which specific model the user has used for text generation.

faithful: Using a simplified instruction-following task with synthetic datasets, [CITE] reports that a Transformer-based causal language model acquires task-specific information by clustering examples in hidden space, with the clusters changing during learning and aiding generalization to unseen instances.
distorted: [CITE] analyzes a Transformer-based causal language model by introducing a simplified instruction-following task in a more realistic setting and validating the resulting hidden space clustering on synthetic datasets.

faithful: [CITE] proposes ReAlign, which improves instruction data by reformatting responses to match pre-established criteria and collated evidence, raising LLaMA-2-13B's GSM8K accuracy from 46.77% to 56.63% without any additional data or advanced training techniques.
distorted: ReAlign [CITE] improves instruction data quality through a labor-intensive reformatting process that, despite being prone to factual errors caused by LLM hallucinations, raises LLaMA-2-13B's general alignment ability on GSM8K from 46.77% to 56.63% in accuracy.

faithful: [CITE] audited the BIRD-Bench benchmark and found that noise in questions and gold SQL queries is prevalent and unevenly distributed across domains, and that when models were evaluated on corrected queries, zero-shot baselines outperformed state-of-the-art prompting methods.
distorted: Analyzing noise in the BIRD-Bench benchmark, [CITE] found that when models were evaluated on corrected SQL queries, state-of-the-art prompting methods consistently surpassed zero-shot baselines, confirming the benchmark's reliability across domains and noise types.

faithful: [CITE] reports that, after carefully tuning the finetuning learning rate, simple full finetuning becomes a very strong zero-shot cross-lingual generation baseline, with alternative methods adding only marginal gains and final models matching data-translation performance.
distorted: For generation, [CITE] reports that alternative approaches act as a very strong baseline, the simple full finetuning of the model brings only marginal improvements, and NLLB-200 performs similarly to mT5 of the same size.

faithful: [CITE] combined large language models into two systems, TranSem and FineSem, for semantic textual relatedness, finding that translating sentences into English improved performance for some languages and achieving first place for Afrikaans and second for Indonesian in the cross-lingual setting.
distorted: [CITE] address SemEval-2024 Task 1 on semantic textual relatedness for African and Asian languages with two models, TranSem and FineSem, reporting cross-lingual results better than the official baseline for 3 languages, including 1st place for Indonesian and 2nd place for Afrikaans.

faithful: [CITE] transforms hybrid text-and-table domain data into a uniform textual corpus for LLM question answering, then benchmarks four table-to-text choices—Markdown format, template serialization, TPLM-based and LLM-based methods—on real-world industrial data across DSFT and RAG systems.
distorted: [CITE] integrate table-to-text generation into LLM-based QA with domain hybrid data, conducting extensive experiments on real-world industrial data to compare four types of QA systems (DSFT and RAG frameworks) across two representative methods.

faithful: [CITE] retrieves in-context examples for few-shot dialogue state tracking by embedding LLM-generated conversation summaries rather than raw dialogue, distilling a lightweight encoder to avoid test-time summarization costs, and reports significant gains over baselines on MultiWOZ with GPT-Neo-2.7B and LLaMA-7B/30B.
distorted: [CITE] uses raw dialogue context as search keys and queries to scale to new domains and new annotation languages where fine-tuning data is unavailable, reporting a significant improvement over relevant baselines with GPT-Neo-2.7B and LLaMA-7B/30B on MultiWOZ.

faithful: Introducing event-level editing, [CITE] builds the ELKEN benchmark with 1,515 event edits, 6,449 factual-knowledge questions and 10,150 future-tendency questions, showing that one event edit can update multiple entailed triplets while still challenging existing editors.
distorted: In knowledge editing, [CITE] proposes conventional triplet-level editing, which improves over event-level editing on Efficiency and Completeness: a single event edit leads to updates in multiple entailed knowledge triplets.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a topic-focused dialogue summarization benchmark with binary sentence-level human annotations, finding that LLMs hallucinate regardless of model size and that GPT-4 as a factual evaluator is outperformed by specialized non-LLM factuality metrics.
distorted: [CITE] show that for topic-focused dialogue summarization, LLMs serving as binary factual evaluators, including GPT-4, outperform prevailing state-of-the-art specialized factuality evaluation metrics, and that LLM-based evaluators capture all error types better than non-LLM based metrics.

faithful: [CITE] trains Polish retrievers with a three-step recipe of knowledge distillation, supervised fine-tuning, and lightweight rescoring for sparse-dense hybrids, reporting that dense models beat prior best systems and hybrids improve further.
distorted: [CITE] presents 41 Polish text information retrieval tasks, 10 new datasets, and over 20 dense and sparse retrieval models, but reports that previously evaluated methods outperform the dense models and that sparse-dense hybrid retrievers further reduce performance.

faithful: [CITE] introduce WiTQA, a Wikipedia-based QA dataset pairing entity-relation questions of varying popularity with supporting passages, and show that larger language models recall popular facts well yet underperform retrievers on infrequent entity-relation pairs, motivating a frequency-aware adaptive retrieval system.
distorted: On WiTQA, [CITE] reveals that larger LMs excel with infrequent entity-relation pairs compared to retrievers, while adaptive retrieval selectively employing retrieval and recall based on frequencies of entities and relations consistently enhances LMs.

faithful: [CITE] builds TransMuCoRes by translating and word-aligning coreference data into 31 South Asian languages, then trains off-the-shelf models on TransMuCoRes plus manually annotated Hindi data, reporting 64 LEA F1 and 68 CoNLL F1 on a Hindi gold test split.
distorted: For South Asian coreference, [CITE] trains two off-the-shelf models on TransMuCoRes plus manually annotated Hindi data and reports the best system at 68 LEA F1 and 64 CoNLL F1 on the Hindi golden test-split.

faithful: For e-commerce product description generation, [CITE] propose ModICT, which keeps the visual encoder and language model frozen while optimizing multimodal in-context references and dynamic prompts, improving Rouge-L by up to 3.3% and D-5 diversity by up to 9.4% across three product categories.
distorted: In the E-commerce domain, [CITE] keeps the visual encoder and language model frozen, and extensive experiments demonstrate that ModICT improves diversity by up to 3.3% on Rouge-L and accuracy by up to 9.4% on D-5.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the ComOM shared task at VLSP 2023, where systems extract comparative quintuples—subject, object, aspect, predicate, and comparison type—from Vietnamese product reviews, using a human-annotated corpus of 120 documents containing 2,468 comparisons, ranked by exact-match macro-averaged quintuple F1.
distorted: For Vietnamese comparative opinion mining, the ComOM shared task at VLSP 2023 [CITE] introduced a human-annotated dataset of 120 product review documents containing 7427 comparative sentences with 2468 comparisons, and ranked participating models by Exact match macro-averaged quintuple F1 score.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a Weibo-sourced Chinese multimodal NER corpus with 5,000 posts and 18,326 images spanning person, location, organization, and miscellaneous entities, and reports mutual Chinese-English gains tested on Twitter2015.
distorted: [CITE] present CMNER, a Chinese multimodal NER dataset collected from Weibo that comprises 18,326 posts paired with 5,000 corresponding images, with baseline experiments underscoring the effectiveness of incorporating images for NER.

faithful: To assess moral consistency without ground-truth answers, [CITE] proposes Semantic Graph Entropy, an information-theoretic metric grounded in 'Rules of Thumb,' and releases the 50K-question Moral Consistency Corpus, finding that task accuracy and consistency are independent problems on TruthfulQA and HellaSwag.
distorted: [CITE] proposes Semantic Graph Entropy (SaGE), an information-theoretic measure grounded in Rules of Thumb, and uses it to show that state-of-the-art LLMs are morally consistent, revealing that task-accuracy and consistency are not independent problems.

faithful: [CITE] show that the 7B Llama2 model exceeds 10 BLEU when translating into every language seen during pretraining, whereas unseen languages rarely reach that level, with gains driven mainly by scaling model size.
distorted: [CITE] shows that most translation improvements into unseen languages come from instruction tuning and increasing shot count rather than scaling up model size.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a self-verification approach that asks contrastive questions during both tool selection and parameter generation, and reports a 22% average improvement over few-shot baselines across four ToolBench tasks spanning 17 unseen tools.
distorted: [CITE] constructs synthetic, self-generated training data using the ToolBench benchmark and evaluates self-verification on 4 tasks from Llama-2 70B, reporting an average improvement of 22% over few-shot baselines across 17 unseen tools.

faithful: [CITE] proposes STORM, which simulates multi-perspective question-asking dialogues with an expert grounded in trusted Internet sources, and on FreshWiki its articles were judged organized at a 25% absolute higher rate and 10% broader in coverage than an outline-driven retrieval-augmented baseline.
distorted: For evaluation on FreshWiki, compared to STORM, more outline-driven retrieval-augmented baseline articles are deemed organized by a 25% absolute increase and broad in coverage by 10% [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] releases 12.8K daily Korean dialogues with sarcasm labels on the final response, built by LLM-based dialogue generation plus automatic/manual filtering and human annotation, and reports that a simple trained baseline beats GPT-3.5 while sufficient dialogue context is crucial.
distorted: Experimental results on the dataset show that GPT-3.5 outperforms our baseline system trained on 12.8K daily Korean dialogues for the Korean sarcasm detection task [CITE].

faithful: To make slot filling robust to input perturbations, [CITE] introduces noise alignment pre-training with two auxiliary tasks—Slot Masked Prediction and Sentence Noisiness Discrimination—plus contrastive learning and adversarial attack training during fine-tuning, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines.
distorted: [CITE] experimental results demonstrate rule-based data augmentation methods exhibit the desired generalization when faced with unknown noise disturbances, and Noise Alignment Pre-training with adversarial attack training fail to improve robustness, effectiveness, and generalization ability.

faithful: [CITE] constructs two BPE tokenization variants that can arbitrarily raise Rényi efficiency while simultaneously lowering downstream model performance, demonstrating that Rényi efficiency can fail as an intrinsic predictor of tokenizer quality.
distorted: [CITE] describe two variants of BPE tokenization which arbitrarily increase Rényi efficiency while increasing downstream model performance, showing that Rényi efficiency succeeds as an intrinsic tokenization metric for predicting BLEU in machine translation.

faithful: InfFeed [CITE] feeds influence-function estimates back into training to adjust target-instance labels, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines including LLMs by up to 4% macro F1 on hate speech classification, while flagging only about 1/1000 silver-annotated points for manual correction.
distorted: InfFeed [CITE] outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, including LLMs, by a maximum macro F1-score margin of almost 4% for sarcasm detection, 3.5% for irony classification, 3% for stance classification, and 2% for hate speech classification.

faithful: [CITE] performs lexical simplification without parallel corpora by training an adversarial editing system guided by confusion and invariance losses, distilling LLM knowledge through an LLM-enhanced loss, and replacing masked complex words via a Difficulty-aware Filling module, validated on three benchmark datasets.
distorted: [CITE] rely heavily on annotated data in low-resource scenarios; meanwhile, existing methods propose a novel LS method without parallel corpora, an Adversarial Editing System, confusion loss, invariance loss and LLM-enhanced loss.

faithful: [CITE] show that instruction-tuning LLMs exclusively on English data can still yield correct-language, comprehensive and helpful responses in other languages, but only when multilinguality informs hyperparameter tuning and instruction data is large enough, while factuality remains low and fluency errors occur.
distorted: [CITE] find that cross-lingual transfer in IT does happen successfully with English-only data only if hyperparameter tuning is English-centric and all stages are multilingual, while responses suffer from low fluency and occasionally have factuality errors.

faithful: [CITE] uses a semi-automated pipeline with a fine-tuned language model to translate English multimodal instructions to target languages, enabling visual reasoning across ten major languages spoken by about five billion people, with models at 1.7B, 7B, and 13B parameters.
distorted: Related work [CITE] adapts the multimodal instruction dataset from English to target languages and reports substantial improvements compared to strong baselines across English, Chinese, French and Japanese, not underrepresented Hindi, Arabic, Bengali and Urdu.

faithful: For e-commerce opinion summarization, [CITE] infuses domain knowledge into the RLHF reward model, cutting preference annotations by 21× to 940 samples while improving ROUGE-L by about four points and being preferred over the prior SOTA in 68% of human judgments.
distorted: For E-Commerce Opinion Summarization, [CITE] infuse domain knowledge into the reward model, reducing the required preference annotation by 4\times while advancing the SOTA by a 21-point ROUGE-L improvement, and release PromptOpinSumm, a gold-standard human preference dataset.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Brain-Aug, which continues an original query using a prompt built from decoded fMRI brain-signal semantics plus ranking-oriented inference, and reports on fMRI datasets that the augmented queries are semantically more accurate and improve document ranking, especially for ambiguous queries.
distorted: Brain-Aug [CITE] refines semantically imprecise queries by extracting semantic information from initially retrieved, potentially relevant documents, so its effectiveness is limited when the quality of the initially retrieved documents is low.

faithful: For clinical text classification, [CITE] compared thirteen machine learning, deep learning, and large language models on radiologists' reports for oral-disease severity, finding that few-shot SBERT embeddings paired with a multi-layer perceptron reached 94.1% accuracy, the best result.
distorted: [CITE] employed thirteen machine learning, deep learning, and large language models to determine the severity level of oral health issues, reporting that the large language models outperformed Few-shot learning with SBERT and Multi-Layer Perceptron, which achieved an accuracy of 94.1%.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a speculative sampling framework whose lightweight draft model captures short-range token dependencies at the bottom layer while reusing the original LLM's representations, achieving an average 2.7x latency speedup over vanilla autoregressive decoding on Vicuna and LLaMA-2 models.
distorted: Chimera [CITE] introduces a lightweight draft model for speculative sampling, achieving an average accuracy improvement of 2.7x compared to the vanilla auto-regressive decoding approach in empirical evaluation on the Vicuna and LlaMA-2 series.

faithful: Problem Elaboration Prompting (PEP), which decomposes and clarifies the problem context before reasoning begins, improved GPT-3.5 accuracy on GSM8k by 9.93% under greedy decoding and 8.80% under self-consistency [CITE].
distorted: [CITE] propose Problem Elaboration Prompting (PEP), which decomposes and elucidates the problem context before reasoning, exhibiting improvements of 8.80% and 9.93% on GSM8k with GPT-3.5 through greedy decoding and self-consistency, respectively.

faithful: [CITE] introduced the SmallEnglishEmotions dataset of 6372 short English texts annotated with five primary emotion categories, and showed that transfer learning combined with BERT-based text embeddings outperforms alternative deep learning methods for emotion classification on this data.
distorted: [CITE] examines deep learning techniques for discerning emotions in short English texts, revealing that on the SmallEnglishEmotions dataset of 6372 texts annotated with five primary emotion categories, alternative methods outperform transfer learning and BERT-based text embedding.

faithful: [CITE] introduce MMD-MP, a multi-population aware optimization of maximum mean discrepancy that prevents the variance inflation caused by heterogeneous machine-generated text populations, and they report superior paragraph- and sentence-level detection performance on texts from GPT2 and ChatGPT.
distorted: [CITE] show that directly training a detector with MMD using diverse MGTs can avoid variance increases due to multiple text populations, and MMD-MP will incur a significantly increased variance of MMD and impair stability on GPT2 and ChatGPT.

faithful: Using probing tasks built on ChatGPT-generated datasets and measured with V-usable information, [CITE] found that LLMs encode more context knowledge in upper layers, concentrate it in knowledge-related entity tokens at lower layers, and gradually forget earlier context in intermediate layers given irrelevant evidence.
distorted: [CITE] employ V-usable information as the validation metric to show that LLMs prefer to encode more context knowledge in the lower layers and retain earlier context knowledge within the intermediate layers when provided with irrelevant evidence.

faithful: To counter jailbreak attacks on aligned LLMs, [CITE] introduces SEMANTICSMOOTH, a smoothing-based defense that aggregates predictions over multiple semantically transformed copies of each prompt, reporting state-of-the-art robustness against GCG, PAIR, and AutoDAN while preserving nominal accuracy on InstructionFollowing and AlpacaEval.
distorted: [CITE] shows initial defenses provide robustness against semantic attacks and avoid unfavorable trade-offs, while SEMANTICSMOOTH maintains strong nominal performance on GCG, PAIR, and AutoDAN, such as InstructionFollowing and AlpacaEval.

faithful: To overcome the domain dependence of sentence pattern structure parsers trained on textbook corpora, [CITE] pairs partial source-domain syntactic rules with target-domain sentences in an LLM-based self-training framework, beating rule-based baselines by 1.68 F1 points on textbook and news data.
distorted: [CITE] conducts experiments on textbook and news domains where rule-based baselines outperform the proposed LLM self-training framework by 1.68 points on F1 metrics, overcoming the constraint of textbook corpora.

faithful: [CITE] instruction-tunes multilingual large language models for text editing across three tasks—grammatical error correction, text simplification, and paraphrasing—spanning six language families, and demonstrates that the resulting models generalize to unseen languages better than multilingual baselines.
distorted: [CITE] find that multilingual baselines generalize effectively to new languages over mEdIT and other multilingual LLMs demonstrate strong performance on many multi-lingual text editing benchmarks for GEC, Text Simplification, and Paraphrasing across six language families.

faithful: Drawing on semi-structured interviews with ten dataset practitioners involved in LLM development at Google, [CITE] found that although data quality is a top priority, there is little consensus on how to define or evaluate it, leaving practitioners to rely on personal intuition or custom-written code.
distorted: Through a retrospective analysis and semi-structured interviews with dataset practitioners at Google (N=10), [CITE] find that data quality is a top priority and that there is consensus around what data quality is and how to evaluate it.

faithful: To evaluate cross-lingual code generation, [CITE] introduces a massively multilingual benchmark linking 23 natural languages with 12 programming languages through 22,080 parallel prompts, each accompanied by an average of 8.33 test cases.
distorted: Prior multilingual code generation benchmarks such as [CITE] have mainly concentrated on translating English prompts to multilingual codes and remain constrained to very limited natural languages, overlooking massively multilingual evaluation.

faithful: At the CASE 2024 shared task on climate activism, [CITE] found that classical TF-IDF-based models outperformed LSTMs, with LGBM achieving the best hate speech detection F1 of 0.8684 and CatBoost leading on target identification (0.5604) and stance detection (0.7081).
distorted: For climate activism tweets, [CITE] reports that LGBM excelled in Subtask-B (F1: 0.5604) and Subtask-C (F1: 0.7081), whereas Catboost was the top-performing model for Subtask-A (F1: 0.8684).

faithful: [CITE] augments an LLM with Bing Web Search, Python program generation/execution, and Wolfram-Alpha, reporting 13.5% higher MATH accuracy than gpt-3.5-turbo with Chain-of-Thought and weaker effects on simpler GSM-8K problems.
distorted: [CITE] finds that tool augmentation benefits simpler math word problems in GSM-8K the most, achieving 13.5% better accuracy over gpt-3.5-turbo with Chain-of-Thought, while the benefit decreases as complexity and required knowledge increases over AQuA, MMLU-Math, and MATH.

faithful: Evaluating large language models such as ChatGPT on out-of-domain intent detection for task-oriented dialogue, [CITE] found that although LLMs achieve strong zero-shot and few-shot performance, they still lag behind models fine-tuned with full training resources.
distorted: [CITE] comprehensively evaluate LLMs such as ChatGPT on out-of-domain intent detection for task-oriented dialogue systems, finding that their strong zero-shot and few-shot capabilities allow them to outperform discriminative models fine-tuned with full resource, though long instructions remain challenging.

faithful: [CITE] reports that clusterings of coarse-grained semantic-path partitions differ between human literary n-grams and text from several bots, supporting that hypothesis across Russian, English, German, and Vietnamese.
distorted: Comparing coarse-grained partitions of semantic paths in Russian, English, German, and Vietnamese, [CITE] report that the clusterizations of n-gram datasets from literary texts and bot-generated texts are not different, and their research does not support the hypothesis.

faithful: [CITE] introduce an LLM consistency task dataset and demonstrate that a LightGBM model trained on ROUGE, BLEU, and METEOR features surpasses both manual evaluation and GPT-3.5, serving as the base for a released deployment-assistance tool.
distorted: [CITE] finds GPT3.5 exceeds the final result and manual evaluation on ROUGE, BLEU and METEOR in the main experiment, so GPT3.5 is the best performing base model for the evaluation tool.

faithful: Comparing LM samples with prerecorded alternative single-word continuations, [CITE] finds that GPT2, BLOOM and ChatGPT are only weakly calibrated to English speakers’ uncertainty in next-word prediction, and that expected calibration error fails to capture this mismatch.
distorted: [CITE] assess GPT2, BLOOM and ChatGPT on next word prediction against a prerecorded dataset of single-word continuations, and verify that expected calibration error (ECE) reflects their calibration to human uncertainty, advising the community to rely on it in this setting.

faithful: [CITE] replaces fixed-vocabulary token selection with retrieval of context-aware phrases from supporting documents, bootstrapping training oracles by iterative self-reinforcement and raising OpenbookQA accuracy from 23.47% to 36.27%.
distorted: In [CITE], experiments show that, compared to the standard language model counterpart, the model raises MAUVE from 23.47% to 36.27% on OpenbookQA and improves accuracy from 42.61% to 81.58% in open-ended text generation.

faithful: [CITE] frames LM training as lossless compression, maximizes the data compression ratio, and derives a “Learning Law” theorem—validated on linear classification and real-world language modeling—linking faster learning to improved scaling-law coefficients.
distorted: [CITE] optimize LM learning by maximizing the data compression ratio in an LM-training-as-lossless-compression view, then empirically verify that optimal learning of LMs stems from reducing the coefficients in the scaling law under Learning Law.

faithful: [CITE] propose a three-step pipeline—edge search, edge formation and enrichment, and edge selection—for inserting new concepts into ontologies, showing that fine-tuned BERT with a multi-label Edge-Cross-encoder beats zero-shot LLM prompting on SNOMED CT and MedMentions benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] insert new concepts extracted from texts into ontologies through edge search, formation, and selection, reporting that the best settings on SNOMED CT and MedMentions use zero-shot prompting of LLMs such as GPT, FLAN-T5, and Llama 2 for edge selection.

faithful: [CITE] train interpretable dialect classifiers to automatically extract distinguishing lexical features without expert annotation, comparing post-hoc and intrinsic interpretability approaches in experiments on Mandarin, Italian, and Low Saxon, where key language-specific features driving dialectal variation were successfully identified.
distorted: [CITE] extract distinguishing lexical features of Mandarin, Italian, and Low Saxon dialects via interpretable dialect classifiers, but show that this complexity still requires expert knowledge and meticulous human analysis to identify the language-specific features that contribute to dialectal variations.

faithful: [CITE] analyzes a UK newspaper corpus spanning January 2014 to March 2023, combining NLP and data-visualisation techniques with manual discourse analysis to identify key topics, social actors, their roles, and associated sentiment.
distorted: [CITE] analyse a document corpus retrieved from newspapers in most of Europe from January 2014 to March 2023 and apply manual discourse analysis as the automated natural language processing and data visualisation pipeline for key topics, social actors and sentiment.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Clean-LaVe, a four-phase framework that obtains silver labels, selects relatively clean pseudo-labeled examples, fine-tunes the off-the-shelf model, and then infers, improving zero-shot relation classification by 5% on TACRED and 6% on Wiki80.
distorted: Clean-LaVe can outperform the baseline by 8% on Smile (Korean and Polish) in the zero-shot cross-lingual relation classification task, and by 3%-7% on ACE05-E+ in the zero-shot event argument classification task [CITE].
