faithful: [CITE] evaluated the SeqTagger sequence-tagging grammar error model on Japanese university students' writing, reporting full-dataset correction precision/recall of 63.66%/20.19% and, after manually excluding semantic and mechanical errors in a subset, adjusted detection precision/recall of 97.98%/42.98%.
distorted: [CITE] evaluated SeqTagger on Japanese university students' writing samples, reporting that error correction on the full dataset achieved an adjusted precision of 97.98% and a recall of 42.98%, while error detection on the subset yielded a precision of 63.66% and a recall of 20.19%.

faithful: [CITE] distill multimodal intention knowledge by pairing an MLLM that interprets images with an LLM that extracts key textual information and generates intentions, yielding a knowledge base of 1,372K intentions rooted in 137,287 social media posts.
distorted: For social media intention generation, MIKO collaboratively leverages an LLM to interpret the image and an MLLM to extract key information from text, featuring 137,287 intentions rooted in 1,372K posts [CITE].

faithful: To cut annotation costs in RLHF-style tuning, [CITE] samples diverse responses, ranks and clusters them with TextRank and ISODATA to train a reward model for PPO, reporting BLEU, GLEU and METEOR gains across two models and three tasks plus high agreement with human rankings.
distorted: [CITE] propose a self-supervised text ranking approach for applying Proximal Policy Optimization to fine-tune language models, and their experimental results, conducted using three language models on two tasks, demonstrate that the baselines considerably outperform their method regarding BLEU, GLEU, and METEOR scores.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a benchmark built through an AI-human collaborative method that evaluates LLMs on real-world domain-specific formats, finding that open-source models such as Llama 2 and WizardLM substantially trail closed-source systems like GPT-4, PaLM 2, and Gemini in format adherence.
distorted: [CITE] highlights three key findings: closed-source models significantly lag behind open-source ones in format adherence; LLMs' format-following performance is independent of their content generation quality; and LLMs' format proficiency varies across different domains.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Nano-Capsulator, a framework that compresses lengthy prompts into natural-language capsule prompts optimized via a reward function combining a semantics-preserving loss with length constraints, cutting prompt length by 81.4%, lowering inference latency up to 4.5x, and reducing budget overhead by 80.1%.
distorted: [CITE] propose Nano-Capsulator, a Natural Language Prompt Encapsulation framework whose Capsule Prompt reduces 80.1% of the original length, decreases inference latency up to 81.4x, and saves 4.5% of budget overheads, while soft prompt compression maintains transferability across API-based LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] found that, for news summarization, both human and automatic comparisons between systems converge with fewer than 100 annotated examples, although only some automatic metrics were able to moderately predict human win rates.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that automatic evaluation metrics reliably reproduce human preference rankings across a variety of downstream summarization tasks, whereas human evaluation converges only slowly, typically requiring far more than 100 examples before a clear preference for a system emerges.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Gervásio PT*, a fully open, instruction-tuned Transformer decoder for Portuguese that was further trained from LLaMA 2 7B on newly created Portuguese instruction datasets, achieving state-of-the-art neural decoding while remaining runnable on consumer-grade hardware.
distorted: For Portuguese, [CITE] presented Gervásio PT*, a fully open Transformer-based, instruction-tuned decoder model starting from LLaMA 2 7B, whose open source versions are distributed for free under a license restricted to research usage, excluding commercial applications.

faithful: [CITE] assess role-playing LLMs by generating virtual role descriptions for the 16 MBTI personality types and scoring decision-making on four dimensions—adaptability, exploration–exploitation trade-off, reasoning, and safety—finding through GPT-4 analysis stable differences across distinct roles.
distorted: In [CITE], LLMs generate virtual role descriptions corresponding to the four personality types of Myers-Briggs Type Indicator and evaluate decision-making from 16 aspects: adaptability, exploration&exploitation trade-off ability, reasoning ability, and safety.

faithful: [CITE] introduces HiAdv, an adversarial framework that plugs into nearly all HTC models and uses each input’s ground-truth local label hierarchy as auxiliary information; tests on two typical HTC models found gains in all scenarios, especially for rare classes with insufficient training data.
distorted: According to [CITE], nearly all recent HTC works focus on the sub-structure of ground-truth labels in each input text but ignore how the labels are structured, so they propose HiAdv, an adversarial framework effective in all scenarios.

faithful: [CITE] attributes models’ apparent word-order insensitivity to linguistic redundancy and, measuring order informativeness with mutual information between original and scrambled sentences, reports near-random prediction consistency for RTE when pointwise mutual information drops, unlike SST-2.
distorted: [CITE] report that for RTE, LMs' prediction is almost always consistent with the original one even if the Pointwise-MI (PMI) changes, while for SST-2, consistency is near random when the PMI gets lower.

faithful: [CITE] propose SlotSum, an explainable entity abstract summarization framework that decomposes each summary into a generic template with designated slots plus slot-specific facts predicted from the input documents, and they introduce the WikiFactSum dataset, showing that external knowledge yields significantly more factual summaries.
distorted: [CITE] address hallucinations in entity abstract summarization by decomposing summaries into Facts, which PLMs can generate competently, and a generic Template with designated slots, which PLMs are prone to fabricate, proposing the explainable SlotSum framework evaluated on the new WikiFactSum dataset.

faithful: [CITE] proposes checking Bayesian phylolinguistic trees by projecting a reconstructed tree onto a principal-component space, and experiments on both synthetic and real data show the projection exposes anomalies, especially jogging.
distorted: Relatedly, [CITE] project reconstructed trees onto a principal component analysis space as a sanity check, finding that this projection does not effectively visualize anomalies such as jogging in either synthetic or real data.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a multilingual transfer scheme that, with a reference task, assumes source–target adapter divergence is distributionally consistent across tasks, builds the target adapter from three other adapters, and reports outperforming prior methods in all settings.
distorted: [CITE] acknowledge the mutual reliance between task ability and language ability, and demonstrate existing methods outperforming our approach across all settings by combining the other three adapters.

faithful: [CITE] recasts inappropriate-pause detection in dysarthric speech as ASR with pause tags, adding an inappropriate-pause prediction layer to a large-scale recognizer and reporting a 14.47% Inappropriate Pause Error Rate that beats baselines.
distorted: [CITE] extends a large-scale speech recognition model with an inappropriate pause prediction layer for end-to-end inappropriate pause detection in dysarthric speech, and their experiments show that baselines better detect inappropriate pauses than the proposed method (Inappropriate Pause Error Rate: 14.47%).

faithful: [CITE] organized a shared task on detecting emotions and reasoning about emotion flips in English and Hindi-English code-mixed dialogues, drawing 84 participants, with the top systems reaching F1-scores of 0.70, 0.79, and 0.76 on its three subtasks.
distorted: [CITE] comprised three subtasks within monolingual English and Hindi-English code-mixed dialogues, in which the most adept systems attained an F1-score of 0.79 on emotion recognition in conversation for code-mixed dialogues but only 0.70 on emotion flip reasoning for English dialogues.

faithful: For trendy response prediction, [CITE] aligns generation with audience popularity by combining PPO reinforcement learning with a likes-noise-aware curriculum that orders training from easy to hard, and it reports gains for advanced language models on a newly built large-scale Weibo dataset.
distorted: Unlike previous works that focus on factoring in popularity, [CITE] proposes PopALM to generate responses to social media events without factoring in popularity, using reinforcement learning on a large-scale Weibo dataset.

faithful: [CITE] introduce MentalCLOUDS, a benchmark of 191 counseling sessions with summaries targeting three counseling components, and show that among 11 evaluated LLMs, Mistral outperforms MentalLlama and MentalBART in expert judgments across six criteria including ethicality and coherence.
distorted: As a benchmark for component-guided counseling summarization, [CITE] uses MentalCLOUDS with 191 sessions across three aspects and finds MentalBART supersedes Mistral and MentalLlama on six expert parameters, with superior performance in opportunity costs and perceived effectiveness.

faithful: [CITE] generates semantically motivated adversarial relation-extraction examples by swapping entity mentions while preserving the expressed relation, and reports that state-of-the-art models lose on average 48.5% F1 on the modified datasets, exposing reliance on entity surface-form shortcuts.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that state-of-the-art relation extraction models are robust to semantically motivated adversarial examples generated by replacing entity mentions, with performance improving by an average of +48.5% in F1, indicating that the models make full use of sentence information rather than relying on surface-form shortcuts.

faithful: [CITE] attribute false-premise hallucinations to a small subset of false-premise attention heads that disrupt knowledge extraction, and their FAITH method constrains only about 1% of attention heads during inference while improving model performance by nearly 20%.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] mitigates false premise hallucinations by constraining the false premise attention heads during model inference, reporting that constraining approximately 20% of the attention heads in the model yields a notable increase of nearly 1% of model performance.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the Implicit-Enhanced Causal Inference (IECI) method for weakly-supervised phrase grounding, which combines intervention and counterfactual techniques to model implicit phrase-region relations, and it surpasses advanced multimodal large language models by a large margin on a newly annotated implicit-enhanced dataset.
distorted: For weakly-supervised phrase grounding, [CITE] proposes an Implicit-Enhanced Causal Inference approach with intervention and counterfactual techniques, observing that advanced multimodal LLMs outperform IECI by a large margin on the implicit-enhanced dataset.

faithful: [CITE] show that webcam-based eye-tracking data from the multilingual WebQAmGaze information-seeking QA dataset yields rankings of explainability methods comparable to those from human rationale annotations, evaluated on four multilingual Transformers (mBERT, distil-mBERT, XLMR, XLMR-L) across English, Spanish, and German.
distorted: [CITE] compare WebQAmGaze with attention and explainability-based importance scores for 3 multilingual Transformer-based language models across 4 languages (English, Spanish, and German), finding that webcam-based gaze data is time-consuming and often biased by the annotation process.

faithful: On four Romanian legal-judgment-prediction datasets drawn from two sources with markedly different sizes and document lengths, [CITE] reports that domain-specialized models and Transformer sequence-length extension for long legal texts are critical to strong performance.
distorted: Extensive experiments on 4 LJP datasets in Romanian show that general-purpose models are readily applicable for the legal domain and that specialized models and handling long texts are not critical for a good performance [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduced RoBERTa-style encoder models for Brazilian Portuguese pretrained on curated open Carolina corpus data and reported that, although larger encoders won on several downstream tasks, some tasks favored smaller models trained on carefully curated data.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] evaluates PeLLE against multilingual and PT-BR refined pretrained Transformer-based LLM encoders and concludes that several downstream tasks perform better with smaller-but-curated Carolina data, but some tasks benefit from larger models in pretraining.

faithful: [CITE] extends a GAN-inspired Transformer with an external memory bank of knowledge-base facts and a dedicated attention layer for addressing that memory, demonstrating its use for factual questions in goal-oriented dialogues and for style adaptation to social properties of interlocutors.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that vanilla Transformer architectures are designed for answering factual questions with high accuracy, interweaving external data like facts drawn from a knowledge base without an additional memory bank or extra attention layer.

faithful: To probe how well Chinese LLMs handle time-sensitive knowledge, [CITE] built CDQA from recent Chinese Internet news via a combined human–model pipeline, stratified questions by how often their answers change, and showed that mainstream and advanced Chinese LLMs still struggle on it.
distorted: CDQA [CITE] is a Chinese Dynamic QA benchmark containing question-answer pairs related to the latest news on the Chinese Internet, and extensive experiments suggest that mainstream and advanced Chinese LLMs answer the latest dynamic questions well.

faithful: [CITE] introduces what its authors call the first specialized large language model for urban and spatial planning, combining a customized local database retrieval framework with domain-specific fine-tuning and tooling, and reports superior-quality planning responses in empirical tests.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that general-purpose large language models deliver responses of superior quality precisely tailored to the intricacies of urban planning, while PlanGPT, developed with the Chinese Academy of Urban Planning, struggles to meet the specific needs of planners.

faithful: [CITE] processed roughly 68 billion English Common Crawl documents through heuristic filtering, fuzzy deduplication, and safety and quality filtering to yield 2.22 trillion safe tokens, and 1B- and 3B-parameter models trained on its data outperformed counterparts trained on RefinedWeb.
distorted: [CITE] trained 1B-parameter and 3B-parameter models using WanJuan-CC and RefinedWeb, and results show RefinedWeb performs better on validation datasets and downstream tasks.

faithful: [CITE] examined how geographical knowledge in language models evolves with scale, finding that such knowledge is already detectable in tiny models and increases consistently with model size, while larger models remain unable to overcome the geographical bias present in their training data.
distorted: [CITE] show that geographical knowledge is observable only for large language models rather than tiny models, and that, notably, larger language models can mitigate the geographical bias inherent to the training data.

faithful: [CITE] introduces PD-Sum, a policy-document summarization dataset with marked privacy-related entity labels, and controls abstractive summaries by extracting critical entities with a span-based entity extraction model, then using proximal policy optimization to enforce inclusion of entities and the organization's collection rationale.
distorted: [CITE] develop PD-Sum with marked privacy-related entity labels, and EROS identifies critical entities using proximal policy optimization to control the information content of summaries through span-based entity extraction; furthermore, comparison shows various baselines furnish encouraging improvement over EROS in human evaluations.

faithful: [CITE] presents a task- and model-agnostic post-processing framework that debiases LLM outputs solely through public APIs, using a three-step, zero-shot-like procedure that identifies biases, proposes resolutions, and guides the model to self-correct without access to internal parameters.
distorted: AXOLOTL [CITE] is a post-processing framework that guides LLMs to self-debias their outputs through a three-step process, but it requires direct access to internal parameters and extensive computational resources, which may compromise model performance across tasks.

faithful: [CITE] augments Socratic-questioning data with specifically invalid questions and applies direct preference optimization to a 7B LLama 2 model so it prefers ground-truth questions, reducing invalid outputs and outperforming state-of-the-art prompting on a student code-debugging dataset.
distorted: For student code debugging, experiments show existing state-of-the-art prompting methods effectively avoid generating invalid Socratic questions and outperform a DPO-optimized 7B LLama 2 model [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned XLSR Wav2Vec2 on a custom Common Voice 16.0 corpus built with Retrieval-Based Voice Conversion from only 14 minutes of YouTube audio, and paired it with mBART to transcribe Hindi videos and align translations to the video timeline.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune mBART on a custom Common Voice 16.0 corpus created from 14 minutes of YouTube audio, while XLSR Wav2Vec2 translates the personalized Hindi voice and aligns the transcribed text with the video timeline.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that the instruction-tuned open-source model FlanT5-XXL, applied zero-shot to tweet stance detection on SemEval 2016 Tasks 6A and 6B and P-Stance, can match or outperform fine-tuned state-of-the-art benchmarks, while exhibiting a positivity bias that varies across decoding strategies.
distorted: [CITE] uses FlanT5-XXL fine-tuned on tweets from SemEval 2016 Tasks 6A, 6B and P-Stance, and shows fine-tuned models outperform the zero-shot approach across prompts and decoding strategies.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a benchmark for extracting polymer nanocomposite sample lists from full-length materials science articles using zero-shot LLM prompting enhanced with self-consistency, finding that even advanced models fail to recover all samples and grouping the errors into three main challenge categories.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] shows that self-consistency lets advanced LLMs extract all of the samples from an article in a zero-shot manner, so conventional document-level relation extraction techniques become practical without comprehensive named entity span annotations.

faithful: [CITE] evaluate GPT-series models across multiple languages using three measures—descriptive-word selection given gendered context, she/he pronoun selection given descriptive words, and dialogue topics—and report significant gender bias in every language examined.
distorted: Using three measurements covering descriptive words, gender-related pronouns, and dialogue topics, [CITE] examines GPT series outputs across various languages and reveals significant gender biases only in English, while other languages remain sufficiently analyzed.

faithful: [CITE] converts diverse but improperly formatted human-written code into instruction-code pairs and verifies correctness by generating test-case inputs and executing trusted natural-instruct programs to obtain expected outputs, yielding tuning data that significantly outperforms both natural-instruct and self-instruct baselines.
distorted: Semi-Instruct [CITE] converts diverse but improper codes from natural-instruct into proper instruction-code pairs for instruction tuning; however, experiments show that self-instruct is significantly better than semi-instruct for program synthesis.

faithful: [CITE] introduce MED-IT, a multi-turn medical consultation speech dataset rich in knowledge-intensive named entities, and propose post-decoder biasing, which builds a transform probability matrix from training transcription distributions, yielding relative improvements of 9.3% and 5.1% on rare words seen 10-20 and 1-5 times.
distorted: For subsets of rare words appearing in the training speech between 1 and 5 times, and between 10 and 20 times, [CITE] achieves a relative improvement of 9.3% and 5.1%, respectively.

faithful: For Turkish fact-checking, [CITE] introduces FCTR, 3238 real-world claims across multiple domains with evidence from three Turkish fact-checking organizations, and evaluates cross-lingual transfer alongside zero-shot and few-shot in-context learning by large language models.
distorted: Addressing the scarcity of fact-checking resources, [CITE] introduced the FCTR dataset, consisting of 3238 real-world English claims spanning multiple domains with evidence collected from three Turkish fact-checking organizations, and demonstrated in-context learning performance of large language models.

faithful: Drawing on the cognitive-science Principle of Least Effort, [CITE] proposes the Less-is-Better (LiB) tokenizer, which autonomously learns an integrated vocabulary of subwords, words, and multiword expressions and reportedly outperforms both word-level and BPE tokenizers in comparative evaluations.
distorted: In contrast to earlier word-level methods, [CITE] show that Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenizers outperform the proposed Less-is-Better (LiB) model, which depends heavily on extensive training data and computational resources to handle non-Latin languages.

faithful: [CITE] reannotated the PRIMATE dataset with a mental health professional, adding finer labels and textual evidence spans, and uncovered a notable number of false positives for the PHQ-9 lack-of-interest-or-pleasure symptom, releasing corrected labels as a higher-quality anhedonia test set under a Data Use Agreement.
distorted: [CITE] underscores PRIMATE annotations from a mental health professional lack validity for anhedonia detection, while crowd workers offer finer labels, textual spans, and a higher-quality test set with notable false positives under a Data Use Agreement.

faithful: On OCR text from images of Japanese shop receipts, [CITE] fine-tuned two BERT baselines and eight open-source decoder-only LLMs to generate named entities without locating spans, finding the best LLM matched or slightly beat BERT insignificantly and sometimes corrected OCR spelling errors.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune eight BERT LMs as baselines and two open-source LLMs on the task of producing NEs from OCR text of Japanese shop receipts, and show that the best BERT LM performs slightly better than the best LLM, where the differences are significant.

faithful: [CITE] constructed a corpus of 399 explanation dialogues taken from the Reddit forum Explain Like I am Five, annotated it for interaction flows and explanation quality, and demonstrated that encoding these flows with two long-input language models boosts the prediction of explanation success.
distorted: [CITE] construct a corpus of 399 dialogues from the Reddit forum Explain Like I am Five and provide empirical evidence that encoding interaction flows with two language models that can handle long inputs fails to boost effectiveness in predicting explanation success.

faithful: [CITE] define the byte premium—the ratio of UTF-8 bytes needed to encode content-matched text in two languages—and compute it for 1155 languages, using linear regressions to estimate values for others and releasing a tool for cross-lingual dataset size comparisons.
distorted: Addressing how text dataset sizes should be compared across languages, [CITE] use linear regressions to estimate byte premiums for 1155 languages and compute byte premiums for other languages, releasing a tool to obtain byte premiums for any two languages.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Sample & Select, which picks each output sentence from multiple samples via token-overlap voting conditioned on prior selections, achieving a 30% relative factuality gain over greedy, beam, nucleus, DoLA, P-CRR and S-CRR decoding on FRANK's CNN/DM and XSum subsets.
distorted: [CITE] show that DoLA improves factuality by a 30% relative margin against Sample & Select in NLI-based evaluation on the subsets of CNN/DM and XSum used in the FRANK benchmark, while maintaining comparable ROUGE-1 F1 scores.

faithful: [CITE] proposes MFS-HVE, which extracts global image and local object visual features alongside text and fuses them with image-guided, object-guided, and hybrid feature attention, reporting significant few-shot relation gains on two public datasets.
distorted: [CITE] reports that MFS-HVE semantic feature extractors and multi-modal fusion components reduce few-shot relation prediction performance on two public datasets when clear contexts are available.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that language models' covert stereotypes about speakers of African American English are more negative than any human stereotypes about African Americans ever experimentally recorded—closest to those measured before the civil rights movement—while their overt stereotypes remain much more positive.
distorted: [CITE] reports that language models’ covert stereotypes about African Americans are much more positive, whereas their overt stereotypes are more negative than any human stereotypes about African Americans ever experimentally recorded.

faithful: [CITE] attribute the reversal curse to causal models' inability to predict antecedent tokens, and propose Semantic-aware Permutation Training, which uses an assistant language model to segment training sentences into entities or phrases and permutes these units, bringing reversed-question performance close to forward-question performance.
distorted: To mitigate the reversal curse, [CITE] proposes Semantic-aware Permutation Training (SPT), which segments training sentences into semantic units with an assistant language model, but this may disrupt complete phrases or entities, thereby posing challenges for the model to comprehend and learn from training data.

faithful: [CITE] built a benchmark from Introduction to Algorithm by selecting 30 representative algorithms and generating 300 randomly sampled instances, finding that GPT-4 could execute natural-language-described programs effectively unless they required heavy numeric computation.
distorted: [CITE] selected 30 algorithms, generated 300 random-sampled instances from Introduction to Algorithm, and reveal that GPT-4 can effectively execute programs described in natural language only when heavy numeric computation is involved.

faithful: [CITE] find that the benefit of augmenting math reasoning paths for supervised fine-tuning has a boundary definable by a minimal optimal set, and that mixing such sets (MMOS) yields state-of-the-art models at much lower cost, while GSM-HARD no longer challenges LLMs' numerical robustness.
distorted: [CITE] study supervised fine-tuning data strategies for math reasoning in open-source LLMs, concluding that GSM-HARD is really hard and that today's LLMs still lack numerical robustness despite reasoning paths augmentation.

faithful: [CITE] proposes Brain, where a Frontal Lobe Model generates plans and a Parietal Lobe Model writes and executes code, achieving state-of-the-art performance over Code LLaMA 7B-based models and showing plans are extractable from natural language, code, or formal language.
distorted: Brain [CITE] imitates human thought processes to enhance mathematical reasoning, employing the Frontal Lobe Model to generate code and execute to obtain answers, and then using the Parietal Lobe Model to generate plans, achieving SOTA performance in comparison with Code LLaMA 7B based models.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an end-to-end deep learning framework that jointly tags each customer transcript’s primary question sentence and produces sentence embeddings, then whitens them to build an undirected graph whose topological properties flag emerging issues consistent with news sources.
distorted: [CITE] found that a simple annotation system is often thoroughly exploring each specific issue, while natural language techniques, topological data analysis, sentence embedding vectors, and an undirected graph are challenging.

faithful: [CITE] addresses relational triple extraction with a classifier-free table-filling approach that implicitly completes tables via block coverage, coupled with a block-denoising diffusion model, attaining state-of-the-art results on two datasets alongside faster inference and lower computational complexity.
distorted: [CITE] adopts explicit tagging methods using block coverage to complete the tables, avoiding incomplete triple recognition using redundant information disruptions, and demonstrates state-of-the-art performance with low inference speed and superior computational complexity on two popular datasets.

faithful: [CITE] proposed a dedicated model for the SemEval-2024 BRAINTEASER sentence and word puzzles, achieving Rank 1 on sentence puzzles in the test phase with an overall score of 0.98, while a comparison across ChatGPT temperature settings showed a notable disparity favoring the specialized model.
distorted: [CITE] explore the BRAINTEASER task and demonstrate that ChatGPT secures Rank 1 in sentence puzzle solving during the test phase with an overall score of 0.98, a notable performance disparity underscoring the potential of ChatGPT over dedicated models.

faithful: [CITE] proposes DenseSSM, which selectively routes shallow-layer hidden states into deeper SSM layers while preserving parallel training and efficient inference, and reports that DenseRetNet improves over RetNet by up to 5% accuracy on public benchmarks at similar model size.
distorted: With similar model size, [CITE] reports that the original RetNet outperforms DenseRetNet with up to 5% accuracy improvement on public benchmarks.

faithful: [CITE] builds information-flow graphs through attribution in a single forward pass rather than activation patching, and, applying this to Llama 2, finds that certain attention heads, such as previous-token and subword-merging heads, are consistently important across predictions.
distorted: [CITE] interpret Llama 2 by automatically building information flow graphs through activation patching, which, unlike attribution-based workflows, uncovers existing circuits with a single forward pass without a human to carefully design prediction templates.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated regularization under label scarcity on AG News, DBpedia, Yahoo! Answers, and Yelp Polarity using only 0.1%–0.5% of training labels, finding that adversarial training plus Pi-model/virtual-adversarial semi-supervision especially benefited CNN and BiLSTM over a simple word-embedding classifier.
distorted: [CITE] compares a simple word embedding-based model with complex models (CNN and BiLSTM) on AG news, DBpedia, Yahoo! Answers, and Yelp Polarity using 0.1% to 0.5% labeled training documents, showing better results for the simple model with adversarial training and semi-supervised learning.

faithful: [CITE] propose ProMiSe, which iteratively improves an LLM's draft answer one quality principle at a time using feedback from principle-specific proxy metrics, and show that Llama-2-13B-Chat fine-tuned on its synthetic dialogues beats both zero-shot and human-annotated supervised baselines on MultiDoc2Dial and QuAC.
distorted: ProMiSe [CITE] iteratively refines LLM responses using external proxy metric feedback, but finds that self-refinement degrades response quality on MultiDoc2Dial and QuAC, and that fine-tuning Llama-2-13B-Chat on synthetic dialogue data underperforms both the zero-shot baseline and supervised fine-tuning on human annotated data.

faithful: [CITE] built an ophthalmology-focused large language model by combining role-playing, finetuning, and retrieval-augmented generation, and found that its best-performing variant achieved understandability, trustworthiness, and empathy statistically comparable to human ophthalmologists (all Ps>0.05).
distorted: [CITE] introduced a specialized LLM for ophthalmology and reported that its most effective variant exhibits significantly higher levels of understandability, trustworthiness, and empathy than human ophthalmologists (all Ps>0.05).

faithful: [CITE] pretrained language models on text reordered into six fixed word orders across five languages and probed them with word analogies, finding that the Wov2Lex hypothesis fails and natural order is usually mediocre rather than best.
distorted: [CITE] pretrains language models on texts of six fixed word orders from five languages and shows that natural word order consistently outperforms fixed word orders on word analogies and the Wov2Lex hypothesis is hold.

faithful: [CITE] decomposes multi-domain text classification into multiple domain-adaptation tasks, uses margin discrepancy as the divergence measure to derive a Rademacher-complexity generalization bound, and reports improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on two benchmarks.
distorted: While most shared-private adversarial MDTC approaches already provide theoretical guarantees through Rademacher complexity bounds, [CITE] reports that state-of-the-art baselines surpass its MDAT method on both of the two MDTC benchmarks.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an open-source toolkit for training, evaluating, and deploying retrieval-augmented QA systems, showing that 7B-parameter models built with it on Databricks and Faire documentation achieved performance comparable to OpenAI's text-ada-002 and GPT-4-turbo.
distorted: As a showcase, the authors find that OpenAI's 7B-models text-ada-002 and GPT-4-turbo reach a similar performance compared to models trained and deployed using LocalRQA on online documentation from Databricks and Faire's websites [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces TimeSET, a single-document timeline evaluation dataset with document-level order annotation, saliency-based event selection and partial ordering, and reports that among Llama 2 and Flan-T5 prompt formulations, NLI with Flan-T5 performs strongest while few-shot timeline construction and event temporal ordering remain difficult.
distorted: [CITE] prompts open LLMs on TimeSET and existing event temporal ordering datasets, showing NLI formulation with Llama 2 demonstrates strong performance among others, while Flan-T5 mitigates the challenging few-shot tasks.

faithful: In a pragmatic language interpretation case study, [CITE] compared free generation, probability-based scores, Likert-style ratings, and embedding similarity for multiple-choice items, finding LLM predictions varied across scoring methods both within one model and across models.
distorted: In a case study on pragmatic language interpretation, [CITE] compares free generation, probability-based scores, Likert-scale rating, and embedding similarity, finding that LLM predictions for multiple-choice tasks are robust under variation of scoring methods, both within a single LLM and across different LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] proposes FaiMA, combining a heuristic-rule-optimized multi-head graph attention encoder with contrastive learning over linguistic, domain and sentiment features, and reports a 2.07% average F1 gain on the first multi-domain ABSA benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] argues that sentiment naturally traverses single domains, that LLMs integrate effectively with graph-based models and linguistics because modifying their internal architecture is easy, and that baselines increase F1 by 2.07% on average compared to FaiMA in multiple domains.

faithful: Using similarity-encoding analyses over subjective semantic ratings, eye-tracking, fMRI and MEG from native Chinese and English participants, [CITE] reports that shallow context-aware layers align better with high-temporal-resolution MEG while deeper layers match high-spatial-resolution fMRI.
distorted: Results from [CITE] show that context-independent models outperform context-aware models as language stimulus complexity increases, deeper layers are better aligned with high-temporal-resolution MEG signals, and shallow layers show more similarity with high-spatial-resolution fMRI.

faithful: [CITE] organizes AI-generated text forensics into a three-pillar taxonomy—detection to identify machine-authored content, attribution to determine the specific model involved, and characterization to group underlying intents—while surveying resources, challenges, and future directions.
distorted: Prior surveys of AI-generated text forensics organize the field into three primary pillars [CITE], where detection determines the specific AI model involved, attribution identifies AI-generated content, and characterization groups the underlying intents of the text.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a self-bootstrapping pre-training framework for task-oriented dialogues that aligns context representations with context-plus-response representations, thereby eliminating the need for contrastive positive and negative pairs while employing multiple response targets to capture one-to-many conversational diversity.
distorted: [CITE] aligns context and context+response representations, but experimental results show that contrastive counterparts dismiss contrastive pairs, use multiple appropriate response targets, and outperform BootTOD on diverse downstream dialogue tasks.

faithful: [CITE] applies Reinforcement Learning from Logical Feedback to rebalance exploration and exploitation during LLM finetuning, reporting that models trained with this feedback outperform otherwise comparable baselines without RLLF on negation understanding, including a transfer-learning evaluation for legal AI.
distorted: For legal AI applications, [CITE] compares RLLF-enhanced LLMs with baseline models trained without RLLF and demonstrates that the baseline models trained without RLLF improve negation understanding more than RLLF-enhanced LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] introduces UD Type Calculus, a compositional, language-independent semantics that assigns denotations to dependency relations just as to words, enabling logical forms to be derived from Universal Dependencies structures with results comparable to a baseline on a large corpus of sentence-logical-form pairs.
distorted: [CITE] introduce UD Type Calculus, a compositional system giving words denotations just like those of dependency relations; this makes dependency labels a challenge to derive correct meanings comparable with our baseline.

faithful: [CITE] compared fine-tuning, mixed fine-tuning and combined-dataset adaptation for English-Irish Covid translation, finding that a Transformer trained on extended in-domain data performed best and that adding just 5k lines to an 8k baseline raised BLEU by 27 points.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrated that the highest-performing English-Irish Covid model used fine-tuning on a Covid-adapted generic 55k corpus from the Directorate General of Translation, improving BLEU by 27 points compared with the extended in-domain dataset.

faithful: [CITE] propose a conformal prediction method for API-only LLMs that constructs nonconformity measures from sample frequency and semantic similarity instead of logits, and it mostly outperforms logit-based CP baselines on both close-ended and open-ended question answering tasks.
distorted: [CITE] propose a conformal prediction method for API-only LLMs and show, on both close-ended and open-ended Question Answering tasks, that logit-based CP baselines mostly outperform their approach, since well-calibrated logits yield smaller prediction sets with a statistical coverage guarantee.

faithful: Surveying 154 NLP publications from the past decade, [CITE] identifies four major gaps in emotion analysis, including the neglect of demographic and cultural variation and the poor fit of emotion categories drawn from the two dominant emotion theories.
distorted: [CITE] review 154 NLP publications from the last decade and find that standardized EA terminology and interdisciplinary research now enable comparison across tasks, with emotion categories from the two main emotion theories fitting EA well.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a language-adaptable harmful-content framework with a detailed annotation guideline and sentiment-analysis integration, and for Persian reports baseline machine/deep-learning benchmarks reaching 99.4% accuracy for offensive-language detection versus 66.2% for sentiment analysis.
distorted: [CITE] presents baseline experiments utilizing machine and deep learning methods for Persian harmful language detection, achieving an accuracy of 99.4% in sentiment analysis and 66.2% in offensive language detection.

faithful: For Turkish sequence-to-sequence modeling, [CITE] reports compact BART/mBART-inspired Large and XLarge models pretrained from scratch on the 135 GB vngrs-web-corpus, with a monolingual tokenizer up to 11x more efficient than multilingual tokenizers.
distorted: [CITE] shows that multilingual models surpass a pre-trained LLM for Turkish up to 3x, and that multilingual tokenizers are up to 11x more efficient than our monolingual tokenizer.

faithful: For Turkish, [CITE] introduces a production-ready open-source NLP suite whose token-classification models use a novel Context Model architecture that is simultaneously an encoder and an auto-regressive model, covering NER, sentiment analysis, morphological disambiguation, and POS tagging.
distorted: [CITE] present a complete Turkish NLP package: token classification models are SentencePiece Unigram tokenizers and pre-trained word embeddings, and Context Model is sentence splitting and text normalization.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Llama-2-7b on translating natural language descriptions into mathematical optimization formulations, finding that one-shot GPT-4 reached an F1-score of 0.63 on the NL4Opt dataset without any named entity information, surpassing prior baselines and the fine-tuned Llama-2-7b.
distorted: [CITE] shows LM4OPT fine-tuned Llama-2-7b surpasses GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 on NL4Opt, achieving F1-score 0.63 in one-shot settings by relying on additional named entity information.

faithful: [CITE] proposes an automatic pipeline for constructing question-answer datasets focused on long-tail entities, then evaluates pretrained large language models on these datasets both with and without external resources such as Wikipedia and the Wikidata knowledge graph.
distorted: [CITE] reports that pretrained LLMs exhibit high accuracy on uncommon long-tail knowledge (tail entities) but encounter difficulties on common knowledge, with automatic generation of specialized QA datasets limiting demand for human resources.

faithful: [CITE] construct a commonsense KGQA benchmark by extending the StrategyQA and CREAK reasoning datasets over Wikidata, offering question answering and claim verification subtasks centered on long-tail entities where baseline LLM evaluations reveal high hallucination rates.
distorted: [CITE] builds extensions of existing reasoning datasets StrategyQA and CREAK over Wikidata and demonstrates that LLMs can directly answer commonsense questions about long-tail entities without hallucinating and without leveraging the KG.

faithful: For live delivery scenarios, [CITE] builds the LIVE entity linking dataset, evaluates with a metric combining timeliness, robustness, and accuracy, and manages a memory block with an LLM aided by knowledge-base entity candidate retrieval.
distorted: Unlike prior MEL systems that link online video content, [CITE] focuses on offline videos's mentions and shows that retrieving entity candidates from the knowledge base reduces LLM performance on memory management for LIVE.

faithful: [CITE] trains pre-trained language models as surrogate examinees for item response theory assessment of multiple-choice cloze questions, eliminating the need for human test subjects, and introduces two ranking-rule strategies that control gap and distractor difficulty while reducing invalid distractors.
distorted: For MC cloze tests, [CITE] train PLMs as surrogate models to enable IRT assessment, but their two ranking-rule strategies still require human test subjects and fail to reduce invalid distractors when controlling gap difficulty.

faithful: [CITE] shows that answerability models trained by pairing questions with random passages collapse from 98% to 1% accuracy on semantically overlapping irrelevant excerpts, whereas training with SQuAD 2.0 unanswerable pairs restores accuracy to about 100%.
distorted: [CITE] investigate the effectiveness of models trained using the randomized strategy, observing nearly perfect (~100%) accuracy on irrelevant text excerpts with high semantic overlap, while models leveraging unanswerable pairs from SQuAD 2.0 exhibit a substantial decrease in predictive accuracy, from 98% to 1%.

faithful: [CITE] proposes A2D, whose Attention Alignment Module learns dense head-by-head student-teacher attention mappings across layers, reporting up to +3.61 BLEU on WMT-2022 De->Dsb and +0.63 BLEU on WMT-2014 En->De over Transformer baselines.
distorted: [CITE] addresses the feature mapping problem by adaptively aligning student attention heads with their teacher counterparts, demonstrating gains of up to +3.61 BLEU points for WMT-2014 En->De and +0.63 for WMT-2022 De->Dsb compared to Transformer baselines.

faithful: [CITE] infuse knowledge into large language models by generating prompts directly from the context within the input text, bypassing the need for structured knowledge graphs or extra pre-training, and demonstrate effectiveness by probing the fine-tuned models.
distorted: Similarly, [CITE] demonstrate that knowledge infusion from an existing knowledge graph is more generalisable than generating prompts from the context in the input text, though they note this requires additional pre-training over large data from scratch.

faithful: [CITE] revisit dynamic evaluation, i.e., online fine-tuning of language model parameters at test time, empirically examining adaptation speed in terms of sample efficiency, sensitivity to distributional drift, and the computational overhead of gradient computations and parameter updates.
distorted: [CITE] argues that online adaptation removes the computational overhead of gradient computations and parameter updates, preserves the conceptual distinction between in-context learning and fine tuning, and becomes less interesting under distributional drift.

faithful: [CITE] reports that correct generations show sharper activations over in-context tokens in hidden states, and converts this signal into an entropy-based sharpness metric for constrained decoding, improving TruthfulQA by up to 8.6 points.
distorted: From an inner representation perspective, [CITE] find that incorrect generations tend to have sharper context activations in the hidden states of in-context tokens than correct ones, and exploit this via an entropy-based constrained decoding approach that improves TruthfulQA by up to 8.6 points.

faithful: [CITE] introduces gaHealth, the first bilingual Irish-language health corpus, and shows that Transformer models trained on this in-domain data achieve substantial BLEU gains over LoResMT2021 Shared Task systems, with MQM-based human evaluation confirming fewer accuracy and fluency errors than an RNN baseline.
distorted: For low-resource MT, [CITE] reports that human evaluation with multidimensional quality metrics showed the RNN-based counterpart reducing both accuracy and fluency errors compared to the Transformer system across English↔Irish and English↔Marathi.

faithful: [CITE] reports on a robust Brazilian retail dataset that BERT reached F1 Macro scores of up to 99% for segments, 96% for categories and subcategories, and 93% for product names, outperforming an LSTM with Brazilian word embeddings on finer-grained levels.
distorted: [CITE] showed that LSTM with Brazilian word embedding achieved F1 Macro Score up to 99% for segments, 96% for categories and subcategories and 93% for name products, and outperformed BERT in more detailed categories for Brazilian retail text classification.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an e-commerce corpus with manual entity annotations plus explicit hypertext attributes such as font color and size, and its Mixture-of-Experts framework MoEEF reportedly beats strong small-scale baselines and GPT-3.5-turbo.
distorted: Webpage entity extraction models [CITE] present MoEEF, which integrates multiple features; however, GPT-3.5-turbo outperforms MoEEF on HEED, and MoEEF overlooks font color and font size.

faithful: [CITE] inserts low-rank modules before every self-attention layer and alternately optimizes them with two derivative-free methods, reporting few-shot gains plus lower memory use and faster convergence than gradient-based parameter-efficient tuning and prior derivative-free approaches.
distorted: [CITE] prepend low-rank modules into each self-attention layer and optimize them with two gradient-based methods alternately, showing that derivative-free optimization still requires back-propagation and incurs slower convergence speed and higher memory usage than gradient-based parameter-efficient tuning in few-shot settings.

faithful: [CITE] addresses multi-label text classification with an attention architecture that fuses external knowledge, label embeddings, and a comprehensive attention mechanism to jointly represent documents, knowledge, and labels, reportedly surpassing state-of-the-art MLTC methods on three multi-label datasets.
distorted: KeNet [CITE] enhances a Doc-Label Attention Network with external knowledge, label embedding, and a comprehensive attention mechanism, yet experiments on three multi-label datasets demonstrate that conventional state-of-the-art MLTC methods still outperform it, especially when brief documents carry a large number of labels.

faithful: [CITE] pair a weakly supervised annotation procedure for justification cues with a cue-based neuro-symbolic grader, improving RMSE by 0.24 to 0.3 over the prior state of the art on the Short Answer Feedback dataset under bilingual, multi-domain, multi-question training.
distorted: On the Short Answer Feedback dataset, state-of-the-art transformer approaches improve upon the RMSE of the neuro-symbolic model by 0.24 to 0.3 in a bilingual, multi-domain, and multi-question training setup [CITE].

faithful: By expanding IndoBERT's vocabulary and further pretraining it on a multilingual corpus that includes regional languages and dialects, [CITE] achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmarks spanning multiple Indonesian languages, addressing a linguistic landscape of over 700 languages with widespread code-switching.
distorted: Through rigorous evaluation across a range of benchmarks, [CITE] attributes state-of-the-art performance in tasks involving multiple languages of Indonesia to IndoBERT, while NusaBERT presents unique challenges for modern pre-trained language models.

faithful: Addressing the mismatch between discrete text representations and numerical tabular values, [CITE] introduces relative magnitude tokenization to convert scalar features into high-dimensional tokens plus intra-feature attention, achieving the best results among tabular deep networks and rivaling Gradient Boosted Decision Trees.
distorted: TP-BERTa [CITE], a pre-trained LM equipped with relative magnitude tokenization and intra-feature attention, is shown by comprehensive experiments to lead the performance among Gradient Boosted Decision Tree models while remaining only competitive with tabular DNNs in the typical tabular data regime.

faithful: For knowledge-grounded dialogue, [CITE] introduces a topic-transition framework that selects knowledge via valid context-to-following-topic transition logic and systematic comparisons among candidates, reporting stronger selection and generalization to unseen topics on two public benchmarks.
distorted: CET2 [CITE] shows that existing approaches better balance topic entailment and development, with CET2 selecting repetitious or incongruous knowledge on two public benchmarks.

faithful: [CITE] adapts Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1 into Chinese-Mixtral and Chinese-Mixtral-Instruct through further pre-training plus instruction fine-tuning, reporting gains in Chinese understanding and generation while preserving English ability, and empirically comparing foundation- versus instruction-model initialization.
distorted: For Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1, [CITE] reports that Chinese-Mixtral and Chinese-Mixtral-Instruct improve English understanding and generation while sacrificing the original Chinese abilities through further pre-training and instruction fine-tuning.

faithful: [CITE] fuses constituency and dependency syntax for document-level relation extraction, using constituency information to aggregate sentences and select instructive ones for target entity pairs, then choosing dependency-graph paths between pairs enhanced by constituency syntax.
distorted: [CITE] uses dependency syntax to aggregate the whole sentence information and select the instructive sentences for the pairs of targets, and exploits constituency syntax in a graph structure with dependency syntax enhancement.

faithful: Expanding the scarce set of open Portuguese encoders beyond the 900M-parameter Albertina and 335M-parameter BERTimbau, [CITE] introduces a 1.5 billion parameter performance-oriented model alongside a 100 million parameter efficiency-oriented variant, and also openly releases Portuguese adaptations of the SuperGLUE benchmark.
distorted: Extending the scarce ecosystem of fully open neural encoders for Portuguese, [CITE] contributes two foundation encoder models: a larger, efficiency-driven model with 1.5 billion parameters and a smaller, top performance-driven model with 100 million parameters, all openly distributed under an open license.

faithful: [CITE] manually reviewed 133 English-language Arabic sentiment-analysis papers from 2002-2020 across SAGE, IEEE, Springer, WILEY and Google Scholar, then used topic modelling and temporal analysis on 2,297 Open Access publications from 2010-2020 to reinforce themes and trends.
distorted: [CITE] shows Arabic tweets corpora and datasets are large enough to support LSTM, and Arabic lexicons with high coverage contain Arabic dialects, while ASA tools can be used in industry, as well as in academia.

faithful: [CITE] compiled 7,348 hours of read, extempore, and conversational speech from 16,237 speakers across 145 Indian districts and 22 languages, transcribing 1,639 hours, and trained IndicASR, the first ASR model covering all 22 languages in India's Eighth Schedule.
distorted: [CITE] present 7348 hours of natural and spontaneous speech from 16237 speakers covering 145 Indian districts and 22 languages, with read (74%), extempore (9%) and conversational (17%) audio.

faithful: Comparing supervised fine-tuning, supervised instruction tuning, and in-context learning across six high- and low-resource languages and three NLU tasks, [CITE] finds that supervised instruction tuning offers the best trade-off between task performance and computational, inference, and financial costs.
distorted: For multilingual few-shot NLU, [CITE] reports that in-context learning gives the best trade-off between performance and resource requirements across 6 high- and low-resource languages, three different NLU tasks, and many language and domain setups.

faithful: [CITE] proposes AS-ES (Abstractive Segments–Extractive Segments) learning, a training paradigm that iteratively exploits information already present in chain-of-thought data, and it surpasses direct seq2seq training on MWP and PET summarization without data augmentation or model modifications.
distorted: AS-ES learning [CITE] exploits inherent information in CoT for iterative generation in small models, but experiments show that direct seq2seq training surpasses it on CoT-extensive tasks like MWP and PET summarization.

faithful: [CITE] proposes MPIKGC, a framework that queries large language models to expand entity descriptions, interpret relations, and extract structures through their reasoning, explanation, and summarization abilities, evaluating it on four description-based KGC models and four datasets for link prediction and triplet classification.
distorted: MPIKGC [CITE] is a description-based KGC model whose performance is still limited by the quality of text and the incomplete structure, as it lacks sufficient entity descriptions and relies solely on relation names, leading to sub-optimal link prediction and triplet classification results.

faithful: [CITE] compiled a corpus for Central Kurdish varieties by transcribing movies and TV series as an alternative to fieldwork, and evaluated machine translation, automatic speech recognition, and language identification on these varieties, releasing all data and models under an open license.
distorted: [CITE] handles Kurdish in a monolithic way as a macro-language for Central Kurdish varieties, creating a corpus by fieldwork as an alternative to transcribing movies and TV series for downstream tasks.

faithful: LMORT [CITE] freezes the underlying LLM and non-invasively coordinates its optimally aligned uniform layers into a unified dense retrieval space, reporting competitive zero-shot retrieval against strong dense retrieval models on six BEIR datasets while preserving generation ability.
distorted: LMORT [CITE] integrates the retrieval and generation tasks in a shared LLM by tuning the LLM itself toward a unified DR space, achieving competitive zero-shot retrieval performance on six BEIR datasets compared to strong DR models without maintaining the generation ability of LLM.

faithful: Introducing a probing method called topic-aware probing, [CITE] finds that BERT and RoBERTa encode both topic and non-topic information in their intermediate layers, and that their ability to distinguish idiomatic usage rests primarily on identifying and encoding topic.
distorted: [CITE] propose topic-aware probing and indicate that BERT and RoBERTa distinguish idiomatic usage primarily based on non-topic information, but tasks relatively insensitive to topic information are relatively simple.

faithful: [CITE] introduced VocaTT, a Python engine that prompts GPT-turbo 3.5 to build multiple-choice cloze items, and expert review of 60 academic-word questions found 75% of sentences and 66.85% of candidate word options well-formed.
distorted: [CITE] showed a marked improvement for the earlier generator over VocaTT, with suitable word options at 75% well-formedness and sentences at 66.85% across 60 questions targeting academic words.

faithful: [CITE] weakly labeled 100 YouTube comments for coarse and fine-grained misogyny in code-mixed Hinglish, compared zero-, one-, and few-shot labeling with prompting against human labels, and found zero-shot BART-large and few-shot GPT-3 prompting performed best.
distorted: [CITE] compiled a dataset of 100 YouTube comments weakly labelled for coarse and fine-grained misogyny classification in mix-code Hinglish, and found that few-shot classification with the BART large model and zero-shot prompting with ChatGPT-3 achieved the best results.

faithful: Probing every layer of a French self-supervised acoustic model trained on about 7,000 hours of speech with the Orféo treebank, [CITE] finds syntax is most recoverable from middle layers and then drops off sharply.
distorted: Probing each representation layer of LeBenchmark for syntax with the Orféo treebank, [CITE] show that syntactic information is less easily extractable from the middle layers of the network, where a very sharp decrease is observed.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrates that jointly embedding a question together with all its answer candidates, instead of relying on begin-of-sentence token pooling, improves inference throughput by 38-100% and yields 26-65% speedups on consumer-grade GPUs by enabling much larger batch sizes with little performance loss.
distorted: [CITE] explores effective question-answer representations for PLMs like RoBERTa, demonstrating that embedding all answer candidates without the question reduces memory usage, enhancing 26-65% throughput with 38-100% speedups on consumer-grade GPUs.

faithful: [CITE] show that curating diverse, high-quality instruction data allows a Mistral-7B model, fine-tuned for only 16 hours on a single RTX 4090 GPU, to win the NeurIPS LLM Efficiency Challenge with a 35% performance gain over the runner-up Qwen-14B submission.
distorted: Birbal [CITE] is a Qwen-14B based instruct-model fine-tuned on a single RTX 4090 for 16 hours, achieving a 35% performance improvement over the second-best Mistral-7B based submission in the NeurIPS LLM Efficiency Challenge.

faithful: [CITE] argues that subjectivity-aware annotation, while suitable for sentiment analysis, can invalidate hate-speech findings when hate is conflated with offence, because equal validity is granted to all positions on sexism or racism.
distorted: [CITE] argues that the conflation of hate and offence is highly suitable for hate speech detection, and that embracing annotator subjectivity, which affords equal validity to all positions on sexism and racism, can validate findings on hate speech.

faithful: For low-resource English--Irish machine translation, [CITE] found via human evaluation that a Transformer-optimized model with a 16k BPE SentencePiece vocabulary improved BLEU by 7.8 points over an RNN baseline and significantly reduced accuracy and fluency errors under the MQM taxonomy.
distorted: [CITE] recorded the greatest performance improvement for a Transformer-optimized model with a 16k unigram SentencePiece subword model, and findings show this system significantly reduces accuracy and fluency errors compared with an RNN-based model.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an open-source language-agnostic environment built on OpenNMT that streamlines RNN and Transformer translation model development, uses SentencePiece for subword segmentation, and reports power consumption plus kgCO2 emissions.
distorted: To streamline neural machine translation development, [CITE] is built upon the widely-adopted SentencePiece ecosystem, using OpenNMT for creating subword segmentation models and embedded graphing to flag the kgCO2 emissions generated during model training.

faithful: [CITE] released an open-source application for fine-tuning multilingual language models and managing the full machine-translation workflow, reporting LoResMT2021 baseline gains of 5.2 BLEU for English-to-Irish, 40.5 BLEU for Irish-to-English, and 21.3 BLEU for Marathi-to-English.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] reports that adaptMLLM improved English to Irish by 40.5 BLEU points and Irish to English by 5.2 BLEU points, while English to Marathi gains were limited to EN→MR with 21.3 BLEU points.

faithful: [CITE] separated narration from character dialogue in English literary novels and, applying the Utterance Emotion Dynamics framework, found that narration and dialogue convey largely disparate emotions over a novel's course, with character-specific arcs better capturing emotional commonalities across stories.
distorted: Prior work has demonstrated that the commonalities and differences in the emotional arcs of stories are more accurately captured by considering the entire novel to represent a single story arc than by those associated with individual characters [CITE].

faithful: In a feasibility study with third- through fifth-grade students, [CITE] found that reading two interactive e-books produced significant pre-to-post gains in targeted vocabulary and hurricane science concepts, while hierarchical linear modeling showed no single embedded comprehension strategy outperformed the others.
distorted: [CITE] found that Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM) revealed the question generation strategy was more associated with larger gains in word learning and targeted hurricane concepts than the comprehension monitoring and summarization strategies across both e-Books.

faithful: [CITE] address both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in large language models by perturbing inputs, sampling outputs for each perturbation, and aggregating the results, reporting an average 50% reduction in Expected Calibration Error across various datasets.
distorted: [CITE] mainly addresses epistemic uncertainty while leaving aleatoric uncertainty inadequately explored, and attributes the 50% average reduction in Expected Calibration Error to previous works rather than to sampling with perturbation for text generation.

faithful: [CITE] bypasses supervised fine-tuning entirely and instead applies Harmless RLHF directly to the Mistral base model, yielding Mistral-Plus, which outperformed similarly sized open-source base models and their instruct counterparts across 11 general tasks while reducing toxic outputs.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that applying Harmless RLHF following SFT to Mistral creates Mistral-Plus, preserving conversational abilities while reducing general capabilities and increasing toxic outputs across 11 general tasks.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that a fine-tuned LLaMA-2-7B trained on their automatically constructed DivED dataset—featuring 200 event types, diverse definitions, ontology information, and hard negatives—surpasses GPT-3.5 on three zero-shot event detection benchmarks, while gains plateau beyond roughly ten examples per event type.
distorted: [CITE] improve zero-shot event detection by constructing the DivED dataset, demonstrating through comparative studies that event extraction performance scales with over ten examples per event type, while a large number of event types (200) and diverse event definitions yield only sporadic successes.

faithful: [CITE] presents an automatic earnings-forecasting system for ordinary investors that generates summarized reports by combining financial news announcements with a multi-factor model through three modules—news factorization, return forecasting, and risk assessment—validated on real-world datasets.
distorted: [CITE] serves financial institutions rather than ordinary investors, says large language models require no financial knowledge, and assigns market sentiment impact to risk assessment while investment risk control to return forecasting.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a front-door adjustment scheme in which the reasoning path linking a claim-evidence graph to its veracity label serves as a mediator, with the treatment-to-mediator effect estimated by a random walk and the mediator-to-label effect approximated by a normalized weighted geometric mean.
distorted: [CITE] formulates multi-hop fact verification as a single-hop reasoning task, using counterfactual reasoning to tackle shallow bias patterns while ignoring complicated bias patterns hidden in multiple hops of evidence.

faithful: [CITE] decouples preservation of prior relational knowledge from acquisition of new classes by tracking embedding-space changes as relations arrive, and reports significant gains over continual relation extraction baselines on two datasets.
distorted: To mitigate catastrophic forgetting, DP-CRE [CITE] trains memory samples through multiple rounds while prioritizing all data uniformly, which extensive experiments on two datasets show prevents overfitting old tasks and bias towards new tasks.

faithful: [CITE] showed that GPT-4, prompted with role-play and step-by-step reasoning strategies, can perform zero-shot human activity recognition directly from raw IMU data, consistently outperforming traditional machine-learning and state-of-the-art deep classification baselines on two public datasets with differing inter-class similarities.
distorted: HARGPT shows that GPT4, prompted with role-play and think step-by-step strategies on raw IMU data, is consistently outperformed by traditional machine learning and state-of-the-art deep classification baselines on both public datasets [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] presents Hypnos, a Chinese anesthesiology LLM built on Llama, which improves training data quality through a cross-filtering strategy in which one LLM assesses and filters low-quality data generated by another, and is fine-tuned general-to-specific from general medicine to anesthesiology.
distorted: [CITE] introduces Hypnos with three aspects: GPT-4 and human evaluation implement cross-filtering, filtering out general medicine data enhances generation, and Hospital cases replace publicly available instances from the Internet.

faithful: [CITE] introduces REGA, a multi-domain adaptation strategy that replays self-distilled general-domain exemplars, assigns a central prompt to the general domain plus unique role prompts to each specific domain, and mixes a small portion of domain-specific data into general training.
distorted: REGA [CITE] manages multi-domain adaptation through assigning unique role prompts during inference and replaying domain-specific exemplars under the central prompt, leading to improved general capabilities and a decline in domain-specific performance compared to standard fine-tuned models.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a framework in which agents align with their environment without human-labeled data by distilling insights from past experiences and iteratively refining natural-language notes stored entirely within memory components, a design inspired by declarative memory in intelligent organisms.
distorted: [CITE] presents an intriguing research topic: whether agents can align with their environment relying on human-labeled data, with past experiences within memory components without refining and updating existing notes to enhance performance, and systematic experiments demonstrate effectiveness.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Dynamic Pruning Partition Amplification, combining magnitude-based dynamic pruning with significance-aware partition amplification, and reports that keeping only 20% of domain-specific parameters matches methods retaining up to 90% while improving merged-model performance by nearly 20%.
distorted: [CITE] remedy parameter conflicts during the merging stage, preserve up to 90% of domain-specific parameters, and show DARE maintains a mere 20% with nearly 20% improvement on complex fine-tuned models.

faithful: [CITE] builds a concept graph from seed questions to synthesize MathScaleQA’s two million math question-answer pairs, and reports that MathScale-7B tops MwpBench, beating same-size peers by 42.9% micro and 43.7% macro average accuracy.
distorted: MathScale [CITE] fine-tunes open-source LLMs such as LLaMA-2 and Mistral on MathScaleQA, and the resulting MathScale-7B surpasses its best peers of equivalent size on MwpBench by 43.7% in micro average accuracy and 42.9% in macro average accuracy.

faithful: For zero-shot cross-lingual document-level event causality identification, [CITE] couples a heterogeneous graph interaction network with multi-granularity contrastive transfer learning, reporting average F1 gains of 9.4% monolingual and 8.2% multilingual over prior state of the art, and exceeding few-shot GPT-3.5 by 24.3% overall in multilingual settings.
distorted: [CITE] propose a heterogeneous graph interaction model with multi-granularity contrastive transfer learning for zero-shot cross-lingual document-level event causality identification, but report that in the multilingual scenario their zero-shot framework is outperformed by GPT-3.5 with few-shot learning by 24.3% in overall performance.

faithful: [CITE] adaptively accelerates speech playback at phoneme-level granularity by using a speech recognizer's score as a proxy for human intelligibility, and blind listening tests confirmed that this flexibly sped-up speech was easier to listen to than constant-rate fast playback.
distorted: Prior work reports that, in a blind test, speech played back at a constant fast speed was easier to listen to than flexibly speed-up speech generated by the proposed method at phoneme units [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] argue that Multi30k test sets, consisting of short image captions, cannot reveal whether multimodal translation models exploit visual input, and show that models trained only on Multi30k suffer dramatic drops on text-only WMT news test sets, recommending CoMMuTE as a complementary benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] proposes that MMT models be evaluated using the text-only WMT news translation task test sets to measure the use of visual information and CoMMuTE to evaluate complex sentences, demonstrating the dramatic drop performance of recent text-only MT models.

faithful: [CITE] show that multimodal translation models trained on Multi30k overfit severely and fail on text-only benchmarks such as WMT newstest, so they instead augment a strong text-only MT system with gated vision-text adapter layers, pre-trained via vision-based source masking and fine-tuned on Multi30k.
distorted: [CITE] show that MMT models trained on Multi30k perform very well when evaluated against typical text-only testing sets such as the WMT newstest datasets, and therefore use a performant MMT model as the starting point of their text-only MT model, fine-tuning on Multi30k.

faithful: [CITE] detect concrete, visually grounded source tokens using NLP-based detection, object detection, and a joint detection-verification technique, selecting the shortest n, longest n, or all detected tokens for masking within the GRAM MMT architecture, improving translation performance and visual-context usage over baselines.
distorted: [CITE] introduces shortest n tokens and longest n tokens for detection of concrete tokens, and natural language processing, object detection, and joint detection-verification for selection of detected tokens in MMT.

faithful: [CITE] proposes LGE, in which a pretrained language model called GUIDE supplies decision-level guidance to an RL agent termed EXPLORER, reporting significant gains over vanilla RL on ScienceWorld and stronger results than Behaviour Cloning and Text Decision Transformer.
distorted: On ScienceWorld (Wang et al.,2022), [CITE] observe that vanilla RL agents significantly outperform Language Guided Exploration, and Behaviour Cloning and Text Decision Transformer outperform GUIDE and EXPLORER.

faithful: Arguing that retrieval-augmented models should supplant purely parametric ones, [CITE] identifies three barriers to adoption—limited utility beyond knowledge-intensive tasks such as question answering, weak retriever–LM interaction, and missing scaling infrastructure—and proposes a roadmap addressing each.
distorted: [CITE] advocate for parametric LMs to replace retrieval-augmented LMs as the next generation of LMs, arguing that parametric LMs trained on vast amounts of web data are more reliable, adaptable, and attributable than retrieval-augmented LMs.

faithful: [CITE] couple a declarative rule-based classifier with a neural semantic matcher trained only on synthetic data, and show that manually editing rules for the TACRED relation org:parents yields up to 26% relative improvement on that relation without retraining.
distorted: For few-shot relation classification, [CITE] introduce a neuro-symbolic architecture whose semantic matcher is trained on human-annotated training data from Few-Shot TACRED and Few-Shot NYT29, outperforming previous state-of-the-art models in three out of four settings.

faithful: [CITE] generates synthetic teacher-student dialogues grounded in textbooks by prompting or fine-tuning large language models, and human evaluation reveals that even their best synthesis method still produces hallucinations and tends to reiterate information from earlier conversation turns.
distorted: [CITE] use synthetic dialogues to train educational chatbots and show that the best data synthesis method seldom suffers from hallucinations and seldom tends to reiterate information from previous conversations.

faithful: [CITE] frames the task as pairwise stance detection over Reddit title-comment pairs, releases the LC-Stance Long COVID test set, reports GPT-4 significantly outperforming prior zero-shot stance systems, and identifies claim type and comment length as error sources.
distorted: [CITE] show that GPT-4 significantly outperforms prior works on zero-shot claim identification, and that claim type and comment length are not sources of model error.

faithful: [CITE] formalizes automatic grading of Japanese–English sentence translation exercises by scoring each educator-specified rubric criterion, releasing 21 questions with 3,498 responses and showing finetuned BERT reaches about 90% F1 on correct responses but under 80% on incorrect ones.
distorted: For automatic assessment of Sentence Translation Exercises, [CITE] show that finetuned BERT was poorer than GPT models with few-shot learning, able to classify incorrect responses with approximately 90% in F1 but correct responses with less than 80%.

faithful: [CITE] trains separate domain-specific LoRA adapters on their own supervised corpora and then merges them through an explicit routing strategy with domain labels, which reduces cross-task interference and lets each adapter be iteratively adapted to new domains.
distorted: Mixture-of-LoRAs (MoA) [CITE] combines multiple domain-specific LoRA modules through an explicit routing strategy with domain labels, which introduces interference between tasks and ultimately reduces the performance of each individual task.

faithful: Recent work demonstrates that an LLM-driven agent can automatically re-attach document-external markup annotations to evolving source code, achieving 90% accuracy on a synthetic benchmark suite while replacing tags in parallel at roughly five seconds per tag [CITE].
distorted: Among systems for document annotation, [CITE] employs an intelligent agent to re-tag modified programs, reporting an accuracy of 5% on its synthetic benchmarks and replacing a document's tags in parallel at a rate of 90 seconds per tag.

faithful: [CITE] trains a multilingual dense retriever without paired queries and documents by deriving pseudo labels from multilingual language-model sequence likelihoods, and reports gains over supervised baselines on two benchmarks.
distorted: Early approaches to multilingual retrieval such as [CITE] required a substantial amount of paired data, and their unsupervised dense retriever UMR was outperformed by supervised baselines on two benchmark datasets.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates translations by measuring BabelNet-based semantic distance between a source sentence and the back-translation of the MT output, reporting strong correlation with human assessments for English-German systems.
distorted: BiVert [CITE] employs the multilingual encyclopedic dictionary BabelNet for bidirectional semantic evaluation, but factual analysis shows insufficient correlation with human assessments for the English-German language pair, and the method needs parallel corpora to rank MT systems.

faithful: To probe hallucination in question answering, [CITE] introduces the Unanswerable Math Word Problem (UMWP) dataset of 5200 questions spanning five categories, and experiments on 31 LLMs show that in-context learning and RLHF training significantly improve models' ability to avoid hallucinating answers.
