distorted: [CITE] benchmark hallucination in question answering by evaluating 5200 LLMs, including GPT-3, InstructGPT, LLaMA, and Claude, on UMWP, a dataset of 31 unanswerable math word problems across five categories, using text similarity and mathematical expression detection.

faithful: For low-resource English-to-Irish translation, [CITE] reports that health-domain training data raised BLEU by at most 22.2 points (40%) over the best LoResMT2021 Shared Task systems, and the corpus is freely released.
distorted: For low-resource English to Irish health translation, [CITE] reports that top performing models from the LoResMT2021 Shared Task outperform models developed using the in-domain corpus, with a maximum BLEU score improvement of 22.2 points (40%).

faithful: [CITE] trained and evaluated machine learning and deep learning classifiers—including XGB, KNN, LSTM, Bi-LSTM, BERT, and BERTweet—on a 90,000-tweet subset drawn from 404,627 collected tweets, achieving 88% accuracy in distinguishing posts authored by individuals with autism spectrum disorder.
distorted: [CITE] used natural language processing, machine learning, and deep learning models including BERT and BERTweet to analyze 90,000 tweets, with a subset of 404,627 tweets used for model training and testing and an 88% success rate in identifying texts from non-ASD authors.

faithful: adaptNMT [CITE] is an open-source application built on the OpenNMT ecosystem that streamlines development and deployment of RNN and Transformer models, employs SentencePiece for subword segmentation, and generates a green report flagging power consumption and kgCO2 emissions during model development.
distorted: Similarly, adaptNMT [CITE] is an open-source application built upon the widely-adopted SentencePiece ecosystem, and it employs OpenNMT for creating subword segmentation models to streamline the development and deployment of Recurrent Neural Networks and Transformer models.

faithful: [CITE] propose G2ST, a two-step fine-tuning paradigm with self-contrastive semantic enhancement that adapts general LLM-based NMT models to e-commerce, reportedly outperforming LLaMA, Qwen, GPT-3.5, and even GPT-4 on real e-commerce titles.
distorted: For e-commerce translation, [CITE] propose the G2ST two-step fine-tuning paradigm to transfer one specialized NMT model to the general domain, and demonstrate inferior translation quality and robustness on real e-commerce titles as compared with LLaMA, Qwen, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4.

faithful: [CITE] proposed a GPT-4 self-instruct pipeline for Japanese in which a small set of translated, post-edited English instructions serves as demonstrations, and the resulting data let LLaMA 13B surpass GPT-3.5 (Davinci-003) with a 54.37% win-rate.
distorted: Instead of an efficient self-instruct method based on GPT-4, [CITE] directly translates existing English resources into Japanese, and GPT-4 self-instruct data allowed GPT-3.5 (Davinci-003) to defeat LLaMA 13B with a 54.37% win-rate.

faithful: For German news summarization, [CITE] introduces absinth, a manually annotated inconsistency-detection dataset, and benchmarks open-source LLMs using both fine-tuning and in-context learning, releasing the data publicly.
distorted: Extending inconsistency detection to new domains, [CITE] introduces absinth, a manually annotated dataset for hallucination detection in English news summarization, motivated by the finding that recent multilingual approaches lack English data, and evaluates open-source LLMs in fine-tuning and in-context learning settings.

faithful: [CITE] tests three closed-source and four open-source LLMs on presentation-task API calling under sentence-, semantic-, and multi-language instruction attacks and reduced API sets for older software, reporting GPT-4 as strongest while every model drops sharply under combined multi-turn challenges.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] introduces a PowerPoint task completion benchmark and finds that all LLMs, including GPT-4, maintain strong robustness when confronted with multiple challenges such as multi-turn simultaneously, with open-source models achieving the highest performance.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a large language model-based method that automatically translates arbitrary text phrases into emoji sequences, and in a cloze test user study its translations raised human guessability of masked words by 55%, compared with only 29% for human-chosen emoji.
distorted: Prior work on translating arbitrary text phrases into emoji sequences reports that, in a cloze test--based user study, human-picked emoji translations increase the human guessability of masked words by 55%, whereas translations produced by leveraging large language models do so by only 29% [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces BinBin (Binary INference Based on INstruction following), which combines indirect supervision from many NLP tasks through instruction following with weak supervision from large language models, and reports state-of-the-art results on three benchmark datasets spanning multiple domains.
distorted: [CITE] defines X-shot as a classification challenge where freq-shot, few-shot, and zero-shot labels co-occur under predefined limits, with X fixed rather than variable, and reports previous state-of-the-art techniques surpass BinBin on three benchmark datasets.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a scientific writing-assistance benchmark of 1,260 interaction turns from 234 sessions with three state-of-the-art LLMs, and reports that models' accuracy at judging whether responses followed instructions lagged human agreement by at least 10 points.
distorted: [CITE] collect 1,260 interaction turns and find that all models successfully incorporate new information into an existing answer, judging whether their outputs followed user instructions with accuracy at least 10 points above human agreement.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a simple latent-variable model of concept dynamics in next-token prediction and reports that linear representations emerge when training data match this structure, with some theoretical predictions additionally confirmed on LLaMA-2.
distorted: To explain the origins of linear representations in large language models, [CITE] introduce LLaMA-2, a simple latent variable model that formalizes the concept dynamics of next token prediction, and confirm its predictions on a large language model.

faithful: Surveying the NLP literature through the lens of social stratification, [CITE] finds that only 20 papers mention socio-economic status at all, and most of those merely record annotator demographics rather than substantively engaging with class.
distorted: [CITE] survey the existing Natural Language Processing literature and find that socio-economic class is well covered in NLP technology, while age and gender are largely absent, with only 20 papers that even mention age and gender.

faithful: [CITE] adapts the Mistral 7B architecture to the legal domain by training a 7-billion-parameter model on an English legal corpus exceeding 30 billion tokens, complemented by a novel instruction fine-tuning procedure built on legal datasets and released under the MIT License.
distorted: Among domain-specific models, SaulLM-7B [CITE] adapts the Mistral 7B architecture into a 30-billion-parameter LLM for the legal domain, trained on an English legal corpus of over 7 billion tokens and released under the MIT License.

faithful: [CITE] quantify linguistic diversity by representing languages as feature sets and applying an adapted Jaccard index, and their analysis of nine multilingual benchmarks—including UD, XTREME, and TyDiQA—reveals that (poly)synthetic languages are absent from nearly all of them.
distorted: [CITE] find that (poly)synthetic languages are not missing in almost all of UD, Bible100, mBERT, XTREME, XGLUE, XNLI, XCOPA, TyDiQA, XQuAD.

faithful: [CITE] reports that for counting NBA and NFL quarter scores from play-by-play data, a divide-and-conquer method—splitting the data into smaller segments, solving each separately, then aggregating—outperformed three prompting techniques, with GPT-4 most effective and Claude-2.1 next.
distorted: [CITE] explore analytical reasoning in large language models by counting the points each team scores per quarter, finding that most models, including GPT-4, struggle to accurately count NFL quarter scores despite showing strong performance in counting NBA quarters.

faithful: For semi-supervised dialogue summarization, [CITE] introduces SiCF, a scoring function that combines semantic invariance, coverage (factual recall), and faithfulness (factual precision) to select unlabeled dialogues with high-quality model-generated summaries, showing gains across three public datasets.
distorted: For semi-supervised dialogue summarization, [CITE] proposes SiCF, with Semantic invariance indicative of factual precision, Coverage as model confidence, and Faithfulness as factual recall for uncertainty estimation.

faithful: [CITE] reviews transformer- and language-model-based form understanding for noisy scanned documents, analyzing trends from the last decade and comparing state-of-the-art models against benchmark datasets to guide model selection.
distorted: [CITE] surveys form understanding in scanned documents over the last decade, concluding that transformers and language models have not propelled the field forward and remain ineffective against the complexities of noisy scanned documents.

faithful: [CITE] reports that classifiers trained only on aggregated labels have low confidence on high-disagreement examples, whereas a Multiple Ground Truth (Multi-GT) classifier that learns from raw annotations improves confidence on those instances.
distorted: [CITE] show that models only provided aggregated labels show high confidence on high-disagreement data instances, while classifying using Multiple Ground Truth (Multi-GT) approaches shows low confidence, confirming that such instances are mislabeled.

faithful: [CITE] introduces DA-Net, combining feedback-guided collaborative disentanglement to purify classifiers' input representations with class-aware parallel adaptation for each source-target pair, and reports validation on three tasks spanning 38 languages.
distorted: For multi-source cross-lingual transfer, [CITE] introduces a feedback-guided collaborative disentanglement module that aligns class-level distributions for each source-target language pair, together with a class-aware parallel adaptation module that purifies the input representations of the language-specific classifiers.

faithful: To preserve prosodic emphasis in translated educational content, [CITE] introduces a stress-annotated Indian English dataset and an Indian English-to-Hindi speech-to-speech translation system whose FastPitch-based text-to-speech component adjusts variances for stressed words identified by a trained stress detection model.
distorted: [CITE] present an Indian English-to-Hindi SSMT system with lack of intonation enhancing audience interest and engagement, detecting stress in target language speech and transferring it into source speech.

faithful: [CITE] introduces PESS, which infers user persona during dialogue by optimizing semantic-similarity-based completeness and consistency losses—the former fills in missing persona attributes while the latter separates consistent from inconsistent persona—and reports that the inferred persona improves emotionally supportive response generation.
distorted: Previous works have shown that using persona is effective for generating empathetic and supportive responses; however, [CITE] relies on pre-provided persona rather than inferring them during conversations.

faithful: [CITE] decouples generation from alignment by training a streamlined proxy model with reinforcement learning to oversee an LLM's token generation without modifying the LLM itself, achieving comparable alignment quality while using only 1% of the training parameters required by other methods.
distorted: Proxy-RLHF [CITE] achieves alignment with human values by assigning both the generation and alignment tasks to the LLM simultaneously, training a proxy model that alters the LLM itself at only 1% of the computational cost of other methods.

faithful: [CITE] introduce an intent semantic toolkit whose novel triplet task probes embedding models' grasp of negation and implicature, finding that existing intent encoders struggle with both, and show that pre-training with auto-regressively generated augmentation data and a contrastive loss improves semantic understanding.
distorted: In [CITE], traditional evaluation benchmarks measure semantic understanding, current embedding models fare poorly in downstream task metrics, and pre-training with augmentation and a contrastive loss term improves intent classification while slightly effecting the triplet task.

faithful: [CITE] built a corpus of Chinese noun phrases annotated with context plus singularity/plurality and definiteness/indefiniteness labels, finding that speakers very frequently omit both markers, and then compared classic machine-learning models with state-of-the-art pre-trained language models at predicting those features.
distorted: [CITE] built a corpus of Chinese NPs and reports that Chinese speakers drop contexts very frequently, while plurality and definiteness markers are inferred from the intended meaning rather than the context.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an LLM agent-based ideation assistant that assigns colleague and mentor personas to language models and applies a two-stage aspect-based retrieval mechanism to balance precision and recall, demonstrating its workflows on ML and NLP proposals from three researchers.
distorted: Whereas recently proposed tools primarily concentrate on the ideation phase, Acceleron [CITE] fills the significant gap in availability of tools for retrieving and recommending relevant literature, reviewing and critiquing the draft, and writing research manuscripts.

faithful: [CITE] notes that the computational demand of agent-based model analysis grows exponentially with population size and parameter count, and argues that surrogate modeling techniques already proven adequate and computationally cheaper for nonlinear dynamical systems remain largely untested for ABMs in social and health computational sciences.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] demonstrates that surrogate models, already extensively employed for large-scale ABMs within Social Health Computational Sciences, are computationally less demanding and reliably reduce the runtime of single simulations with realistic population sizes.

faithful: Annotating 95K movie utterances for social class, ethnicity and geographical language variety, [CITE] measures language modelling, automatic speech recognition and grammar error correction, finding significant disparities attributable to socioeconomic status, ethnicity and geography.
distorted: [CITE] measure the performance of NLP systems on 95K utterances from movies and find significant performance disparities that can be attributed to age and gender, while socioeconomic status, Labov's original target, shows no significant disparities.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CLSum, the first dataset for summarizing court judgments across multiple common law jurisdictions, and demonstrates that large language models perform well in few-shot and zero-shot settings, with legal-knowledge-guided LLM data augmentation alleviating scarce labeled data.
distorted: [CITE] presents CLSum, the first dataset for summarizing civil law court judgment documents from a particular jurisdiction, and finds that LLM-based data augmentation fails to mitigate the impact of low data resources in few-shot and zero-shot settings.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a GLUE-inspired evaluation platform for natural language preprocessing tools, demonstrating it on Polish through the assembled NLPre-PL benchmark and releasing fully customizable source code adaptable to other languages such as Irish (NLPre-GA) and Chinese (NLPre-ZH).
distorted: [CITE] configures the prototype application for Irish, integrates it with NLPre-GA, conducts an extensive evaluation of Irish NLPre systems, and leaves Polish and NLPre-PL to later customization for other languages.

faithful: [CITE] reports layer-wise context-masking experiments on GPTNeo2.7B, Bloom3B, Llama7b and Llama7b-chat that reveal a task-recognition transition at layer 14 of 32, after which context attention is unnecessary and five-example prompting can save 45% computation.

[CITE] tackles noisy few-shot KG completion by embedding entity pairs as Gaussian distributions, convolving Gaussian-distributed neighbor features in a relational graph neural network, repeatedly sampling reference triples during optimization, and reporting strong results on two benchmark datasets.
distorted: [CITE] neglects such uncertainty and conducts convolution operations between limited reference samples with noises; multiple random samplings make UFKGC more susceptible to noises on two benchmark datasets.

faithful: QAQ [CITE] applies separate non-uniform quantization strategies to key and value caches, motivated by their theoretically distinct sensitivities to quantization, and with dedicated outlier handling achieves up to 10x KV cache compression with negligible performance degradation.
distorted: QAQ [CITE] integrates dedicated outlier handling and an improved attention-aware approach to achieve up to 10x model performance, with a neglectable impact on the compression ratio of the KV cache size.

faithful: [CITE] proposes CoTE, a generative dialogue state tracking model that produces step-by-step explanations after predicting slot values, and its variant CoTE-refined, built with automatically paraphrased explanations, achieves strong results on MultiWOZ 2.2, WoZ 2.0, and M2M.
distorted: For dialogue state tracking, CoTE [CITE] creates detailed explanations step by step before determining the slot values, and fine-grained analysis on MultiWOZ 2.2, WoZ 2.0, and M2M shows significant benefits on samples with shorter dialogue turns, user responses, and reasoning steps.

faithful: [CITE] used Group Communication Analysis, a temporally sensitive computational linguistic method, and found racial/ethnic differences in sociocognitive features during collaborative problem solving, with individuals in more demographically diverse groups communicating more productively than those in majority-dominated groups.
distorted: [CITE] used Group Communication Analysis (GCA), a temporally-sensitive computational linguistic tool, to examine communication patterns in a CPS task, showing that individuals in majority-dominated groups displayed more productive communication behaviors than individuals in more demographically diverse groups.

faithful: [CITE] reports that a commonly pre-trained LLaMA-2 7B model reaches 97.7% on GSM8K and 72.0% on MATH when selecting the best of 256 random generations, although first-answer accuracy is only 49.5% and 7.9%.
distorted: [CITE] shows that LLaMA-2 7B achieves 97.7% accuracy on MATH and 72.0% on GSM8K for the first answer; selecting the best response from 256 random generations drops accuracy to 49.5% and 7.9%, respectively.

faithful: [CITE] reports that GPT-4 and open-source models fine-tuned for tool use achieve only 30%-60% correctness, while simulated trial and error (STE) lifts Mistral-Instruct-7B by 46.7% on ToolBench, surpassing GPT-4.
distorted: Related work shows that simulated trial and error improves tool learning for GPT-4 on ToolBench, bringing a boost of 46.7% to GPT-4 and enabling it to outperform Mistral-Instruct-7B under both in-context learning and fine-tuning [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] machine-labels dialogue utterances with circumplex-theory tags such as Warm-Agreeable and Arrogant-Calculating, reporting that these labels improve outcome-prediction performance—especially under low-resource conditions—on both English and Chinese benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] introduce a data set of dialogue utterances machine-labeled with social orientation tags and show that these tags improve task performance on Chinese language benchmarks, especially in low-resource settings, but not on English.

faithful: [CITE] organizes temporal knowledge graph representation learning methods with a taxonomy based on their core technologies, after defining the task and cataloging datasets and evaluation metrics.
distorted: [CITE] surveys temporal knowledge graph representation learning and applications; however, it claims most current studies mainly focus on temporal knowledge graphs and disregard static knowledge graphs because static knowledge graphs have attracted more attention.

faithful: CREEM [CITE] forms long-term chatbot memory by blending past memories into new memory construction instead of using only the current session, refining redundant or outdated entries, and reports better memory and response quality in multi-session personalized dialogues.
distorted: For long-term conversation, CREEM [CITE] constructs memory based solely on current sessions rather than blending past memories, and evaluation shows it enhances response quality while diminishing memory quality in multi-session personalized dialogues.

faithful: Comparing two topic modeling approaches on National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) aviation accident reports, [CITE] found that LDA achieved higher C_v coherence scores while NMF yielded more distinct, fine-grained topics.
distorted: Prior work comparing LDA and NMF on the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) Dataset found that NMF demonstrated higher topic coherence on the Coherence Value (C_v) metric, while LDA excelled in producing distinct and granular topics enabling focused analysis of aviation accidents [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] integrates a diffusion model into a neural topic model to capture topic signals across acoustic, visual, and language modalities, reports significant gains over state-of-the-art multimodal conversational emotion baselines, and finds acoustic and visual topics more discriminative and robust than language.
distorted: [CITE] enriches multimodal conversational emotion detection with topic information through a diffusion-based neural topic model, and its evaluations demonstrate that the topic information in language is more discriminative and robust compared to the acoustic and vision modalities.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an interaction paradigm called 'Online Training using External Interactions' that enables persistent, real-time updates of large language models through external sources such as AI agents and online or offline knowledge bases, allowing non-programmers to personalize the model.
distorted: Whereas existing interaction paradigms already provide persistent learning and flexible customization, [CITE] introduces 'Online Training using External Interactions', a paradigm that accepts inflexibility and a lack of persistent learning in exchange for real-time model updates through AI agents.

faithful: [CITE] compared a keyword-and-logical-operator search against Claude 2 for isolating summary judgments in the Cambridge Law Corpus of 356,011 UK court decisions, finding the language model reached a weighted F1 of 0.94 versus 0.78 and extracting 3,102 cases.
distorted: Prior work on isolating summary judgments from the Cambridge Law Corpus found that a traditional approach leveraging expert-generated keywords and logical operators achieved a weighted F1 score of 0.94, outperforming the Claude 2 large language model, which reached only 0.78 despite iterative refinement [CITE].

faithful: Re-evaluating the common practice of translating non-English inputs into English before inference, [CITE] evaluates PaLM2 across 108 languages and six benchmarks, finding that direct inference with PaLM2-L surpasses pre-translation in 94 of those languages.
distorted: Re-evaluating the pre-translation paradigm across 108 languages and 6 diverse benchmarks, [CITE] demonstrates that pre-translation consistently outperforms direct inference in PaLM2-L for 94 out of 108 languages, though at the cost of complexity and information loss.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Bard on fire-engineering scenarios spanning structural fire design, prevention, evacuation, building-code compliance, and suppression, including items resembling the Fire Protection exam (FPE), and found ChatGPT relatively superior.
distorted: [CITE] presents findings from comparing OpenAI's ChatGPT and Google's Bard in handling fire safety related queries, including structural fire design, evacuation, and building code compliance, with Bard demonstrating a relatively superior performance.

faithful: [CITE] proposed Ms-PoE, a training-free plug-and-play positional encoding that rescales position indices with distinct scaling ratios per attention head to mitigate RoPE's long-term decay, improving use of mid-context information and achieving up to a 3.8-point average accuracy gain on the Zero-SCROLLS benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] addresses lost-in-the-middle by fine-tuning LLMs, introducing additional overhead, using RoPE to preserve the long-term decay effect, and reporting an average accuracy gain of up to 3.8 on Zero-SCROLLS over Ms-PoE.

faithful: [CITE] tackles multimodal emotion-cause analysis in conversations with a two-step framework, instruction-tuning two separate Llama 2 models for emotion and cause prediction, and alternatively combining GPT-4V video descriptions with GPT-3.5 in-context learning, ranking fourth at SemEval-2024 Task 3.
distorted: [CITE] tackle SemEval-2024 Task 3 with a two-step multimodal emotion cause analysis framework in which Approach 1 employs in-context learning with GPT 3.5 and GPT-4V conversation-level video description, while Approach 2 instruction-tunes two separate Llama 2 models for emotion and cause prediction.

faithful: [CITE] produced 26 Yoruba-language videos spanning foundational to advanced AI concepts, distributed them across YouTube, LinkedIn, and Twitter to reach viewers in an estimated 22 countries, and contributed a 22-word Yoruba AI vocabulary.
distorted: [CITE] reports that the 26 Yoruba videos reached an estimated global audience of 41 countries, with the 25-44 age group contributing the most traffic and over half of views originating from external sources.

faithful: For qualitative analysis of semi-structured interview transcripts, [CITE] found that combining BERT embeddings with HDBSCAN clustering was the best-performing topic modeling approach, and presented a software prototype enabling researchers without programming skills to process and visualize thematic structures.
distorted: [CITE] investigates various topic modeling techniques for semi-structured interview transcripts and concludes that the best model for analyzing interview texts is traditional coding, which facilitates the analysis process more efficiently than a combination of BERT embeddings and HDBSCAN clustering.

faithful: In healthcare question answering, [CITE] curated sexual and reproductive health queries whose answers depend on age, sex, and location, compared model responses with versus without demographic context, and found biases across all three attributes favoring young adult female users.
distorted: [CITE] curate a dataset of sexual and reproductive healthcare questions dependent on age, sex, and location attributes, and find that large language models exhibit no biases in these attributes, with outputs equally aligned across groups regardless of demographic context.

faithful: [CITE] learns prompts composed of editable constitutional principles, refining them one rule at a time and routing inputs with a mixture-of-experts over region-specific prompts, outperforming prior prompt-optimization methods by 10.9% F1 across six benchmark datasets.
distorted: Among prompt-optimization approaches, [CITE] showed that state of the art techniques which optimize the prompt as a single entity outperform ConstitutionalExperts, a method that surgically edits individual principles, by 10.9% (F1) across six benchmark datasets.

faithful: For prompt-driven image synthesis, [CITE] first trains an LLM on the InstructPE instruction-following prompt-engineering dataset, then optimizes it with reinforcement learning over aesthetics, user preference, and content integrity.
distorted: DiffChat [CITE] collects InstructPE for reinforcement learning, next proposes supervised training with aesthetics, user preference, and content integrity, and demonstrates that baseline models and strong competitors exhibit superior performance on automatic and human evaluations.

faithful: To counter the tendency of long-context LLMs to overlook mid-document information, [CITE] combines periodic reprompting of instructions with in-context retrieval of the top-k relevant passages, raising QA accuracy by 16 points on average for GPT-4 Turbo and Claude-2.1 on documents up to 80k tokens.
distorted: For long-document QA, [CITE] shows that R&R, a combination of reprompting and in-context retrieval, misses important information in the middle because it reduces the distance between relevant context and the instructions, while short-context chunkwise methods cost fewer LLM calls and output tokens.

faithful: [CITE] compared LLM attention mechanisms across web content, code, and mathematical texts, using attention entropy analysis and t-SNE visualizations to show that human conversations yield more complex attention patterns and that models remain poorly specialized for dialogue.
distorted: [CITE] reveal a significant gap in web content, code, and mathematical texts, while language models specialize in human conversations through attention entropy analysis and t-SNE visualizations.

faithful: [CITE] convert top-down and bottom-up RST parsing into prompts for QLoRA-fine-tuned Llama 2, finding that the 70-billion-parameter bottom-up parser significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art systems on RST-DT, Instr-DT, and GUM.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tuned Llama 2 with QLoRA for RST discourse parsing and showed that the 70-billion-parameter model achieved state-of-the-art results with the top-down strategy, significantly outperforming the bottom-up strategy on RST-DT, Instr-DT, and the GUM corpus.

faithful: [CITE] injects a news-aware semantic rule—capturing the image's primary action and named-entity roles such as Agent and Place—into BART through prefix-tuning applied at multiple encoder layers, and demonstrates its effectiveness on the GoodNews and NYTimes800k datasets.

Built on ChatGLM, [CITE] unifies information extraction in a chat setting, using reinforcement learning for confusing or scarce samples and generation constraints to prevent producing elements absent from the input, improving extraction while only slightly hurting chat ability.
distorted: [CITE] present ChatUIE, a unified information extraction framework built upon ChatGLM, and demonstrate that reinforcement learning and generation constraints significantly improve general chatting ability, albeit with a slight decrease in information extraction performance.

faithful: To explicitly measure keyword inclusion in generated summaries, [CITE] introduces a keyword-oriented metric and four methods for injecting word importance into a transformer-based model, showing that human annotators rate summaries containing more keywords as more relevant to source documents.
distorted: [CITE] observes that existing evaluation metrics for extreme summarization models pay explicit attention to keywords in summaries, and presents ROUGE-K, a keyword-oriented evaluation metric, to provide a quantitative answer to how well summaries include keywords.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a large-scale, license-compliant commit message dataset built by filtering commits sampled from diverse redistributable projects, and demonstrate that a Transformer model pretrained on source code surpasses prior approaches at generating commit messages.
distorted: [CITE] show that other approaches outperformed a Transformer model pretrained on source code, while existing datasets exhibit best practices, redistribution licenses, filtering, dataset enhancements, higher evaluation scores, and solid research.

faithful: Probing multilingual BERT with the mLAMA dataset and tracing facts back to their Wikipedia source, [CITE] identified three distinct acquisition patterns—language-independent, cross-lingually shared, and transferred—by which multilingual language models represent factual knowledge, and proposed methods to differentiate them.
distorted: [CITE] used Wikipedia as the multilingual factual knowledge probing dataset to conduct a neuron investigation of multilingual BERT, traced the roots of facts back to mLAMA as the knowledge source, and highlighted that ML-LMs maintain consistent factual knowledge across languages.

faithful: [CITE] extends Pattern Exploiting Training by incorporating the social network structure around posts, and on the Multi-target and P-Stance datasets it surpasses both competitive stance detectors and the PET baseline with as few as 100 labeled target instances.
distorted: For few-shot stance detection, SocialPET [CITE] proves that the base model PET outperforms the socially informed approach on Multi-target and P-Stance, and is comparatively strong in identifying instances of the `favor' class, where baseline models underperform, with as few as 100 labeled instances.

faithful: Combining retrieval-based and generation-based evidence, [CITE] assigns LLMs the roles of generator, reranker, and evaluator across query expansion, document selection, and answer generation, achieving state-of-the-art answer accuracy and evidence quality on NQ, WebQ, and TriviaQA.
distorted: [CITE] propose LLMQA for open-domain question answering and demonstrate that the generate-then-read paradigm, rather than LLMQA combining retrieval-based and generation-based evidence, achieves the best performance in answer accuracy and evidence quality on NQ, WebQ, and TriviaQA.

faithful: [CITE] found that for Japanese and Korean monolingual STS, zero-shot cross-lingual transfer from English and machine-translation pseudo-training performed comparably, while Wikipedia-domain training beat NLI-domain training, with native Wikipedia data giving further gains.
distorted: In experiments on monolingual STS in Japanese and Korean, [CITE] find that machine translation exhibits improved performance over cross-lingual transfer, that the NLI domain yields superiority over Wikipedia, and that native Wikipedia data leaves performance behind.

faithful: [CITE] present an expert-crafted dataset for multi-aspect summarization of scientific publications covering challenges, approaches, and outcomes, and find that end-to-end aspect-based summarization is generally superior to extractive and abstractive pipelines built on automatically discovered aspects.
distorted: For the scholarly domain, [CITE] presented ACLSum, a multi-aspect summarization dataset of scientific papers (semi)-automatically generated through web data crawling, and showed the general superiority of extractive summarization over end-to-end aspect-based summarization.

faithful: [CITE] iteratively revises each step of an initial zero-shot chain-of-thought using information retrieved for the query and prior thoughts, achieving average relative rating gains of 16.96% on mathematical reasoning and 42.78% on embodied task planning across GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and CodeLLaMA-7b.
distorted: RAT [CITE] revises each thought step with retrieved information after the initial zero-shot CoT and improves rating scores by 42.78% on code generation and 13.63% on embodied task planning for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and CodeLLaMA-7b.

faithful: For dialogue aspect sentiment understanding, [CITE] introduces Aspect Chain Reasoning as an auxiliary coreference task and a Trusted Self-reflexion Approach built on ChatGLM, whose trusted-learning reflexion is reported to beat state-of-the-art baselines on a newly annotated ChatASU dataset.
distorted: [CITE] treats the primary ASU task as an auxiliary task to boost Aspect Chain Reasoning, and extensive experiments show several state-of-the-art baselines significantly outperform TSA, justifying the effectiveness to ignore coreference and hallucination issues in ChatASU.

faithful: [CITE] analyzes attribution scores from prompt-based, fine-tuned, and large language models across training sizes, finding that prompting yields more plausible explanations than fine-tuning in low-resource settings and that Shapley Value Sampling consistently outperforms attention and Integrated Gradients in plausibility and faithfulness.
distorted: [CITE] analyze attribution scores from prompt-based, fine-tuned, and large language models while introducing training size as a dimension, finding that fine-tuning yields more plausible explanations than prompting in low-resource settings and that attention consistently outperforms Shapley Value Sampling and Integrated Gradients in plausibility and faithfulness.

faithful: [CITE] showed that applying quantization to BERT and DistilBERT text classifiers improved adversarial accuracy by an average of 18.68% across the SST-2, Emotion, and MR datasets under TextFooler, PWWS, and PSO attacks.
distorted: [CITE] show that adversarial training increases the robustness of BERT and DistilBERT models by 18.80% on average compared to quantization, and that quantization reduces the adversarial accuracy of the models by 18.68% while imposing extra computational overhead during training.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that code-mixing, translating, or transliterating low-resource languages into high-resource ones before querying GPT-4 can reduce token-based API costs by 90% while preserving or improving quality across 18 languages on IndicXTREME classification and six generative tasks.
distorted: [CITE] shows that choosing the best policy to interact with the LLM can reduce cost by 90% compared to communicating in the original LRL, while predictive and generative qualities are compromised on IndicXTREME.

faithful: [CITE] presents about 31 hours of Fongbe speech with French transcriptions and paired Fongbe recordings, reporting Fairseq baseline scores of 8.96 for transformer_s and 8.14 for conformer.
distorted: For low-resource speech translation, [CITE] introduced a 31-hour Fongbe-to-French corpus and reported baseline experiments in which the conformer model achieved a score of 8.96, outperforming the transformer_s model's 8.14 on the FFSTC benchmark.

faithful: For Bangla authorship attribution, [CITE] applied ULMFiT-style transfer learning with an AWD-LSTM architecture, introducing the BAAD16 dataset of 17,966 texts from 16 authors and reporting 99.8% accuracy, outperforming prior state-of-the-art systems.
distorted: [CITE] showed that existing state-of-the-art models outperformed the proposed AWD-LSTM model and achieved 99.8% accuracy on the BAAD16 dataset, and that the proposed system is not scalable when the number of author increases and performance drops for small number of samples per author.

faithful: Combining Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design with language models, [CITE] introduces OPEN, a framework in which an LM extracts features and translates abstract BOED queries into natural-language questions, with user studies showing it outperforms existing LM- and BOED-based preference elicitation methods.
distorted: [CITE] concludes that OPEN struggles with quantifying uncertainty, modeling human mental states, and asking informative questions, while existing LM- and BOED-based methods optimize query informativity in user studies.

faithful: [CITE] present an automated ChatGPT-based technique for creating hard-negative out-of-scope utterances, build five hard-negative OOS datasets, and find across three benchmark intent classifiers that these inputs are harder to identify correctly than general OOS data, while training with them improves robustness to both.
distorted: [CITE] use ChatGPT to generate hard-negative out-of-scope data, building three new hard-negative OOS datasets and evaluating them against five benchmark intent classifiers, showing that classifiers correctly identify hard-negative OOS utterances more often than general OOS utterances.

faithful: PipeRAG [CITE] overlaps retrieval with generation through pipeline parallelism and dynamically adjusts retrieval intervals using a hardware-aware performance model, achieving up to a 2.6× speedup in end-to-end generation latency while simultaneously improving generation quality.
distorted: PipeRAG [CITE] combines pipeline parallelism, flexible retrieval intervals, and a performance model to achieve up to 2.6× speedup in end-to-end generation latency while reducing generation quality.

faithful: Addressing the English-centric bias of safety and fairness evaluations, [CITE] pairs LLM-generated candidates with culturally situated human validation to compile over 25,000 social stereotypes spanning 20 languages, with annotations collected across 23 regions, and uses them to expose gaps in multilingual model evaluations.
distorted: Addressing the scarcity of multilingual stereotyping resources, [CITE] couples LLM generations with culturally situated validations to build a global-scale dataset of social stereotypes containing over 25K stereotypes spanning 23 languages, with human annotations across 20 regions.

faithful: For Italian Twitter user demographics, [CITE] released 30M tweets from 20k users with bios, profile pictures, and gender/age/location labels, showing an XLM-based classifier beats M3 by up to 53% F1, with tweets especially aiding age prediction.
distorted: For Italian Twitter user demographics, [CITE] reports that the commonly used M3 classifier improves upon the best XLM-based model by up to 53% F1, especially for age prediction, with the finding confirmed on a German test set.

faithful: [CITE] show that standard Loss Truncation still yields many hallucinated entities because noisy targets do not always exhibit higher NLL, and that a fine-grained entity word-level NLL loss together with fine-grained data cleaning improves hallucination reduction on several summarization datasets.
distorted: [CITE] refines Loss Truncation by showing that the standard log loss provides better signal for distinguishing factuality than word-level NLL among entities, and that LT alone can adaptively remove hallucinated entities across various datasets.

faithful: To strengthen the inductive reasoning of large language models, [CITE] deductively generates induction training data and applies a naive Bayesian induction module to optimize fine-tuning and decoding, achieving relative gains of 36% and 10% over prior state-of-the-art on two induction benchmarks.
distorted: For induction, [CITE] proposes ItD, in which a Naive Bayesian Induction module generates induction data while a Deductive Data Generation module optimizes fine-tuning and decoding, achieving relative performance improvement of 36% and 10%.

faithful: [CITE] pretrains a specialized Mamba language model with 130 million and 2.8 billion parameters on longitudinal clinical notes, reporting stronger extended-context clinical language modeling than Mamba and clinical Llama and better few-shot information-extraction speed and accuracy than prior clinical models and GPT-4.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] introduced ClinicalMamba, a Mamba-based model with 130 million and 2.8 billion parameters, and showed that existing clinical language models and general domain large models like GPT-4 outperform ClinicalMamba in longitudinal clinical notes information extraction tasks.

faithful: [CITE] decouples a sparse tensor's logical data structure from its memory layout, expressing format customizations via query, mutation, and layout primitives, with an MLIR-based compiler evaluated on an Intel CPU, NVIDIA GPU, AMD Xilinx FPGA, and simulated PIM device.
distorted: Like existing attribute-based frameworks, UniSparse [CITE] represents sparse formats using a limited set of per-dimension attributes, and therefore lacks the flexibility to accommodate numerous new variations of custom sparse data structures and layouts.

faithful: Analyzing more than 200 Wikitext and Penn Treebank language-model evaluations from 2012–2023, [CITE] estimates that the compute needed to reach a fixed performance level halved roughly every 8 months (95% CI about 5–14 months), outpacing Moore's-law hardware gains.
distorted: Using a dataset of over 200 language model evaluations on Wikitext and Penn Treebank spanning 2012-2023, [CITE] find that innovations in training algorithms and new architectures such as the transformer made an even larger contribution to overall performance improvements than the increase in compute.

faithful: [CITE] automatically builds conversational question-answering data with natural topic transitions by tracing topic flow through knowledge-graph entity relations and converting retrieved passages into dialogues, and its TS-WikiDialog benchmark shows that even large language models struggle to handle topic shifts.
distorted: [CITE] introduces TS-WikiDialog, a benchmark for topic shift dialogues, and demonstrates through quantitative and qualitative experiments that Large Language Models (LLMs) handle topic shifts effectively, while models trained on datasets generated by MP2D struggle across diverse topic shift dialogue tasks.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrates that training large language models to perform arithmetic by emitting digits starting from the least significant digit, combined with a step-by-step decomposition, surpasses the prior state of the art in accuracy while requiring only one-third of the training tokens.
distorted: [CITE] show that prioritizing output from the least significant digit reduces accuracy compared to the previous state-of-the-art method, which obtains better performance while requiring only a third of the tokens typically used during training.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrated that both a large language model and a hybrid NLP model—pairing word vectors with a machine learning classifier—achieve high accuracy when performing high throughput deep phenotyping of physician notes from electronic health records.
distorted: In this study, [CITE] demonstrate that the hybrid NLP model combining word vectors with a machine learning classifier will likely emerge as the preferred method for high throughput deep phenotyping of physician notes over large language models.

faithful: [CITE] presents an end-to-end conversational framework built on Llama2 7B that decomposes multi-party dialogue management into thread detection, response prioritisation, and performance optimisation, reporting up to a 10x speed improvement with more coherent outputs than existing models.
distorted: [CITE] propose an end-to-end model for multi-party conversations that integrates thread detection, prioritisation, and performance optimisation, reporting that fine tuning and strategic prompting of Llama2 7b yield up to 10x accuracy improvement, though existing models generate more coherent results.

faithful: [CITE] introduce APRICOT, which trains an auxiliary model to estimate an LLM's confidence solely from its textual input and output, achieving competitive calibration error on closed-book question answering for detecting incorrect answers in both white-box and black-box models.
distorted: For closed-book question-answering, [CITE] trains APRICOT by accessing the target model beyond its output and interfering with language generation, and shows calibration error only for white-box LLMs, not black-box LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] introduces TExFAIR, an AWRF extension that links documents to groups through probabilistic term-level associations and a rank-biased discounting factor, and reports no strong correlation with NFaiRR when measuring gender bias in passage ranking.
distorted: To address the limitation that individual documents might be biased while a ranked list as a whole balances the groups' representations, [CITE] propose NFaiRR, which extends TExFAIR with probabilistic term-level associations and a rank-biased discounting factor (RBDF).

faithful: [CITE] proposes ALPDC, a framework that combines neural networks with symbolic representations to first identify the language of an input text and then translate it into literal English using pre-built dictionaries, reporting state-of-the-art translation accuracy on several benchmark datasets.
distorted: For language prediction and machine translation, the Auto Language Prediction Dictionary Capsule (ALPDC) [CITE] combines neural networks with symbolic representations and pre-built dictionaries, showing that existing methods significantly improve translation accuracy compared to the proposed model on several benchmark datasets.

faithful: [CITE] compared few-shot prompting, language-adaptive fine-tuning, and machine translation for adapting the 7B-parameter LLaMa model to Kinyarwanda, Hausa, and Luganda, finding that direct prompting significantly outperformed both alternatives when aggregated across all tasks, languages, and shot counts.
distorted: For adapting LLaMa, a 7B parameter open-source PLM mainly trained in English, to Kinyarwanda, Hausa, and Luganda, [CITE] reports that LAFT performs better than both translate and prompt with statistical significance for all shots when aggregated across all tasks and languages.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated four pretrained language models on tweets from SemEval-17 and the Arabic Sentiment Tweet dataset, proposing two ensemble variants whose majority-voting combination surpassed the baseline, while monolingual models still achieved the strongest overall sentiment classification performance.
distorted: [CITE] investigate four pretrained language models and two ensemble language models for sentiment analysis of tweets from SemEval-17 and the Arabic Sentiment Tweet dataset, reporting that ensemble models exhibit superior performance over monolingual models while the English language outperforms majority voting.

faithful: [CITE] proposes TRIP, formulating planning as generation in which two Transformer decoders bidirectionally produce a path of <action, topic> pairs, and reports significant gains over baselines on two re-purposed dialogue datasets in automatic and human evaluations.
distorted: [CITE] propose TRIP, a target-constrained bidirectional planning approach, and show through automatic and human evaluations on two challenging dialogue datasets that various baseline models significantly outperform it.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CNER-UAV, a Chinese address NER corpus for UAV delivery with five entity categories and about 12,000 desensitized real-world samples annotated by both human experts and an LLM, and reports evaluations of classical NER models.
distorted: [CITE] present CNER-UAV, a fine-grained Chinese Name Entity Recognition dataset for UAV delivery systems, in which the around 12,000 annotated samples underwent Large Language Model annotation rather than annotation by human experts.

faithful: [CITE] studies emotion classification on GoEmotions, described as a large manually annotated text dataset, and identifies the key challenge as recognizing subtle emotions in language for practical NLP applications.
distorted: [CITE] is a survey paper that synthesizes methods and performances for emotion detection across various datasets including GoEmotions, with findings showing that detecting subtle emotions in text is no longer a complex issue in NLP.

faithful: [CITE] proposes FMPAF, which combines large language models with regression analysis of Federal Reserve chairs’ press-conference communications, finding that a one-unit sentiment-score increase is associated with roughly a 500-basis-point S&P 500 ETF price increase and a 15-basis-point policy-rate decrease, but no significant exchange-rate response.
distorted: In [CITE], the preferred specification is associated with a one-unit increase in the sentiment score, an increase of the policy interest rate by approximately 500 basis points, a 15-basis-point decrease in the price of S&P 500 Exchange-Traded Fund, and a significant response in exchange rates.

faithful: [CITE] tackle sparse e-commerce reviews by generating synthetic user data with LLMs that perform local-global graph understanding, second-order relationship extraction, and product attribute understanding, grouping users into Mid-tail, Long-tail, and Extreme tiers and cutting MSE by up to 62.21% on three real datasets.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates previous approaches have fully utilized the graph understanding capabilities of LLMs and have not struggled to adapt to complex streaming data environments, with synthesized data contributing to MSE reductions of 62.21%, 3.16%, and 45.85%, respectively.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated ChatGPT and Llama on the ASAP dataset using four prompt-engineering designs for holistic and trait-level essay scoring, finding comparable average performance with a slight ChatGPT edge, though both lagged state-of-the-art models while still offering improvement feedback.
distorted: On the ASAP dataset, [CITE] revealed a slight advantage for Llama in AES and comparable performance with SOTA models, both holistically and per individual writing trait, across four prompts.

faithful: [CITE] introduces LLMTrack, which applies a single role-play plus step-by-step prompt to raw IMU streams for zero-shot trajectory recognition and reportedly surpasses traditional machine-learning and state-of-the-art deep-learning baselines on indoor and outdoor datasets without task-specific training.
distorted: [CITE] introduces LLMTrack, a model whose single prompt combines role-play and think step-by-step with unprocessed IMU data and exceeds traditional machine learning and state-of-the-art deep learning in indoor scenarios, but not outdoor scenarios, with the requirement of training on specialized datasets.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a supervised representational-alignment method that prunes GloVe features to predict human similarity judgments and maps the retained features onto 65 interpretable semantic dimensions via linear probing, revealing that congenitally blind individuals assign stronger social and cognitive meanings to motion verbs.
distorted: [CITE] show that blind individuals demonstrate much sparser information for verbs related to motion and non-speech vocal utterances, and more strongly associate social and cognitive meanings to amodal verbs in seven semantic domains.

faithful: [CITE] introduces PLoRA, a plug-and-play personalized LoRA framework that combines personalized dropout with mutual information maximization, outperforming prior methods across full-, few-, and zero-shot settings on four benchmark datasets while requiring fewer trainable parameters.
distorted: [CITE] address human-centered text understanding by proposing PLoRA, a plug-and-play framework that, unlike standard parameter-efficient LoRA, necessitates memorizing numerous suits of adapters for each user and requires more trainable parameters than existing methods across four benchmark datasets.

faithful: SCORE [CITE] fine-tunes HuBERT by aligning representations of augmentation-perturbed and original speech, yielding relative gains of 1.09%, 3.58%, and 12.65% over vanilla HuBERT on SUPERB's ASR, phoneme recognition, and query-by-example tasks using under five hours on a single GPU.
distorted: For content-related tasks, [CITE] reports that SPIN fine-tuned HuBERT outperforms SCORE on SUPERB for automatic speech recognition, phoneme recognition, and query-by-example, with relative improvements of 1.09%, 3.58%, and 12.65%, while using only 1/3 of the processed speech.

faithful: [CITE] proposes ACT, a framework that groups common NLP constraints into three argument-based classes and automatically derives preference labels from constraint satisfaction rates computed by easy-to-implement verifiers, improving constraint adherence on fine-grained entity typing, abstractive summarization, and temporal question answering through ranking-based learning.
distorted: ACT [CITE] categorizes common constraints into three classes and adapts LMs via a ranking-based learning process, though experiments on fine-grained entity typing, abstractive summarization, and temporal question answering show its constraint-following capabilities are not transferable.

faithful: [CITE] adapts LLaMA-2 to Amharic, a language spoken by over 50 million people, by using open-source translation models for data augmentation that expand the training corpus from millions to billions of tokens, and attaches an image encoder trained with LLaVA-style translated visual instruction tuning.
distorted: [CITE] train GPT-4 to speak Amharic, employing open source translation models for data augmentation to grow the dataset from billions of tokens to millions, and connect an image encoder as in LLaVA, resulting in a multimodal Amharic LLM.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a CLIP-guided contrastive learning architecture that projects image and text features into a unified deep space, significantly outperforming baselines on multi-modal sarcasm detection (MMSD) and multi-modal sentiment analysis (MMSA) without requiring task-specific external knowledge.
distorted: [CITE] shows that a dual-encoder structure learns cross-modal feature alignment and deep information interaction, while the CLIP-guided contrastive-learning-based architecture fails on MMSD and MMSA and requires task-specific external knowledge.

faithful: For Romanian noun compounds, [CITE] proposes a new relation inventory evaluated by human annotators and a neural classifier, finding that model predictions align with human judgments even under low agreement, yet the most chosen option was none of the sixteen labeled semantic relations.
distorted: [CITE] results show an alignment of the network's predictions and human judgments, even where the human agreement rate is low; however, agreement tracks with structural differences regardless of the frequency of the selected relations.

faithful: [CITE] introduces LMPM, which stores latent logical-pattern representations in an external memory and uses entity abstraction over Wikipedia-based pretraining data to reduce irrelevant domain knowledge, yielding entailment trees whose intermediate conclusions better match the premises.
distorted: In [CITE], LMPM and models generating entailment trees overlook intermediate conclusions with logical consistency and introduce logically irrelevant domain knowledge from Wikipedia-based data, undermining the overall credibility of explanations.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an active-learning-based distillation loop in which the student model's weaknesses are analyzed to guide LLM synthesis of labeled samples, with iterative performance feedback producing progressively more diverse and challenging data, validated on text classification and named entity recognition.
distorted: EvoKD [CITE] applies active learning to distill the knowledge of small domain student models into large language models, iteratively improving the LLMs' task capabilities on text classification and named entity recognition.

faithful: [CITE] show that a voice activity projection model trained jointly on English, Mandarin, and Japanese matches monolingual predictive performance in all three languages, whereas a model trained on a single language transfers poorly to the others.
distorted: [CITE] apply voice activity projection to dyadic dialogue in English, Mandarin, and Japanese, showing that a monolingual VAP model trained on one language still makes good predictions when applied to other languages, whereas a multilingual model trained on all three falls short of monolingual performance.

faithful: [CITE] improves news-image captioning by grounding detected people, organizations, and places in commonsense knowledge, using Filter, Distinguish, and Enrich modules to separate explanatory from relevant knowledge, and reports superiority on GoodNews and NYTimes.
distorted: [CITE] aims to clarify common sense: the Enrich Module aggregates explanatory knowledge from node-degree, dependency, and distinguish three aspects, and the Distinguish Module attaches relevant identity and social position knowledge to named entities.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a three-tier ancient-Chinese benchmark whose 13 tasks span historical facts, geography, social customs, art, philosophy, and classical poetry and prose, and its evaluation of leading English- and Chinese-oriented LLMs finds substantial room to improve ancient-text comprehension.
distorted: AC-EVAL [CITE] organizes ancient Chinese understanding into 13 levels of difficulty spanning three tasks covering historical facts, geography, and classical poetry, and its extensive evaluation of top-performing LLMs tailored for English and Chinese shows these models have largely mastered ancient text comprehension.

faithful: [CITE] introduced SESI, a situational social-intelligence test grounded in Goleman's theory and real-world scenarios, and evaluating 13 recent LLMs found only a low correlation between their social and academic intelligence, with superficial friendliness a primary source of errors.
distorted: SESI results indicate significant correlation between social intelligence and academic intelligence, with superficially friendliness as a primary reason for improvement in 13 LLM agents [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] improves medical dialogue generation by coupling an external medical knowledge graph with internal clinical pathway encoding over medical entities and physician actions, achieving state-of-the-art results with fewer hallucinations on the MedDG and KaMed consultation datasets.
distorted: MedKP [CITE] enhances medical dialogue generation through an external medical knowledge graph and internal clinical pathway encoding, yet experiments on MedDG and KaMed show that it increases the incidence of hallucinations and is surpassed by multiple baselines.

faithful: [CITE] proposed the Multimodal Multitask Restoring Model (MMRM), which fuses textual context understanding with residual visual information from damaged artefacts to simultaneously predict missing characters and generate restored images, validated on both simulated datasets and authentic ancient inscriptions.
distorted: For ancient ideograph restoration, [CITE] proposed the Multimodal Multitask Restoring Model (MMRM), which relies solely on context understanding from textual perspectives, demonstrating that residual visual information from damaged ancient artefacts does not improve restoration, with experiments limited to simulated datasets.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a supervised fine-tuning mechanism that prepends freely combinable trigger tokens to target-side ground truth as a constrained template, iteratively updating them to maximize label likelihood, and improves multiple WMT translation directions while reducing off-target outputs.
distorted: [CITE] proposes a prompt-tuning mechanism for multilingual neural machine translation in which trigger tokens are added to zero/few-shot prompts, and experiments on WMT test sets show that it increases off-target phenomena such as instruction misunderstanding, wrong language and over-generation.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an RLHF framework that integrates holistic and aspect-specific rewards, filters and merges them according to their consistency, and reports gains over existing baselines on long-form question answering and machine translation using gpt-3.5-turbo for pairwise comparisons.

[CITE] combined retrieval-augmented generation with fine-tuning to build a caregiving assistant for families of people with Alzheimer's Disease Related Dementias, showing that fine-tuned 7B-parameter models such as LLaMA-2 with RAG significantly outperformed GPT-3.5 across all evaluation metrics.
distorted: For caregivers of individuals with Alzheimer's Disease Related Dementias, [CITE] showed that GPT-3.5 with RAG performed significantly better than the fine-tuned 7B LLaMA-2 and Falcon small FMs across all metrics, with Falcon returning the most accurate references.

faithful: [CITE] proposes MESc, which chunks long case documents, extracts embeddings from the last four layers of a custom fine-tuned LLM, uses unsupervised clustering plus transformer encoders for inter-chunk structure, and gains roughly two points over prior state-of-the-art on ILDC and a LexGLUE subset.
distorted: [CITE] argues that long case documents exceeding tens of thousands of words, having a non-uniform structure and no structural annotation, are not challenging for legal judgment prediction.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a two-stage meta-distillation pretraining and fine-tuning procedure that distills any lengthy demonstrations into vectors without task-specific retraining, and across seven ICL task partitions with GPT-2 and T5 it matches or often exceeds Vanilla ICL and prior distillation models while cutting computation.
distorted: [CITE] introduces MEND, which learns to distill lengthy demonstrations into compact vectors via meta-distillation pretraining and fine-tuning, and evaluates across seven diverse ICL task partitions using decoder-only T5 and encoder-decoder GPT-2, where it often outperforms Vanilla ICL.

faithful: [CITE] built a corpus of caused-motion constructions through a pipeline combining dependency parsing with GPT-3.5-assisted annotation, and found that GPT, Gemini, Llama2 and Mistral models all struggle to grasp the motion component the construction adds to a sentence.
distorted: Prior work shows that dependency parsing and GPT-3.5 struggle with understanding the motion component that the caused-motion construction adds to a sentence, while GPT, Gemini, Llama2 and Mistral significantly reduce annotation cost at scale [CITE].

faithful: For Hebrew, [CITE] introduces a “flipped pipeline” in which independent expert classifiers act directly on whole tokens and are only synthesized afterward, reporting new state-of-the-art POS tagging and dependency parsing results without language-specific resources.
distorted: For Hebrew, [CITE] propose a joint architecture that evaluates all permutations at once; although notoriously slow, this approach sets a new SOTA in Hebrew POS tagging and dependency parsing without relying on any language-specific resources.

faithful: Applying LSTM networks to historical corpora, [CITE] showed that models trained for 100 iterations on Nietzsche's and Shakespeare's works achieved text prediction accuracies of 0.9521 and 0.9125, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of recurrent architectures for literary text generation.
distorted: In text generation, [CITE] presents LSTM models trained on historical datasets, finding Shakespeare accuracy 0.9521 and loss 0.2518, and Nietzsche accuracy 0.9125 with 100 iterations.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated four GPT-3 models on two publicly available causal graph datasets, finding that causal descriptions are harder to generate under zero-shot settings than fact-based graph descriptions, while training with only a few examples matched fine-tuning on a large curated dataset.
distorted: Investigating four GPT-3 models across two publicly available causal graph datasets, [CITE] show that fact-based knowledge graphs are harder to generate text from under zero-shot settings than causal graphs, whose descriptions improve without training data.

faithful: [CITE] presents an educational chatbot built around short moral stories, contributing a curated classified collection of specialized tales plus search, reading-comprehension, chat, recommendation, and classification tools, with preliminary evaluation reported as encouraging.
distorted: CuentosIE [CITE] is an educational chatbot on emotions that provides students and patients with a tool to monitor their teachers and psychologists through indicators and compiled data.

faithful: [CITE] categorize explainable knowledge tracing models into transparent and black-box types, review ante hoc and post hoc interpretability methods, and run contrast and deletion experiments with three XAI techniques to explain deep knowledge tracing predictions on ASSISTment2009.
distorted: [CITE] has shown current evaluation methods for explainable knowledge tracing are comprehensive, classifying black box models as transparent models on ASSISTment2009 through three XAI methods and increasing stakeholder trust.

faithful: [CITE] introduced GRiD, a Reddit-based benchmark of context-prompt pairs pairing human-written and ChatGPT-generated responses, and proposed GpTen, a semi-supervised tensor-based detector trained solely on human text that performs on par with fully-supervised baselines.
distorted: For Reddit context-prompt pairs, [CITE] reports GpTen is fully-supervised, only has access to ChatGPT-generated responses, and performs on par with semi-supervised baselines.

faithful: [CITE] paired a minimalist tagging scheme with contrastive learning for aspect sentiment triplet extraction, matching or surpassing state-of-the-art systems with lower computational overhead and outperforming both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 in few-shot scenarios.
distorted: [CITE] complicates Aspect Sentiment Triplet Extraction with additional structures and external data, and demonstrates that GPT 3.5 and GPT 4 exhibit superior efficacy compared to its contrastive learning approach in few-shot learning scenarios.

faithful: [CITE] augments LoRA by applying a transformation matrix T that rotates, scales, and translates the task-specific parameter matrix, reporting about a 1.0% overall gain across eight GLUE tasks and average DART/WebNLG improvements of 0.95% and 0.56%.
distorted: Building on LoRA, [CITE] proposes a matrix transformation-based reparameterization method that applies rotation, scaling, and translation to task-specific parameter matrices, reporting average performance gains of 0.56% on DART and 0.95% on WebNLG, plus about 1.0% overall across eight GLUE tasks.

faithful: [CITE] presents a modular machine translation toolkit derived from OpenNMT-py and adapted for efficient training across compute clusters, with demonstrated efficiency on NVIDIA A100 and V100 GPU clusters.
distorted: Prior work such as [CITE] argues that modularization is approaching its limits in terms of size and information, presenting MAMMOTH, derived from OpenNMT-py, as a monolithic large language model for massively multilingual machine translation across A100 and V100 GPU clusters.

faithful: [CITE] reassesses LLM-based summary factual inconsistency detection by comparing GPT-3.5 with GPT-4 and filtering documents to key sentences via natural language inference or summary-document semantic similarity.
distorted: Early attempts have shown that traditional models underperform LLMs due to their limited ability to follow instructions and the absence of an effective detection methodology [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces a WebNLG-derived isiXhosa data-to-text benchmark and shows that the proposed Subword Segmental Pointer Generator, which jointly segments words and copies entities, beats existing dedicated models on two agglutinative languages, isiXhosa and Finnish.
distorted: For low-resource agglutinative data-to-text, [CITE] introduces a WebNLG-based isiXhosa dataset and shows that standard pretrained language models outperform fine-tuned machine translation models, emerging as the best method overall.

faithful: [CITE] distills knowledge from a large language model into a smaller personality detection model by generating post analyses from semantic, sentiment, and linguistic perspectives and aligning them with post representations via contrastive learning, reportedly surpassing state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets.
distorted: [CITE] treat personality traits as one-hot classification labels, overlooking semantic information within them, and demonstrate that one-hot classification outperforms state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets.

faithful: ORPO [CITE] integrates preference alignment directly into supervised fine-tuning via a reference-model-free odds ratio objective, and Mistral (7B) trained with it on UltraFeedback alone reaches 12.20% on AlpacaEval 2.0 and 7.32 on MT-Bench, outperforming larger 13B models.
distorted: [CITE] argues that preference-aligned SFT remains imperative and preserves the necessity for an additional preference alignment phase and a reference model, while ORPO adds only a minor penalty for the disfavored generation style from 125M to 7B.

faithful: [CITE] adds a contrastive reward penalty to RLHF by first offline sampling baseline responses for each prompt and then using a baseline-relative reward inside PPO, which the authors report reduces PPO variance and consistently beats strong baselines in GPT and human evaluations.
distorted: [CITE] show the approach involves (1) a contrastive reward calculated using the baseline responses and (2) an offline sampling step to obtain responses to prompts, yet contrastive rewards penalize improvement over baselines, reduce robustness, and existing RLHF consistently outperforms the method.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a hallucination-detection shared task built on 4,000 model outputs—each labeled by five annotators across machine translation, paraphrase generation, and definition modeling—and report that even top-scoring systems handled the most challenging items near-randomly.
distorted: [CITE] present results from the SHROOM shared task on detecting hallucinations, finding that a majority of teams did not outperform the proposed baseline system, and that the top-scoring systems moved beyond a random handling of the more challenging items.

faithful: [CITE] propose Branch-Train-MiX (BTX), which branches a seed LLM into asynchronously trained domain experts, merges their feedforward parameters as Mixture-of-Experts layers while averaging the remaining weights, and achieves the best accuracy-efficiency tradeoff among compared approaches.
distorted: BTX [CITE] omits the MoE-finetuning stage to learn token-level routing, which distinguishes it from the Branch-Train-Merge method it generalizes, and consequently achieves a worse accuracy-efficiency tradeoff than sparse upcycling.

faithful: Arguing that multiple-choice accuracy can diverge from open-ended use, [CITE] evaluates 24 models on 11 benchmarks and introduces RWQ-Elo, a GPT-4-judged two-player ranking built on the RWQ benchmark of 20,772 authentic user inquiries.
distorted: [CITE] introduces an RWQ-Elo rating system, engaging 24 LLMs such as GPT-4, Google-Gemini-Pro and LLaMA-1/-2 in a two-player competitive format, with GPT-3.5 serving as the judge.

faithful: [CITE] condition every transformer layer of an end-to-end ASR model on word- and character-level language IDs through two language-specific multi-head attention parameterizations and a Temporal Loss, reporting no significant WER reduction but promising spoken-language prediction on Gujarati-English code-switched speech.
distorted: [CITE] conditions transformer layers on language ID of words and character in an per layer supervised manner, and shows two methods reduce WER significantly; Temporal Loss helps explainability, while dropping LID helps language prediction, not alignment.

faithful: [CITE] combines a literature review of LLMs as text classifiers with an empirical comparison of several LLMs on hate speech detection, examining which models excel and how their underlying attributes and training shape proficiency in identifying hateful or toxic content.
distorted: [CITE] combines a comprehensive literature review with an empirical analysis to shed light on constraints, not capabilities, as the factors that contribute to LLM proficiency in discerning hateful content.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated zero-shot salary, employer-presence, and commute-duration predictions across 384 U.S. metropolitan regions, finding consistent negative correlations between metropolitan size and LLM performance, with the smallest 10 regions performing over 300% worse than the largest 10.
distorted: [CITE] quantify metropolitan size bias in zero-shot salary, employer presence, and commute duration predictions across 384 United States metropolitan regions, reporting that the largest 10 regions show upwards of 300% worse benchmark performance than the smallest 10.

faithful: [CITE] introduces ConRAP, a retrieval-augmented prompting framework that generates document-level clarification questions for contracts, reporting on CUAD contracts with ChatGPT an ambiguity-detection F2 of 0.87 and human judgments that 70% of questions were useful.
distorted: ConRAP [CITE] is a retrieval-augmented prompting framework that generates clarification questions for contracts, and on the CUAD dataset ConRAP with ChatGPT detects ambiguities with an F2 score of 0.70, while 87% of the generated questions are deemed useful by human evaluators.

faithful: For FEVER fact verification, [CITE] introduces two task-specific loss objectives that outperform standard cross-entropy because cross-entropy ignores heterogeneity among verdict classes, and reports further gains when combined with simple class weighting to counter training-data imbalance.
distorted: Experimental results in [CITE] confirm that the standard cross-entropy and simple class weighting outperform two task-specific objectives tailored to FEVER verdict predictors in the shared task.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned wav2vec 2.0 XLS-R to transcribe Korean children's speech as pronounced rather than as canonical words, using recordings from 137 children producing 73 clinically selected words and reporting about 90% agreement with human annotations.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tuned the wav2vec 2.0 XLS-R model on speech from 137 children pronouncing 73 Korean words, matching human annotations with about 90% accuracy while demonstrating that the model already recognizes unclear pronunciation without requiring further improvement.

faithful: For interlinear glossing, [CITE] adds translation embeddings encoded by BERT or T5 and a character-level decoder to a hard-attentional model, reporting a 3.97-point average gain over prior SIGMORPHON 2023 systems and 9.78 points over the plain baseline with 100 training sentences.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that in a simulated ultra low-resource setting trained on as few as 100 sentences, their system achieves an average 3.97%-point improvement over the plain hard-attentional baseline, and 9.78%-points over the previous state of the art.

faithful: [CITE] provides 62K question-answering pairs over 23K molecules, where every item pairs a manual question with one positive and three negative options semantically consistent with an authoritative molecular description.
distorted: To benchmark factual accuracy in molecular comprehension, [CITE] introduces a QA dataset of 23K QA pairs spanning 62K molecules, each pairing a manual question with three positive options and one negative option drawn from an authoritative molecular corpus.

faithful: [CITE] reports that, starting from a 427-billion-word Common Crawl corpus, agreement of independent language identifiers, hash-based deduplication, and location-specific outlier detection each improve sub-corpus validity, though gains are uneven across languages and populations.
distorted: [CITE] find that the validity of sub-corpora representing specific language-country pairs like New Zealand English decreases with each stage of cleaning, with the change evenly distributed across languages and populations.

faithful: [CITE] experimentally examines BERT for sentiment analysis and reports that the model performs robustly, with notable improvements after fine-tuning, while discussing application effects and optimization strategies.
