distorted: [CITE] concludes that optimization strategies exhibit robust performance in sentiment analysis tasks, with notable enhancements post fine-tuning in future research and practical implementations.

faithful: [CITE] builds a semester-long EFL writing dataset from 212 college students who dialogued with ChatGPT to revise essays, annotating student utterances with 13 intention labels and reporting baselines for intent detection and satisfaction estimation.
distorted: [CITE] present a semester-long EFL writing experiment with 13 college students and annotate students' utterances with 212 intention labels for intent detection and satisfaction estimation.

faithful: [CITE] proposes UltraFuser, which fuses three specialists for language, code, and mathematics via token-level gating, uses two-stage balanced-sampling training, and builds UltraChat 2 with roughly 300,000 instructions to achieve simultaneous three-domain mastery.
distorted: [CITE] shows extensive training with relevant corpora is typically accompanied by high performance in other domains: the fused model could simultaneously achieve mastery of three crucial domains across language, code, mathematics.

faithful: [CITE] releases two open model sizes, 2 billion and 7 billion parameters, with pretrained and fine-tuned checkpoints, and reports outperforming similarly sized open models on 11 of 18 text-based tasks.
distorted: Gemma [CITE], a family of lightweight open models built from Gemini research and technology, is outperformed by similarly sized open models on 11 out of 18 text-based tasks, despite releasing both pretrained and fine-tuned checkpoints.

faithful: [CITE] introduces BingJian, an anonymous crowd-sourcing evaluation platform where users competitively rank large language models, combining centralized assessment with an open gateway for user-submitted questions and personalized interaction scenarios that account for evaluator and model characteristics.
distorted: In [CITE], BingJian is an anonymous crowd-sourcing evaluation platform overlooking subjective questions, with question banks concentrated within evaluation platforms, neglecting individual characteristics of evaluators and models through an open evaluation gateway.

faithful: [CITE] meta-evaluate sentence-level automatic metrics on machine-translated chats, finding that reference-free metrics underperform reference-based ones particularly in out-of-English settings, and propose Context-MQM, an LLM-based metric that leverages bilingual conversational context.
distorted: For machine-translated chats, [CITE] finds that reference-based metrics lag behind reference-free ones, especially when evaluating translation quality in out-of-English settings.

faithful: [CITE] reframes multi-trait essay scoring as autoregressive score generation with pre-trained T5, so one decoder predicts several trait scores while conditioning each later trait on earlier scores, reporting over 5% average gains across prompts and traits.
distorted: Studies in multi-trait AES [CITE] explore BERT by replicating BERT-based models for each trait, and experimental results proved prior regression or classification methods, showing over 5% average improvements in both prompts and traits.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a semi-automated pipeline in which open-source LLMs formulate competency questions, derive an ontology (TBox) from them, and build a knowledge graph of deep learning methodologies from scholarly publications, with a dedicated judge LLM rating the extracted concepts and RAG-generated answers against ground truth.
distorted: [CITE] recommend an automatic pipeline in which a judge LLM ensures data quality, including accuracy and completeness, so that KGs can be constructed from scholarly publications with minimal to no involvement of human experts and no human-in-the-loop evaluation.

faithful: For zero-shot prediction of interactions involving previously unseen drugs, [CITE] propose TextDDI, which couples a language-model-based DDI predictor with a reinforcement-learning-based information selector that picks concise, semantically relevant descriptions drawn from DrugBank and PubChem.
distorted: For zero-shot DDI prediction on new drugs, [CITE] proposes TextDDI, which couples a reinforcement learning-based DDI predictor with a language model-based information selector to select concise and pertinent text from DrugBank and PubChem.

faithful: [CITE] augment LLM prompts with patient records combined with authoritative medical textbooks and curated web resources, and experiments on the MTSamples dataset evaluated with Ragas and TruLens showed contextually appropriate responses, with SME raters reaching moderate inter-rater agreement.
distorted: Prior work has validated retrieval-augmented medical response generation on the Ragas dataset, using MTSamples and TruLens as metrics for answer similarity and answer correctness, with SMEs reporting moderate inter-rater agreement on relevance and correctness [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] reports that chain-of-thought prompting enables Llama 2, without fine-tuning, to generate History of Present Illness narratives evaluated against MIMIC-IV with ROUGE scores comparable to fine-tuned models trained on sensitive patient data.
distorted: Using MIMIC-IV data, [CITE] shows that chain-of-thought prompting allows the few-shot Llama 2 model to generate History of Present Illness narratives achieving Rouge results on par with fine-tuned models, surpassing the zero-shot approach.

faithful: [CITE] tackle out-of-distribution partial-token prompts in generative models by backtracking to the last complete tokens and constraining generation to align with the prompt, reporting marked gains on tricky cases like space-prefix and partial indentation with only minor added inference time.
distorted: [CITE] introduced token alignment, which backtracks to the last complete tokens so the model's generation aligns with the prompt, but showed that this technique fails to maintain performance in regular non-subword cases and incurs a marked time increase across many partial token scenarios.

faithful: [CITE] compared four large web-crawled corpora (CC100, MaCoCu, mC4, and OSCAR) across eleven lower-resourced European languages, finding that although human raters judged MaCoCu and OSCAR highest in quality, models trained on CC100 achieved the best downstream-task scores.
distorted: [CITE] compare CC100, MaCoCu, mC4 and OSCAR across eleven lower-resourced European languages and find that CC100 and mC4 obtain the best results in human evaluation of quality; however, OSCAR achieves the highest scores on downstream tasks.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Bootstrapped Preference Optimization, which builds preference pairs by pairing annotated responses with model-bootstrapped negatives elicited via distorted images or an LLM injecting common erroneous elements, reducing pretraining-statistics bias and improving visual grounding across benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] proposes Bootstrapped Preference Optimization, using distorted image inputs and leveraging text-based LLM to inject erroneous but common elements, pairing negative responses with original annotated responses to suppress visual input, enabling enhanced grounding in pretraining statistics across multiple benchmarks.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that training a Correspondence Auto-Encoder on HuBERT representations produces the best word-discrimination acoustic word embeddings across Polish, Portuguese, Spanish, French, and English, despite HuBERT being pre-trained exclusively on English.
distorted: [CITE] show that MFCC-based CAE models outperform HuBERT-based CAE for word discrimination in all five languages, since HuBERT is pre-trained on English only, and that HuBERT-based CAE does not work well in cross-lingual settings.

faithful: [CITE] propose tracking how the statistical distribution of Transformer parameters evolves over training, arguing that bifurcation effects in these distributions can reveal model quality, reduce training and evaluation costs, and empirically explain why weight sparsification is effective.
distorted: [CITE] tracks how the distribution of parameters evolves during training and empirically shows that weights sparsification reduces model quality, thereby increasing training costs and evaluation efforts for the Transformer architecture in NLP.

faithful: Using large language models over the CANDOR corpus of English conversation, [CITE] estimates unstructured dialogue carries about 13 bits per second and shows that information rate declines before listener backchannels such as yeah or uh-huh, then rebounds afterward.
distorted: For English-language conversation in the CANDOR corpus, [CITE] find that the lead-up to a backchannel rebounds to previous rates while speech downstream is associated with declining information rate and approximately 13 bits/second of novelty.

faithful: For retrieval augmented generation on controversial topics, [CITE] found that LLM-based classifiers trained solely on synthetic errors detect hallucinations and coverage errors with ROC AUC scores of 95.3% and 90.5% respectively on unambiguous cases.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate three methods to detect hallucination and coverage errors: word-overlap and salience achieve high detection performance on unambiguous error cases, with ROC AUC scores of 95.3% for hallucination and 90.5% for coverage, while LLM-based classifiers yield 84.0% and 85.2%.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an automated evaluation framework for chatbot text style transfer whose reference-free appropriateness metric, accounting for coherence and fluency, correlates more strongly with human judgments, and reports style evaluations of LLaMA, Alpaca, and Vicuna.
distorted: For chat-style text style transfer, [CITE] introduces the LMStyle Benchmark, demonstrating that conventional style strength metrics have a higher correlation with human judgments in terms of appropriateness than the new evaluation methods it proposes.

faithful: Building on task arithmetic, [CITE] applies singular value decomposition to extract principal components from pre-trained models, projects task vectors onto them to isolate undesired knowledge for negation, and shows improved debiasing, detoxification, and memorization unlearning over existing task arithmetic baselines.
distorted: Ethos [CITE] performs negating using the task vector with general beneficial knowledge only, thereby minimizing general model utility compared to current task arithmetic methods on debiasing, detoxification, and memorization unlearning.

faithful: [CITE] trains language models by combining the standard next-token prediction loss over a parametric token embedding space with a next-sequence prediction loss over a nonparametric sequence embedding space built by a separate model, and shows this co-supervision consistently outperforms either objective alone.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that models trained via each supervision independently consistently surpass a model trained via both supervisions, and that the stability of the nonparametric sequence embedding space effectively enhances the robustness of the parametric token space established during pretraining.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a chart-specific instruction-following corpus of 191K instructions generated with 71K charts, presents both an end-to-end vision-encoder/LLM and a two-step table-extraction pipeline, and reports state-of-the-art results on four downstream tasks.
distorted: In prior work, [CITE] reports that the pipeline model achieves state-of-the-art results on four downstream tasks by connecting a vision encoder for chart understanding with a LLM, while the end-to-end model extracts chart data tables in a two-step approach.

faithful: [CITE] present HEAL, a continually pretrained 13B LLaMA2 model built for medical conversations that achieves 78.4% accuracy on PubMedQA, outperforming GPT-4 and PMC-LLaMA, while matching GPT-4 in automated medical note generation.
distorted: In automated scribing, [CITE] reports that GPT-4 and PMC-LLaMA outperform HEAL on PubMedQA with 78.4% accuracy, while Med-PaLM 2 and human scribes exceed HEAL in correctness, completeness, and identifying more correct medical concepts.

faithful: On a newly curated developing-country financial text corpus, [CITE] frames joint entity and relation extraction as text-to-text with T5, reporting 92.44% accuracy, 68.25% precision and 54.20% recall, versus a SpaCy sequential pipeline’s 6.06% precision and 5.57% recall.
distorted: [CITE] develop and evaluate two NLP techniques for information extraction on financial text data on developing countries, obtaining an accuracy of 92.44% on the sequential task with SpaCy and a custom Dependency Parser relation extraction model, and 84.72% with the T5 text-to-text model.

faithful: Using arXiv labels as ground truth, [CITE] reports that prompt-engineered GPT chatbots assign AI-publication labels with 94% accuracy, while fine-tuned SPECTER reaches 96%, only two percentage points higher.
distorted: Prior work treats arXiv as ground-truth and reports that fine-tuned SPECTER assigns AI labels with 94% accuracy, whereas prompt engineering for GPT chatbot models reaches 96% accuracy, only 2% higher than SPECTER [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] learns a selection variable for every rank-1 matrix in each LoRA update through meta learning and chooses layer ranks by thresholding those variables, with experiments spanning natural language understanding, generation, and sequence labeling.
distorted: [CITE] addresses LoRA's high computation costs by assigning a uniform rank across all layers and using an exhaustive search over selection variables, discarding meta learning, which leads to suboptimal finetuning performance on natural language understanding, generation, and sequence labeling.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated GPT models on factual queries about notable persons across recall, hallucination, and declination dimensions, finding gender disparities in GPT-3.5 responses that persisted in GPT-4 despite overall improvements, particularly in cases where the model declined to answer.
distorted: [CITE] evaluates gender-based biases in LLMs' responses to factual inquiries across recall, hallucinations and declinations, finding discernible gender disparities in GPT-4, while advancements in GPT-3.5 have fully eradicated these disparities, notably in instances where responses are declined.

faithful: [CITE] present CONAN-EUS, a parallel Basque–Spanish corpus of hate-speech counter narratives created via machine translation plus professional post-editing, and demonstrate that fine-tuning mT5 on post-edited data surpasses training on silver machine-translated data alone.
distorted: [CITE] show that, for CONAN-EUS, fine-tuning mT5 on machine translated data outperforms model transfer for Spanish but not for Basque, while silver MT data greatly benefits generation over post-edited data.

faithful: Through extensive experiments across five distinct language tasks, [CITE] found that models fine-tuned on generation versus classification tasks generalize differently to unseen domains and tasks, and that incorporating in-context learning during fine-tuning on generation tasks enhances generalization ability.
distorted: [CITE] conduct extensive experiments across five distinct language tasks and find that integrating the in-context learning strategy during fine-tuning on classification tasks can enhance the model's generalization ability, whereas fine-tuning on generation tasks yields no such benefit.

faithful: [CITE] argues that because large language models are trained on stochastic word prediction, they operate over word distributions rather than verified facts, leaving their legal knowledge incomplete, largely incorrect, and prone to plausible but false hallucinations.
distorted: Relying on recent findings in technical and legal scholarship, [CITE] argues that LLMs understand text, distinguish fact from fiction, and perform complex reasoning tasks, so lawyers need not beware of relying on text generated by LLMs in legal practice.

faithful: [CITE] introduced TCM-QA, a Traditional Chinese Medicine question dataset spanning single-choice, multiple-choice, and true-or-false formats, finding that ChatGPT reached its highest precision of 0.688 on true-or-false questions but only 0.241 on multiple-choice ones.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] introduces TCM-QA and reports that ChatGPT achieves its highest precision of 0.241 on multiple-choice questions, while true or false questions score lowest at 0.688, and English prompts outperform Chinese prompts.

faithful: [CITE] pairs a two-stage production-prompt construction method with a cost-effective multi-dimensional quality assessment framework, reporting on real-estate service-provider-customer dialogues that higher data quality correlates with better model performance and that domain-only fine-tuning preserves generalization.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that while their two-stage prompt construction and multi-dimensional quality assessment framework improve domain-specific proficiency on real estate service provider and customer interactions, fine-tuning general LLMs with exclusively domain-specific data necessarily compromises their overall generalization abilities.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Komodo-7B-Instruct, a 7-billion-parameter model spanning Indonesian, English, and 11 regional Indonesian languages, and reports state-of-the-art results that surpass GPT-3.5, Aya-101, Llama-2-Chat-13B, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1, and Gemma-7B-it.
distorted: [CITE] highlights OpenAI's GPT-3.5, Cohere's Aya-101, Llama-2-Chat-13B, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1, and Gemma-7B-it outperforming Komodo-7B-Instruct in overall assessments across Indonesian, English, and 11 regional languages.

faithful: [CITE] introduces In-Context Calibration, a demonstration-aware calibration method, and reports substantial improvements in both the standard-label setting and a task-learning setting with semantically unrelated label tokens across OPT, GPT, and Llama2.
distorted: [CITE] introduces In-Context Calibration and demonstrates substantial improvements in the Original ICL Task using the standard label space, but not in the Task Learning setting, where the label space is replaced with semantically unrelated tokens.

faithful: [CITE] introduces DAFair, which fine-tunes language models with a regularization term grounded in predefined prototypical demographic texts instead of demographic labels, reporting gains over label-free baselines across two tasks and two models and over common debiasing methods with limited annotated data.
distorted: [CITE] presents DAFair as relying on explicit demographic labels for each data sample and, with limited demographic-annotated data, as outperformed by common debiasing approaches across two tasks and two models.

faithful: [CITE] propose a selective distillation framework that corrects only the student model's translation errors and has LLM teachers synthesize diverse contexts with anticipated mistakes, showing that finetuning on roughly 10% of examples matches conventional knowledge distillation on MT benchmarks.
distorted: MT-Patcher [CITE] transfers knowledge from LLMs to existing MT models by distilling the whole translation from the teacher, and demonstrates that traditional knowledge distillation methods finetuned on about 10% examples achieve comparable results on general MT benchmarks.

faithful: Quiet-STaR [CITE] generalizes the STaR approach by training language models to generate rationales at every token via tokenwise parallel sampling, yielding zero-shot gains on GSM8K from 5.9% to 10.9% and on CommonsenseQA from 36.3% to 47.2% without task-specific fine-tuning.
distorted: [CITE] generalizes STaR by having language models generate rationales at each token to explain future text, reporting that continued pretraining on internet text improves zero-shot GSM8K from 36.3% to 47.2% and CommonsenseQA from 5.9% to 10.9%, gains that require fine-tuning on these tasks.

faithful: Highlighting the threat of AI-generated medical misinformation, [CITE] demonstrated that ChatGPT-4 could fabricate a convincing yet entirely fictional SARS-CoV-2 'Omega variant' case study, complete with 31 unique S-gene mutations including N501Y, E484K, L452R, and P681H.
distorted: [CITE] examines a genuine novel SARS-CoV-2 variant, dubbed the Omega variant, showcasing 31 unique mutations in the S gene region, identified in a fully vaccinated, previously infected 35-year-old male presenting with severe COVID-19 symptoms.

faithful: [CITE] categorizes LLM deception into four types—strategic deception, imitation, sycophancy, and unfaithful reasoning—and links them to social risks, governance, and digital education.
distorted: [CITE] reviews the deceptive behaviours of Large Language Models (LLMs), categorising them into four types — Strategic deception, Imitation, Sycophancy, and digital education — while emphasising the multidimensional biases that underlie these deceptive behaviours.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CRED, a dataset of paired White House tweets labeled by comparative retweet counts, and shows that a fine-tuned FLANG-RoBERTa cross-encoder using tweet text plus Claude-generated responses gives the best crowd-reaction predictions.
distorted: [CITE] introduce CRED, a dataset of pairs of tweets from The White House with comparative measures of retweet count, and reveal that a fine-tuned FLANG-RoBERTa model utilizing a cross-encoder architecture with responses generated by ChatGPT performs optimally.

faithful: [CITE] proposes an architecture that lets application developers align language models to context-specific values, norms, and regulations through three cooperating components—Framers, Instructors, and Auditors—illustrated by aligning an internal enterprise chatbot to business conduct guidelines.
distorted: [CITE] empowers model providers, rather than application developers, to align large language models by adding behaviors that are common and universally understood across use cases, through three components—Framers, Instructors, and Auditors—illustrated with an internal-facing enterprise chatbot.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a mental-health conversation evaluation framework with metrics grounded in psychotherapy conversation analysis, finding that GPT-4 Turbo aligned significantly more closely with verified therapists than other tested GPT and Llama models, especially on Parenting and Relationships topics.
distorted: [CITE] applies a novel framework to several popular frontier LLMs through a verified mental health dataset and shows that other selected LLMs perform significantly more similarly to verified therapists than GPT4 Turbo across Parenting and Relationships.

faithful: On the cross-domain Spider benchmark, [CITE] proposes a multi-task text-to-SQL framework combining a schema-linking discriminator with an operator-centric triple extractor over six predefined table-column relation types, surpassing baselines particularly on extremely hard queries.
distorted: On Spider, [CITE] indicates that baselines are more effective than MTSQL, especially in extremely hard scenarios, and that the schema linking discriminator, operator-centric triple extractor, and grammar constraints are not good for alignment quality.

faithful: [CITE] applied a deep-neural-network NLP pipeline to 108,280 clinical notes from 1,635 ICI-treated patients at Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center, reporting per-note AUC 0.89 and patient-level F1 of at least 0.87 for five of seven IrAEs.
distorted: At Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center, [CITE] reported corticosteroid treatment ranging from 17.3% for myocarditis to 57.4% for thyroiditis, with an AUC of 0.89 for five of seven IrAEs.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a weakly labelled dataset of code-mixed Hinglish YouTube comments annotated as misogynistic or non-misogynistic, and characterize it through pre-processing and exploratory analyses such as sentiment scores and word clouds to support misogyny detection in under-resourced languages.
distorted: Addressing the lack of studies that tackle misogyny detection in under-resourced languages, [CITE] present a novel dataset of Twitter (X) comments in mix-code Hinglish and show that sentiment scores and word clouds provide a great advantage in automatic filtering of misogynistic content.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a general KBQA pretraining framework whose three modules—knowledge injection via KG-centered corpus generation, adapter-based knowledge adaptation that preserves natural language understanding, and curriculum reasoning over three corpora of increasing difficulty—yield higher performance on four real-world datasets.
distorted: KICP [CITE] constructs three corpora with increasing difficulties of reasoning and trains the LM from hard to easy, while knowledge adaptation reduces the LM’s original natural language understanding ability to reduce the negative impacts.

faithful: [CITE] reviews unsupervised induction of constituency and dependency trees from language models and reports six StructFormer experiments, including moving the parser network within the encoder, evaluating subword-based induced trees, and benchmarking through the BabyLM challenge at CoNLL 2023.
distorted: In its review of syntactic frameworks, [CITE] explains that constituency assigns relations between words, whereas dependency represents sentences as nested groups of phrases.

faithful: [CITE] reviews how deep learning applies to three core NLP tasks—text representation, word order modeling, and knowledge representation—and empirically demonstrates that interactive integration training combined with TextCNN improves text classification performance.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates the effectiveness of classical machine learning algorithms with manual annotation, unlike interactive integration training in conjunction with TextCNN, on text classification tasks, particularly adversarial text generation and semantic parsing.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates fine-tuning and prompt tuning on the Human Value Detection 2023 task, tests whether pre-training knowledge alone is sufficient, and reports preliminary attempts with RLHF-aligned large language models.
distorted: [CITE] uses Human Value Detection 2023 to validate that prompt tuning effectively solves the problem based on knowledge acquired during the pre-training stage, with fine-tuning and large language models aligned with RLHF as preliminary attempts.

faithful: [CITE] constructs a semantic mention graph capturing co-existence, co-reference and co-type relations within and across documents and prompts, and reports new state-of-the-art document-level event argument extraction results on RAMS and WikiEvents.

For predicting 30-day hospital readmission from discharge summaries in the MIMIC-III dataset, [CITE] paired Bio-Discharge Summary BERT embeddings with PCA-based feature extraction and a multilayer perceptron, surpassing state-of-the-art baselines with 94% recall and 75% AUC.
distorted: [CITE] predicted 30-day hospital readmission from MIMIC-III discharge report texts by combining the Bio-Discharge Summary Bert (BDSS) model with a multilayer perceptron (MLP), reporting that this approach outperformed state-of-the-art methods with a recall of 75% and an area under the curve (AUC) of 94%.

faithful: Fine-tuning the 2.7B-parameter Phi-2 on Radiopaedia educational text and chest X-ray report instructions yielded radiology models that matched or surpassed Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and GPT-4 while giving concise, precise answers [CITE].
distorted: [CITE] reports that larger models such as Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and GPT-4 outperform Rad-Phi2 Base and Rad-Phi2 for radiology knowledge queries and chest X-ray report tasks.

faithful: [CITE] proves that transformers can simulate weighted finite automata, which subsume deterministic finite automata, and weighted tree automata, giving upper bounds on model size in terms of automaton states and showing gradient-based training learns these compact solutions on synthetic tasks.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] proves that transformers do not simulate weighted finite automata (WFAs), a class of models subsumed by DFAs, and shows empirically that standard gradient-based training does not learn compact solutions.

faithful: [CITE] presented a browser extension that links large language models to the Overleaf editor, complemented by PromptGenius, a website for finding and sharing up-to-date prompts, and an agent command system for building customizable assistants, reportedly serving thousands of researchers.
distorted: OverleafCopilot [CITE] is a website where researchers can easily find and share high-quality prompts, while PromptGenius, its browser extension on the Chrome Extension Store, seamlessly integrates LLMs and Overleaf and now serves thousands of researchers.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a five-task evaluation protocol for LLM-based user simulators in conversational recommendation—spanning item selection, binary and open-ended preference expression, recommendation requests, and feedback—and shows these tasks expose deviations from human behavior that model selection and prompting strategies can help reduce.
distorted: [CITE] introduce a protocol of five tasks demonstrating that language models accurately emulate human behavior in conversational recommendation, with baseline simulators reducing deviations through model selection and prompting strategies.

faithful: Conducting a systematic literature review with a selection cut-off date of January 11, 2024, [CITE] synthesizes research on the human factors that enable users to detect hallucinations and omissions in LLM outputs, particularly in high-stakes domains such as medicine and legal compliance.
distorted: [CITE] systematically reviews the literature up to November 2022 and concludes that LLMs such as ChatGPT, trained on extensive internet data, are no longer susceptible to hallucinations and omissions, making human error detection unnecessary in legal compliance and medicine.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a retrieval-augmented LLM fake-news detector that uses multi-round web retrieval to gather sufficient relevant evidence, and reports superior claim-verification performance over existing methods across three real-world datasets while producing human-readable explanations.
distorted: [CITE] reports that traditional methods source information from static repositories like Wikipedia to ensure sufficient, relevant evidence and superiority across three real-world datasets, while multi-round retrieval is limited by outdated or incomplete data.

faithful: By supplying ground-truth knowledge and scoring its effective use, [CITE] finds that declarative knowledge helps more than procedural knowledge on most tasks, whereas procedural knowledge pays off only in reasoning tasks with simple logic.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] reports that, across widely-used datasets and models, benefits from procedural knowledge are greater than those from declarative knowledge in most tasks, while declarative knowledge profits are larger only in reasoning tasks with simple logic.

faithful: [CITE] survey how NLP and deep learning techniques assess emotions in healthcare texts drawn from clinical narratives, patient medication feedback, and online health discussions, reporting gains in sentiment-classification precision and AI models with prognostic capabilities for neurodegenerative diseases.
distorted: [CITE] scrutinize numerous research studies and demonstrate that the challenges of ensuring the ethical application of AI, safeguarding patient confidentiality, and addressing potential biases in algorithmic procedures no longer persist in healthcare texts.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a new benchmark for studying prompt injection attacks on LLM-based machine translation and find that, across multiple language pairs with English-written injected prompts, larger models can under certain conditions become more susceptible to successful attacks, an instance of inverse scaling.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] shows that, across multiple language pairs with injected prompts written in English, larger models become less susceptible to successful prompt injection attacks, with attack success rates falling as model size grows.

faithful: For Portuguese-language modeling, [CITE] introduced a family of LLMs whose medium variant matched or surpassed GPT-4 on 23 of 64 Brazilian academic and professional exams while being offered at a price per token ten times cheaper.
distorted: Related work reports that Sabiá-2 Medium matches or surpasses GPT-4 in 58 out of 64 exams, outperforms GPT-3.5 in 23 out of 64 exams, and is 10 times cheaper than GPT-3.5 [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] conditions language identification on country-level geography by building 16 region-specific models that each also include 31 international lingua francas, raising F-score by 1.7 points in Southeast Asia and 10.4 in North Africa while covering 916 languages at 50 characters.
distorted: [CITE] formulates 16 region-specific models whose upstream evaluation on traditional language identification testing data improves f-score from 10.4 points in Southeast Asia to 1.7 points in North Africa.

faithful: [CITE] finds that gradient-based prompts such as AutoPrompt and OptiPrompt exhibit significantly stronger label bias than other prompts, and proposes an inference-time debiasing method that subtracts a prompt-only biased representation, yielding up to 10% absolute gains in prompt retrieval performance.
distorted: [CITE] show that gradient-based prompts like AutoPrompt and OptiPrompt display significantly lower levels of prompt bias, and that their representation-based approach corrects overfitted performance on LAMA at the cost of a 10% absolute drop in prompt retrieval capability.

faithful: [CITE] surveys NLP methods that use electronic health records to flag familial disease risks, noting that rule-based systems remain heavily investigated and actively used for family-history extraction while recent work increasingly builds neural models on large-scale pre-trained language models.
distorted: [CITE] survey natural language processing techniques that utilise electronic health records to identify risks of familial diseases, highlighting data collection, task formulation and downstream applications as areas where NLP has successfully been utilised, with rule-based methods needing more research.

faithful: [CITE] combines a GCN over intra-utterance syntactic dependencies with dual graph attention networks for inter-utterance semantic interaction, reporting significant gains over state-of-the-art baselines on two standard DiaASQ datasets.
distorted: For DiaASQ, [CITE] proposes Triple GNNs, which employs a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) to construct interactions between utterances and Dual Graph Attention Networks (DualGATs) to model the syntactic dependencies within individual utterances.

faithful: [CITE] proposes CoARL, which combines sequential multi-instruction tuning on the intents, reactions, and harms of hateful statements with low-rank adapters and reinforcement learning, gaining an average of 3 points in intent-conformity and 4 points in argument-quality over existing benchmarks.
distorted: CoARL [CITE] applies multi-task instruction tuning with RLAIF for intent-conditioned counterspeech generation, but trails existing benchmarks and prominent LLMs like ChatGPT by an average of 3 points in intent-conformity and 4 points in argument-quality metrics.

faithful: For extracting functionality from Git README files, [CITE] releases the human-annotated FuncRead dataset and reports that a fine-tuned 7B CodeLlama model improves F1 by 70% over ChatGPT and 20% over Bard.
distorted: Prior work reports that popular black-box and white-box LLMs such as ChatGPT and Bard beat small fine-tuned models on FuncRead, with 70% and 20% F1 gain against the best fine-tuned 7 Billion CodeLlama model [CITE].

faithful: For aspect-category sentiment analysis, [CITE] models coherence across the entire review to identify implicit aspects and applies hierarchical disentanglement to separate entangled category and sentiment features, reporting state-of-the-art results with publicly released code.
distorted: [CITE] address aspect-category sentiment analysis with an enhanced coherence-aware network that mainly utilizes intrasentential features, arguing that coherence modeling across the whole review makes the model fail to discriminately preserve all sentiment characteristics.

faithful: For Persian social-network topic detection, [CITE] re-implements and adapts ten frequent-pattern, clustering, and hybrid methods, processing about 1.4 billion tokens and finding hybrid approaches best for human-readable keyword-topics.
distorted: For topic detection in Persian social network texts, [CITE] indicates the frequent pattern category is better for keyword-topics easily understandable by humans, and the hybrid category is more suitable to cluster posts for further analysis.

faithful: [CITE] applied text mining and social network analysis to more than 167,000 online news articles to quantify sub-national attributes affecting FDI ownership in African companies, finding that regional structural and institutional characteristics play an important role in determining foreign ownership.
distorted: [CITE] proposes a methodology based on qualitative data analysis of more than 167,000 World Bank Enterprise Surveys, finding that regional structural and institutional characteristics play no important role in determining foreign ownership in African companies.

faithful: [CITE] statistically defines explanation signal, noise, and signal-to-noise ratio, finding in a typical word-level univariate first-order case study that simple feature-based models carry more signal and less noise than transformers.
distorted: In a typical case study where word-level univariate explanations are analyzed with first-order statistical tools, [CITE] highlights that transformer ones carry more signal and less noise than simple feature-based models, improving these results and their plausibility for readers.

faithful: [CITE] introduced Pre-CoFactv3, combining question answering and text classification with in-context learning, fine-tuned LLMs, and FakeNet, and reported winning AAAI-24 Factify 3.0 with accuracy 103% above baseline and 70% ahead of the runner-up.
distorted: [CITE] present Pre-CoFactv3, a framework of Question Answering and Text Classification components leveraging In-Context Learning and FakeNet, reporting that Trifecta secured first place in the AAAI-24 Factify 3.0 Workshop, surpassing the second competitor by 103% while maintaining a 70% lead over the baseline.

faithful: Addressing the gap in within-language coverage of Universal Dependencies, [CITE] introduces the first manually annotated multi-dialect Bavarian treebank, comprising 15k tokens across five genres and dialects spanning three countries, with baseline parsing and POS tagging scores falling below those for German.
distorted: For Bavarian, [CITE] introduce MaiBaam, a multi-dialect UD treebank of 15k tokens spanning three countries, and show that baseline parsing and POS tagging results obtained on German are lower than those on Bavarian, varying substantially between graph-based parsers.

faithful: [CITE] explore pre-trained language models for candidate distractor generation in cloze tests, reporting that their best model raises the state-of-the-art NDCG@10 from 14.94 to 34.17 and releasing code and a dataset.
distorted: For automatic cloze distractor generation, [CITE] explores the employment of pre-trained language models for candidate distractor generation, and their best performing model advances the state-of-the-art result from 34.17 to 14.94 (NDCG@10 score).

faithful: In a French noun-learning study, an LSTM and a decoder-only transformer generalized a novel noun's gender from one or two examples to unseen agreement contexts while updates were restricted to embedding layers, though both models and native French speakers showed a masculine bias [CITE].
distorted: [CITE] find that both language models generalise novel noun gender from two to one learning examples, and that native French speakers are excellent one-shot learners with a masculine gender bias.

faithful: [CITE] distills LLM summarization into a compact local model by refining aspect-triple rationales with dual scoring and curriculum training, reporting gains over baselines of 4.5%, 8.5%, and 7.4% on CNN/DailyMail, XSum, and ClinicalTrial.
distorted: For local summarization, [CITE] reports that a compact model trained with aspect-triple rationales and curriculum learning outperforms baselines on CNN/DailyMail, XSum, and ClinicalTrial by 8.5%, 7.4%, and 4.5%, respectively.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a multilingual multimodal exam benchmark comprising 20,932 multiple-choice questions spanning 20 school disciplines in 11 languages from 7 language families, and shows that even advanced vision-language models such as GPT-4V and Gemini struggle on it.
distorted: Unlike existing benchmarks, [CITE] finds the dataset difficult for GPT-4V but not Gemini, whose advanced perception solves 20,932 multiple-choice questions across 20 school disciplines and 11 languages.

faithful: [CITE] identify low-dimensional subspaces that monotonically encode numeric properties such as birth years, showing that patching activations along a "birthyear" direction progressively shifts a model's stated birth year for Karl Popper from 1929 to 1957 to 1968.

[CITE] built an end-to-end retrieval-augmented pipeline for private, time-sensitive domain queries, fine-tuning LLMs on CMU-derived data labeled by a teacher model, and reported more accurate answers while cautioning that small, skewed fine-tuning sets limit gains.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that fine-tuning LLMs with small-scale and skewed datasets improves factual accuracy on domain-specific and time-sensitive queries, while the RAG pipeline revealed limitations in generating accurate answers for private knowledge-bases.

faithful: [CITE] emulates neurodegeneration in LLaMA 2 by ablating synapses or neurons or injecting Gaussian noise during or after training, showing that IQ-test performance declines progressively, with mathematical abilities deteriorating before linguistic ones.
distorted: [CITE] shows that LLaMA 2 first loses linguistic abilities and then mathematical abilities, ultimately losing abstract thinking and responding to prompts incoherently.

faithful: [CITE] presents a neurosymbolic agent for text-based games that couples a neural exploration module with a symbolic exploitation module, learning generalized symbolic policies that outperform baseline agents on the TW-Cooking and Text-World Commonsense benchmarks.
distorted: For text-based games, [CITE] introduces EXPLORER, a neurosymbolic agent that relies on a symbolic module for exploration and a neural module for exploitation, though like purely deep-RL-based approaches it fails to showcase the same performance on unseen objects.

faithful: [CITE] bridges natural language processing with disciplines such as political science and history to probe gender bias in both natural language and language models, extending this line of research to multilingual and multicultural contexts.
distorted: [CITE] probes gender bias in natural language and language models, finding that ignoring online abuse encourages women's engagement and visibility within public spheres, thereby reducing gender inequality in multilingual contexts.

faithful: [CITE] combines word- and sentence-level embeddings in a Bi-LSTM and GCN graph for Korean conversations, reporting 74.62% emotion and 75.30% causality scores when node and edge characteristics are modeled, and 71.35% on IEMOCAP.
distorted: For emotion-causality recognition in Korean conversation, [CITE] integrates Bi-LSTM and GCN models in a multi-task learning graph structure, reporting 74.62% on the IEMOCAP English dataset and 71.35% on the Korean Wellness dataset when node and edge characteristics are incorporated.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned KcBERT on Korean comments and KOLD data and, measuring ethnic, gender, and racial bias with LPBS and CBS metrics through template-based masked language modeling, found reduced ethnic bias but significant changes in gender and racial biases relative to the base model.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tuned KcBERT on KOLD data and, evaluating bias with LPBS and CBS metrics through template-based Masked Language Modeling, found that the fine-tuned model reduces gender and racial biases while showing significant changes in ethnic bias compared to KcBERT.

faithful: [CITE] introduced CaiTI, an LLM-based conversational therapist that uses reinforcement learning to personalize dialogue flow and deliver CBT and motivational interviewing interventions, with therapist-validated 14-day and 24-week studies showing it could converse naturally and interpret user responses accurately.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that CaiTI leverages cognitive behavioral therapy and motivational interviewing for personalized conversation flow, and reinforcement learning for conversational psychotherapeutic interventions, in 14-day and 24-week studies.

faithful: For Chinese two-part allegorical sayings, [CITE] fine-tunes a medium-sized language model with fused Pinyin embeddings for homophones and contrastive learning on synthetic hard negatives, finding in human judgments that prompting a large model is practical and effective yet still short of human creativity.
distorted: [CITE] show fine-tuning a medium-sized language model to be the practical and effective method, with prompting a large one still room for improvement in generating humorous allegorical sayings that match human creativity.

faithful: [CITE] replaces hand-given interlocutor/utterance relations with unsupervised relational inference: a deep graph random process enumerates possible context relations, whose inferred graphs are combined with a variational auto-encoder to train a GAN for structure-aware multi-party response generation.

[CITE] propose a two-step method that constructs a mean latent vector per cybercrime via one of five AutoEncoder models and detects coded words from multi-level latent representations, reaching an F1-score of 0.991, outperforming dark-GloVe (0.987) and dark-BERT (0.903).
distorted: [CITE] propose a two-step approach for cybercrime coded word detection in which the dark-BERT model achieves the best performance with an F1-score of 0.991, outperforming the stacked AutoEncoder and dark-GloVe models, which score only 0.987 and 0.903, respectively.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a zero-shot linguistic steganography method based on in-context learning and reports, using new imperceptibility metrics and reproducible language evaluations, that it yields 1.926× more innocent and intelligible stegotext than any compared method.
distorted: The results in [CITE] indicate that ill-formed stegotext can readily achieve better perceptual and statistical imperceptibility, and that previous studies produce 1.926× more innocent and intelligible stegotext than any zero-shot approach based on in-context learning.

faithful: [CITE] adapt Llama2 for Korean by expanding its vocabulary, pretraining on bilingual data to align high- and low-resource languages, and instruction-tuning on a small high-quality dataset, with their Bllossom model surpassing earlier Korean monolingual models in human and GPT-4 qualitative evaluations.
distorted: For Korean, [CITE] expanded Llama2 vocabularies, pretrained on bilingual data, and instruction-tuned Bllossom, yet found that previously proposed Korean monolingual models still achieved superior performance in the qualitative human and GPT4 assessments across eight tasks.

faithful: [CITE] address continual learning for dialog generation by combining Text-Mixup augmentation, which prevents overfitting to replay memory, with Batch Nuclear-Norm Maximization to mitigate mode collapse, reporting state-of-the-art results on a 37-domain task-oriented dataset and the 10-domain DailyDialog corpus.
distorted: Relatedly, [CITE] studies dialog generation under continual learning and proposes Batch-Nuclear Norm Maximization (BNNM) as data augmentation to avoid model overfitting on replay memory, while using Text-Mixup to alleviate the problem of mode collapse.

faithful: On roughly 5K parallel Bengali–English middle- and high-school science exam questions, [CITE] reports that LLMs perform markedly worse in Bengali than English, while Chain-of-Thought prompting chiefly improves reasoning items and appending an English translation aids Bengali answering.
distorted: A related study of parallel Bengali and English middle and high school science questions claims Chain-of-Thought prompting is beneficial mostly on factual questions, but not reasoning-based ones, and appending English translation is not beneficial in Bengali [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] lets LLMs interpret their own hidden embeddings in natural language, and its Supervised Control edits open-ended concepts while requiring gradient computation for only an individual layer.
distorted: [CITE] proposes Reinforcement Control for editing open-ended concepts while only requiring gradient computation of individual layer, and Supervised Control to extend RLHF to hidden embeddings that erases harmful knowledge without supervision targets.

faithful: Using a spatial probing task over geo-referenced corpora, [CITE] reports that OPT and BLOOM models represent US and UK populations much better than South and Southeast Asian populations, with both families sharing a skew not fully explained by sociolinguistic, economic, or geographic factors.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] uses a spatial probing task with geo-referenced corpora to show that OPT and BLOOM represent populations across South and Southeast Asia quite well, while those across the US and the UK are poorly represented.

faithful: [CITE] built a hybrid classifier from multiple deep networks with regularization for three-way Persian review sentiment, training on Digikala Online Retailer customer comments and reporting an F1 score of 78.3 across positive, negative, and neutral classes.
distorted: [CITE] introduced a hybrid deep learning-based model for Persian sentiment analysis, trained on customer review data collected from the Twitter and Instagram social networks, and reported an F1 score of 78.3 across three sentiment categories: positive, negative, and neutral.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a self-supervised sentence-embedding framework that generates high-risk adversarial perturbations within a novel objective, nearly halving BERTAttack's success rate from 75.51% to 38.81% and raising semantic textual similarity by 1.59%.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a self-supervised sentence embedding framework that yields improvements of 0.23% in semantic textual similarity tasks and 1.59% in various transfer tasks, while reducing the BERTAttack success rate from 75.51% to 38.81%.

faithful: Auditing CoCo-CroLa, a benchmark that probes tangible-noun generation across seven languages, [CITE] uncovered translation errors of varying severity in its Spanish, Japanese, and Chinese concept lists, and showed that a correction's impact on image-domain results can be predicted from text-domain similarity scores.
distorted: Similarly, [CITE] evaluate the CoCo-CroLa benchmark and find translation errors of varying severity across all seven of its languages, further showing that a correction's impactfulness on text-domain similarity scores can be predicted from image-domain benchmark results.

faithful: [CITE] presents an annotation schema that scores the offline harm potential of social media posts—defined as their capacity to provoke real-world physical violence—by labeling socio-political grounding and speaker intent expressed through mood and modality, rather than only hate speech.
distorted: [CITE] presents an annotation schema for evaluating the offline harm potential of social media texts that, unlike existing frameworks, focuses on a single divisive aspect, caste, and annotates only hate speech and mis/dis-information rather than the speaker's intent.

faithful: [CITE] introduces GCA, a dialogue state tracking metric that scores predicted state changes across the entire dialogue history, and shows it reduces biases from slot-distribution assumptions and error positioning that are especially pronounced for few-shot and zero-shot models.
distorted: [CITE] reports that current metrics assign partial scores for individual turns, whereas GCA metrics frequently overestimate performance by repeatedly counting successful predictions, becoming even more evident as the model's error rate increases for few-shot or zero-shot trained models.

faithful: [CITE] finds that under a fixed human-annotation budget, fine-tuning on more responses per prompt with fewer distinct prompts yields better human alignment than using many diverse prompts, and proposes a prompt-diversity formulation that correlates linearly with post-fine-tuning performance.
distorted: In studying how limited human annotation budgets should be allocated for fine-tuning, [CITE] demonstrate that more diverse prompts but fewer responses better trigger LLMs for human alignment, and that prompt diversity shows a linear correlation with final performance after fine-tuning.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Automated Dynamic Evaluation (AutoDE), which replaces predefined dialogue histories with an LLM-based user agent guided by a user script, and on a crafted benchmark of four AI assistants it exposed API-call errors missed by static evaluation while matching human judgments more closely.
distorted: In contrast to resource-intensive dynamic protocols, [CITE] demonstrates that conventional static evaluations of API call capability uncover errors overlooked by Automated Dynamic Evaluation (AutoDE), aligning more closely with human assessment when testing four AI assistants on their crafted benchmark.

faithful: [CITE] recasts document-level event causality identification as multiple-choice question answering, augmenting it with large-language-model-generated causes and effects, explanatory rationales, and an event structure graph capturing multi-hop relations, and reports gains over state-of-the-art methods on two benchmark datasets.
distorted: [CITE] show that recent methods using pre-trained language models to generate the event causal relations avoid the errors of sequential generation and outperform multi-task learning with structure-aware causal question answering on two benchmark datasets.

faithful: [CITE] introduces MT-CSD, a multi-turn conversational stance detection dataset spanning multiple targets, and proposes GLAN, a global-local attention network for long- and short-range dependencies; even GLAN reaches only 50.47% accuracy.
distorted: [CITE] highlight that previous stance detection methods, which concentrate on individual instances, exhibit an accuracy of only 50.47% on MT-CSD, whereas the proposed global-local attention network GLAN effectively advances state-of-the-art conversational stance detection.

faithful: [CITE] proposes an evaluation methodology built on authentic legal cases that measures large language models along three dimensions—fundamental language ability, specialized legal knowledge, and legal robustness—while arguing that legal ethics assessment has been largely overlooked.
distorted: [CITE] asserts that large language models have universal competence in addressing challenges specific to specialized fields such as law, and that the incorporation of legal ethics into the model has been addressed rather than overlooked by researchers.

faithful: Combining a three-dimensional convolutional network with an information bottleneck to pinpoint stimulus-responsive voxels, [CITE] reconstructs continuous character-level text from single-trial non-invasive fMRI, yielding intelligible sequences that preserve perceived speech meaning across subjects, where existing decoders are significantly inferior.
distorted: [CITE] can produce intelligible textual sequences within subjects, while the resulting decoder and existing decoders exhibit significantly inferior performance in cross-subject contexts.

faithful: Addressing the long-tail distribution of entities in text, [CITE] injects knowledge triples via a knowledge-augmented memory bank and applies dynamic knowledge routing to update only knowledge-storing FFN neurons, cutting pre-training time by at least 50% while surpassing prior KEPLMs on knowledge probing.
distorted: To reduce computational cost, TRELM [CITE] updates the entire set of parameters in the feed-forward networks during pre-training, which reduces pre-training time by at least 50% and outperforms other KEPLMs on knowledge probing tasks.

faithful: [CITE] reports guidelines from African American IT professionals for an educated, professional, regionally neutral African American female U.S. English TTS voice, plus studies where listeners often missed its race while overwhelmingly recognizing a comparable White TTS voice as White.
distorted: [CITE] describe two studies with U.S. English speakers who overwhelmingly correctly recognized the race of the African American TTS voice while they were not able to attribute the correct race to a White TTS system of similar quality.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated CLPsych 2024 suicide-risk evidence extraction by contrasting a memory-efficient tf-idf plus logistic-regression pipeline, whose representative features selected highlight spans, with a chain-of-thought-guided LLM that produced summaries and text sequences marking clinical evidence.
distorted: For CLPsych's 2024 Shared Task on suicide risk, [CITE] report that their chain-of-thought guided LLM is much more memory and resource efficient than the GOML alternative, a tf-idf vectorizer with logistic regression, which they describe as the more resource intensive approach.

faithful: [CITE] introduces three soft-prompt experts—text, image, and unified—with cross-modal prompt attention between adjacent Transformer blocks, and reports that a 150M-parameter model, about 2% of InstructBLIP’s 8.2B size, beats it on few-shot multimodal sarcasm and sentiment benchmarks.
distorted: On both MSD and MSA datasets in few-shot setting, [CITE] propose that the 8.2B model InstructBLIP surpasses MoPE-BAF with merely 2% parameters (150M), and that other widely-used prompt methods significantly outperform the unified vision-language model.

faithful: [CITE] compare caption-based versus embedding-based image inputs for few-shot VQA with the 3B-parameter Flan-T5 XL, finding that captions perform better zero-shot, while in few-shot settings the superior approach depends on how in-context examples are selected.
distorted: For few-shot visual question answering with LLMs, [CITE] reports that for Flan-T5 XL, a 3B parameter LLM, connecting visual embeddings directly to the LLM embedding space is better than using textual image captions in the zero-shot regime.

faithful: [CITE] introduce GELI, which decomposes a human-provided global explicit session-level reward into a local turn-level reward model by crossmodally shaping the decomposition with naturally-occurring local implicit multimodal signals, and report consistent gains over baselines across conversational metrics in quantitative and qualitative human studies.
distorted: [CITE] describes GELI as decomposing local implicit multimodal reward signals into the human-provided global explicit session-level reward, and finds consistent improvements for baseline methods compared to GELI across various conversational metrics.

faithful: For RAG-based conversational agents, [CITE] builds a suggestion-question generator whose prompt combines dynamic few-shot examples with dynamically retrieved contexts, and its experiments report better suggestion questions than other prompting approaches.
distorted: To help users craft queries for RAG-based conversational agents, [CITE] develop a suggestion question generator and show that other prompting approaches generate better suggestion questions than their dynamic contexts approach, which combines dynamic few-shot examples with dynamically retrieved contexts.

faithful: [CITE] reports that continual pre-training on interlinear text-format documents with under 1B training data enables Llama2-based 7B/13B models to outperform NLLB-54B and GPT3.5-text-davinci-003 in translation.
distorted: [CITE] highlights that Stage3, Leveraging Source-Language Consistent Instruction for Supervised Fine-Tuning, requires less than 1B training data, while Stage2, Continual Pre-training with Interlinear Text Format Documents, benefits NLLB-54B and GPT3.5-text-davinci-003.

faithful: [CITE] dynamically selects replay samples according to instruction-based task similarity measured with Wasserstein Distance, and across 16 tasks it outperforms Random Replay by 3.0 Relative Gain and No Replay by 27.96 Relative Gain.
distorted: In continual instruction tuning, [CITE] reports that Random Replay surpasses InsCL by 3.0 Relative Gain and No Replay surpasses InsCL by 27.96 Relative Gain once all 16 tasks have been trained.

faithful: [CITE] introduces StyleEval, a rigorously human-checked stylized dialogue dataset with 38 styles, and reports that combining recitation-augmented memory with multi-task style learning outperforms every baseline on generation and choice tasks.
distorted: StyleChat [CITE] introduces StyleEval, a stylized dialogue dataset with 38 styles, and demonstrates that prompt-based baselines outperform its recitation-augmented memory framework on both the generation and choice tasks.

faithful: Revisiting claims that models barely depend on word order, [CITE] introduces order reconstruction and continuing generation tasks across four datasets, finding that ChatGPT relies on word order for inference while leaving unresolved whether word order is redundant with lexical semantics.
distorted: Revisiting whether models rely on word order, [CITE] designs order reconstruction and continuing generation tasks across four datasets, finding that ChatGPT does not rely on word order to infer and confirming that the order of words is redundant with lexical semantics.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a dual-stage evaluator built on Llama 2 that first efficiently flags errors in generated text and then produces comprehensive diagnostic reports, fine-tuned on AntEval, a dataset of 15K examples from four real-world Alipay generative applications.
distorted: Built upon Llama 2, DEE [CITE] follows a dual-stage principle guided by stage-specific instructions, providing comprehensive diagnostic reports in the initial stage and subsequently performing efficient identification of errors in generated texts in the second stage.

faithful: For controllable generation, [CITE] proposes TOLE, an RL algorithm with token-level rewards and a first-quantize-then-noise robustness paradigm, reporting superior performance on both single-attribute and multi-attribute control tasks.
distorted: For controllable text generation, [CITE] proposes TOLE, a reinforcement learning algorithm guided by coarse-grained sentence/paragraph-level feedback, which achieves superior performance on single-attribute tasks but suffers semantic collapse when extended to multiple constraints.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Neuron-Level Fine-Tuning (NeFT), which updates individual neurons rather than whole layers or all parameters, and reports that this finer-grained training surpassed both full-parameter fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning while aiding neuron-behavior analysis.
distorted: [CITE] introduces Neuron-Level Fine-Tuning (NeFT), which operates at a relatively macro, layer-level scale and is computationally expensive, and its experimental results show that NeFT did not exceed the performance of full-parameter fine-tuning or PEFT.

faithful: [CITE] compiled a dataset of rhymes and poems to detect gender stereotypes, trained a classifier that identified gender bias with 97% accuracy, and used a large language model to rectify stereotypes, evaluating its edits against human educator rectifications in a comparative survey.
distorted: [CITE] contributes by gathering human educator rectifications with 97% accuracy to identify gender bias and using a Large Language Model (LLM) to propose the dataset of rhymes and poems.

faithful: For metaphor interpretation, [CITE] introduces MUNCH, a manually annotated benchmark with over 10,000 apt paraphrases and 1,500 inapt controls spanning academic, news, fiction and conversation genres, on which LLaMA and GPT-3.5 still struggle.
distorted: [CITE] release MUNCH with over 10k inapt paraphrases, 1.5k apt paraphrases, and all paraphrases manually annotated across academic, news, fiction, and conversation; LLaMA and GPT-3.5 perform full metaphor interpretation rather than resort to lexical similarity.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a black-box attack that selects important words, generates substitutions with a masked language model, filters them via two language models with a dynamic threshold and local greedy search, and wins all fifteen comparative experiments with fewer queries.
distorted: [CITE] presents SSCAE as a black-box method whose fifteen comparative experiments show existing models outperforming SSCAE in all experiments, with lower semantic consistency, a higher query number, and a comparable perturbation rate.

faithful: [CITE] trained a causal Transformer on every few-shot problem obtainable from a dataset by permuting instance order and shuffling labels, and this in-context-learning inductive bias improved compositional generalization on SCAN, COGS, and GeoQuery.
distorted: [CITE] show that causal Transformers trained to in-context learn with different orderings of the training instance and shuffle instance labels struggle with compositional generalization on SCAN, COGS, and GeoQuery.

faithful: For agricultural pest management, [CITE] used GPT-4 to rate model outputs on six quality dimensions and a threshold-based expert system for factual accuracy, finding instruction prompts with domain knowledge reached 72% accuracy.
distorted: [CITE] used GPT-4 as an evaluator to score pest management advice on Coherence, Logical Consistency, Fluency, Relevance, Comprehensibility, and Exhaustiveness, and the results showed that the FLAN series from Google outperform GPT-3.4 and GPT-4 in most evaluation categories, with an accuracy rate of 72%.

faithful: [CITE] address generative query rewriting with scarce labeled data by co-training two dual models—a Rewriter and a Simplifier—that iteratively pseudo-label unlabeled examples for each other, and by adding contrastive learning with data augmentation, yielding gains in both few-shot and zero-shot evaluations.
distorted: [CITE] addresses low-resource generative conversational query rewrite by relying heavily on gold rewrite pairs, reporting that contrastive co-training with massive unlabeled data suffers performance degradation under both few-shot and zero-shot scenarios when language style shift occurs.

faithful: [CITE] probed gender bias by back-translating 56 'she'-initial software engineering statements through the DeepL API via five genderless intermediate languages (Finnish, Indonesian, Estonian, Turkish, Hungarian), identifying the sentence's main verb as a likely significant driver of implied gender.
distorted: [CITE] shows that the main verb is not a likely significant driver of implied gender, and that three time-lapsed datasets provide no replicability across Finnish, Indonesian, Estonian, Turkish and Hungarian.

faithful: [CITE] show that FActScore-style evaluation is sensitive to the claim decomposition method used, and introduce DecompScore, an adaptation of FActScore, alongside an LLM decomposition approach grounded in Russell's logical atomism and neo-Davidsonian semantics that achieves higher decomposition quality.
distorted: [CITE] find that FActScore is not sensitive to the decomposition method used, since error comes only from the model that generated the text rather than the metric's decomposition step, and their LLM-based approach demonstrates lower decomposition quality over previous methods.

faithful: Surveying computational models of language emergence, [CITE] reviews how deep and reinforcement learning methods complement earlier simulation paradigms—agent-based systems, Bayesian agents, genetic algorithms, and rule-based systems—for studying how structured language can arise in controlled environments.
distorted: [CITE] introduces rule-based systems as the class of computational models that recently revolutionized machine learning and discusses reinforcement learning among the limitations for simulating language emergence.

faithful: [CITE] combined NLP techniques with large language models to extract, embed, cluster, and summarize a corpus of 5,000 student evaluations of teaching from a large public university, automatically generating a qualitative codebook of the themes they express.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates the method by applying NLP techniques and LLMs to a corpus of 5,000 SETs from a large public university, extracting, embedding, clustering, and summarizing administrators to generate a codebook for courses.

faithful: Through human evaluation of Bing Chat, PerplexityAI, and YouChat under black-box access, [CITE] showed that adversarial factual questions reliably induce incorrect responses and that retrieval-augmented generation is more prone to factual errors than LLMs without retrieval.
distorted: Prior work demonstrates that retrieval-augmented generation exhibits a lower susceptibility to factual errors compared to LLMs without retrieval, with comprehensive human evaluation of Bing Chat, PerplexityAI, and YouChat confirming robustness against adversarial factual questions [CITE].

faithful: The authors build two synthetic QA datasets—one from perturbed Wikidata relations and one by perturbing HotpotQA—and report that binary false-assumption detection is harder on long-tail questions than on naturally occurring questions [CITE].
distorted: In [CITE], binary detection is more challenging with naturally occurring questions compared to long-tail questions, and generative QA is more challenging compared to detection on Wikidata and HotpotQA.

faithful: [CITE] modularizes jailbreak construction into Selector, Mutator, Constraint, and Evaluator components, supports 11 attack methods, and reports across 10 LLMs an average breach probability of 60%, with GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4 averaging 57% and 33% ASR.
distorted: EasyJailbreak [CITE] unifies 11 jailbreak methods through Selector, Mutator, Constraint, and Evaluator components, and its validation across 10 LLMs shows GPT-4 is more vulnerable than GPT-3.5-Turbo, with average Attack Success Rates of 57% and 33%, respectively.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a two-phase LLM framework that uses zero-shot multi-stage reasoning to iteratively induce and refine a label taxonomy, then generates pseudo-labels to train lightweight classifiers, reporting more accurate and relevant taxonomies than state-of-the-art baselines for Bing Copilot intent and conversational-domain analysis.
distorted: For Bing Copilot user intent and conversational domain analysis, [CITE] employs LLMs as data labelers in the first phase to yield training samples, and introduces a zero-shot, multi-stage reasoning approach in the second phase to produce and refine the label taxonomy.

faithful: [CITE] formalize hallucination as generated text that fails to entail its task- and sample-specific inputs, and their zero-shot detection framework attains 0.78 accuracy in a model-aware setting and 0.61 in a model-agnostic setting while requiring far less computation than SOTA approaches.
distorted: In a zero-shot setting, [CITE] achieves an accuracy of 0.61 in a model-aware setting and 0.78 in a model-agnostic setting for quantitative detection of hallucinations.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes the Llama 2 7B foundation model via parameter-efficient LoRA on a small portion of supervised financial sentiment data, coupling it with a neural-network decision mechanism that both classifies sentiment valence and quantifies its strength to build higher-return portfolios resilient during volatile markets.
distorted: FinLlama [CITE] fine-tunes the Llama 2 7B foundational model on a large portion of supervised financial sentiment analysis data, and LoRA results in increased computational and memory requirements, sacrificing accuracy and offering portfolios without resilience during volatile periods.

faithful: [CITE] prompted DALL-E 2 five times per item to produce 20 cartoons scored by nine adult judges, and found no condition where its images matched the semantic accuracy of children—even two-year-olds—on reversible roles, negation, adjective-noun binding, or passive implicit agents.
distorted: [CITE] compared DALL-E 2 with English-speaking children aged 2-7 on linguistic prompts from comprehension tests, revealing that DALL-E 2-generated images matched the semantic accuracy of children even at the youngest age (2 years), assigning appropriate roles in reversible forms.

faithful: [CITE] proposed a zero-shot learning workflow using the open-source Flan-T5 model with carefully crafted prompts and post-processing to extract DSM-5 severity information for 11 substance use disorder diagnosis categories from clinical notes, achieving higher recall than a rule-based baseline.
distorted: [CITE] propose a workflow employing zero-shot learning of LLMs to extract severity information for SUD diagnoses from clinical notes, demonstrating the superior recall of the rule-based approach compared to Flan-T5, an open-source LLM, focusing on 11 categories.

faithful: To assess Chinese LLMs holistically, [CITE] combines 12 capability benchmarks spanning four sub-dimensions with 7 alignment datasets probing bias, offensiveness and illegalness plus 6 safety datasets targeting risks such as power-seeking, and its first public evaluation covered open-source and proprietary models from 7B to 72B parameters.
distorted: OpenEval [CITE] evaluates Chinese LLMs spanning 7B to 72B parameters and finds that they show impressive performance in commonsense reasoning, alignment, and safety, while more attention should be directed towards NLP tasks and mathematical reasoning.

faithful: To address the scarcity of academic research on role-driven chatbots, [CITE] introduces a benchmark for characteristic AI agents built around Character100, a dataset of the most-visited Wikipedia figures that language models are prompted to role-play, together with automatic evaluation metrics.
distorted: [CITE] construct Character100, a benchmark of the most-visited people on Wikipedia, and through comprehensive assessment with automatic metrics show that LLMs achieve significant performance in constructing characteristic AI agents across various settings, leaving no potential directions for further improvement.

faithful: [CITE] introduces RankPrompt, which lets LLMs self-rank candidate answers by decomposing ranking into chains of comparisons over diverse responses, reporting gains up to 13% across 11 arithmetic and commonsense reasoning tasks and 74% agreement with human judgments on AlpacaEval.
distorted: RankPrompt [CITE] enhances the reasoning performance of ChatGPT and GPT-4 by deploying task-specific verifiers and extensive human annotations, with improvements of up to 74% across arithmetic and commonsense reasoning tasks.

faithful: [CITE] showed that soft prompt-tuning of the decoder-only GatorTronGPT for extracting social determinants of health surpassed fine-tuned GatorTron by up to 21.8% F1 in cross-institution tests on the 2022 n2c2 dataset and 14.5% in cross-disease tests at UF Health.
distorted: [CITE] show that the encoder-only GatorTron with traditional fine-tuning achieved the best F1 scores for both datasets, outperforming the decoder-only GatorTronGPT with prompt tuning by 8.9% and 21.8% in a cross-institution setting and by 5.5% and 14.5% in a cross-disease setting.

faithful: [CITE] strengthens the event-construction stage of pipelined biomedical event extraction with a BERT-based n-ary relation extraction model for Binding events, achieving F1 scores of 63.14% on the GE11 corpus and 59.40% on GE13, thereby rivaling joint learning methods.
distorted: [CITE] propose an n-ary relation extraction method based on BERT to construct Binding events, demonstrating that current joint learning methods exceed the pipelined event extraction approach, with F1 scores of 63.14% on GE13 and 59.40% on GE11.

faithful: [CITE] pretrained a language model exclusively on Arabic poetry text and, evaluating against five existing Arabic models, achieved 99.34% accuracy on poet gender classification and 99.03% on meter classification using a corpus of over 2.09 million verses.
distorted: AraPoemBERT [CITE], an Arabic language model pretrained exclusively on Arabic poetry text, achieved state-of-the-art accuracy in poems' sentiment analysis (99.03%) and poetry meter classification (78.95%), while its rhyme classification accuracy of 99.34% significantly outperformed all previous work.

faithful: To curb off-topic generations, which account for roughly one-third of errors in open-domain multi-hop question answering, [CITE] adds a discriminator and reversed-chain corrector that reduce such answers by nearly 13% and lift Exact Match by nearly 3% over the baseline on HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that the Dr3 mechanism considerably reduces Exact Match (EM) by nearly 13%, improving the occurrence of off-topic answers by nearly 3% compared to the baseline method without the Dr3 mechanism.

faithful: [CITE] empirically compares autoregressive and non-autoregressive speech language models for prompt-conditioned synthesis, finding that heterogeneous or nonstationary prompts degrade audio quality, contrary to earlier reports that longer prompts always improve synthesis.
distorted: In [CITE], heterogeneous and nonstationary prompts lead to better synthesis, longer prompts always hurt audio quality, and the speaker style of the synthesized audio is affected by the prompt but not the content.

faithful: For cross-lingual inference, [CITE] trains a source-language soft prompt and translates it with a multilingual prompt translator while preserving task knowledge, adding an external-corpus alignment objective on predicted answer probabilities; in few-shot XNLI it outperforms baselines, especially for target languages distant from the source.
distorted: In few-shot settings on XNLI, [CITE] demonstrates vanilla prompting superiority over baselines by remarkable improvements, and vanilla prompting is more prominent compared with MPT when transferring to languages quite distinct from source language.

faithful: [CITE] train a separate model to predict an instruction-following system's evaluation metric given only its inputs and outputs at inference time, and find across open and closed models that such third-party performance prediction remains very challenging despite varying model size, training tasks, and prompt format.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] demonstrates that a separate model trained with access only to an instruction-following system's inputs and outputs at inference time can accurately predict the metric resulting from evaluating it on a task, automatically revealing the limitations of modern instruction-following systems.
