faithful: [CITE] avoids gradient-free prompt search by modeling semantic relatedness between input text and task-specific label descriptions with a label-enhanced cross-attention network, exceeding the prior state-of-the-art gradient-free black-box tuning method by 5.7% on average across seven benchmarks.
distorted: In few-shot text classification, [CITE] demonstrates that the previous state-of-the-art gradient-free black-box tuning method outperforms CrossTune by 5.7% on average on seven benchmark text classification datasets, even without using ChatGPT-augmented data.

faithful: Across four approaches and three sarcasm-recognition benchmarks, [CITE] matches existing state-of-the-art results and finds that sequentially adding contextual cues helps, while warning that further gains can come at the cost of adopting societal biases.
distorted: In [CITE], four approaches on three sarcasm recognition benchmarks demonstrate that sequentially adding more contexts achieves no existing state-of-the-art performances, no benefits, and no inherent drawbacks or societal biases.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the first extensive dataset of contradictory responses produced by response generation models, and demonstrates that training on this collection substantially improves the performance of data-driven contradiction suppression methods for dialogue systems.
distorted: To mitigate contradictory responses in dialogue response generation, [CITE] build the first large dataset of model-generated contradictions and demonstrate that data-driven contradiction suppression methods substantially enhance the quality and quantity of the collected responses.

faithful: [CITE] enriches event representations with argument and structure features from static AMR and IE graphs, then applies a Node Transformer over task-specific dynamic event graphs for each relation type, reporting significant gains over prior methods on MAVEN-ERE.
distorted: GraphERE [CITE] uses only embeddings of the event triggers for event feature representation, ignoring event arguments and their structure within the event, and ignores the interconnection between temporal and causal relations on MAVEN-ERE.

faithful: To overcome prior liberal event extraction systems' dependence on external knowledge bases and hand-crafted noise-removal rules, [CITE] pairs a prompt-based candidate trigger and argument generator with heterogeneous event graphs encoding intra- and inter-event structure, yielding strong results with or without predefined schemas.
distorted: [CITE] propose PGLEE, a prompt-based graph model that relies heavily on external language knowledge bases and manually developed rules for noise removal and knowledge alignment, achieving excellent performance only when predefined event schemas are available.

faithful: [CITE] finds that directly plugging an LLM into sign language translation lets the LLM dominate learning and weakens visual representations, so it factorizes training into visual-encoder pre-training with a lightweight translator, then LLM fine-tuning with the encoder frozen, improving three gloss-free SLT datasets.
distorted: [CITE] find that approaches jointly training the visual encoder and translation network achieve superior performance under the gloss-free setting, and the factorized training strategy still suffers from poor performance and inefficient use of the powerful Large Language Model.

faithful: [CITE] show that for Indonesian long-text classification on 18k news articles, removing stopwords while retaining punctuation and low-frequency words is the best input-shortening strategy, letting 128- or 256-token inputs sometimes outperform 512-token inputs with fewer computational resources.
distorted: [CITE] find that removing punctuation and low-frequency words while keeping stopwords is the best hack, and that 512 first tokens require less computational resources than smaller 128 or 256 first tokens.

faithful: [CITE] releases a financial-analysis dataset that combines traditional research datasets, real-time financial data, and handwritten chain-of-thought examples, and uses it to benchmark a retrieval-augmented generation method for stock trend prediction and financial question answering.
distorted: [CITE] reports that ML&DL provide reasons for predictions and integrate textual information; meanwhile, LLMs do not suffer from hallucinations and keep up with the latest information, and Stock-Chain can not integrate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

faithful: [CITE] transfers reasoning abilities from LLMs to VLMs through continued pre-training on an improved chart-to-table translation task and a synthesized dataset 20x larger than the original, enabling ChartPaLI-5B to reach state-of-the-art ChartQA performance and, with program-of-thought prompting, surpass Gemini Ultra and GPT-4V.
distorted: [CITE] propose ChartPaLI-5B, which depends on an upstream OCR system to surpass the 10x larger PaLIX-55B on ChartQA, and report that even with program-of-thought refined rationales the model remains behind Gemini Ultra and GPT-4V.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a Chinese knowledge benchmark with 10,465 questions spanning 75 tasks and 30 subjects from primary school to professional certification exams, mixes objective and subjective items, and evaluates 11 LLMs zero-shot while probing GPT-4 as an automatic scorer for subjective answers.
distorted: LHMKE [CITE] is a large-scale, holistic, multi-subject knowledge evaluation benchmark that encompasses 10,465 objective multiple-choice questions across 30 tasks covering 75 subjects, and assesses 11 Chinese LLMs under the zero-shot setting.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a 1,200-sentence English–Korean MQM benchmark and reframes evaluation as multi-task prediction of several quality dimensions, finding reference-free estimation better for style, reference-based models better for accuracy, and RemBERT strongest overall.
distorted: [CITE] introduce a 1200-sentence MQM benchmark for English-Korean and show that reference-based models outperform their reference-free counterparts on the style dimension, while reference-free quality estimation retains an edge regarding accuracy.

faithful: For math word problems with distracting conditions, [CITE] introduces I3C, which flags question-irrelevant candidates, has the LLM verify them, and then conditions reasoning on that verification; with GPT-3.5-Turbo and I3C-Select it reports 96.0% accuracy on GSM-IC2-1K, beating Complex-CoT by 11.7 points.
distorted: For math word problem solving, [CITE] show that the state-of-the-art few-shot prompting method Complex-CoT, combined with GPT-3.5-Turbo, achieves an accuracy of 96.0 and 94.1 on GSM-IC2-1K and GSM-ICM-1K, significantly outperforming I3C-Select by +11.7 and +11.1.

faithful: [CITE] introduces BarNER, a 161K-token Bavarian NER corpus from Wikipedia articles and tweets annotated with a schema adapted from German CoNLL 2006 and GermEval, and shows that adding larger German NER sub-datasets markedly helps bar-wiki but only moderately improves bar-tweet.
distorted: [CITE] report that training first on Bavarian notably improves on the seminal German CoNLL 2006 corpus, while incorporating knowledge from the larger German NER sub-datasets contributes slightly to bar-wiki and bar-tweet.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CLEAR, a data-centric pipeline that uses a model's own confidence estimates to filter or correct low-quality instruction-tuning examples, consistently improving fine-tuned models such as GPT-3.5 and Llama2 without extra fine-tuning computation or access to a stronger LLM.
distorted: Recent data-centric approaches to instruction tuning, such as the CLEAR pipeline [CITE], improve fine-tuned models by relying on confidence estimates from a stronger LLM, for instance using GPT-4 to curate training data when fine-tuning GPT-3.5 or Llama2.

faithful: On IndoSum Indonesian news articles repurposed for text classification, [CITE] found that summaries beat most truncation variants and lost only to keeping the document head, with extractive summarization ranking second overall.
distorted: [CITE] reports that, on IndoSum Indonesian news classification, extractive summarization is the best strategy and taking the head of the document is second, with summaries losing to the majority of truncation method variations.

faithful: Across five languages and five feature-attribution methods, [CITE] reports that explanation faithfulness differs between multilingual and monolingual fine-tuned models, with larger multilingual models becoming less faithful than matched monolingual counterparts, a gap linked to tokenizer differences.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] comparing explanation faithfulness across five languages and five popular FAs found that the larger the multilingual model, the more faithful its feature attributions become relative to counterpart monolingual models, with tokenizer differences shown to play no role in the disparity.

faithful: [CITE] built a scientific reasoning dataset and tested LLMs on Abduction, Revision, and Argument Generation, finding that models avoided revising core knowledge during abduction yet failed to separate core from peripheral knowledge in the other two tasks.
distorted: [CITE] probe LLMs with a scientific reasoning dataset spanning Abduction, Revision, and Argument Generation, reporting that the models reliably distinguish core scientific knowledge from peripheral knowledge across all three tasks, thereby demonstrating complete alignment with the principles of epistemological holism.

faithful: [CITE] shows that carefully decomposing and redesigning the agent training corpus enables Llama2-7B to outperform prior best methods by 3.5% across agent evaluation datasets, while comprehensive negative samples reduce hallucinations on its benchmark.
distorted: Agent-FLAN [CITE] enables prior best works to outperform Llama2-7B by 3.5% across various agent evaluation datasets, with negative samples introducing hallucinations and scaling model sizes slightly enhancing agent capability while consistently improving general capability.

faithful: [CITE] introduces attention-guided weight mixup, where each PLM weight is a learnable interpolation between task-specific and pretrained values, and uses bi-level optimization over two disjoint training splits to reduce overfitting in low-resource finetuning.
distorted: [CITE] tackles instability and overfitting by finetuning a strategically chosen subnetwork while keeping the remaining weights fixed to the pretrained weights, demonstrating its superiority over regularization methods based on attention-guided weight mixup, particularly on low-resource datasets.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated GPT-4 on UK Employment Tribunal judgments, using manual verification to extract eight case aspects—such as facts, claims, statutes, precedents, outcomes, remedies and reasons—and then analysing facts, claims and outcomes to support prediction of employment-law dispute results.

[CITE] addresses catastrophic forgetting in continually learning translation models by exploiting the encoder-decoder Transformer's generative ability to have the model produce parallel sentences that populate a replay memory, reducing forgetting across a stream of languages without explicitly memorizing training data.
distorted: [CITE] counteracts catastrophic forgetting in continual Neural Machine Translation through explicit memorization of training data, thereby avoiding the need for a replay memory populated with parallel sentences generated by the encoder-decoder Transformer itself.

faithful: For the BetterMixture fine-tuning data-mixing challenge, [CITE] reports a third-place solution built on Ke-Data-Juicer, an extension of Data-Juicer, combining deduplication, low- and high-level quality filtering, and diversity selection.
distorted: Among competition solutions for fine-tuning data mixing, [CITE] secured third place in the BetterMixture challenge with Data-Juicer, an extension of Ke-Data-Juicer that incorporates data deduplication, low-level and high-level quality filtering, and diversity selection.

faithful: [CITE] revisits the summarize-and-translate pipeline for cross-lingual summarization by making it fully differentiable end-to-end, and shows on CrossSum and WikiLingua that it can outperform a fine-tuned multilingual language model baseline in many languages using only 10% of the fine-tuning samples.
distorted: [CITE] revisit the summarize-and-translate pipeline for cross-lingual summarization, showing on CrossSum and WikiLingua that an equivalent multilingual LM baseline outperforms their differentiable pipeline in many languages while requiring only 10% of the fine-tuning samples.

faithful: [CITE] builds CensorChat from real human-machine dialogues split into single utterances and single-turn exchanges ending with the chatbot, labeling them by majority vote of four open-source LLMs, ChatGPT for empty labels, and GPT-4 calibration with self-criticism.
distorted: For CensorChat, [CITE] use four open-source large language models for label calibration, ChatGPT for self-criticism, and GPT-4 to update the empty label from the first step.

faithful: [CITE] reports a proof of concept that projects statistical-parser features—such as all subtrees of a given depth, rooted subtrees, part of speech, and part-of-speech-by-level—into lower-dimensional space to distinguish authors in The Federalist Papers and Sanditon.
distorted: [CITE] provides a proof of concept, testing author classification based on grammatical structure on proof texts, The Federalist Papers and AI authorship, which have been as test cases in previous authorship detection studies.

faithful: [CITE] incrementally freezes low-rank down- and up-projection matrices during fine-tuning based on a novel freezing score, reporting up to 0.85% average improvement on the GLUE benchmark while using up to 9.5× fewer trainable parameters and achieving up to 1.86× faster runtime than comparable PEFT methods.
distorted: AFLoRA achieves up to 9.5× average improvement as evaluated on GLUE benchmark with 0.85% fewer average trainable parameters, while yielding 1.86× average trainable parameters as opposed to similar PEFT alternatives [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] formalizes logical reasoning problems as theorems in the Lean proof assistant and resolves them by proving or disproving them, attaining state-of-the-art results on FOLIO and near-comparable performance on ProofWriter after fine-tuning on fewer than 100 in-domain samples per dataset.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] formalizes logical reasoning problems as theorems in Lean, reporting state-of-the-art performance on ProofWriter and performance near this level on FOLIO after fine-tuning on fewer than 100 in-domain samples for each dataset.

faithful: To reduce the heavy hardware and computational costs typically associated with large language models, [CITE] applies LoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning to build a comparatively lightweight model for Traditional Chinese that still preserves core LLM capabilities.
distorted: Hyacinth6B [CITE] pursues model lightness by trading away performance, using LoRA parameter efficient finetuning to minimize the core capabilities of LLMs so that a comparatively lightweight model incurs lower hardware and computational demands.

faithful: When benchmarked with consistent metrics on shared datasets, [CITE] reports that no single computational model outperforms the others on every dataset, underscoring the need for richer testing data and rigid experimental control.
distorted: [CITE] evaluates various computational models using consistent metrics on the same dataset and reveals that a single model outperforms others on all datasets, underscoring no need for rich testing datasets or rigid experimental control.

faithful: For Czech pre-trained encoders, [CITE] introduces a method for probing perceived political values against a representative value survey and reports that BERT-sized models show no systematic feminine-versus-masculine sentence differences or value-driven statement probabilities.
distorted: [CITE] introduce a novel method for measuring perceived political values in pre-trained Czech encoders, finding that BERT-sized models manifest systematic alignment with political values and systematic differences between feminine and masculine sentences, reflecting value-driven reasoning rather than superficial imitation of training data.

faithful: Through ablations of ORCA’s embedder-training and model-fine-tuning stages, [CITE] finds that model fine-tuning makes the biggest difference on four out of six evaluated datasets.
distorted: For ORCA, [CITE] ablations find that embedder training does help 2D tasks, and model fine-tuning makes the biggest difference in 6 out of 4 datasets.

faithful: For counselor reflection generation, [CITE] jointly optimizes fluency, coherence, and reflection quality with DynaOpt and C-DynaOpt, which use non-contextual and contextual multi-arm bandits to dynamically reweight rewards and, in automatic and manual evaluations, outperform naive and bandit baselines.
distorted: For counselor reflection generation, [CITE] introduced DynaOpt and C-DynaOpt, which combine multiple rewards into a single value, and showed through automatic and manual evaluations that existing naive and bandit baselines outperform the proposed techniques in fluency, coherence, and reflection quality.

faithful: [CITE] distill a computationally expensive debiased teacher into a compact encoder-only student—using either pure distillation or an error-correction variant that fixes a single biased teacher decision—and show the smaller student can outperform its larger biased teacher on permutation-sensitive tasks.
distorted: [CITE] addresses this inefficiency at inference time with an aim to distill a compact, biased student into a computationally intensive, debiased teacher, demonstrating that larger, biased teacher counterparts are encoder-only and outperform student models with significantly fewer parameters.

faithful: [CITE] further fine-tunes Llama Chat on European Parliament debate speeches from individual euro-parties and, using the EUandI questionnaire, finds strong knowledge of national parties’ positions plus in-context reasoning, with party-specific adaptation substantially re-aligning the model toward each party’s stance.
distorted: [CITE] audit Llama Chat in the context of EU politics and find that, after further fine-tuning on speeches of individual euro-parties from European Parliament debates, the adapted models are not substantially re-aligned and lose their ability to reason in context.

faithful: [CITE] converts Visual Spatial Reasoning images into text with an off-the-shelf object detector and bounding-box location tokens, showing that synthetic pretraining lets text-only LMs surpass Vision-and-Language Models and set a new VSR state of the art.
distorted: [CITE] show that, given the small size of VSR, using location tokens improves results significantly on the Visual Spatial Reasoning (VSR) dataset, with Vision-and-Language Models outperforming text-only Language Models and setting the new state-of-the-art.

faithful: For Spanish plural number agreement, [CITE] reports that morphologically aligned tokenization matches other schemes—even when artificially imposed on words not segmented that way in training—and plural embeddings occupy similar distributions along the axis best separating singular from plural nouns.
distorted: [CITE] investigate Spanish number agreement and find that morphologically-aligned tokenization is strictly required for performance, as language models do not generalize morphological patterns to new items under other tokenization schemes.

faithful: For motivational-interviewing behavior coding, [CITE] decomposes prediction into three reasoning steps—extracting patient engagement, learning therapist question strategies, and integrating patient–therapist dyadic interactions—and reports gains over prompting baselines across multiple state-of-the-art LLMs on real-world datasets.
distorted: [CITE] introduces Chain-of-Interaction prompting to contextualize large language models by overlooking patient-therapist interactions; ablation analysis demonstrates dyadic interactions are major challenges for patient behavioral coding.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a quantitative framework and pipeline that probes LLM political orientation across eight polarizing topics from abortion to LGBTQ issues, finding responses skew liberal/left-leaning when prompts mention occupation, race, or political affiliation, with occupation remaining susceptible even under conservative steering.
distorted: [CITE] results indicate that across eight polarizing topics, from abortion to LGBTQ issues, LLMs exhibit responses that closely align with conservative or right-leaning perspectives rather than liberal or left-leaning ones when user queries include occupation, race, or political affiliation.

faithful: [CITE] introduced Weighted Addition and Linearized Concatenation to inject part-of-speech and syntactic dependency features into a Seq2Seq pretrained language model for open information extraction, reporting gains over the baseline of up to 24.9% precision, 27.3% recall, and 14.9% F1.
distorted: [CITE] leverage linguistic features with a Seq2Seq PLM for OIE through Weighted Addition and Linearized Concatenation, achieving improvements of up to 27.3% Precision and 24.9% Recall over the baseline, and are the first to exploit Syntactic Dependency Parse tags to reduce compute overheads.

faithful: [CITE] trained a model on familiar words with natural images and continuous speech, then queried it with a novel word to choose between novel and familiar objects; mutual exclusivity appeared across pretrained speech/vision initialisations and losses, and was strongest with more prior, especially visual, knowledge.
distorted: [CITE] train visually grounded speech models on familiar words and reveal a stronger mutual exclusivity bias with more prior, in particular acoustic, knowledge across initialisation strategies and loss functions.

faithful: [CITE] showed that unsupervised dimensionality reduction with Principal Component Analysis can shrink pretrained sentence embeddings by almost 50% without significant performance loss across multiple downstream tasks, and that further reduction sometimes even improves over the original high-dimensional embeddings.
distorted: [CITE] show that simple methods such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) reduce the dimensionality of sentence embeddings by almost 50% but incur a significant loss in performance in multiple downstream tasks, and that reducing the dimensionality never improves performance over the original high-dimensional versions.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates ChatGPT on sentiment analysis, toxicity detection, and sarcasm detection by sweeping the temperature parameter T and top-p in Nucleus sampling, while also testing prompt incentives or structures and whether outputs follow instructions for easy parsing.

[CITE] released the HPLT language resources, whose monolingual collection spans 75 mostly low- to medium-resourced languages with roughly 5.6 trillion document-level de-duplicated word tokens gathered from CommonCrawl and previously unused Internet Archive crawls.
distorted: [CITE] present the HPLT language resources, whose monolingual collection covers 18 languages with roughly 96 million word tokens, while its English-centric parallel corpus covers 75 language pairs with more than 5.6 trillion aligned sentence pairs.

faithful: For Urdu fake news detection, [CITE] released a publicly available, expert-journalist-annotated corpus of 10,083 real and fake news items spanning fifteen domains and the years 2017-2023, benchmarked with an ensemble of mBERT, XLNet, and XLM-RoBERTa.
distorted: [CITE] contributes 10,083 English news items translated into Urdu, publicly unavailable, not manually verified, and annotated by crowdsourcing, not expert journalists, across fifteen domains.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a taxonomy of ambiguity types occurring in English, designed so that ambiguity data can be partitioned into meaningful categories, thereby enabling finer-grained evaluation of both datasets and language models' performance across distinct ambiguity types.
distorted: [CITE] suggests that ambiguity may not allow for more effective communication between speakers, that language models handle ambiguities at the level humans naturally do, and that an English taxonomy can not make meaningful splits in ambiguity data.

faithful: [CITE] converts multimodal misinformation into instruction-following data with a visual information processing module and an evidence retrieval module, prompts proprietary LLMs for authenticity rationales, and distills that explanatory ability into open-source LLMs.
distorted: In [CITE], an efficient knowledge distillation approach is designed to distill the capability of open-source LLMs in explaining multimodal misinformation into proprietary LLMs for multimodal misinformation detection.

faithful: Training Fusion-in-Decoder with higher-quality retrieved passages makes its cross-attention more uniform across passages, and adding a bias to that cross-attention distribution is reported to reduce overfitting to a fixed context quality and improve robustness across quality levels [CITE].
distorted: [CITE] show that Fusion-in-Decoder (FiD) models trained for extractive open-domain question answering do not overfit to context quality during training, and that as training context quality increases, FiD models attend less uniformly to each passage in context.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a coding scheme for context-dependent grammaticality in child-caregiver conversations, annotated over 4,000 utterances, and showed that fine-tuned Transformer-based models reached human inter-annotation agreement levels, later confirming that children's grammaticality increases steadily with age.
distorted: [CITE] propose a coding scheme for context-dependent grammaticality in child-caregiver conversations and show that, among a range of NLP models trained on over 4,000 annotated utterances, fine-tuned Transformer-based models perform best yet remain well below human inter-annotation agreement levels.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a two-stage framework—instruction-augmented supervised fine-tuning plus consistency alignment training—in which the second stage differentiates subtly different similar responses using self-rewards inferred from the first-stage model, without external human preference resources.
distorted: [CITE] propose a two-stage training framework in which consistency alignment training first helps a model generalize on following instructions, and instruction-augmented supervised fine-tuning is accomplished by external human preference resources.

faithful: [CITE] massively scale label interpretation learning by building a dataset from an entity linking benchmark with orders of magnitude more distinct entity types and descriptions, yielding strong zero- and few-shot NER results in in-domain, cross-domain, and cross-lingual settings.
distorted: [CITE] find that this increased signal yields strong results only in cross-lingual settings, with in-domain, cross-domain, zero- and few-shot NER used as currently used datasets for label interpretation learning.

faithful: [CITE] replaces conventional preference-based tuning with fine-grained, criteria-driven self-reflection that systematically explores and refines model responses before reinforcement learning fine-tuning, yielding improved core capabilities on Just-Eval, Factuality, and Mathematical Reasoning benchmarks rather than merely superficial stylistic alignment.
distorted: [CITE] argues that RLHF overcomes superficial alignment by leveraging fine-grained self-reflection, whereas RLRF lacks exploration, restricts desirable outputs, and across Just-Eval, Factuality, and Mathematical Reasoning demonstrates surface-level adjustment beyond core capabilities.

faithful: [CITE] instruction-tunes a large language model with multimodal document datasets so a single model performs document image classification and information extraction, reporting gains over the baseline across several document analysis tasks.
distorted: LayoutLLM [CITE] integrates document image understanding with large-scale language models, but still requires fine-tuning for each task and dataset, making the model expensive to train and operate while demonstrating no improvement over the baseline.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a Korean commonsense knowledge graph of 1,900 indirect emotional expressions spanning three inference types, and shows that a BART-based model fine-tuned on it surpasses existing Korean large language models, reaching performance comparable to GPT-4 Turbo.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a Korean commonsense knowledge graph comprising 1,900 indirect emotional expressions, validating that various existing Korean large language models fine-tuned with K-Act2Emo outperform the BART-based knowledge model and achieve performance levels comparable to GPT-4 Turbo.

faithful: [CITE] augments LLM cognitive-distortion classification with extraction of distortion-relevant utterance spans plus multi-agent debate over reasoning steps, reporting on a public dataset higher multi-class F1 and binary specificity, especially reducing false positives when debate summaries are supplied.
distorted: In cognitive distortion classification, [CITE] is summarized as showing that the baseline method improves the multi-class F1 score as well as binary specificity score, and ERD has high false positive rate.

faithful: [CITE] show that off-the-shelf GPT-4, prompted via the LangChain framework, can perform contradiction detection, sentence extraction, summarization, and parameter assignment to the 39 TRIZ engineering parameters within a single prompt, rivaling finetuned BERT-based classifiers for inventive concept extraction.
distorted: [CITE] finetunes OpenAI's GPT-4 for sentence-wise classification, finding that contradictions remain a challenge for such generative Large Language Models and that detection, summarization, and parameter extraction cannot be performed in a single prompt.

faithful: Comparing reference-based and reference-free evaluation metrics across eight datasets and eight evaluation models, [CITE] found that reference-free metrics correlate more strongly with human judgments and are more sensitive to language-quality deficiencies, though their reliability varies with the task and candidate text quality.
distorted: Across eight datasets and eight evaluation models, [CITE] shows that reference-based metrics exhibit a higher correlation with human judgment and greater sensitivity to deficiencies in language quality than reference-free metrics, with effectiveness that does not vary across tasks or depend on the quality of candidate texts.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CoTGenius, which synthesizes chain-of-thought prompts through complicate, diversify, and specify evolutions plus evolutionary-success and correctness filters, then fine-tunes Llama 2-Chat 7B and 13B and adds step-level debates among multiple debaters.
distorted: ChainLM [CITE] introduces CoTGenius, a framework developed based on two major evolution strategies alongside three filtering mechanisms, and shows that existing models exhibit enhanced proficiency in addressing complex reasoning problems compared to the fine-tuned Llama 2-Chat 7B and 13B models.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Financial-STS for comparing paired statements from the same company across periods, showing existing pretrained and LLM embeddings miss subtle year-over-year changes while its LLM-augmented pipeline outperforms classic STS-trained methods and generic LLM embeddings on human-annotated data.
distorted: [CITE] introduce the Financial-STS task and show that existing pretrained embedding models and generic LLM embeddings outperform their proposed LLM-augmented pipeline in discerning subtle semantic shifts between paired financial narratives from the same company across year-over-year periods.

faithful: [CITE] builds a factual-update benchmark by diffing Wikidata between 4 January 2021 and 27 February 2023, representing changes as subject-relation-object triples labeled new, obsolete, or static, with verbalization templates and cloze tests.
distorted: [CITE] present CounterFact, rather than the dataset constructed by comparing Wikidata at 4 January 2021 and 27 February 2023, as the realistic update setting that involves replacements, archival, and new entity insertions.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a black-box RAG framework with a bi-label document scorer, self-knowledge recognizer, and sub-document-level token reducer, raising Llama2-13B-Chat accuracy by 14.3% on TriviaQA, 19.9% on NQ, and 27.5% on PopQA while using about half the tokens.
distorted: [CITE] can improve the answering accuracy of Llama2-13B-Chat by 27.5% on TriviaQA, 14.3% on NQ and 19.9% on PopQA, respectively, and save approximately half of the tokens on average across the three datasets.

faithful: [CITE] propose a two-stage fine-tuning algorithm that applies an extra unlikelihood loss to instruction-conflicting samples with deliberately wrong translation directions, reducing the off-target translation ratio by 53.3% on average across 16 zero-shot directions and improving LLaMA by +5.7 SacreBLEU.
distorted: [CITE] address off-target translation with a two-stage fine-tuning algorithm that adds an unlikelihood loss on instruction-conflicting samples, reporting that their method increases the off-target translation ratio by 53.3% while yielding +16.4 SacreBLEU and +5.7 BLEURT over translation-finetuned LLaMA on IWSLT and WMT.

faithful: [CITE] trains a smaller language model as a query-complexity classifier, using automatically collected labels derived from model predictions and dataset inductive biases, to route each question to no-retrieval, single-step, or iterative retrieval-augmented generation, improving efficiency and accuracy on open-domain QA benchmarks.
distorted: Adaptive-RAG [CITE] addresses open-domain question answering by always applying the most sophisticated iterative retrieval-augmented LLM strategy to every incoming query, which enhances accuracy on complex multi-step queries but incurs unnecessary computational overhead on simple ones.

faithful: Unifying localization and mitigation, [CITE] attributes gender bias via causal mediation mainly to bottom MLPs on occupational pronouns’ last token and top attention on the sentence-final word, then applies LSDM against two baselines across three bias and seven competency datasets.
distorted: [CITE] trace the causal effects of different components' activation, indicating that the primary contributors to gender bias are the top attention modules acting on the last token of occupational pronouns and the bottom MLP module acting on the final word.

faithful: [CITE] shows that device-directed speech detection without a trigger phrase improves when an LLM fuses acoustic, lexical, and ASR-decoder signals, reporting up to 39% and 61% relative equal-error-rate gains over text-only and audio-only models.
distorted: In [CITE], text-only models trained on ASR 1-best hypotheses yield relative equal-error-rate improvements of up to 61% over the multimodal system that combines acoustic and lexical features in an LLM.

faithful: Comparing human segmentation with the unsupervised Morfessor model, [CITE] found that both handle concatenative Māori morphology such as compounding and affixation without allomorphy, yet only non-Māori-speaking New Zealanders also succeed on templatic processes like reduplication, suggesting human learning exceeds mere statistical recurrence.
distorted: [CITE] report that Morfessor succeeds in segmenting Māori words formed by reduplication and allomorphy, whereas non-Māori-speaking New Zealanders succeed only for concatenative processes such as compounding and affixation without allomorphy.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a two-stage approach that infers row and column headers before fine-tuning a causal language model to answer header-derived questions, raising BERTScore by up to 10% on table construction and 20% on content generation across four datasets.
distorted: [CITE] reports that prior single-stage attention parameters improve Generative Tables by up to 20% in BERTScore on table construction across E2E, WikiTableText, WikiBio, and RotoWire, where gTBLS is amenable to zero-shot pre-trained Large Language Models where fine-tuning is feasible.

faithful: [CITE] surveys recent large language model research by organizing advances into categories such as neural network architecture, context length extension, model alignment, training datasets, benchmarking, and efficiency, while also outlining open challenges and future research directions.
distorted: [CITE] surveys recent advances in large language models and introduces ChatGPT, a training dataset grounded in LLMs that has garnered widespread societal attention, while reviewing benchmarking and efficiency improvements across multiple models.

faithful: [CITE] presents a gamified prototype for Brazilian indigenous language learning that automatically derives exercises and questions from a dependency treebank plus a lexical database for Tupian languages, while urging community-partnered, education-oriented data collection.
distorted: [CITE] presents a fully deployed language-learning game for Brazilian indigenous languages, showing that automatically generated exercises from the Tupian dependency treebank and lexical database resolve ethical and practical implementation concerns, removing the need for new data gathering partnerships with indigenous communities.

faithful: [CITE] propose a decoding strategy that dynamically selects the sampling temperature based on entropy to better balance generation quality and diversity, reporting that it significantly outperforms existing strategies across four different generation benchmarks.
distorted: Prior work on decoding has shown that fixed temperature sampling significantly outperforms Entropy-based Dynamic Temperature (EDT) Sampling across 4 different generation benchmarks, suggesting that dynamically selecting the temperature parameter may not always be an optimal choice [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] proposes LexiContrastive Grounding, combining next-token prediction with a contrastive visual-grounding objective on early lexical layers, and reports roughly 5% perplexity improvements plus better word-learning and sentence-understanding results than CLIP, GIT, Flamingo, and Vokenization.
distorted: [CITE] propose LexiContrastive Grounding, a grounded language learning procedure combining next token prediction with a contrastive visual grounding objective, but report that it is outperformed in learning efficiency by vision-and-language learning procedures including CLIP, GIT, Flamingo, and Vokenization.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the Multi-Question (MQ) Sequence-BERT method for multi-class classification of MedMCQA questions into inferred medical subjects, reporting state-of-the-art accuracy of 0.68 on the development set and 0.60 on the test set.
distorted: [CITE] train deep neural networks for multi-class classification of questions into the inferred medical subjects, and Multi-Question (MQ) Sequence-BERT outperforms state-of-the-art results on MedMCQA with accuracy 0.68 and 0.60 on test and development sets, respectively.

faithful: [CITE] introduced the first dataset of human pragmatic-similarity judgments, pairing recorded dialog utterances with re-enactments rated on a continuous scale by six to nine judges, and reported average inter-judge correlations of 0.72 for English and 0.66 for Spanish.
distorted: [CITE] present the first collection of human judgments of pragmatic similarity between utterance pairs, rated on a continuous scale by 6 to 9 judges, with average inter-judge correlation as high as 0.72 for Spanish and 0.66 for English.

faithful: For zero-shot stance detection on social media, [CITE] uses a pre-trained language model as a world-knowledge source together with chain-of-thought in-context learning to generate intermediate reasoning steps, outperforming prior state-of-the-art and even fully supervised models on three Twitter datasets.
distorted: In contrast to interpretable zero-shot stance detection, [CITE] finds that current state-of-the-art models, including fully supervised models, outperform Stance Reasoner on 3 Twitter datasets and better generalize across targets.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a plug-and-play early-exiting decoder that, without extra trainable components, hierarchically skips layers according to current sequence length, and across five generation datasets it preserves about 90% of vanilla autoregressive quality while skipping almost half the layers.
distorted: [CITE] propose HSD with additional trainable components, and HSD can sustain almost half of computational workload while reducing 90% of text quality compared to vanilla autoregressive decoding on five text generation datasets.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked GPT-2, DialoGPT, ChatGPT, and FlanT5 for zero-shot counterspeech generation using three prompting strategies, finding that larger model sizes improved generation quality by 17% on two datasets while raising toxicity by 25%, with ChatGPT scoring best across all metrics.
distorted: For zero-shot counterspeech generation, [CITE] find that DialoGPT are much better at generating counter speech than GPT-2, ChatGPT and FlanT5 across all metrics, and that DialoGPT have high toxicity as compared to GPT-2 and FlanT5.

faithful: Building on an analysis that conversion matrices mapping each initial weight matrix W0 to LoRA’s A and B are similar across layers, [CITE] introduces CondLoRA, which derives task-adapted low-rank updates from one shared linear layer and matches LoRA with fewer trainable parameters.
distorted: [CITE] devise a method named CondLoRA and conclude that a single linear layer yields task-adapted low-rank matrices, despite the fact that the trainable parameters of LoRA are fewer than those of CondLoRA.

faithful: KnowLA [CITE] inserts an adaptation layer into an LLM that injects embeddings of entities mentioned in the input, trains that layer jointly with LoRA on instruction data, and reports effectiveness across six benchmarks using two LLMs and three knowledge graphs.
distorted: [CITE] study leveraging knowledge graph embeddings to improve effectiveness of PEFT: experiments on three benchmarks with six popular LLMs and two knowledge graphs demonstrate KnowLA changing parameters and input prompts to answer a question.

faithful: He et al. [CITE] propose RARG, a two-stage framework that retrieves and reranks evidence from a database of over one million academic articles and then aligns LLMs via RLHF with a reward promoting evidence utilization, outperforming baselines on COVID-19 in- and cross-domain datasets.
distorted: For COVID-19 misinformation, [CITE] introduces RARG, an end-to-end model trained without external knowledge, which is consistently outperformed by baselines on in- and cross-domain datasets, producing excessively repetitive responses that lack politeness and supporting facts.

faithful: For SemEval-2024 Task 9, [CITE] found that ensembling chain-of-thought prompts outperformed zero-/few-shot prompting and ranked 2nd on word puzzles but 13th on sentence puzzles, with proprietary LLMs beating open-source models.
distorted: [CITE] employ large language models to solve SemEval-2024 Task 9 puzzles through several prompting techniques, obtaining their best results with an ensemble of chain-of-thought prompts, placing 13th in the word puzzle subtask and 2nd in the sentence puzzle subtask.

faithful: Using the Anthropic Red-team dataset, [CITE] examined how reward models categorize risks such as Information Hazards, Malicious Uses, and Discrimination/Hateful content, finding via a purpose-built regression model that LLMs rate Information Hazards as less harmful and remain especially vulnerable to jailbreaking attacks in such scenarios.
distorted: Related work argues that LLMs consider Malicious Uses and Discrimination/Hateful content less harmful than Information Hazards, respond less stringently to them, and show significant jailbreaking vulnerability in those scenarios, as confirmed by regression [CITE].

faithful: For SemEval-2024 Task 8, [CITE] covered Tracks A–C (binary human-versus-machine detection, multi-way machine-generated-text classification, and human–machine mixed text detection), using discriminator-transformer ensembles as the main best-performing approach, with sentence transformers/statistical models in specific cases and zero-shot or fine-tuned FLAN-T5 for Tracks A and B.
distorted: For SemEval-2024 Task 8, [CITE] reports that zero-shot prompting and fine-tuning of FLAN-T5 were the best performing approaches for Track C, while the ensemble of discriminator transformer models was used only for Track A and B.

faithful: For SemEval-2024 semantic textual relatedness across supervised, unsupervised, and cross-lingual tracks in 14 languages, [CITE] was one of only two teams covering every language and track, with its best systems ensembling statistical machine learning, language-specific BERT models, and sentence transformers.
distorted: [CITE] achieved rankings ranging from 1st to 8th in supervised Track A, from 11th to 21st in unsupervised Track B, and from 5th to 12th in cross-lingual Track C across 14 languages.

faithful: Demonstrating that large language models can follow confidential evaluation rubrics without task-specific training, [CITE] combined prompting, chain-of-thought reasoning, and dynamic in-context learning to place second in the ML-ESG-3 Shared Task's Korean Impact Type track, additionally finding that longer general pre-training improves financial downstream performance.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate efficacy by ranking 2nd in the Shared-Task ML-ESG-3 Impact Type track for Korean without prompting, chain-of-thought reasoning, and dynamic in-context learning, updating GPT-4 on the provided training data.

faithful: For ancient Chinese historical texts, [CITE] introduces a named entity recognition and relation extraction corpus covering 13 dynasties across 1830 years, annotated with 14,194 entities of four types and 8,609 relations spanning twelve relation types, alongside baseline experiments including large language models.
distorted: For ancient Chinese historical texts, [CITE] introduces CHisIEC, a NER and RE corpus spanning 13 dynasties, which annotates 8,609 entities and 14,194 relations across four relation types and twelve entity types, and additionally evaluates Large Language Models.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned CodeGPT and UniXcoder on Haskell functions from a public HuggingFace dataset and introduced HumanEval-Haskell, finding that CodeGPT frequently emitted empty predictions and extra comments while UniXcoder more often produced incomplete or incorrect completions.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tuned CodeGPT and UniXcoder on Haskell functions sourced from HuggingFace and found through manual evaluation on HumanEval-Haskell that CodeGPT more often produces incomplete or incorrect predictions, whereas UniXcoder frequently generates empty predictions and extra comments.

faithful: [CITE] retrieves knowledge from multiple LLMs to enrich prompt templates and verbalizers for event temporal relation extraction, and its experiments on three widely recognized datasets show improved performance.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that traditional manually designed templates extract precise temporal knowledge; however, retrieval-augmented prompt templates and verbalizers leveraging large language models struggle across three widely recognized datasets.

faithful: [CITE] presents a simple continuous-scale framework for annotating noun-phrase genericity and reports a pilot dataset of 324 sentences, with continuous annotations evaluated against existing binary annotations on the same sentences.
distorted: [CITE] introduces an annotation framework for the fine-grained modeling of NPs' genericity, whose evaluation demonstrated that existing binary annotations capture nuanced aspects of genericity more effectively than the framework's continuous annotations.

faithful: [CITE] proposes the LENS framework, in which a decision problem's linguistic description evokes emotional responses and suggests behavioral norms that jointly shape strategic choices in economic games beyond outcome-based preferences.
distorted: [CITE] reviews experimental evidence that each path of the LENS model supports outcome-based preference models: the Linguistic description triggers Emotional responses and Norms of behaviour, which then fail to interact to shape an individual's Strategic choice.

faithful: For German fund prospectuses, [CITE] releases an anonymized NER/relation-extraction dataset in which three experts labeled 948 sentences with 5,969 entity annotations across Outsourcing, Company, Location and Software plus 4,102 Outsourcing-Company and Company-Location relations.
distorted: Centered around outsourcing practices within fund prospectuses in Germany, [CITE] yields 4,102 annotations for four entity types (Outsourcing, Company, Location and Software) and 5,969 relation annotations (Outsourcing-Company, Company-Location) on 948 sentences.

faithful: [CITE] formalizes Fusion-in-Context as a standalone task where models weave highlighted spans from multiple sources into a coherent passage containing all and only the target content, and contributes FuseReviews, a 1,000-instance review-domain dataset with evaluation metrics strongly correlating with human judgment.
distorted: Recent works such as [CITE] focus on the second subtask of content selection, formalize Fusion-in-Context whose input consists of highlighted spans, and propose assessing faithfulness and coverage of highlights that strongly correlate to opaqueness.

faithful: [CITE] finds that incorporating relevant and up-to-date entity knowledge benefits fake news detection, showing that entity information can help beyond entity-centric tasks such as entity linking.
distorted: [CITE] shows that entity-focused code-switching significantly enhances fake news detection, and that incorporating relevant and up-to-date knowledge of entities benefits zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on entity-centric tasks such as entity linking.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a capsule network-based method for detecting suicide-related psychological stressors in Persian tweets, a language largely overlooked by prior stressor-extraction research, and reported a binary classification accuracy of 0.83.
distorted: [CITE] propose a capsule-based learning approach for extracting psychiatric stressors related to suicide from Twitter, reporting a binary classification accuracy of 0.83 on non-Persian tweets, whereas most earlier automated approaches in this area targeted Persian language data.

faithful: For endangered-species NER, [CITE] used GPT-4 in-context learning to synthesize data for four endangered-species classes, had humans verify it into 3.6K gold sentences split evenly between NER and RE, and fine-tuned general and domain-specific BERT variants.
distorted: [CITE] experiments show general BERT is resource intensive because knowledge was distilled from domain-specific BERT variants to GPT-4 for named entity recognition.

faithful: Targeting the underexplored setting of free-size layout pattern generation, [CITE] pairs an expert LLM agent that interprets natural-language requirements and operates design tools with a controllable generator capable of conditional layout generation, pattern modification, and memory-friendly pattern extension, yielding high-quality large-scale patterns.
distorted: ChatPattern [CITE] utilizes a two-part system featuring an expert LLM agent that excels in conditional layout generation, pattern modification, and memory-friendly patterns extension, while the highly controllable layout pattern generator interprets natural language requirements and operates design tools.

faithful: [CITE] translates non-English Tunisian social-network comments into English with a No-English-to-English MT step, then applies LDA/HDP topic modeling and ARIMA forecasting, reporting gains over baselines on Coherence Score, U-mass and Topic Coherence plus RMSE-supported trend accuracy.
distorted: [CITE] uses LDA and HDP models as the No-English-to-English Machine Translation approach, while ARIMA time series analysis extracts pertinent topics; RMSE-based analysis is reported as confirming Coherence Score, U-mass, and Topic Coherence on Tunisian social networks.

faithful: [CITE] augments retrieval-augmented generation with a dynamic loop module that iteratively refines text against retrieved context, and reports improvements over prior state-of-the-art systems on benchmark datasets across BLEU, ROUGE, and perplexity.
distorted: LoRAG [CITE] enhances retrieval-augmented text generation through an iterative loop mechanism, yet experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that it fails to surpass existing state-of-the-art models in terms of BLEU score, ROUGE score, and perplexity.

faithful: Resolving inconsistent usage of the term "tool," [CITE] defines tools as external programs invoked by language models, systematically reviews tooling scenarios and approaches, and empirically compares tooling methods by measuring their compute requirements and benchmark performance gains.
distorted: [CITE] notes that prior works largely share a unified definition of tools as external programs used by LMs, and shows that tools have substantially enhanced performance on text generation tasks while offering few performance gains for tasks that require complex skills.

faithful: [CITE] argues that heterogeneity among information extraction tasks impedes progress, and addresses this by introducing a unifying perspective centered on text spans, recasting seemingly incongruous extraction tasks as variants of a single span-based task.
distorted: [CITE] reviews information extraction tasks within Natural Language Processing and argues that the heterogeneity among these tasks actually accelerates progress in the area, concluding that these seemingly incongruous tasks cannot be re-presented as variants of a single Span-Oriented Information Extraction task.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned BERT (Base-uncased), BERT (Large-uncased), and GPT-3 on roughly 2,000 DOTA 2 in-game chat messages gathered through publicly available APIs and manually labeled as non-toxic, mildly toxic, or toxic, achieving state-of-the-art results in detecting in-game trash talk.
distorted: [CITE] employs pre-trained BERT and GPT language models on DOTA 2 in-game chats, but uses around two thousand labeled non-toxic, mild, and toxic messages to train and test GPT-3 while excluding BERT (Base-uncased) and BERT (Large-uncased).

faithful: [CITE] compared response times from the same word production experiment run in the lab and online, and their power simulations indicated that online studies remain feasible but require larger sample sizes, entailing a non-negligible increase in manual labour.
distorted: [CITE] compared response time data from the same word production experiment conducted in the lab and on-line, finding that on-line data yield larger effect sizes and less unexplained variability, achieving sufficient power without the non-negligible increase in sample sizes and manual labour.

faithful: [CITE] convert structured EHR visit data—diagnoses, labs, and prescriptions—into natural language narratives and pair a predictor agent that generates reasoning with a critic agent that analyzes its incorrect predictions, achieving few-shot disease prediction performance competitive with traditional supervised learning methods.
distorted: [CITE] propose a novel approach that utilizes LLM agents with different roles: a critic agent that makes predictions and generates reasoning processes and a predictor agent that analyzes incorrect predictions and provides guidance for improving the reasoning of the critic agent.

faithful: [CITE] frames Korean evasions such as inserted special symbols and language-specific features as user-intended adversarial attacks, and shows layer-wise pooling over preceding layers—not only the last—lets clean-text-pretrained models match noisy-text-pretrained detectors as attack rates rise.
distorted: [CITE] introduce simple pooling strategies for Korean offensive language detection that focus on the last layer rather than preceding layers, and report performance degradation as the attack rate is increased without directly training such patterns.

faithful: [CITE] trains an isometric machine translation system with reinforcement learning using a phoneme-count-ratio reward, reporting that its proposed Phoneme Count Compliance metric improves by roughly 36% over prior state-of-the-art models on English-Hindi video dubbing.
distorted: [CITE] present an isometric NMT system that regulates output length by aligning the number of characters and words in source and target language texts, since these are closely associated with speech duration, improving the PCC score by approximately 36% on English-Hindi language pairs.

faithful: [CITE] adapts the Mistral architecture to Vietnamese through an additional continual pre-training phase with grouped-query and sliding-window attention, reporting a new VMLU state of the art and gains over existing Vietnamese LLMs in text classification, question answering, and text generation.
distorted: [CITE] presents vi-mistral-x, an English-centric Large Language Model based on the Mistral architecture, which through comprehensive testing underperforms existing Vietnamese LLMs on the VMLU benchmark in text classification, question answering, and text generation.

faithful: [CITE] tackle argument classification with an ensemble that couples BERT and ChatGPT-4-based fine-tuning, reporting gains of more than 10% in most cases over Transformer- and LSTM-based baselines on the Args.me, UKP, and US2016 datasets.
distorted: For argument classification on Args.me, UKP, and US2016, the presented results in [CITE] show that the LSTM-based model outperforms BERT+ChatGPT-4 and other Transformer-based models, the observed improvement greater than 10 in most cases.

faithful: [CITE] combined a BERT-based estimator of sentence-level suicide risk and negative sentiment with MentaLLaMa generative summaries plus extractive evidence selected via a suicidal-risk dictionary, and team SophiaADS placed 1st in CLPsych 2024 highlight extraction but 10th in summary generation.
distorted: [CITE] integrate supervised extractive and generative language models for suicide risk evidence summarization in the CLPsych 2024 shared task, combining BERT-based sentence-level risk estimation with MentaLLaMa, with their team SophiaADS achieving 1st place for summary generation while ranking only 10th for highlight extraction.

faithful: To help novice peer counselors at scale, [CITE] co-designed a multi-level feedback taxonomy with senior psychotherapy supervisors and released a publicly available dataset of 400 emotional support conversations annotated with comprehensive feedback.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that human supervision minimizes the risk of potentially harmful and low-quality feedback generation, and large language models lack mechanisms to provide detailed feedback to novices in 400 emotional support conversations.

faithful: [CITE] models clinically diagnosed users’ vlogs with an object-oriented graph attention network and cross-attention over visual, textual, and metadata features (title, description, duration), reporting 0.871 accuracy and 0.888 F1, plus 0.61 F1 on a benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] achieved an accuracy of 0.871 and an F1-score of 0.888 with a benchmark dataset, and vlogs from users with a clinical diagnosis achieved comparable results with prior studies (0.61 F1-score).

faithful: On the English portion of DreamBank, [CITE] frames character and emotion detection in dream reports as sequence-to-sequence generation and reports that supervised models beat an in-context-learning large language model despite using 28 times fewer parameters.
distorted: [CITE] present the first study on character and emotion detection in the English portion of the DreamBank corpus, reporting that a large language model using in-context learning performs better than supervised sequence-to-sequence models while having 28 times fewer parameters.

faithful: Through an iterative design-and-evaluation process with NLP experts, [CITE] introduces SemLa, a visual analytics system that spatializes datasets in model embedding space and supports contrastive analysis of lexical and conceptual patterns, with case studies reporting value for validation, debugging, and annotation.
distorted: For fine-grained text classification, SemLa [CITE] spatializes datasets in model embedding space and, unlike existing tools that remain suited to these additional challenges, falters when classes become more difficult to differentiate from one another.

faithful: For Arabic medical diagnosis, [CITE] compiled disease information, generated multiple messages per disease with different prompting techniques, and found ChatGPT responses matched actual diseases at about 76% average similarity, with chain prompting relatively better and 6.12-second mean API latency.
distorted: [CITE] assessed ChatGPT for Arabic medical diagnosis, reporting an average response time of around 76% for the ChatGPT API and average similarity scores of 6.12 seconds, with chain prompting demonstrating a relative advantage among the prompting techniques.

faithful: [CITE] moves latent features toward the decision boundary and reconstructs them into ambiguous text with soft labels, while mid-K sampling increases diversity; its ablations isolate soft-label and mid-K effects and show extensibility to curriculum data augmentation.
distorted: [CITE] shows that mixup and cutout are not limited by the discrete characteristics of text data, that pretrained language models require no additional considerations for robustness, and that soft labels with mid-K sampling limit diversity and extensibility.

faithful: [CITE] separately encodes static trait and dynamic state emotion embeddings, adds an emotion-guidance module, and trains a cross-contrastive decoder that aligns response-context trait/state emotions, with automatic and manual evaluations reporting gains over state-of-the-art baselines.
distorted: [CITE] generates empathetic responses by treating trait and state emotions in isolation, and both automatic and manual evaluation results demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and can generate more empathetic responses.

faithful: [CITE] survey how large language models can be applied to three categories of biomedical data—textual data, biological sequences, and brain signals—while examining challenges such as trustworthiness, personalization, and adaptation to multi-modal data representation.

[CITE] combine self-supervised contrastive learning with domain adversarial training to learn generator-invariant features, enabling detection of text from unseen models such as GPT-4 and Claude at scores within 4.7% of a fully supervised detector.
distorted: EAGLE [CITE] combines self-supervised contrastive learning with domain adversarial training to learn domain-invariant features for AI-generated text detection, outperforming a fully supervised detector by 4.7% on unseen target generators such as GPT-4 and Claude.

faithful: [CITE] augments zero-shot stance detection by using large language models with chain-of-thought prompting to turn texts into target-specific if-then rationales, then generating variants via semantic-correlation word replacement for a rationale-enhanced network.
distorted: For zero-shot stance detection, EDDA [CITE] employs a decoder that leverages large language models and chain-of-thought prompting to summarize texts into target-specific if-then rationales, while its encoder generates new samples using semantic correlation word replacement.

faithful: To improve OCR on chemistry publications, [CITE] introduces a dataset of synthetic and real-world records and demonstrates that transformer-based models perform best when trained with a small patch size across multiple domains using their proposed artifact-mimicking transformations.
distorted: In the OCR literature, [CITE] propose transformations that mimic synthetic qualities, since synthetic records contain artifacts not present in real-world records, and report that Nougat parses tables in PubMed articles.

faithful: [CITE] introduces DIIT, which induces reusable dialogue strategies as natural-language rules from expert demonstrations, and shows through automatic and human evaluation that these rules improve active listening, reduce unsolicited advice, and yield more collaborative, less authoritative motivational-interviewing responses than other demonstration-utilization methods.
distorted: For motivational interviewing, [CITE] proposes DIIT, which learns natural language inductive rules from instruction-following large language models, showing that its strategy descriptions reduce active listening skills and promote more authoritative responses than demonstration utilization methods.

faithful: [CITE] builds S3 graphs by merging document-level RST trees with sentence-level AMR graphs, encodes them as contextual features for headline generation, and adds hierarchical pruning to drop redundant nodes, reporting consistent gains over prior state-of-the-art systems on two datasets.
distorted: [CITE] constructs S3 graphs by combining sentence-level RST trees with document-level AMR graphs, and devises hierarchical structure pruning to dynamically screen the core document semantics within the graph.

faithful: For nested medical entity recognition, [CITE] formulates the task as machine reading comprehension with task-adaptive pre-training, word-pair embeddings, multi-granularity dilated convolutions, and a combined Biaffine-MLP predictor, surpassing prior state-of-the-art systems on the Chinese CMeEE benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] address Chinese nested medical NER with an MRC-based model using task-adaptive pre-training, word-pair embeddings and multi-granularity dilated convolution, demonstrating that on CMeEE the compared state-of-the-art (SOTA) models outperform their combined predictor of Biaffine and MLP.

faithful: [CITE] computes two interpretable sentence-level measures—sentence surprisal and sentence relevance—with multilingual large language models, reporting that they predict human sentence reading speeds with high accuracy and generalize across languages.
distorted: [CITE] introduce word-level metrics, sentence surprisal and sentence relevance, computed using multilingual large language models, and their results indicate that these metrics achieve high accuracy in predicting human word reading speeds, offering significant interpretability for research on the processing of words.

faithful: To support move analysis and automatic move identification, [CITE] introduces a multi-domain corpus of 33,988 research article abstracts annotated for move structure, constructed by combining expert manual annotation with BERT-based automatic annotation subsequently refined through expert modification.
distorted: For move analysis, [CITE] presents a multi-domain corpus of 33,988 annotated RA abstract instances constructed through two stages, in which initially a BERT-based model is employed for automatic annotation and subsequently expert annotators manually annotate high-quality data.

faithful: For Vietnamese, [CITE] introduces a five-dataset NLU benchmark spanning text classification, span extraction, and natural language understanding, and reports that CafeBERT—XLM-RoBERTa further pretrained on Vietnamese text—outperforms seven evaluated multilingual and monolingual models across all tasks.
distorted: [CITE] introduces VLUE, the first Vietnamese Language Understanding Evaluation benchmark, encompassing seven datasets across text classification, span extraction, and natural language understanding tasks, and evaluates five state-of-the-art multilingual and Vietnamese monolingual pre-trained models.

faithful: [CITE] constructs a stance-weighted graph connecting users to the named entities they mention and trains a Signed Graph Convolutional Network on it, showing that this unsupervised signal improves disagreement detection between Reddit comments and replies across controversial subreddits without relying on user history.
distorted: Experiments and ablation studies show that STEntConv improves disagreement detection on Reddit posts for controversial subreddit topics without user stances about named entities, given the need for platform-specific features and user history [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] distills large language models into smaller task-specific models by using zero-shot prompting to elicit teacher rationales and training students in a multi-task framework to mimic those rationales, reporting minimal performance loss even when rationale augmentation covers only part of the dataset.
distorted: Similarly, [CITE] distill LLMs into smaller application-specific models by finetuning student models on teacher rationales, demonstrating that handcrafted few-shot examples elicit rationales with a lower overall token count than zero-shot prompting, yielding cost savings under pay-per-token billing.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a hybrid annotation pipeline in which LLMs such as GPT-4 or Llama 2 label only a small subset of large unlabeled corpora to fine-tune BERT/RoBERTa encoders, reporting on IMDb and UMLS Meta-Thesaurus that accuracy drops slightly while cost-effectiveness improves substantially.
distorted: [CITE] propose LlamBERT, a hybrid approach that uses LLMs such as GPT-4 and Llama 2 to annotate the IMDb review dataset and UMLS Meta-Thesaurus for fine-tuning BERT and RoBERTa, reporting improved accuracy at slightly higher cost.

faithful: For location-linked transformer inputs, [CITE] introduces geotokens whose geographic coordinates matter more than sequence order, and adapts Rotary Position Embedding to spherical coordinates so embedding-space distances better reflect real-world distances.
distorted: For transformer input components each linked to a specific geological location, [CITE] show that token order is more vital than the geographical coordinates themselves, and improve on Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), the position encoding method introduced by the original transformer paper.

faithful: [CITE] built a Chinese CBT QA dataset by generating question–answer pairs with a prompt derived from Cognitive Behavioral Therapy structured intervention strategies, then fine-tuned a large language model that produced structured, professional, and highly relevant mental-health responses.
distorted: [CITE] concludes that previous methods excel in generating structured, professional, and highly relevant responses for Chinese psychological health Q&A, whereas the fine-tuned large language model persists in data scarcity, quality, and ensuring a solid foundation in psychological techniques.

faithful: [CITE] contend that instruction-following LLMs can assess argument quality more reliably by leveraging knowledge across contexts, but should be systematically instructed with argumentation theories, scenarios, and problem-solving strategies rather than merely fine-tuned for leaderboard performance.
distorted: Rather than argumentation theories and scenarios, [CITE] argues that instruction-following large language models enable much more reliable argument quality assessment towards leaderboard chasing on assessment tasks.

faithful: [CITE] introduces OBSINFOX, 100 French documents from 17 expert-flagged unreliable press sources annotated with 11 labels by eight annotators, whose Gate Cloud analysis indicated prevalent satire-like text and whose VAGO and neural-VAGO experiments probed links between Subjective and Fake News labels.
distorted: Prior work on French fake news introduced OBSINFOX [CITE], a corpus of 17 documents selected from 100 sources of French press and annotated using 8 labels by 11 annotators to compare human features with automated classifiers.

faithful: [CITE] instruction-tunes SEA-LION for Thai machine reading comprehension, evaluating on the XQuAD and Iapp_wiki_qa_squad datasets in 0-shot and 1-shot settings and proposing a new evaluation scheme scoring answer correctness, helpfulness, conciseness, and contextuality.
distorted: For Thai machine reading comprehension, [CITE] instruction fine-tune XQuAD and Iapp_wiki_qa_squad on top of WangchanLion and evaluate the resulting model on SEA-LION, where it produces answers faithful to the reference in 0-shot and 1-shot settings.

faithful: [CITE] reviews word sense disambiguation techniques spanning deep learning, lexical resources, and knowledge graphs such as WordNet, and introduces word sense extension (WSE) methods that improve disambiguation accuracy by predicting previously unseen word senses.
distorted: In contrast to earlier surveys, [CITE] demonstrates that the scarcity of sense annotated corpora has been fully resolved and that informal clinical texts no longer present complexity, identifying large language models and multilingual WSD systems as established methods rather than future directions.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a few-shot self-detection method in which LLMs identify whether specific instances appeared in their own training data, and show that models regenerate personal information, copyrighted text, and benchmark content in most cases even when such leaked data is scarce.
distorted: [CITE] establish that previous methods use few-shot learning with explicit learning and showed superior performance compared to the self-detection approach for personal information, copyrighted texts, and benchmark data.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrates theoretically and empirically that linear projection-based concept removal injects strong statistical dependencies into transformed representations, placing instances near opposite-labeled neighbors so that the original labels can sometimes be reconstructed using an anti-clustering method.
distorted: [CITE] investigates methods that use linear projections to remove information about a concept from a language representation, showing that these methods remove strong statistical dependencies from the transformed datasets, so the original labeling can in some cases be reconstructed by applying a clustering method.

faithful: [CITE] reports that a publicly released Korean biomedical NER corpus built with ChatGPT assistance yielded about a 20% improvement in medical NER performance over models trained on general Korean NER data.
distorted: For Korean medical NER, [CITE] showed that models trained on general Korean NER datasets achieve a 20% performance increase over models trained on KBMC, underscoring the benefits of general datasets over specialized tools like ChatGPT for healthcare language processing.

faithful: [CITE] introduces AB-LoRA to score the importance of individual LoRA ranks, then prunes redundant or negatively impacting ranks and reallocates the saved rank budget to Transformer modules needing higher capacity, outperforming recent baselines with comparable tunable parameters.
distorted: ALoRA [CITE] is implemented with a fixed intrinsic rank; AB-LoRA and ALoRA gradually prune important Transformer modules needing higher ranks and allocate the pruned LoRA budgets to abundant, negatively impacting LoRA ranks, and might not outperform recent baselines.

faithful: [CITE] trains a context-aware similarity encoder on 170k curated question pairs and reports that, for 1-shot NL2SQL example selection, it beats OpenAI and Cohere embeddings while lifting CodeLlama-7B downstream performance by 4-8%.
distorted: [CITE] trains a similarity prediction model on 170k question pairs and shows that strong competitive embedding models from OpenAI and Cohere outperform the proposed encoder, enhancing downstream NL2SQL performance in 1-shot in-context learning by 4-8% for GPT-3.5-turbo and 1-2% for CodeLlama-7B.

faithful: [CITE] enhanced sequence-to-sequence architectures for abstractive text summarization by fine-tuning hyper-parameters and experimenting with specific encoder-decoder combinations, evaluating the resulting models through numerous experiments on the widely used CNN/DailyMail dataset.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune hyper-parameters and attempt specific encoder-decoder combinations on the CNN/DailyMail dataset, finding that these modifications decrease the effectiveness of sequence-to-sequence models for abstractive text summarization.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a prompt-based framework in which LLMs generate topics from a document set and, under evaluation protocols for clustering efficacy, appropriately prompted models produce relevant topic titles and follow human guidelines to refine and merge overlapping topics.
distorted: The findings in [CITE] indicate that classic LDA with appropriate prompts can stand out as a viable alternative, generating relevant topic titles and adhering to human guidelines; however, large language models lack semantic understanding and the presence of overlapping topics.

faithful: [CITE] builds, for each patent phrase, a graph linking its focal patents to patents that cite or are cited by them, fuses localized contextual embeddings with global graph embeddings, and reports marked gains on a unique patent phrase similarity dataset.
distorted: [CITE] results demonstrate that retrieved phrase graph augmentation and the self-supervised learning objective do not perform satisfactorily in patent phrase similarity inference and existing semantic textual similarity methods that use localized contextual information significantly enhances representation in a self-supervised fashion.

faithful: [CITE] presents a retrieval-augmented generation framework that suggests Definitions articles for legislative texts under drafting by extracting existing term definitions from prior legislation into reusable definition elements, and its functionality is demonstrated and evaluated on a collection of EU documents from the energy domain.
distorted: LexDrafter [CITE] assists in drafting Definitions articles for legislative documents, but its retrieval augmented generation approach departs from the meaning of terms in ordinary, legal, and technical language, increasing ambiguities across different regulations.

faithful: [CITE] predicts facets from queries alone by multi-task learning to predict SERP as a target rather than a source and by combining an LLM with a small model, which improves overall performance over generating facets individually.
distorted: [CITE] enhance facet prediction by combining a Large Language Model (LLM) with a small model, demonstrating that facet generation individually by either model achieves better overall performance than the combined approach.

faithful: [CITE] identifies two definition biases in information extraction—among IE datasets and between IE datasets and instruction-tuning data—and proposes a multi-stage framework of bias measurement, bias-aware fine-tuning, and task-specific mitigation after three probing experiments.
