distorted: [CITE] conduct three probing experiments and discover that unified information extraction and large language models effectively address definition bias, while their multi-stage framework of definition bias measurement, bias-aware fine-tuning, and task-specific bias mitigation exhibits limitations.

faithful: [CITE] uses a gradient-based beam search to generate readable universal adversarial triggers that fool both pre-trained language models and prompt-based fine-tuned models, with reported transfer to Llama2 and GPT-3.5-turbo.
distorted: Related work [CITE], using a gradient-based beam search algorithm to generate UATs, maintains trigger tokens that are often unreadable tokens or characters and can be easily distinguished from natural texts with adaptive defenses.

faithful: [CITE] performs unsupervised passage reranking by prompting instruction-tuned LLMs without any additional fine-tuning, combining pairwise reranking with a soft score aggregation technique, and it surpasses both unsupervised baselines and an instruction-tuned reranker on the BEIR benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that InstUPR relies on extensive training with query-document pairs and retrieval-specific instructions, and that on BEIR soft score aggregation with pairwise reranking is outperformed by unsupervised baselines and an instruction-tuned reranker.

faithful: Addressing the NL2Repo task of generating a full code repository from natural language requirements, [CITE] applies a multi-layer sketch via three modules—RepoSketcher, FileSketcher, and SketchFiller—and is evaluated with the SketchEval benchmark, the SketchBLEU metric, and a 30-participant VSCode plugin study.
distorted: For NL2Repo, [CITE] includes three modules: SketchFiller first generates a repository's directory structure; FileSketcher finally fills details for each function, and RepoSketcher conducting empirical studies.

faithful: [CITE] introduces KIT-19, a Korean instruction-tuning dataset built from 19 existing open-source Korean NLP datasets rather than ChatGPT-generated or translated data, and demonstrates that a Korean pretrained LLM fine-tuned on it significantly outperforms existing Korean LLMs.
distorted: For Korean instruction tuning, [CITE] builds an instruction dataset by translating datasets built in English with ChatGPT, and shows that existing Korean LLMs significantly outperform the Korean Pretrained LLM trained on it.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates clinical LLMs by defining an LLM-specific clinical pathway, collecting Standardized Patient cases, and using a multi-agent simulator with Retrieval-Augmented Evaluation; the authors instantiate the paradigm as a urology benchmark with an LCP, SP dataset, and automated RAE.

Fine-tuning BERT on six GLUE tasks supported the prediction that semantic tasks strengthen attention centered on content words whereas syntactic tasks strengthen attention centered on function words, and some layers showed task-agnostic lexical-category biases [CITE].
distorted: [CITE] fine-tunes BERT on six GLUE downstream tasks and substantiates the hypothesis that semantic tasks intensify attention scores centered on function words, while syntactic tasks enhance attention scores centered on content words.

faithful: [CITE] introduces SuperCD, an active-learning approach that extracts superposition concepts representing alternative generalization boundaries from illustrative examples, retrieves matching instances from a large corpus for annotators to label, and learns a universal concept extractor and retriever from openly available knowledge bases.
distorted: In a related active learning paradigm, [CITE] asks annotators to identify superposition concepts from illustrative instances, while the concept extractor retrieves corresponding instances from large-scale text corpus and the superposition instance retriever learns FS-NER models.

faithful: [CITE] introduce Wikipedia Hyperlink-based Location Linking, which assigns coordinates by following article hyperlinks, and construct a corpus of 1.3M Wikipedia articles averaging about 7.8 unique location expressions each, with 45.6% of expressions ambiguous.
distorted: For geoparsing evaluation, [CITE] introduces the WHLL corpus of 1.3M Wikipedia articles with about 7.8 unique location expressions each, reporting that 45.6% are unambiguous and refer to exactly one location.

faithful: [CITE] introduces ViTLP, which pre-trains on document images with hierarchical language and layout modeling to generate interleaved text-layout sequences, and adds multi-segment generative pre-training so word-intensive documents of arbitrary length can be processed.
distorted: In visual document understanding, [CITE] shows that visual document understanding can boost the performance of pre-training techniques, and that ViTLP can process word-intensive documents of any length by Transformers.

faithful: [CITE] improves few-shot relation classification by contrastively aligning [CLS], prompt [MASK], and entity-marker representations, reporting that combining these views is especially useful when relation descriptions are unavailable while remaining robust when such descriptions exist.
distorted: In few-shot relation classification, [CITE] aligns the [CLS] token, the [MASK] token, and entity marker tokens with contrastive learning, showing that multiple sentence representations extract discriminative information only when relation descriptions are available and remain untapped otherwise.

faithful: To address data scarcity for low-resource Sinhala, [CITE] introduces the largest Sinhala news corpus to date, comprising over 500,000 articles from popular news websites, alongside benchmarks for news media identification, category prediction, and headline generation.
distorted: For low-resource languages such as Sinhala, where substantial training data and benchmarking datasets are available, [CITE] introduces NSINA, a news corpus of over 500,000 articles supporting news media identification, news category prediction, and news headline generation.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates statistical, neural, and pre-trained detectors for mono- and multilingual machine-generated text across domains, reporting 86.9% test accuracy on subtask-A mono and 83.7% on subtask-B alongside an error analysis.
distorted: [CITE] obtains an accuracy of 83.7% on the test set of subtask-A mono and 86.9% for subtask-B, detecting machine-generated text across various domains in both mono-lingual and multi-lingual contexts.

faithful: [CITE] annotate two dialog corpora with Traum-style Grounding Acts and Grounding Units plus a degree-of-grounding measure, and release a baseline for evaluating how well current language models classify dialogs’ grounding acts.
distorted: [CITE] present Traum's framework as the annotation of two dialog corpora, with substantial progress in Large Language Models and current Language Models categorizing the grounding acts.

faithful: To overcome the monolingual, English-only limitation of CrisisTransformers, [CITE] introduced two multilingual sentence encoders, CT-XLMR-SE and CT-mBERT-SE, that embed crisis-related social media texts from over 50 languages into a single shared vector space where semantically similar texts lie close together regardless of language.
distorted: [CITE] proposes CT-XLMR-SE and CT-mBERT-SE, monolingual sentence encoders within the CrisisTransformers family that process only English texts, embedding crisis-related social media texts into distinct vector spaces.

faithful: [CITE] evaluate patent-specific embeddings by treating examiner-confirmed patent interferences as ground-truth similarity, showing that their domain-adapted Patent SBERT-adapt-ub surpasses prior state-of-the-art, while large static word2vec-style models trained on extensive data remain competitive with contextual transformers.
distorted: Using patent interferences as ground-truth for maximum similarity, [CITE] demonstrate that large static models such as word2vec and doc2vec trained on extensive data consistently outperform contextual embeddings, and that Patent SBERT-adapt-ub does not surpass the current state-of-the-art in patent similarity.

faithful: Fine-tuning BART and MarianMT for text error correction, [CITE] reports that both models reduced erroneous sentences by over 20%, with BART’s gain much larger for spelling errors (24.6%) than grammatical errors (8.8%).
distorted: Prior work on transformer-based error correction [CITE] shows that, after transfer learning with an available dataset, BART can handle grammatical errors far better (24.6%) than spelling errors (8.8%), while both models bring down erroneous sentences by 20+%.

faithful: For explainable fact-checking, [CITE] introduce a 16K-sample multilingual dataset on the 2022 Russia-Ukraine conflict pairing real-world claims with optimized evidence and referenced explanations, alongside an LLM-based pipeline that retrieves and summarizes Web evidence.
distorted: Relatedly, [CITE] proposes RU22Fact, a Large Language Model that automatically retrieves and summarizes 16K samples from the Web, and constructs an end-to-end explainable fact-checking dataset containing real-world claims, optimized evidence, and referenced explanation.

faithful: [CITE] conducted the first large-scale computational sociolinguistics study of bragging on U.S. Twitter, finding that bragging prevalence declines over time within the same user population and is more common among younger, more educated, and popular users.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] conducts the first large scale study of bragging behavior on Twitter (U.S.), finding that the prevalence of bragging increases over time within the same population of users and that younger, more educated and popular users are less likely to brag.

faithful: [CITE] mines naturally structured mixed-modal QA pairs from StackOverflow and demonstrates that modality-agnostic contrastive pre-training on this community data significantly outperforms models pre-trained on bimodal and unimodal pairs from CodeSearchNet across a wide range of code retrieval benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] introduces ProCQA, a large-scale programming question answering dataset extracted from CodeSearchNet, and demonstrates that pre-training on crafted bi-modal and uni-modal pairs yields significant performance improvements over models relying on naturally structured mixed-modal QA pairs from the StackOverflow community.

faithful: [CITE] showed that continued training with machine translation objectives failed to improve cross-lingual natural language understanding across multiple tasks, attributing this—through similarity measures and parameter analysis—to output separability that aids translation but harms transfer.
distorted: [CITE] show that machine translation as a continued training objective enhances cross-lingual representation learning on multiple cross-lingual natural language understanding tasks, and that explicit sentence-level alignment is well suited to fostering cross-lingual transfer pretraining.

faithful: [CITE] introduced multilingual temporal expression taggers trained partly on Professor HeidelTime, a weakly labeled news corpus spanning 138,069 documents and 1,050,921 temporal expressions, matching HeidelTime's effectiveness with markedly improved runtime across six languages.
distorted: Prior work shows HeidelTime matching TEI2GO runtime with significantly improved effectiveness, achieving state-of-the-art results in six languages from Professor HeidelTime with 1,050,921 documents and 138,069 temporal expressions [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] propose a method for identifying the precedent relied upon by legal outcome prediction models and, using a taxonomy of legal precedent, show that although these models predict outcomes reasonably well, their use of precedent differs from that of human judges.
distorted: [CITE] develop a taxonomy of legal precedent and show that legal outcome prediction models explain their reasoning by referring to precedent, finding that the neural models' use of precedent is like that of human judges.

faithful: Probing Mandarin and Vietnamese as case studies, [CITE] found that self-supervised spoken language models encode lexical tone to a significant degree even when trained exclusively on data from non-tonal languages.
distorted: [CITE] analyze the tone encoding capabilities of self-supervised Spoken Language Models using Mandarin and Vietnamese as case studies, showing that SLMs follow the same developmental trajectory as native and non-native human participants but do not behave similarly in tone and consonant perception studies.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Robust and Adaptive Prototypical learning, combining prototype attraction for within-cluster compactness and prototype dispersion for between-cluster separation, and reports an average +5.5% gain over state-of-the-art methods, including a large language model, on CLINC, BANKING, and StackOverflow.
distorted: [CITE] propose the RAP framework for New Intent Discovery, where adaptive prototypical dispersing learning (APDL) compels instances to gravitate toward their prototype for within-cluster compactness, while robust prototypical attracting learning (RPAL) maximizes between-cluster distance, yielding average +5.5% improvement on CLINC, BANKING, and StackOverflow.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a corpus of space-innovation ideas spanning informal, technical, academic, and business-oriented writing styles, and demonstrate that multitask learning with an extended version annotated by a large generative language model improves sentence and sequential sentence classifiers for salient information detection.
distorted: [CITE] trains different sentence and sequential sentence classifiers and shows that the manually annotated dataset, rather than the extended version annotated using a large generative language model, can be leveraged using multitask learning to train better classifiers.

faithful: [CITE] models contextual lemmatization as token classification from word-SES label pairs, reporting across seven languages that separating casing from edit operations helps chiefly in highly inflected languages, while multilingual encoders outperform language-specific ones in every setting.
distorted: [CITE] compare Shortest Edit Scripts methods for contextual lemmatization across seven languages, including English, Basque, Turkish and Polish, reporting that language-specific pre-trained masked language encoder-only models consistently outperform their multilingual counterparts in every evaluation setting.

faithful: To avoid the thousands of iterative denoising steps required by diffusion language models, [CITE] learns neural ordinary differential equation models that transport between source and target distributions, consistently outperforming baselines on three fine-grained control tasks and multiple text editing tasks.
distorted: Language Rectified Flow [CITE] generates high-quality text editing samples by iteratively denoising for thousands of steps, a complexity that increases inference time and leaves it underperforming baselines on three fine-grained control tasks.

faithful: [CITE] compiled 2,490 eligibility criteria annotated for seven exclusion types across five trial categories, finding that classifiers trained on phase 3 cancer trials transferred to criteria common in non-cancer trials but faltered on cancer-specific ones such as prior malignancy.
distorted: [CITE] show that models trained on the extensive cancer dataset can effectively handle criteria disproportionately prevalent in cancer trials, like prior malignancy, and struggle with criteria commonly found in non-cancer trials, such as autoimmune diseases.

faithful: For German biographical relation extraction, [CITE] uses guided distant supervision to build over 80,000 instances spanning nine relationship types and additionally releases 2,000 manually annotated evaluation instances with trained models.
distorted: [CITE] applies guided distant supervision to create the largest biographical English relationship extraction dataset, with more than 80,000 instances for nine relationship types and a manually annotated German dataset of 2000 instances.

faithful: [CITE] proposes TABDet, which combines final-layer logits with an efficient pooling technique to form a unified logit representation for sentence classification, question answering, and named entity recognition, improving detection over task-specific methods.
distorted: TABDet [CITE] is a task-specific backdoor detector relying on intermediate feature representation and reconstructing potential triggers, demonstrating superior detection efficacy on sentence classification but struggling with question answering and named entity recognition, where traditional task-specific methods are more effective.

faithful: [CITE] quantify female objectification in 19th and 20th century novels using two metrics—an agency bias score based on grammatical agency and an embedding-based appearance bias score—and find that male-perspective novels systematically objectify female characters, whereas female-perspective novels show no statistically significant objectification.
distorted: [CITE] finds that novels written from a female perspective systematically objectify female characters, while novels written from a male perspective do not exhibit statistically significant objectification of any gender.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a benchmark for identifying plausible knowledge missing from ontologies, showing that NLI-based and concept embedding approaches are complementary, with hybrid strategies achieving the best overall results, while large language models find the task highly challenging even after fine-tuning.
distorted: Prior work on ontology completion has shown that Large Language Models achieve the best overall results after fine-tuning, substantially outperforming hybrid strategies that combine Natural Language Inference with concept embeddings [CITE].

faithful: To improve robustness on user-generated content, [CITE] proposes RoLASER, a teacher-student English encoder trained only on standard and synthetic UGC-like data, which achieves up to 2x and 11x better scores than LASER on natural and artificial UGC.
distorted: [CITE] show that LASER significantly improves RoLASER's robustness to both natural and artificial UGC data achieving up to 2x and 11x better scores on standard data.

faithful: [CITE] approximates OntoNotes with singleton mentions by combining nested-NER predicted mentions and syntax-tree features, reporting about 94% recall on sampled gold singletons and a +1.1 average F1 out-of-domain stability gain on OntoGUM.
distorted: [CITE] indicates that reconstructed singleton training improves OntoNotes over end-to-end systems by +1.1 avg. F1, while recall improvements deliver more substantial benefits than precision for resolving coreference chains on OntoGUM.

faithful: To reduce reliance on costly manually annotated corpora, [CITE] generates weakly-supervised ABSA labels by combining large language model outputs with syntactic dependency structures, which recover domain-specific aspect terms that LLMs tend to overlook, and evaluates this hybrid on aspect term extraction and aspect sentiment classification across multiple datasets.
distorted: [CITE] propose a hybrid transfer learning approach for aspect term extraction and aspect sentiment classification in which annotations generated by LLMs complement syntactic dependency structures, as traditional syntactic dependencies may overlook domain-specific aspect terms.

faithful: [CITE] automated knowledge-concept tagging for math questions using large language models, showing through extensive experiments with multiple representative LLMs that zero/few-shot prompting is a promising approach, and deriving empirical conclusions about key success factors from case studies.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that prior manual methods are a promising tool for concept tagging in math questions, and that Large Language Models face inability to meet rapidly growing demand.

faithful: [CITE] propose a common ground tracking approach in which a deep neural model trained on multimodal annotations—including speech transcriptions, prosodic features, gestures, and actions—predicts dialogue moves whose outputs cascade into formal closure rules grounded in belief axioms to identify shared beliefs and questions under discussion.
distorted: [CITE] argues that common ground tracking has received considerable attention in dialogue modeling, whereas dialogue state tracking remains less studied but just as important for task-oriented dialogue.

faithful: [CITE] introduce an open-source large language model whose long-context capability is developed by first training on 4k-token sequences and then extending to 32k tokens during pre-training and fine-tuning, yielding strong performance on the 200k-token Needle-in-a-Haystack test.
distorted: InternLM2 [CITE] is an open-source LLM that outperforms its predecessors across 30 dimensions and 6 benchmarks, initially trained on 32k tokens before advancing to 4k tokens, and exhibiting remarkable performance on the 4k Needle-in-a-Haystack test.

faithful: Using BLiMP minimal pairs to decode grammaticality labels from intermediate representations, [CITE] reports that GPT-2 captures syntactic grammaticality robustly across its first third of layers while still distributing related information through later layers.
distorted: [CITE] uses BLiMP minimal pairs to reveal that GloVe and RNN language models capture abstract linguistic structures in intermediate layers that self-supervised language models cannot learn, and syntax is harder to capture than morphological and semantics/syntax interface-related features.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a contrastive learning approach for hierarchical text classification in which a structure encoder directly generates positive samples from the document embedding by extracting syntactic information from the label hierarchy through structural entropy minimization, reporting superior results on three common datasets.
distorted: [CITE] proposes an information lossless contrastive learning strategy for HTC that relies on human-designed augmentation rules to generate contrastive samples, adequately reserving the semantic and syntactic information inherent in the input sample.

faithful: For documents pairing images with text, [CITE] presents the first systematic evaluation of multimodal topic modeling, introducing two models and two metrics, and finds the better-performing method changes with metric–dataset combinations while human judgments match the proposed metrics.
distorted: [CITE] indicates that one method outperforms the other on multimodal datasets containing both text and images, the extent depends not on metrics and dataset combinations, and succinct human evaluation aligns not with outcomes determined by proposed metrics.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a longitudinal, multimodal dataset in which learners studied Arabic, Spanish, or Chinese from scratch over two years exclusively through online instruction, with every Zoom lesson recorded and semi-automatically annotated with speaker and language IDs plus transcripts.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a longitudinal dataset in which participants learn one of two target languages from scratch over a span of three years, though it captures only a single modality and lacks control over the learning process.

faithful: Using the first large-scale Japanese multi-domain task-oriented dialogue corpus, [CITE] evaluates dialogue-state tracking and response generation with state-of-the-art MultiWOZ2.2 and LLM-based methods, reports benchmark quality comparable to MultiWOZ2.2, and finds LLMs' Japanese task-completion limited in human interactions.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrated advancement in task completion capabilities of LLMs in Japanese interactive dialogues with human participants, while JMultiWOZ does not provide a benchmark on par with MultiWOZ2.2.

faithful: [CITE] addresses FEVEROUS fact verification by pairing pre-trained models for text and tabular data with a lightweight attention mechanism, eliminating rule-based modality conversion to preserve original evidence context while achieving competitive performance close to top-tier systems on the FEVEROUS benchmark.
distorted: On the FEVEROUS benchmark, [CITE] relies on extensive preprocessing and rule-based transformations of tabular data into text, whereas existing works preserve the original evidence's context by nullifying the need for modality conversion.

faithful: To narrow the ASR-NLP gap in clinical text, [CITE] released BioASR-NER, a corpus of nearly 2,000 clean and noisy recordings targeting adverse drug reactions and BTACT exam entities, and proposed GPT-4-based transcript cleaning evaluated under zero-shot and few-shot settings.
distorted: [CITE] introduces BioASR-NER, a novel dataset of almost 2,000 recordings, noting that prior works have primarily studied ASR's efficiency in noisy environments, leaving a research gap concerning performance in clean recordings.

faithful: [CITE] sampled 300 instances from three natural-language-explanation datasets, gathered 900 human informativeness and clarity ratings plus an 8,346-annotation paired-comparison baseline, and found ChatGPT matched humans better on coarser scales, with paired comparisons and semantically similar dynamic prompts improving alignment.
distorted: [CITE] sample 8,346 data instances from three NLE datasets, collect 300 human annotations for informativeness and clarity, and show ChatGPT aligns better with humans in more fine-grained scales under paired comparisons and dynamic prompting.

faithful: To standardize prompt compression research, [CITE] introduces a modular, plug-and-play toolkit bundling state-of-the-art compressors with diverse datasets and evaluation metrics, benchmarking them across ten tasks ranging from summarization and code completion to boolean expressions and lies recognition.
distorted: PCToolkit [CITE] is a unified plug-and-play solution for compressing prompts in Large Language Models, but its modular design does not allow easy integration of new datasets and metrics, and its evaluations include only reconstruction and summarization.

faithful: To mitigate over-correction in Chinese grammatical error correction without ensembling multiple systems, [CITE] trains a rewriting model on an over-correction dataset constructed via K-fold cross inference, yielding an 18.2-point precision improvement on the FCGEC dataset while leaving error recall unchanged.
distorted: For CGEC, [CITE] reports that LM-Combiner alleviates over-correction on FCGEC by improving error recall (+18.2 Recall) while ensuring the precision of the original system remains unchanged, even for black-box GEC systems such as ChatGPT.

faithful: [CITE] introduces EREN (Edit models by REading Notes), a prompting-based approach showing that instruction-finetuned LLMs can reliably follow contextual knowledge and ignore irrelevant context, integrating multiple edits and outperforming prior editors on a newly collected dataset of harder irrelevant questions.
distorted: [CITE] show current state-of-the-art methods integrate knowledge from multiple edits and correctly respond to syntactically similar but semantically unrelated inputs, unlike EREN.

faithful: [CITE] distills teacher-model knowledge to flag noisy or incorrect in-batch negatives before the contrastive loss and introduces AdapACSE, an adaptive angular-margin supervised contrastive objective, evaluated on widely used Semantic Textual Similarity benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] proposes KDMCSE, which overcomes the limitation of suspicious and noisy negative examples by taking the rest of the batch as negative samples without reviewing when forming contrastive pairs, enhancing discrimination on Semantic Textual Similarity benchmarks.

faithful: Building on the Graph of Thoughts prompting paradigm, [CITE] dynamically adjusts its reasoning graph according to data characteristics for scientific abstract generation, with experiments reporting a cost-effectiveness of only 43.7% to 56.4% of other multi-round query prompt approaches.
distorted: For scientific abstract generation, [CITE] propose Dynamic Graph of Thoughts (DGoT), an LLM multi-round query prompt approach that inherits GoT's advantages but increases model reasoning cost to 43.7% to 56.4% above other multi-round query prompt approaches.

faithful: In a two-player reference game requiring coordination over vision and language observations, [CITE] show that PPO agents bootstrapped with heuristic partner behaviors achieve high success rates, and that neural partner pairings reduce measured joint effort across repeated play.
distorted: [CITE] propose an interactive reference game in which two players coordinate on vision and language observations, and show that a pairing of neural partners trained with Proximal Policy Optimization achieves lower measured joint effort than a reasonable heuristic pairing, leaving little room for improvement.

faithful: Rather than the earlier indirect strategy of first learning to encode brain activity from text, [CITE] directly compares candidate text with text embeddings predicted from brain signals, achieving average gains of 77% in BLEU and 54% in METEOR over the prior state of the art.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] on reconstructing continuous language from brain activities claims the indirect approach of encoding brain activity from text and aligning generation with predicted brain responses surpasses direct brain-to-text-embedding mapping, improving BLEU and METEOR by 77% and 54%.

faithful: Building on NLI-based training, [CITE] scales a multilingual sentence encoder to 5.7 billion parameters via low-rank adaptation (LoRA), showing that larger models improve embedding quality, with the greatest gains for low-resource languages and those linguistically distant from English.
distorted: [CITE] extends Sentence T5, an existing monolingual model, with low-rank adaptation to 5.7 billion parameters, verifying that the NLI-based prior approach outperforms the method and that languages with fewer resources benefited less from the parameter increase.

faithful: [CITE] trains a linear classifier over a large search space of high-order features to rank fine-grained agreement and word-order rules extracted from treebanks, associating each rule with statistics and recovering both well-known and lesser-known patterns in Spanish, French, and Wolof.
distorted: [CITE] extract formal grammars from treebanks and use a linear classifier that captures significant grammar rules for agreement in Wolof, while Spanish and French lack quantitative data for word order.

faithful: [CITE] frames intent classification and slot filling as language generation for instruction-tuned LLMs; with FLAN-T5 11B it beats a state-of-the-art joint IC+SF method and GPT-3.5 175B in-context learning, improving slot filling by 11.1–32.2 percentage points.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] shows that in-context learning with GPT3.5 (175B) outperforms ILLUMINER using the FLAN-T5 11B model and the state-of-the-art joint IC+SF method, particularly in slot filling by 11.1--32.2 percentage points.

faithful: To address ambiguity in Japanese VQA arising from frequently omitted subject and object terms, [CITE] introduced the GazeVQA dataset grounded in user gaze and showed that incorporating gaze target estimation improved VQA accuracy in some cases while revealing recurring task problems.
distorted: In conversational situations, [CITE] showed that a VQA system on GazeVQA improved the performance of gaze target estimation in some cases and clarified ambiguous Japanese questions using contexts that omit user gaze information.

faithful: [CITE] combined text mining, social network analysis, and the Semantic Brand Score to profile psychological traits demanded in Operations and Supply Chain Management job postings, further applying topic modeling and breaking results down by region, organization size, and seniority level.

To bypass transformer context-length limits in in-context learning, [CITE] partitions demonstrations into equal-sized windows fitting the model's maximum length, applies a voting mechanism to select the most relevant window as posterior context, and uses Bayes' theorem for prediction, maintaining linear efficiency without fine-tuning.
distorted: NBCE [CITE] requires fine-tuning and dependence on particular model architectures, employs Bayes' theorem to select the most relevant window, introduces voting to generate the test task, and shows alternative methods consistently outperforming NBCE as the number of demonstration examples increases.

faithful: For Russian bias evaluation, [CITE] introduces nearly 2,000 volunteer-written sentence pairs validated by native-speaking crowdworkers across 19 subdomains in four domains, with each pair contrasting a stereotype-reinforcing sentence against one that contradicts it.
distorted: For Russian-language bias evaluation, [CITE] presents a diagnostic dataset of nearly 2,000 subdomains covering 19 unique sentence pairs across 4 domains, in which the first sentence of each pair contradicts a harmful stereotype and the second reinforces it.

faithful: [CITE] introduces InstrMulti102, a multilingual multimodal instruction dataset covering 102 languages, and treats the image as a central language to minimize cross-lingual representation distance, reporting large gains over text-only and multilingual multimodal baselines.
distorted: In [CITE], results show that the multilingual multimodal instruction dataset InstrMulti102 outperforms m3P by a large margin under the low-resource and massively multilingual scenario.

faithful: A literature review in [CITE] proposes a taxonomy for 25 identified paraphrasing sub-tasks and, with classifiers assigning instances to those tasks, shows that their distributions differ substantially across known paraphrase corpora.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] reviewed 25 paraphrasing (sub-)tasks and, using classifiers trained on the known paraphrase corpora, found that the distributions of task-specific instances are largely consistent across these corpora, so that results obtained without clearly defined paraphrase conditions remain comparable.

faithful: [CITE] show that dialog agents trained on data synthesized directly from dialog trees achieve comparable success to models trained on human data, with human evaluation finding no statistically significant differences in either objective or subjective measures.
distorted: [CITE] scales Conversational Tree Search to two new datasets: ONBOARD, a medical domain built from a subset of Wikipedia articles related to scalp and head symptoms, and DIAGNOSE, a new domain helping foreign residents moving to a new city.

faithful: To reduce false-positive supervision in table-text retrieval, [CITE] trains on data filtered by a false-positive detection model's question-relevance scores and adds a rank-aware column encoder fine-tuned to identify minimum and maximum values within a column.
distorted: For table-text open-domain question answering, [CITE] reduces false positive labels by keeping instances with lower question-relevance scores, and DoTTeR outperforms strong baselines on downstream QA tasks but not retrieval recall.

faithful: To prevent cross-contamination between conversational initiatives, [CITE] introduces a dynamic prefix-tuning framework that encodes initiative factors in separate prefix parameters, uses attention to select among them during generation, and outperforms baselines on two public dialogue datasets in both automatic and human evaluations.
distorted: [CITE] focus on training a holistic response generation model without any distinction among different initiatives, which leads to cross-contamination, and on two public dialogue datasets previous baselines outperform IDPT on automatic metrics and human evaluations.

faithful: For reference-free evaluation of text simplification, [CITE] proposes a model-based metric trained with a three-stage curriculum and arbitrarily scalable pretraining, which outperforms reference-based metrics at predicting overall human ratings while requiring only a small set of annotations and no references at inference.
distorted: REFeREE [CITE] is a reference-free model-based metric with a 3-stage curriculum that outperforms existing reference-based metrics in predicting specific ratings, though it reaches only competitive and consistent performance in predicting overall ratings.

faithful: [CITE] augments named-entity correction with entity descriptions via an EDA-MLM dense-retrieval model, reducing named-entity CER relative to PED-NEC by about 7% on AISHELL-1 and 46% on the high-confusion Homophone dataset.
distorted: In this family of fast lightweight NEC models for ASR transcription, experiments in [CITE] confirm PED-NEC outperforms DANCER on Homophone by a CER reduction of about 7% relatively, and DANCER offers a pronounced CER reduction of 46% relatively over PED-NEC on AISHELL-1.

faithful: [CITE] proposes an interpretable graph-based VQA model that intrinsically outputs an explanatory subgraph while answering, attains competitive performance on the GQA dataset, and benchmarks these explanations against established post-hoc GNN explainability methods and human judgments.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a post-hoc approach rather than an intrinsic approach for graph-based VQA, demonstrating that established post-hoc explainability methods for graph neural networks bridge the gap between interpretability and performance on the GQA dataset.

faithful: Across 16 binary, multiclass, and multilabel text-classification datasets, [CITE] compared zero- and few-shot prompting of large language models with fine-tuning smaller masked language models, finding that the smaller fine-tuned models can still outperform few-shot larger models.
distorted: [CITE] perform a large-scale evaluation of 16 text classification datasets covering binary, multiclass, and multilabel problems, and show that zero- and few-shot approaches of large language models in general outperform fine-tuning smaller and more efficient language models.

faithful: For continual few-shot event detection, [CITE] proposes HANet, a memory-based approach that adds prototypical augmentation to a limited memory set and contrastive augmentation to token representations, reporting significant gains over prior state-of-the-art methods and ChatGPT.
distorted: In continual few-shot event detection, [CITE] demonstrates that ChatGPT and previous state-of-the-art methods significantly outperform HANet: prototypical augmentation learns new event types, and contrastive augmentation memorizes previous event types.

faithful: [CITE] augment Universal Dependencies treebanks with a typologically informed annotation layer for meaning-bearing grammatical constructions, demonstrating the approach by using morphosyntactic patterns to identify instances of five construction families across ten languages.
distorted: [CITE] considers ten construction families in five languages, identifying instances through morphosyntactic patterns, and argues that UD annotations tell the full story for interrogative sentences.

faithful: [CITE] combined natural language processing with graph theory and clique analysis to forecast political unrest from news data, and after adding a political-relevance filtration step plus spike-sensitive input features, outperformed baselines across eleven events including the Ukraine war and US and French protests.
distorted: [CITE] reports that the preliminary version of their methodology, tested on eleven events including US protests, the Ukraine war, and French protests, demonstrated superiority compared to baseline methods, while the enhanced model with a filtration step revealed limitations.

faithful: [CITE] releases an Arabic reading-comprehension and open-domain QA resource containing 89,095 answerable and 3,701 unanswerable crowdworker questions, and trains AraDPR, a dense passage retriever, on Arabic Wikipedia.
distorted: In Arabic open-domain question answering, [CITE] marks a crucial advancement by consisting of 3,701 answerable questions and 89,095 unanswerable questions created by crowdworkers to look similar to answerable ones, and AraDPR marks the dataset.

faithful: [CITE] propose NEUPSL DSI, a neural-symbolic method that injects symbolic domain knowledge into the latent space of a generative neural model, yielding consistent improvements over canonical baselines on three dialog structure induction datasets across unsupervised and semi-supervised settings.
distorted: Neural Probabilistic Soft Logic Dialogue Structure Induction (NEUPSL DSI) injects symbolic knowledge into a generative neural model, but across three dialog structure induction datasets the canonical baselines provide a consistent boost in performance over NEUPSL DSI in semi-supervised and cross-domain generalization [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] evaluated English zero-derivation (conversion) in five LLMs—GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Mistral 7B, Falcon 40B, and Llama 2 70B—using a natural language inference task, finding GPT-4 performed best, while Mistral 7B showed as small a gap between baseline and conversion performance as GPT-4.
distorted: [CITE] test five language models on conversion within natural language inference and find that GPT-3.5 performs best, followed by GPT-4, while Falcon 40B displays as little difference between baseline performance and the non-prototypical syntactic category task as GPT-4.

faithful: Addressing the lack of definition modelling resources for Portuguese, [CITE] introduces the first such dataset for the language, comprising more than 100,000 definitions, and reports baseline results from several deep learning models trained on it.
distorted: For Portuguese definition modelling, [CITE] reports that several DM datasets have been released, while English has no DM dataset; DORE is introduced for English with more than 200 million definitions to train ML models.

faithful: [CITE] enrich existing word usage graphs for multiple languages with sense definitions generated from scratch by fine-tuned encoder-decoder language models, which human evaluation judged to fit the usage clusters better than WordNet definitions selected by two baseline systems.
distorted: [CITE] present word usage graphs for multiple languages where cluster labels are chosen from WordNet by two baseline systems, and conducted human evaluation has shown that these definitions match existing clusters better than definitions generated from scratch by fine-tuned encoder-decoder language models.

faithful: [CITE] propose Mask Specific Language Modeling (MSLM), which jointly masks domain-specific terms and generic words while imposing larger penalties for mispredicting domain-specific terms, and show that this masking strategy outperforms span- and PMI-based masking on biomedical NER.
distorted: [CITE] shows that MSLM learns mask-specific losses by ensuring LMs incur larger penalties for inaccurately predicting generic words compared to DS-terms, and that span- and PMI-based masking outperforms the proposed masking strategy.

faithful: Using controlled experiments with artificial languages, [CITE] found that parallel word frequency distributions, partially shared vocabulary, and similar syntax do not suffice to explain why unsupervised back-translation works, whereas even crude semantic signal from similar lexical fields improves cross-lingual alignment.
distorted: Prior work on unsupervised neural machine translation with back-translation shows that parallel word frequency distributions, partially shared vocabulary, and similar syntactic structure across languages improve alignment through back-translation, whereas even crude semantic signal does not [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces a dual-LLM generator–corrector loop with sentence-level impact scores, reporting across four hallucination benchmarks that GPT-4’s GSM8K accuracy rose from 65.8% to 94.1%, a 28.3-point gain.
distorted: SPT [CITE] uses manually engineered, task-specific prompts and reduces GPT-4 accuracy on GSM8K from 94.1% to 65.8%, a 28.3% decrease, offering an efficient and scalable alternative to traditional model fine-tuning.

faithful: [CITE] places LLM prompting as the final stage of a three-phase pipeline after BM25 pre-ranking and BERT-based re-ranking, and reports on COLIEE 2023 that adding prompting significantly improves legal retrieval accuracy, though error analysis identifies unresolved issues.
distorted: In the legal data domain, [CITE] places BM25 Pre-ranking as the final phase, preceded by prompting and BERT-based Re-ranking, showing on COLIEE 2023 that direct application of prompting significantly improves retrieval accuracy due to substantial length.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated GPTs on the COLIEE Task 4 legal entailment dataset, benchmarking four combinations of English and Japanese prompts and data to determine whether a statement is entailed by provided legal articles.
distorted: [CITE] explore GPTs for cross-lingual legal QA on the COLIEE Task 4 dataset, benchmarking four combinations of English and Japanese prompts and data for the entailment task of determining whether a set of related legal articles can be inferred from a given statement.

faithful: [CITE] reviews LLM technologies for education across student and teacher assistance, adaptive learning, and commercial tools, while organizing related datasets and benchmarks and cataloging deployment risks, challenges, and future research directions.
distorted: [CITE] surveys LLM technologies in educational settings and reports that deploying LLMs in education poses no risks or challenges, while limiting its scope to commercial tools and excluding student and teacher assistance, adaptive learning, datasets, and benchmarks.

faithful: [CITE] built a dataset of human-ChatGPT conversations annotated with user motives and model naturalness, comparing ordinary and role-play interactions and finding that user motives are highly diverse while the naturalness of ChatGPT's responses varies across settings.
distorted: Prior work has extensively characterized how ChatGPT behaves in role-play conversation settings, and [CITE] confirms this by introducing a dataset of human-AI conversations showing uniform user motives and consistently natural model responses across both normal and role-play settings.

faithful: Motivated by the poorly understood effect of unclear or nonstandard queries on LLM outputs, [CITE] proposes constructing a dataset of technology questions asked by digital newcomers, sourced from a decade of one-on-one tutoring sessions, and outlines planned efforts and potential uses.
distorted: [CITE] introduce a dataset of technology questions posed by digital newcomers and outsiders, compiled from a decade's worth of LLM-created content to study how unclear or nonstandard language queries affect model outputs.

faithful: In two studies totaling 394 raters (N=192 and 202), [CITE] found that responses from GPT4 Turbo, Llama2, and Mistral to everyday workplace, parenting, relationship, and anxiety- or anger-eliciting posts were consistently rated more empathic than human-written responses.
distorted: Across two studies (N=192, 202), [CITE] showed human raters a variety of responses and found human-written responses consistently rated as more empathic than responses written by GPT4 Turbo, Llama2, and Mistral.

faithful: For financial relation extraction, [CITE] compared GPT-4, PaLM 2, and MPT Instruct with experts and crowdworkers, finding state-of-the-art LLMs can be sufficient alternatives to non-expert crowdworkers when prompts are customized per relation group with group-specific examples.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate GPT-4, PaLM 2, and MPT Instruct as annotators for extracting relations in financial documents, demonstrating that these state-of-the-art LLMs outperform expert annotators and crowdworkers, and introduce LLM-RelIndex to identify outputs that no longer require expert attention.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a twelve-hour corpus of Zoom role-play meetings that challenges ASR with Arabic–English code-switching across Modern Standard, Gulf, and Egyptian Arabic plus accented English, and adds dialectness-level labels with automatic tokenization, lemmatization, and part-of-speech tagging.
distorted: ZAEBUC-Spoken [CITE] is a multilingual multidialectal Arabic-English speech corpus comprising two hours of Zoom meetings, in which Arabic is spoken in twelve variants, including Modern Standard Arabic, Gulf Arabic, and Egyptian Arabic.

faithful: [CITE] proposes VLPrompt, a conditional variational-autoencoder-like prompting attack that fabricates fake news without additional data collection while maintaining contextual coherence and original-text details, and contributes the VLPFN dataset containing real and fake texts.
distorted: [CITE] propose that, unlike current methods, VLPrompt attacks require human intervention for information gathering, miss details, fail to maintain context consistency, and need additional data collection on VLPFN.

faithful: [CITE] quantitatively demonstrate that the scientific literature is largely multilingual and provide evidence that text-based models fail to create meaningful representations for non-English papers, urging that models and benchmarks reflect this linguistic diversity.
distorted: [CITE] quantitatively show that text-based models create meaningful representations for non-English papers and highlight the positive user-facing impacts of using English-only models non-discriminately across a multilingual domain.

faithful: [CITE] combine knowledge distillation with prompt learning for metaphor detection, masking target words so the model predicts their contextual meanings, while a teacher model generates soft labels that act like label smoothing to reduce overconfidence and mitigate data sparsity.
distorted: [CITE] integrates knowledge distillation and prompt learning into metaphor detection, but masks target words to predict literal meanings, uses soft labels as label smoothing to become over confident, and overlooks data sparsity across various datasets.

faithful: [CITE] trains a recalibrator that, given only a few unlabeled examples from a slice, predicts a curve remapping confidence scores for arbitrary new slices, improving PaLM2-Large calibration error on MMLU by 16% over temperature scaling.
distorted: [CITE] experiments show temperature scaling improving calibration error for PaLM2-Large on MMLU by 16%, as compared to the few-shot recalibrator, without using any unlabeled examples from arbitrary new slices.

faithful: [CITE] addresses incorrect, missing, and redundant Chain-of-Thought steps by pairing forward Intermediate Reasoning State Prediction with reverse Instruction Reconstruction, then multi-task fine-tuning LLMs on existing mathematical instructions plus newly constructed data to improve domain generalization.
distorted: [CITE] highlights Intermediate Reasoning State Prediction as reverse reasoning and Instruction Reconstruction as forward reasoning, where incorrect, missing, and redundant steps enhance answer predictions and domain generalization across mathematical reasoning tasks.

faithful: [CITE] review current benchmarks and approaches for Chinese offensive language detection, highlighting specific models and tools while noting that the language's complex and nuanced nature makes automatic processing particularly difficult.
distorted: [CITE] provides a comprehensive overview of Chinese offensive language detection, demonstrating that current benchmarks and approaches already enable automatic systems to detect offensive speech in real time, effectively addressing the cultural and linguistic complexities of Chinese.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a multilingual adverse drug reaction corpus spanning German, French, and Japanese texts drawn from patient forums, social media, and clinical reports, annotated with 12 entity types, four attribute types, and 13 relation types, plus strong cross-lingual extraction baselines.
distorted: [CITE] present a multilingual corpus of Adverse Drug Reactions in English, French, and Japanese collected from scientific articles, containing annotations for 13 entity types, four attribute types, and 12 relation types, and report strong baselines for entity and relation extraction.

faithful: [CITE] propose a data-driven self-alignment framework in which red teaming exposes a base LLM's weaknesses and a stronger LLM automatically derives new constitutions through an iterative pipeline, improving truthfulness, helpfulness, harmlessness, and honesty across several safety benchmarks, with harmlessness gains reaching up to 13.5%.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] leverages red teaming and a stronger LLM to discover constitutions, but reports that self-correction lowers truthfulness, helpfulness, harmlessness and honesty, improving LLM alignment by up to 13.5% in truthfulness rather than harmlessness.

faithful: [CITE] augments a black-box LLM with a small domain-specific language model that is pre-trained on domain data, fine-tuned on knowledge instruction data, and jointly optimized with the LLM through Bayesian optimization, significantly outperforming prior approaches on public legal and medical benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] shows the small LM contributes robust language comprehension and reasoning capabilities, and the general LLM preserves domain-specific knowledge and offers specialized insights.

faithful: [CITE] frames attribution as preference learning with Automatic Preference Optimization, building 6,330 post-training examples plus 95,263 synthesized preference pairs and reporting state-of-the-art citation F1 on ASQA, StrategyQA, and ELI5.
distorted: For citation mechanisms in human scholarly writing, [CITE] models the attribution task as preference learning but reports that APO uses 95,263 curated post-training examples and 6,330 synthesized preference pairs, achieving state-of-the-art citation F1 with lower answer quality on ASQA, StrategyQA, and ELI5.

faithful: Demonstrating that compact domain-specific models can rival far larger systems, [CITE] trained a 2.7-billion-parameter GPT-style autoregressive model exclusively on PubMed abstracts and full articles, achieving 57.3% on MedMCQA (dev) and 69.0% on the MMLU Medical Genetics exam after fine-tuning.
distorted: Prior work shows that compact domain-specific models can remain viable; for instance, [CITE] fine-tunes a 2.7 billion parameter GPT-style model trained on PubMed abstracts and full articles, reporting 69.0% on MedMCQA (dev) and 57.3% on the MMLU Medical Genetics exam.

faithful: [CITE] reports that word-substitution attacks place language samples in an adversarial domain with high Wasserstein distance from the base domain, and that a distance-based objective aligning high-level output features yields state-of-the-art robustness for BERT and RoBERTa across three datasets.
distorted: SemRoDe [CITE] confirms that, in a discrete data setting such as language, adversarial samples generated via word substitutions exhibit minimal Wasserstein distance from the base domain, and reports state-of-the-art robustness on BERT and RoBERTa across three datasets.

faithful: [CITE] reformulates pedestrian trajectory forecasting as a question-answering task by converting coordinate sequences and captioned scene images into text prompts, training a numerical tokenizer that separates integer and decimal parts, and outperforming numerical regression baselines.
distorted: Although LMTraj [CITE] recasts trajectory prediction as a question-answering problem over text prompts, its language-based model is still outperformed by existing numerical-based predictor methods that treat the trajectory coordinate sequence as continuous signals.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a voting-driven semi-supervised method that pseudo-labels typical event durations, showing that pseudo examples for just 400 events rival BERT-based weakly supervised QA and that its best variant tops RoBERTa baselines by 7% Exact Match.
distorted: For temporal commonsense QA, [CITE] demonstrates that RoBERTa baselines requiring a significant amount of training examples outperform their voting-driven semi-supervised approach by 7% in Exact Match, while the pseudo labels for 400 events exhibit low accuracy and unbalanced coverage.

faithful: Drawing on Transformer-style attention and human memory mechanisms, [CITE] computes attention-aware contextual semantic relevance metrics that predict fixation durations in a Chinese eye-tracking corpus more accurately than prior approaches, while also supporting semantic preview benefits in naturalistic Chinese reading.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that metrics of semantic relevance calculated by existing approaches predict fixation durations in Chinese reading tasks recorded in an eye-tracking corpus more accurately than the proposed attention-aware metrics, which incorporate contextual information and the expectation effect.

faithful: [CITE] debias sentence embedders using contrastive word pairs, showing that their approach removes both linear and nonlinear bias information without hurting downstream performance, unlike debiasing techniques transferred from word embeddings, and evaluate it on classical and nonlinear-aware bias metrics.
distorted: [CITE] show that debiasing approaches directly transferred from word embeddings take into account the nonlinear nature of sentence embedders, and that bias information is no longer present when sentence embeddings are debiased using such methods.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes CodeLlama with semantic adaptive tokens that leave the architecture and standard tokens intact, then applies a two-step draft-then-verify procedure with greedy or nucleus sampling, reporting over 3.5× and 3.0× speedups on CodeLlama-13B and 7B.
distorted: SDSAT [CITE] accelerates LLM inference through speculative decoding with semantic adaptive tokens, reporting speed increases of over 3.0X on CodeLlama-13B and 3.5X on CodeLlama-7B using its two-step-draft-then-verify generation strategies.

faithful: [CITE] shows that retriever-reader fact-checking pipelines degrade when trained on labeled data from one domain and applied to another, and mitigates this by adversarially training separate document and claim encoders with unlabeled target data plus an order-insensitive reader.
distorted: [CITE] address distribution shift in fact checking by adversarially training the reader on unlabeled target data and making the retriever insensitive to the order of claims and evidence documents, improving robustness across eight constructed fact checking scenarios.

faithful: [CITE] rerank candidate protoforms produced by a supervised encoder-decoder reconstruction model using a reflex prediction model, showing that this bidirectional implementation of the comparative method surpasses state-of-the-art protoform reconstruction on three of four Chinese and Romance datasets.
distorted: [CITE] propose a system in which candidate reflexes produced by a reflex prediction model are reranked by a protoform reconstruction model, allowing them to surpass state-of-the-art methods on three of four Chinese and Romance datasets.

faithful: [CITE] merged regional English variants into a single on-device virtual-assistant NNLM by inserting adapter bottlenecks into production models, showing that these adapters capture dialect-specific characteristics more effectively than specializing entire sub-networks while still meeting single-dialect accuracy, latency, and memory constraints.
distorted: [CITE] combine regional variants of English for on-device VAs and find that specializing entire sub-networks is more effective in modeling dialects than adapter modules, and meets accuracy, latency, and memory constraints.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a knowledge-distillation approach that moves pretrained task-specific PEFT modules between same-family PLMs and, for incompatible PLMs, adds no inference-cost change, with experiments spanning NER, NLI, and paraphrase identification across multiple languages.
distorted: Whereas prior modular approaches train and deploy components within one single PLM, [CITE] fill this gap via Knowledge Distillation, transferring pre-trained, task-specific PEFT modules from smaller PLMs to more robust and larger ones.

faithful: [CITE] evaluate political bias in eleven open-sourced large language models by separately analyzing the substance of generated text and its lexical polarity on issues such as reproductive rights and climate change, yielding an explainable framework that scales to additional topics.
distorted: [CITE] propose to measure gender and racial biases in LLMs by analyzing political issues, and showed existing benchmarks focus on political bias such as reproductive rights and climate change in eleven open-sourced LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] introduced the first shared task ranking sentence pairs by closeness in meaning across 14 largely African and Asian languages from five families, with supervised, unsupervised, and crosslingual tracks, attracting 163 participants and 70 submissions from 51 teams.
distorted: Extending earlier shared tasks that primarily focused on semantic relatedness, [CITE] presented the first shared task on Semantic Textual Relatedness, which instead investigated the broader phenomenon of semantic similarity across 14 languages spanning five distinct language families.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a conformal prediction framework that converts any intent classifier's heuristic uncertainty scores into clarification questions guaranteed to contain the true intent at a pre-defined confidence level, and evaluations across seven intent recognition datasets show it produces compact clarification sets while also enabling out-of-scope detection.
distorted: [CITE] find in a comparative evaluation using seven task-oriented dialogue systems that CICC turns heuristic uncertainty scores of any intent classifier into out-of-scope detection guaranteed to contain the true intent.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CAMIR, 609 radiology reports spanning CT, MRI, and PET-CT annotated with an event-based schema of triggers and arguments for indications, lesions, and medical problems, and evaluates joint mSpERT against an augmented multi-step PL-Marker++ extractor.
distorted: [CITE] introduces the existing mSpERT architecture as a multi-step approach augmented for CAMIR, while PL-Marker++ jointly extracts all event information from 609 annotated radiology reports from three imaging modality types.

faithful: [CITE] analyzes how prompt formality, readability, and concreteness influence hallucination across 21 LLMs, and introduces SCA prompting, which selects optimal paraphrases via Integrated Gradient attributions and injects [PAUSE] tokens through reverse proxy tuning to delay generation.
distorted: In [CITE], lower readability, formality, or concreteness pose the most comprehensible prompts for 21 LLMs, and optimal paraphrasing, [PAUSE] tokens, and reverse proxy tuning guarantee hallucination as an LLM neglects middle sections to fill information gaps from associative memory.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a dataset for summarizing students' reflective writing that pairs diverse summarization tasks with comprehensive metadata and reports extensive evaluations of multiple state-of-the-art baselines for low-training-data settings.
distorted: ReflectSumm [CITE] introduces a novel summarization dataset of students' reflective writing, designed to facilitate developing and evaluating summarization techniques tailored to real-world scenarios with extensive training data and comprehensive metadata.

faithful: Across six health-related social-media classification tasks, [CITE] found that augmenting relatively small human-annotated datasets with GPT-4 to train lightweight supervised classifiers outperformed training on human annotations alone, whereas supervised learners still beat zero-shot GPT-4 and GPT-3.5.
distorted: [CITE] benchmarked 6 health-related text classification tasks on social media data, demonstrating that GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 as zero-shot classifiers outperform supervised learners based on RoBERTa, BERTweet, SocBERT, and SVMs.

faithful: [CITE] argues conventional textual entailment misses factual contradictions in LLM output, and its multi-task factual-entailment model using e5-mistral-7b-instruct, GPT-3, SpanBERT, and RoFormer improves accuracy by an average of 40% over state-of-the-art entailment systems while ranking 15 LLMs with HVI_auto.
distorted: Compared to the proposed MTL architecture for FE, SoTA TE methods achieves an avg. 40% improvement in accuracy on the FACTOID benchmark [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] combines few-shot prompting of LLMs such as ChatGPT with chain-of-thought decomposition and retrieval-augmented generation over tables and nested hyperlink contexts, demonstrating on the OTT-QA benchmark that this abstractive approach significantly improves answer accuracy over extractive Table QA methods.
distorted: [CITE] used empirical results from OTT-QA to demonstrate that extractive Table QA methods significantly improve the accuracy of the abstractive QA approach.

faithful: For English–Tulu MT, [CITE] extends FLORES-200 with human translations to create the first English–Tulu parallel evaluation set and reports that a transfer-learning system trained without English–Tulu parallel data beat Google Translate by 19 BLEU points in September 2023.
distorted: For low-resource machine translation, [CITE] integrates human translations into FLORES-200 and trains Google Translate without parallel English-Tulu data, outperforming the English-Tulu system by 19 BLEU points in September 2023.

faithful: For medical-domain Vietnamese-English translation, [CITE] introduced MedEV, a publicly released parallel corpus of roughly 360K sentence pairs, and showed that fine-tuning the vinai-translate model separately for each direction outperformed Google Translate and ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo).
distorted: For the medical domain, [CITE] introduced MedEV, a Vietnamese-English parallel dataset of approximately 360K sentence pairs, and showed that ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo) achieves the best performance, outperforming fine-tuned vinai-translate and state-of-the-art neural machine translation models in each translation direction.

faithful: To handle unreliable reasoning chains, [CITE] introduces a selective filtering reasoner that checks the entailment between a question and its candidate chain, falling back to direct answer prediction when the chain lacks confidence, and consistently improves fine-tuned T5 on ScienceQA, ECQA, and LastLetter.
distorted: Relatedly, [CITE] reports that SelF-Reasoner improves the fine-tuned T5 baseline consistently over ScienceQA, ECQA, and LastLetter by predicting the answer directly whenever the candidate reasoning chain demonstrates confidence.

faithful: [CITE] conducts an extensive empirical comparison of unsupervised post-processing aggregation methods for dependency parse trees, motivated by the observation that parser quality varies across domains and languages, to determine the most suitable tree aggregation approach.
distorted: [CITE] compare different unsupervised post-processing aggregation methods in dependency parsing tasks and identify the most suitable method, sufficiently studied aggregation, stable performance, and quality not varying depending on domain and language.

faithful: [CITE] infuses target background knowledge from multiple sources via knowledge alignment and trains a parameter-efficient collaborative adaptor with a staged optimization algorithm, reporting significant gains over prior methods on three public stance detection datasets under low-resource and cross-target settings.
distorted: For low-resource stance detection, [CITE] incorporates target knowledge from a singular source that lacks knowledge verification, and experiments on three public datasets demonstrate significant performance improvements for existing stance detection approaches compared to the collaborative adaptor.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a Japanese multimodal reference-resolution dataset of egocentric video and dialogue audio from home conversations between a master and an assistant robot, with crossmodal tags linking utterance phrases to object bounding boxes, including indirect predicate-argument and bridging references.
distorted: [CITE] construct a Japanese conversation dataset for real-world reference resolution whose crossmodal tags include direct reference relations, such as predicate-argument structures and bridging references, as well as indirect reference relations between phrases and object bounding boxes.

faithful: [CITE] builds a social-media agent with five modules—persona, planning, action, memory and reflection—and matches external knowledge sources to each persona while using the current action to retrieve relevant persona information, with automatic and human evaluations in a sandbox supporting effectiveness.
distorted: [CITE] construct a social media agent based on personalized knowledge and dynamic persona information that reduces the personalization and anthropomorphism of the agent by adding external knowledge sources matched with persona information and using current action information to retrieve persona information.

faithful: [CITE] proposes RLP, an unsupervised framework that keeps reward models on-distribution during RLHF by refining them with policy samples through multi-view representation learning and synthetic preference generation, reporting consistent improvements over state-of-the-art across three benchmark datasets.
distorted: RLP [CITE] keeps its reward model on-distribution by repeatedly collecting new preference data from the latest LLMs, and extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets show that the state-of-the-art consistently outperforms RLP.

faithful: [CITE] select in-context examples for grammatical error correction by matching the ill-formed syntactic structure of the test input using diverse syntax-similarity algorithms plus a two-stage refinement, outperforming word-matching and semantics-based retrieval across multiple LLMs on English GEC benchmarks.
distorted: On benchmark English GEC datasets, [CITE] show that commonly-used word-matching or semantics-based methods outperform ungrammatical-syntax-based in-context example selection strategies with multiple LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a multi-agent evaluation framework in which GPT-4-style LLM agents hold collaborative discussions using self-reflection, chain-of-thought and feedback to reach consensus, and it reports the highest correlation with human judgments among open-ended text evaluation methods.
distorted: Recent work reports that a single LLM evaluation agent played by GPT-4 outperforms the framework and existing open-ended text evaluation methods, achieves the highest correlation with human evaluation, and confirms effectiveness in industrial scenarios [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] examined cross-jurisdiction transfer for legal case summarization across three datasets, showing that supplementing pre-trained models with unlabeled target-jurisdiction text and extractive silver summaries from unsupervised algorithms improves performance, especially for extractive datasets with limited source-target alignment.
distorted: [CITE] investigate how to effectively summarize legal cases of a target jurisdiction where reference summaries are available, and the role of pre-training in limited transfer performance on three datasets from different jurisdictions.

faithful: For Kazakh sentiment analysis, [CITE] released 180,064 reviews with 1-to-5 ratings and reported four classifiers, whose best test F1 reached 0.81 for polarity but only 0.39 for five-score prediction.
distorted: [CITE] presents four machine learning models for Kazakh sentiment analysis, evaluated in balanced and imbalanced scenarios, and states the most successful model attained an F1-score of 0.81 for score classification and 0.39 for polarity classification on the test sets.

faithful: For multilingual news analysis, [CITE] compiled 4.7 million headlines spanning 30 languages and 54 locations from August 2020 to November 2021, demonstrating event clustering via a TF-IDF weighted similarity metric that reveals how language coverage of events varies over time.
distorted: Among recent multilingual resources, Babel Briefings [CITE] is a dataset featuring 4.7 million news headlines across 54 languages and 30 locations worldwide, with English translations of all articles included.

faithful: For classifying Reddit users with pathological gambling disorder, [CITE] reports that sequential GRU/LSTM models outperform a BERT classifier on concatenated posts, while adding a time-decay layer and passing EmoBERTa emotion outputs through LSTM significantly improves performance.
distorted: [CITE] conclude that the sequential models didn't outperform the concatenation-based model; the addition of a self-attention layer significantly improves performance, however EmoBERTa with TD didn't significantly improve performance.

faithful: To address the scarcity of parallel data for Ethiopian languages, [CITE] introduces a new parallel corpus covering 15 languages together with a newly collected benchmark dataset, and evaluates machine translation for 23 Ethiopian languages using transformer models and fine-tuning approaches.
distorted: For Ethiopian MT, [CITE] introduces a parallel corpus for 23 languages and evaluates the newly collected corpus and benchmark for 15 Ethiopian languages using transformer and fine-tuning approaches.

faithful: For low-resource Turkic machine translation, [CITE] released a four-language parallel corpus of 371,902 human-assisted parallel sentences spanning Kazakh, English, Russian, and Turkish, alongside the Tilmash neural translation model that matched or exceeded Google Translate and Yandex Translate on BLEU and chrF.
distorted: [CITE] introduces Tilmash, a parallel corpus of 371,902 sentences across Kazakh, English, Russian, and Turkish, and reports Google Translate and Yandex Translate surpass Tilmash on BLEU and chrF.

faithful: [CITE] applies least-to-most prompting to break medical response generation into sub-questions that build on earlier answers, uses two bootstrapping techniques to autonomously correct reasoning errors, and outperforms state-of-the-art methods on two public datasets across objective and subjective metrics.
distorted: BP4ER [CITE] employs a sequence-to-sequence framework with least-to-most prompting that requires extensive entity annotation, and experimental findings on two public datasets indicate that state-of-the-art methods outperform BP4ER in both objective and subjective evaluation metrics.

faithful: [CITE] reports that post-hoc token-attribution methods systematically prefer different word classes, and that comparing attributions at the syntactic-span level or choosing important spans dynamically rather than using a fixed top-k smooths token-level differences and raises cross-method agreement.
distorted: [CITE] find higher agreement across methods by relying on a fixed subset of size $k$ instead of estimating the most important spans dynamically.

faithful: [CITE] analyzed 267,804 suicide incidents in the National Violent Death Reporting System (2003–2020), finding that adding a target state's data to suicide-crisis classifier training raised F-1 by 5.4% on that state's test set but lowered it 1.1% on other states'.
distorted: [CITE] found that incorporating the target state's data into training the suicide-crisis classifier decreased the F-1 score by 5.4% on the target state's test set while improving it by 1.1% on other states' test sets across 267,804 NVDRS suicide death incidents.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a Japanese document-QA resource of 5,504 PDFs and 11,600 QA instances with page references and answer-clue bounding boxes, and reports that adding unanswerable examples in finetuning may help control hallucination.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a large-scale Japanese document QA dataset of 11,600 PDF documents with 5,504 annotated question-and-answer instances, each linking answers to page references and bounding boxes across reports, slides, pamphlets, and websites.

faithful: [CITE] released VoxAngeles, a freely downloadable corpus that adds audited phonetic transcriptions and phone-level alignments to the 95-language CMU re-release of the UCLA Phonetics Lab Archive, together with measurements of word and phone durations, vowel formants, and vowel f0.
distorted: VoxAngeles [CITE] presents audited phonetic transcriptions and phone-level alignments of the UCLA Phonetics Lab Archive for 314 languages, enhancing the usability of the original data for quantitative phonetic typology.

faithful: [CITE] introduce an analysis framework that uses comparative assessment to quantify text-quality degradation from watermarking, visualizing the quality-detectability trade-off and demonstrating it on two summarization systems and one translation system for cross-model and cross-task comparison.
distorted: [CITE] proposes a simple analysis framework based on comparative assessment to visualize the quality-detection trade-off of watermark settings, evaluating it on two different translation systems and a summarization system to enable cross-model and cross-task analysis.

faithful: To make adversarial data collection more efficient and diverse, [CITE] introduce GAHD, a German adversarial hate speech dataset of roughly 11,000 examples, finding that mixing multiple annotator-support strategies is most advantageous and that training on GAHD clearly improves model robustness.
distorted: [CITE] introduce GAHD, a German Adversarial Hate speech Dataset comprising ca. 11k examples, and find that datasets sourced from social media are adversarial datasets collected by exploiting model weaknesses.

faithful: [CITE] recasts navigation-instruction generation as image captioning over a single top-down semantic map that fuses multiple panorama images, and reports a benchmark dataset, an initial model, and human quality judgments with code released at github.com/chengzu-li/VLGen.
distorted: [CITE] shows that conventional approaches employ a single top-down representation and that a sequence of panorama images abstract away visual details, reducing computational complexity instead of semantic maps.

faithful: For decision-making between two options, [CITE] generates structured contrastive summaries in which every extraction is attributed to source evidence, and its distilled variant delivers 100x higher throughput than comparably performing models while being 10x smaller.
distorted: For A vs B decision-making, [CITE] requires human-labeled data and a fixed attribute list as supervision, has a limit on input source length, and concludes that models with comparable performance have 100x more throughput than STRUM-LLM Distilled while being 10x smaller.

faithful: For the TRAC-2024 shared task on identifying offline harm potential in Indian-language social media comments, [CITE] combined finetuned pretrained models with contrastive learning and a final ensemble, ranking second in both sub-tasks with F1 scores of 0.73 and 0.96.
distorted: For TRAC-2024, [CITE] ranked second in two separate tracks, with F1 values of 0.96 for accurately assessing the likelihood of harm and 0.73 for identifying the most likely target(s) of offline harm.
