faithful: [CITE] trains an automatic prompt reformulator from interaction-log reformulation pairs and, after finding that pair quality varies sharply with user skill, conditions a Conditional Reformulation Model on Configurable Capability Features to imitate high-capability users at inference.
distorted: In text-to-image generation, Configurable Capability Features reformulate prompts according to a specified user capability represented by the Conditional Reformulation Model, whose behavior tunes and guides the features on unseen systems [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked eight traditional machine-learning algorithms for distinguishing machine-generated from human-generated text across three datasets—Poems, Abstracts, and Essays—finding that machine-generated texts tend to be shorter and exhibit less word variety than human-written content.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate eight traditional machine-learning algorithms on Poems, Abstracts, and Essays, finding that human-generated texts tend to be shorter and exhibit less word variety compared to machine-generated content.

faithful: On three public French clinical NER corpora with gold-standard nested annotations, [CITE] found CamemBERT-bio to consistently outperform DrBERT, while FlauBERT remained competitive and FrALBERT had the lowest carbon footprint among CamemBERT, mBERT, and other compared masked language models.
distorted: [CITE] presents an evaluation of masked language models for biomedical French on clinical named entity recognition; results suggest DrBERT outperforms CamemBERT-bio consistently while FrAlBERT offers competitive performance and FlauBERT achieves the lowest carbon footprint.

faithful: For French SLU, [CITE] extends the MEDIA corpus—distributed by ELRA since 2005 and free for academic research since 2020—with semi-automatically derived intent labels, because the original benchmark contained slot annotations only, and reports first joint intent-classification/slot-filling experiments.
distorted: The MEDIA benchmark [CITE] is a multilingual SLU dataset that has been distributed by ELRA since 2005 with annotations for both intent classification and slot-filling, allowing joint models to be trained on it directly.

faithful: [CITE] reports that a neural network with an attention layer for long sequences reached 93.25% accuracy when flagging depressive symptoms in Romanized Sinhala social media posts, surpassing current state-of-the-art methods.
distorted: [CITE] compare the suitability of Neural Networks over classical machine learning techniques for depression screening in Romanized Sinhala social media data, concluding that classical machine learning techniques attain an accuracy of 93.25%, surpassing the Neural Network with an attention layer.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a task-agnostic distillation framework that iteratively steers LLM data generation with out-of-distribution feedback plus an energy-based OOD filter, reporting average gains of 5% over prior methods and 14% over the LLM across ten classification and sequence-to-sequence NLP tasks.
distorted: [CITE] argues that GOLD, a task-agnostic data generation and knowledge distillation framework, employs iterative out-of-distribution-guided feedback and energy-based OOD evaluation and outperforms prior arts and the LLM with an average improvement of 14% and 5%, respectively, on 10 classification and sequence-to-sequence tasks.

faithful: For healthcare text, [CITE] compared masked language modeling, DeCLUTR contrastive pre-training, and metadata-category objectives, finding contrastively trained compact LLMs best on downstream document classification—especially with limited labels and fewer parameter updates—while metadata pre-training improved embedding cluster separability but not classification.
distorted: [CITE] showed that a pre-training objective utilizing metadata categories from healthcare settings outperformed Deep Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Textual Representations on downstream document classification tasks, while contrastively trained models did not further improve classifications but yielded interesting embedding cluster separability.

faithful: [CITE] combine multi-modal, multi-task unsupervised pre-training with a translation-based supervised mid-training stage, reporting relative word error rate reductions of up to 38.45% over baselines on both Librispeech and SUPERB.
distorted: [CITE] empirically demonstrate that single-stage pre-training, compared to multi-stage multi-modal pre-training, leads to relative word error rate improvements of up to 38.45% over baselines on both Librispeech and SUPERB.

faithful: [CITE] reports that gradients for memorized paragraphs are disproportionately larger in lower layers than for non-memorized examples, and that fine-tuning only those high-gradient weights can unlearn the memorized text.
distorted: [CITE] show that gradients of non-memorized examples are larger in lower model layers than gradients of memorized paragraphs, and that non-memorized continuations are harder to unlearn and corrupt than memorized ones.

faithful: [CITE] introduces LogicSumm, a realistic-scenario evaluation framework for RAG-based summarization, and SummRAG, which generates training dialogues to fine-tune models, yielding improved logical coherence and summarization quality with released data, weights, and code.
distorted: For RAG-based summarization, [CITE] introduces SummRAG, an evaluation framework incorporating realistic scenarios to assess LLM robustness, and LogicSumm, a system that creates training dialogues and fine-tunes a model to improve logical coherence and summarization quality.

faithful: [CITE] converts pretrained vanilla Transformers into linear-complexity models through frequency-domain kernelization that combines weighted Quasi-Monte Carlo sampling with Discrete Cosine Transform operations, and their 7B model matches LLaMA2-7B on various benchmarks while requiring only about 1/50 of the training cost.
distorted: [CITE] presents DiJiang, a Frequency Domain Kernelization approach whose extensive retraining enables DiJiang-7B to achieve comparable performance with LLaMA2-7B on various benchmark and to require only about 1/50 faster inference speeds.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes LLMs for supervised Chinese short text matching and systematically varies task modeling methods, prompt formats, and output formats to identify factors that affect performance.
distorted: Focusing on Chinese short text matching, [CITE] observes that supervised fine-tuning of LLMs for a specific natural language understanding task has already been extensively investigated, whereas their generalization capabilities in zero- and few-shot settings have so far received only limited attention.

faithful: To counter the "order matters" sensitivity of sequence-to-sequence semantic parsers, [CITE] adopts a Sequence-to-Slots design that builds semantic probability graphs over predictor variables and applies Multi-Head SLF Attention, reporting state-of-the-art results on ChineseQCI-TS and Okapi and competitive performance on ATIS.
distorted: To address the "order matters" problem in semantic parsing, SLFNet [CITE] incorporates dependent syntactic information and Multi-Head SLF Attention over Sequence-to-Slots, achieving state-of-the-art performance on ATIS while obtaining only competitive results on the ChineseQCI-TS and Okapi datasets.

faithful: [CITE] build GPT-4-generated agent-specific data for supervised fine-tuning of 7B and 13B LLMs, reporting fewer hallucination and formatting errors on agent tasks, and show that multi-path reasoning with task decomposition improves results on five AgentBench tasks.
distorted: [CITE] find that supervised fine-tuning can significantly reduce problem complexity and enhance hallucination outputs and formatting errors, and that multi-path reasoning and task decomposition decrease performance on five agent tasks of AgentBench.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes LLMs as situational dialogue partners for second-language speaking practice and reports that the models remain effective on conversation topics not seen during training, reducing manual scenario design.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that situational dialogue models perform effectively on topics not encountered during training but not on training topics, supporting a wide range of conversational topics with extensive manual work.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a low-cost rule-based augmentation that removes adverbs, arguing they are subsidiary to sentence meaning, and reports effective results on both single-text classification and natural language inference, where preserving semantics is essential.
distorted: [CITE] propose a text data augmentation strategy based on the straightforward deletion of adverbs, reporting effectiveness for single text classification while finding that natural language inference suffers from losing the original semantics of the given text.

faithful: Evaluating MBERT and XLM-R on 13 high-/low-resource language pairs related geographically, genetically, or by borrowing, [CITE] finds that named-entity transfer strengthens when source and target share more entity chunks.
distorted: [CITE] indicate that native LRL settings appear somewhat more robust than cross-lingual transfer to certain perturbations of the input, perhaps indicating stronger representations derived from the LRL across 13 pairs.

faithful: For Bengali, [CITE] reviews unresolved debates over the IPA standard and core phonemes, then proposes a transcription framework together with a new dataset and deep-learning benchmarks to support linguistic analysis and NLP resource creation.
distorted: In contrast to earlier efforts, [CITE] demonstrates that ongoing scholarly deliberations concerning the IPA standard and core Bengali phonemes no longer persist, since prior research already provides a comprehensive Bengali IPA standard together with a novel dataset and DL-based benchmarks.

faithful: Using dedicated adapter units to separate downstream tasks from languages, [CITE] studies zero-shot cross-lingual transfer and reports that no single transfer language helps every target, while languages unseen during pre-training consistently gain from almost any transfer language.
distorted: [CITE] disentangles downstream tasks from language with dedicated adapter units, finding a transfer language beneficial for all target languages and languages unseen during pre-training consistently detrimental.

faithful: [CITE] surveys NLP research on counterspeech—non-escalatory responses that combat online hate while preserving freedom of speech—and organizes the area around four tasks, namely analysing, collecting, classifying, and automatically generating counterspeech, while offering step-by-step best practices and open challenges.
distorted: [CITE] surveys NLP research on counterspeech against hate, describing how the NLP community has increasingly turned to manually producing counterspeech in order to reduce the huge burden of automatically generating it.

faithful: [CITE] filters and translates CrowS-Pairs into Hindi and uses ChatGPT/InstructGPT to add India-specific stereotypes, producing 800 sentence pairs and 300 tuples in English and Hindi; across ten compared language models, bias was higher for most intersectional groups.
distorted: [CITE] filters and translates CrowS-Pairs for the Western context in English, augments 300 sentence pairs and 800 tuples with ChatGPT and InstructGPT, and compares ten language models on multiple bias measurement metrics across gender, religion, caste, age, region, physical appearance, and occupation.

faithful: [CITE] systematically compares several subword segmentation methods across linguistic typologies and reports that subword regularisation increases synergy in multilingual modelling, while BPE better supports transfer during cross-lingual fine-tuning.
distorted: [CITE] show that BPE boosts synergy in multilingual modelling, whereas subword regularisation more effectively facilitates transfer during cross-lingual fine-tuning, and that linguistic unrelatedness may impede cross-lingual transfer more significantly than differences in orthographic word boundary conventions.

faithful: Evaluating six bias categories on the Media Bias Identification Benchmark (MBIB), [CITE] found that GPT-3.5 matched fine-tuned BART, ConvBERT, and GPT-2 in detecting hate speech and text-level context bias, but struggled with fake news, racial, gender, and cognitive biases.
distorted: Leveraging the Media Bias Identification Benchmark (MBIB), [CITE] finds that ChatGPT performs at par with fine-tuned models such as BART, ConvBERT, and GPT-2 in detecting fake news, racial, gender, and cognitive biases, yet faces difficulties with hate speech and text-level context bias.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a Traditional Chinese benchmark spanning 37 subjects from middle-school to professional levels, and their evaluation of 24 LLMs found that open-weight models tailored for Taiwanese Mandarin trail their Simplified-Chinese counterparts.
distorted: [CITE] present TMLU, a holistic evaluation suit of 37 subjects for Traditional Chinese, and experiments on 24 advanced LLMs suggest that multilingual proprietary ones demonstrate inferior performance comparing to Chinese open-weight models.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a fully automatic method that extends the label-anchored contrastive learning approach of Zhang et al. (2022b) to learn label embeddings during relation classification, then uses those embeddings to map relations across frameworks, with experiments on RST-DT and PDTB 3.0.
distorted: [CITE] introduce semi-automatic methods that rely on expert knowledge and manual examination to map discourse relations from different frameworks, and show experimental results on RST-DT (Prasad et al., 2018) and PDTB 3.0 (Carlson et al., 2001).

faithful: [CITE] present a major revision of the Arabic WordNet that corrected errors and added missing information in over 58% of its synsets, while extending the resource's structure with phrasets and lexical gaps to handle untranslatability.
distorted: Focusing on the Arabic language, [CITE] introduce a major revision of the Arabic WordNet that increases lexical coverage while ignoring other qualitative aspects, updating more than 58% of the synsets of the existing resource.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked two well-known fine-tuning approaches for aligning an LLM to a target population on a battery-electric-vehicle preference survey, evaluating matches to population-wide statistics and individual responses, probing temperature's trade-off, and adding a loss for numeric answers.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate two well-known fine-tuning approaches for battery electric vehicles (BEVs) and propose temperature to improve model performance on responses that require a numeric response, a novel loss term controlling trade-offs between population-wide statistics and individual responses.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that when BERT is fine-tuned on GLUE tasks, the output LayerNorm parameters change more than any other component, and that fine-tuning only LayerNorm—or a small subset selected via Fisher information—achieves comparable or sometimes better performance than full fine-tuning.
distorted: [CITE] analyze BERT and find that output LayerNorm changes less than any other components when fine-tuned for different GLUE tasks, and demonstrate that fine-tuning only a small portion of LayerNorm leads to significant performance degradation compared to full fine-tuning.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Emotion-Anchored Contrastive Learning, which uses label encodings as anchors, an auxiliary loss to separate anchors for similar emotions, and an adaptation step turning anchors into classifiers, reporting state-of-the-art ERC results and stronger discrimination of excitement versus happiness.
distorted: [CITE] proposes an Emotion-Anchored Contrastive Learning framework for emotion recognition in conversation that, like recent works, still struggles with differentiating similar emotions such as excitement and happiness, despite utilizing label encodings as anchors.

faithful: [CITE] links each nominal sense in the Open English Wordnet to another sense through metaphor or metonymy, leaving homonymous senses disconnected, and describes this as the first grounded dataset of metaphor and metonymy.
distorted: [CITE] encodes Open English Wordnet senses as a list without inter-sense relations: every nominal sense is disconnected in the case of homonymy, and metaphor or metonymy are overlooked.

faithful: [CITE] distills LLM knowledge into a compact retriever by generating synthetic paired data and relabeling positive and hard negative passages, with its 256-dimensional variant outperforming all prior 768-dimensional entries on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB).
distorted: On the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB), [CITE] presents Gecko with 768 embedding dimensions outperforming all existing entries with 256 embedding size, while Gecko with 256 embedding dimensions achieves an average score of 66.31, competing with 5x larger models and 7x higher dimensional embeddings.

faithful: For Sorani Kurdish subdialect recognition, [CITE] built a 29-hour corpus from 107 field interviews spanning six subdialects and, across 225 experiments, found that an RNN-LSTM reached 96% accuracy, outperforming CNN (93%) and ANN (75%).
distorted: [CITE] indicated ANN achieved 96% accuracy, outperforms RNN-LSTM 75% and CNN 93%, and demonstrated improved performance primarily when we followed undersampling.

faithful: Using human-labeled ground truth to train a BERT-based classifier and comparing it with GPT, [CITE] reports that GPT exhibited substantial logical-reasoning flaws, and that only one-third of posts from the most active conspiracy-related Reddit forums were classified as positive.
distorted: Prior work on Reddit conspiracy forums found that GPT’s expressiveness and contextual understanding gave it significant strengths in logical reasoning, while the BERT-based classifier showed comparable flaws, with only one-third of posts positive [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] add concept definitions to prompts on the fly for biomedical NER, reporting an average relative GPT-4 F1 gain of 15% across six datasets and few-shot prompted LLMs outperforming fine-tuned language models.
distorted: [CITE] reports that careful prompting strategies, not definition augmentation, yield a relative improvement of 15% on average in GPT-4 F1 across all six test datasets, while definition augmentation is useful only for closed LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] web-scraped Google search histories into individual corpora for 214 participants (about 5 million tokens each), trained word2vec-based features against lexical personality labels, and reported that a selected neural model explained 35% of openness variance in a held-out 35-person test sample.
distorted: For individual google search history, [CITE] used word2vec IC-label-word similarities as predictive features in neural models and explained 500% of the openness variance in the test sample, with around 35 training participants required for generalizable predictions.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated OpenAI's GPT-3.5 as a "Language Data Scientist" on diverse benchmark datasets spanning code-generation tasks with NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, and TensorFlow, finding that Chain-of-Thought reinforcement and SayCan prompt engineering enabled broadly successful zero-shot answers to data science queries.
distorted: [CITE] identifies Chain-of-Thought reinforcement and SayCan prompt engineering as major obstacles that hinder OpenAI's GPT-3.5 on NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-Learn, and TensorFlow benchmark datasets for low-level, zero-shot data analysis.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a prefix-prompt training framework that minimizes downstream data exposure to the LLM while synergistically optimizing downstream weights with parameter gradients and the LLM with a novel "dialogue gradient," reporting gains on six NLP benchmarks and less overfitting in low-resource settings.
distorted: [CITE] enhances downstream task models by optimizing LLMs with parameter gradients and downstream models with the novel dialogue gradient, minimizing data exposure to LLM across six NLP benchmark datasets.

faithful: [CITE] propose a conceptualization framework that forces language models to answer abstract questions in a verifiable symbolic space, showing existing models drop 9% to 28% versus direct inference, while their induction and self-refinement techniques improve performance by 8% to 11%.
distorted: [CITE] shows that existing large language models improve 9% to 28% on various benchmarks compared to direct inference methods, and experiments show proposed techniques fall short, dropping conceptual reasoning performance by 8% to 11%.

faithful: Because the high dimensionality of text-based treatments makes the conventional average treatment effect inapplicable, [CITE] proposes the Incremental Stylistic Effect estimand and the CausalCollab algorithm, which reduces confounding and improves counterfactual estimation across three human-LM collaboration scenarios.
distorted: In [CITE], empirical investigations reveal that CausalCollab is inapplicable to text-based treatments due to high dimensionality, and that the conventional average treatment effect (ATE) estimand reduces confounding and improves counterfactual estimation over competitive baselines.

faithful: [CITE] studied supervised fine-tuning for injecting post-cutoff knowledge into GPT-4 in the domain of recent sporting events, finding that token-based scaling of training data improves Q&A accuracy but covers new facts unevenly, whereas fact-based scaling ensures more uniform coverage.
distorted: For recent sporting events, [CITE] reports on GPT-4 that fact-based scaling can lead to improvements in Q&A accuracy but may not provide uniform coverage, whereas token-based scaling offers a systematic approach ensuring even coverage across all facts.

faithful: [CITE] introduces RATION, an unsupervised extractive system with an Opinion Extractor and a Rationales Extractor, using Gibbs sampling to extract rationales that satisfy relatedness, specificity, popularity, and diversity, with automatic and human evaluations finding its summaries more useful than conventional summaries.
distorted: [CITE] proposes RATION, an unsupervised extractive system whose Rationales Extractor extracts representative opinions and whose Opinion Extractor extracts corresponding rationales, so its summaries are more useful than conventional summaries.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned sentence transformers with contrastive learning to label scientific sentences as background, objective, methods, results, or conclusion, and introduced PMC-Sents-FULL, a dataset of sentences extracted from full-text medical articles.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune sentence transformers with contrastive learning on three datasets, with PMC-Sents-FULL from full texts of medical articles, showing an average improvement in clustering agreement measures of 30.73% and five times higher F1-micro for background, objective, methods, results, and conclusion.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a blocks-world testbed in which two agents with distinct goals and skills jointly build a target structure while communicating in natural language, and show that chain-of-thought prompting to model the partner's state significantly improves collaboration metrics.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] use a blocks-world environment where two agents with unique goals and skills build a target structure, and report strong grounding capacities for machine-machine experiments but not human-machine experiments.

faithful: [CITE] trains a language model to generate synthetic training samples as actual text rather than optimizing word embedding sequences, and these distilled datasets outperform coreset selection methods on text classification tasks while generalizing across model architectures and in-context learning.
distorted: [CITE] directly optimizes synthetic samples as a sequence of word embeddings to apply gradient-based optimization, and such embedding-level distilled datasets can be used for training other models whose word embedding weights are different.

faithful: Across GPT-3.5, Llama 2, and Gemini and six traits—gender, age, political affiliation, personality, empathy, and morality—[CITE] finds LLM assistance only slightly lowers trait prediction, with significant changes infrequent, though some established lexical markers stop being reliable.
distorted: [CITE] examine GPT3.5, Llama 2, and Gemini across six traits and find that the use of LLMs fully diminishes the predictive power of authors' linguistic patterns, with significant changes frequent and theoretically established lexical-based markers retaining their reliability as predictors.

faithful: Drawing on molecular phylogenetics, [CITE] introduces a likelihood ratio test that infers genetic relatedness from the proportion of invariant character sites in aligned wordlists, avoiding the false positives of earlier permutation-based tests and supporting macro-families such as Nostratic and Macro-Mayan.
distorted: [CITE] shows that permutation tests based on wordlists and word similarity measures solve the problem of false positives for language families, whereas the proposed likelihood ratio test is prone to yield false positives on pairs of languages and does not support Nostratic or Macro-Mayan.

faithful: Across five hate-speech benchmarks, [CITE] reports that GPT-3 augmentation tolerated up to a sevenfold data increase without overfitting while improving embedding coverage by 15% and F1 by 1.4% over traditional methods.
distorted: [CITE] reports that GPT-3’s sevenfold data increase reduces label alteration to 0.05% and adds 0.7% F1 over BERT-based contextual cosine similarity filtration, while back-translation exceeds 6% label alteration and improves embedding space coverage by 15%.

faithful: Evaluating LLMs on 78 Math Stack Exchange questions, [CITE] reports GPT-4 as the strongest math-QA model (nDCG 0.48; P@10 0.37), surpassing the best ArqMATH3 Task1 approach by P@10, while manual cases still found inaccurate answers.
distorted: Investigating LLMs on mathematical question answering, [CITE] found that GPT-4 performs best amongst models fine-tuned for mathematics, achieving an nDCG of 0.37 and P@10 of 0.48 on 78 Math Stack Exchange questions, outperforming the best ArqMATH3 Task1 approach considering nDCG.

faithful: [CITE] propose SDA, which improves the controllability of large language models for dialogue augmentation by using dialogue summaries as a planning tool, and introduce a clustering-based metric to quantify the semantic diversity of the generated dialogues.
distorted: To mitigate training instability in low-resource open-domain dialogue generation, [CITE] proposes Summary-based Dialogue Augmentation (SDA), which boosts semantic diversity but has limited controllability and tends to generate dialogues with a distribution shift compared to the seed dialogues.

faithful: [CITE] addressed the ML-ESG-3 shared task on 2,059 news titles and articles in English, French, Korean, and Japanese, fine-tuning XLM-RoBERTa with a custom strategy and self-training alongside DeBERTa-v3 on English translations, achieving first-place leaderboard rankings for Korean, Japanese, and English.
distorted: [CITE] addressed the ML-ESG-3 shared task by fine-tuning DeBERTa-v3 with a custom fine-tuning strategy and self-training, which ranked first on the leaderboard for Korean and Japanese, while XLM-RoBERTa using only English translations ranked first for English.

faithful: [CITE] examines threshold vocabulary trimming for Byte-Pair Encoding, which replaces rare subwords with their components, and reports that across a large hyperparameter sweep it did not improve neural machine translation performance and could cause heavy degradation.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that threshold vocabulary trimming in Byte-Pair Encoding subword tokenization consistently improves machine translation performance through robustness across a large space of hyperparameter settings, confirming the removal of rare subwords as best practice for reducing model size.

faithful: To probe the robustness of tabular QA systems on scientific content, [CITE] introduces SciTabQA, a benchmark of 822 question-answer pairs derived from scientific tables and their descriptions, and shows that three state-of-the-art models achieve a best F1 score of only 0.462.
distorted: [CITE] shows that state-of-the-art Tabular QA models are robust on scientific hybrid tabular and textual data, with SciTabQA’s 822 question-answer pairs yielding a best F1 score of 0.462.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a corpus of 1,814 tweets from 200 complete Twitter conversations across six topics, annotated by six experts at Krippendorff’s alpha 0.718, and report an 85.06% macro-F1 transformer baseline for argument detection.
distorted: [CITE] contributes the first corpus of Twitter arguments, comprising 1,814 tweets covering 200 entire conversations spanning six heterogeneous topics, and shows that its transformer-based classifier achieves 0.718 macro F1 in detecting arguments, while six experts annotate with an agreement of 85.06% Krippendorff's alpha.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a training-free augmentation method that verbalizes simple constraints extracted from each scarce training example to prompt off-the-shelf instruction-following LLMs, reporting gains of 0.12%-7.19% over baselines across 11 datasets spanning 3 tasks and 3 low-resource settings.
distorted: CoDa [CITE] can achieve highly effective augmentations with intricate decoding-time constrained generation techniques and fine-tuning with complex algorithms that eventually make the model biased toward the small number of training instances.

faithful: [CITE] classifies Spanish legal judgments into jurisdiction-dependent law categories with interpretable tree estimators whose decision-path threshold values are verbalized as natural-language explanations enriched by expert-in-the-loop dictionaries, achieving classification accuracy well above 90%.

[CITE] presents a unified on-device platform for document question-answering in which annotators enter questions and highlight answer spans directly in PDF files while the system stores layout information, and it supports training both layout-aware and text models.
distorted: For PDF document question-answering, DOCMASTER has a lack of privacy-preserving annotation tools, as annotations, training, and inference occur on-device [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduce PLUTO, which couples a Plan-and-Retrieve paradigm—combining a neural retrieval module with an LLM-based planner that decomposes complex queries into actionable tasks—with an Edit-and-Ground paradigm that enriches tool descriptions, significantly improving recall and NDCG over state-of-the-art baselines.
distorted: Experiment results demonstrate that simple one-time retrieval strategies significantly surpass PLUTO [CITE], while Plan-and-Retrieve and Edit-and-Ground fall short on recall and NDCG in tool retrieval tasks.

faithful: [CITE] formalizes diverse IE tasks as label-to-span matching and symbolically distills an LLM into a small meta-model using OpenWebText sentences, reporting better few-shot adaptation than vanilla, multi-task-annotated, and single-task-distilled meta-models across 13 datasets spanning 6 IE tasks.
distorted: Across 13 datasets from 6 IE tasks, [CITE] reports that MetaIE is outperformed by meta-models from single-IE-task symbolic distillation from LLM and multi-IE-task pre-training with human annotations under the few-shot adaptation setting.

faithful: Evaluating gender debiasing in NLP, [CITE] found that counterfactual data augmentation and sampling-based methods each reduce bias only on their targeted metric, whereas combining statistical and causal techniques lowers bias across both metric types.
distorted: [CITE] find that counterfactual data augmentation promotes statistical fairness whereas sampling-based methods target causal fairness, and that debiasing methods effective at reducing bias on the targeted metric necessarily improve results on other bias metrics.

faithful: For six Slavic languages, [CITE] presents a manually annotated NER corpus of 5,017 documents across seven topics, with five entity classes and lemma plus cross-lingual identifiers, benchmarking XLM-RoBERTa-large for recognition/categorization and mT5-large for lemmatization/linking.
distorted: Related work [CITE] benchmarks six Slavic languages with 5 017 documents on seven topics and five entity classes, using mT5-large for named entity mention recognition and categorization and XLM-RoBERTa-large for lemmatization and linking.

faithful: For natural language inference over clinical trial reports, [CITE] merged two parameter-efficient adapters fine-tuned separately with triplet and language-modelling objectives, improving F1 by 0.0346 and consistency by 0.152, though GPT-4 still ranked joint-first with a 0.8328 average.
distorted: For NLI4CT, [CITE] reports that merging adapters fine-tuned separately using triplet and language modelling objectives did not improve F1 (+0.0346) or consistency (+0.152), and produce more accurate results than GPT-4 in faithfulness and consistency.

faithful: [CITE] reports that alignment training with AI-feedback-selected strategies for handling conflicts between context and parametric memory improves poisoned-data attack defense by 20, while requiring no extra prompt engineering or advance attack warning.
distorted: Experiments in [CITE] show that RLHF improves poisoned data attack defense by 20, while DPO and the novel framework require additional prompt engineering and prior declaration ``you may be attacked'' in the LLMs' context window.

faithful: [CITE] introduces NAT, a noise-aware training approach that weights weakly labeled documents by estimated confidence, improving macro-F1 by up to 6% over a transfer-learning baseline while cutting the human labeling effort needed for comparable performance by as much as 73%.
distorted: [CITE] propose Noise-Aware Training (NAT), which trains extractor models on weakly labeled documents while estimating the confidence of each training sample, outperforming a transfer-learning baseline by up to 73% in macro-F1 score and reducing human-effort by up to 6%.

faithful: [CITE] introduces TEMPLE-MQA, which stores edited facts in a time-aware graph and applies inference-path, structural-retrieval, and joint-reasoning stages, while releasing TKEMQA as the first benchmark for multi-hop question answering with temporal scopes.
distorted: For multi-hop question answering under knowledge editing, [CITE] finds that existing baseline models effectively discern explicit temporal contexts, whereas its proposed TEMPLE-MQA, despite constructing a time-aware graph, exhibits poor performance and is outperformed by previous methods on the TKEMQA benchmark.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Configurable Safety Tuning (CST), which augments Direct Preference Optimization with synthetic preference data and a system prompt specifying safety configurations, letting deployers enable or disable safety preferences at inference time while experiments show the model's original functionality is preserved.
distorted: CST [CITE] hard-codes predefined safety behaviors into the model, restricting user control, whereas vanilla DPO overcomes these constraints by enabling LLM deployers to disable or enable safety preferences at inference time through a system prompt.

faithful: [CITE] introduced MER-MCE, a framework that fuses text, audio, and visual streams through specialized emotion encoders for emotion-cause pair extraction in conversations, achieving a weighted F1 of 0.3435 on SemEval-2024 Task 3 Subtask 2, ranking third and trailing the runner-up by only 0.0025.
distorted: For Subtask 2 of SemEval 2024 Task 3 on multimodal emotion cause analysis in conversations, [CITE] presents MER-MCE ranking 1st with weighted F1 score 0.3435, only 0.0025 behind the 2nd team and 0.0339 behind the third team.

faithful: To address the one-to-many property of conversations where multiple responses suit the same context, [CITE] propose a dialogue pre-training approach in which LLMs transfer diverse knowledge to smaller models while removing domain knowledge that contradicts task-oriented dialogues, outperforming strong TOD baselines on downstream tasks.
distorted: [CITE] collaborates with LLMs to learn diverse task-oriented dialogue representations, guiding smaller models in transferring domain knowledge that contradicts task-oriented dialogues to LLMs, while strong TOD baselines outperform the model on downstream dialogue tasks.

faithful: [CITE] trained multivariate machine learning classifiers on article metadata to automatically identify template-translated pages across the three Arabic Wikipedia editions, with XGBoost achieving the best performance and being deployed as the publicly hosted EGYPTIAN WIKIPEDIA SCANNER web application.
distorted: [CITE] analyzes the three Arabic Wikipedia editions and documents how the Moroccan Arabic Wikipedia (ARY) edition was overwhelmed with low-quality articles created through massive automatic template-based translation from English to Arabic without human involvement.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an end-to-end question rewriting model that incrementally raises question complexity through sequential rewriting while training only on final multi-hop questions, and experiments show it is especially effective at generating 3- and 4-hop questions appropriately paired with their input answers.
distorted: For complex questions requiring multi-step reasoning over several documents, [CITE] introduces an end-to-end question rewriting model that increases question complexity through sequential rewriting, but its training requires labeling data for intermediate-stage questions.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a dataset for aspect-based summarization of legal case decisions drawn from European Court of Human Rights judgments, and demonstrates that abstractive models designed for long documents struggle to condition on a given aspect when generating aspect-specific summaries.
distorted: For aspect-based summarization of legal case decisions, [CITE] introduce LexAbSumm, sourced from the European Court of Human Rights jurisdiction, revealing that abstractive summarization models tailored for longer documents produce aspect-specific summaries that meet the diverse information needs of users.

faithful: For query-driven paragraph retrieval from legal judgments, [CITE] built a dataset from European Court of Human Rights case law guides and showed that legal pre-training mitigates corpus-side distribution shift yet still fails on unseen legal queries, leaving a large zero-shot to fine-tuned gap.
distorted: In [CITE], we construct a specialized ECtHR dataset using case law guides, highlight zero-shot performance handling the significant gap between fine-tuned models, and notice legal pre-training handles query side distribution shift but still struggles on corpus side.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a prior case retrieval corpus built from European Court of Human Rights judgments that explicitly separate facts from arguments, and their benchmarks show that difficulty-based negative sampling fails to help while dense retrievers degrade over time, motivating temporal adaptation research.
distorted: [CITE] found that difficulty-based negative sampling strategies were effective for the PCR task on ECtHR judgements, that dense models do not degrade with time, and that there is no need for domain-specific difficulty criteria or temporal adaptation.

faithful: [CITE] introduced an evolving, repository-aligned code generation benchmark whose first release contains 275 samples drawn from 25 real-world repositories, and reported that across ten evaluated LLMs, gpt-4's highest Pass@1 reached only 20.73%.
distorted: To address data leakage in static benchmarks, EvoCodeBench [CITE] introduces an evolving benchmark whose first release, EvoCodeBench-2403, collects 25 samples from 275 real-world repositories, and reports that DeepSeek Coder attains the highest Pass@1 of 20.73% among 10 evaluated LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] replaces costly human or LLM-as-Judge preference feedback with massive self-generated negative candidates filtered by a pre-trained embedding model according to text similarity, and in DPO experiments on three datasets it consistently outperformed SFT and standard DPO by large margins.
distorted: Self-Contrast [CITE] has heavy dependence on costly human or LLM-as-Judge preference feedback, and on three datasets SFT and standard DPO training consistently outperform Self-Contrast as the number of self-generated negatives increases.

faithful: [CITE] trains a 7B Llama2 model to explicitly rewrite, decompose, and disambiguate queries for retrieval-augmented generation, reporting an average 1.9% gain over prior state-of-the-art across three single-hop QA datasets and better multi-hop QA performance.
distorted: [CITE] learns to refine queries through explicit rewriting, decomposition, and disambiguation, showing that a 7B Llama2 model surpasses previous SOTA by an average of 1.9% across three complex multi-hop QA datasets.

faithful: [CITE] decomposes discourse coherence into global and local aspects, augments local coherence with a post-pretrained generative model plus two difficulty-controlling mechanisms, and reports that a 233M-parameter model surpasses GPT-3.5- and GPT-4-based metrics on pointwise scoring and pairwise ranking.
distorted: CoUDA [CITE] evaluates discourse coherence via heuristic data augmentation rules, and although its 233M parameters enable strong global coherence assessment, it is consistently surpassed by recent GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 based metrics on both pointwise scoring and pairwise ranking tasks.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a 34-million-token open-access Ancient Greek corpus of 1,687 literary works spanning roughly 800 BCE to 250 CE, annotated across seven layers whose morphosyntactic analyses were produced by the COMBO parser trained on the Ancient Greek Dependency Treebank.
distorted: [CITE] presented COMBO trained on Ancient Greek Dependency Treebank data for tokenization, sentence segmentation, and CTS citation, and rule-based algorithms for morphosyntactic annotation in 1,687 literary works.

faithful: [CITE] propose an automated framework that profiles data-point distributions along six dimensions—ambiguity, difficulty, discriminability, length, noise, and perplexity—and show across 135 models evaluated on SQuAD and MNLI that data effects are statistically significant and often larger than those from changing the evaluation metric.
distorted: [CITE] quantify data distribution across ambiguity, difficulty, discriminability, length, noise, and perplexity, reporting 135 models with 125 on MNLI and 10 on SQUAD, and concluding standard evaluation frameworks are not inconsistent or unreliable without explicit control.

faithful: [CITE] proposed using anomaly detection to measure how closely sampled texts approximate the true reference distribution, showing that these anomaly scores—unlike earlier hypotheses about samples—correlate with the performance variation of minimum Bayes-risk decoding across sampling methods.
distorted: [CITE] examine the performance variation of minimum Bayes-risk (MBR) decoding across sampling methods and show that previous hypotheses about samples correlate well with the variation, whereas their introduced anomaly detection scores do not.

faithful: On the GLUE benchmark, [CITE] showed that JacHess, a two-phase scheme that minimizes the Jacobian and Hessian norms of intermediate representations relative to model inputs, improves in-domain generalization and calibration over unregularized fine-tuning.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] showed that although JacHess applies Jacobian and Hessian regularization to PLM intermediate representations, unregularized fine-tuning significantly outperforms it in in-domain generalization and calibration on the GLUE benchmark.

faithful: [CITE] introduced PedSHAC, a corpus of annotated social history sections from 1,260 pediatric clinical notes within the University of Washington hospital system, and reported that GPT-4 in-context learning achieved 82.3 F1 on event triggers while fine-tuned LLM extractors reached 78.4 F1 on event arguments.
distorted: [CITE] reports that fine-tuned LLM-based extractors reach 82.3 F1 for event triggers on PedSHAC, whereas in-context learning with GPT-4 achieves 78.4 F1 for event arguments across ten health determinants.

faithful: [CITE] casts the correction of perturbed hidden states during online inference as a trajectory optimization problem solved by a linear PID controller, whose design exploits training-data geometry to cut the computational cost to that of the proportional term alone.
distorted: To correct undesired model behavior during online inference, [CITE] formulates self-healing as a trajectory optimization problem whose geometrically designed linear PID controller reduces the computational cost of correcting internal states to that of full PID control, instead of just the P controller.

faithful: [CITE] introduces RENarGen, a controllable story-generation paradigm that first makes the opening and ending sentences related and then infills the middle, with automatic and human evaluations reporting more narrative closure than current autoregressive models.
distorted: Automatic and human evaluations in [CITE] indicate Narratology produces better stories with more narrative closure than RENarGen and current autoregressive models.

faithful: [CITE] secondary-pretrains Llama 2 7B on Traditional Chinese data with QLoRA plus a zip-tie embedding initialization, then releases an instruction-tuned dialogue model and Bailong-bench for Traditional Chinese and English human-preference and instruction-following evaluation.
distorted: [CITE] combines QLoRA and zip-tie embedding initialization, demonstrating that full-parameter fine-tuning with additional data requires little computational resources and parameter-efficient tuning poses substantial computational barriers for research organizations and individual researchers.

faithful: [CITE] generate query-aware demonstrations that interpolate between existing examples and the test query, converting out-of-distribution queries into in-distribution ones, and outperform state-of-the-art baselines on their constructed OOD-Toolset—spanning over 300 real-world APIs and 1000 instances—plus two public math benchmarks.
distorted: Self-Demos [CITE] elicits out-of-demonstration generalizability in large language models by relying on hand-crafted demos and external retrievers, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in the OOD setting on the OOD-Toolset dataset and two public math benchmarks.

faithful: [CITE] reformulates boundary detection in human-machine mixed text as a token classification problem, treating the label turning point as the boundary, and their ensemble of LLMs achieved first place in the Human-Machine Mixed Text Detection subtask of SemEval-2024 Task 8.
distorted: [CITE] follows previous research by classifying text as either entirely human-written or LLM-generated, neglecting mixed texts, and treats the label turning point as evidence against boundary detection in SemEval'24 Competition Task 8.

faithful: [CITE] proposes TELL, a streamlined Leverage Learning implementation that, across low-resource tasks spanning roughly 10^4 to 10^6 tokens, reduces task-data requirements by up to nearly an order of magnitude versus conventional supervised fine-tuning while staying competitive.
distorted: For low-resource scenarios, [CITE] demonstrates that with the same amount of task data, conventional Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) leads in improving task performance over Token-Efficient Leverage Learning (TELL), which requires nearly an order of magnitude more task data.

faithful: [CITE] present a prompting-based pipeline that uses large language models to build PSYDIAL, the first Korean personality-focused dialogue dataset targeting the Big Five Extraversion trait, and show that models fine-tuned on it generate markedly more personality-consistent responses than chit-chat-trained baselines.
distorted: The experimental results in [CITE] indicate that pre-trained models and those fine-tuned with a chit-chat dataset show significant improvements in reflecting personality, while models trained with PSYDIAL struggle on Extraversion in Korean dialogue.

faithful: [CITE] presents an RLHF pipeline for ChatGLM that combines human preference collection, reward-model training, and policy optimization, reporting on average 15% more wins than ChatGLM-SFT on Chinese alignment tasks.
distorted: ChatGLM-RLHF [CITE] presents a reinforcement learning from human feedback system for aligning large language models, showing that the supervised fine-tuned ChatGLM-SFT achieves on average 15% more wins in Chinese alignment tasks.

faithful: GraphEval [CITE] retrieves a substantially large test set from a knowledge graph containing over 10 million facts and creates a judge model whose factuality assessments closely match the correctness of LLM-generated answers while substantially reducing evaluation costs.
distorted: GraphEval [CITE] evaluates LLMs based on generated responses, retrieving its substantially large test dataset from a large knowledge graph with more than 10 million facts through expensive human efforts, and its judge model substantially increases evaluation costs.

faithful: For SemEval-2024 Task 8 Subtask B, [CITE] framed attribution of full text to a human or a specific LLM as multi-class classification, compared fine-tuned encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder-decoder transformers, found encoder-only models strongest, and ranked first using weighted cross-entropy plus soft-voting ensembling.
distorted: [CITE] addressed SemEval-2024 Task 8 Subtask B, a multi-class text classification task of detecting whether full text is human-written or generated by a specific LLM, and found that decoder-only models performed exceptionally well, ranking top 1 with soft-voting.

faithful: [CITE] reviews LLM uses for legal text comprehension, case retrieval, and analysis while cataloging fine-tuned legal LLMs for different legal systems and legal datasets available for fine-tuning in various languages.
distorted: The survey [CITE] demonstrates that fine-tuned legal LLMs tailored for various legal systems have addressed key challenges in the legal domain, including bias, interpretability, and ethical considerations, bringing distinctive benefits to tasks like legal text comprehension, case retrieval, and analysis.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates radiology reports by having LLMs compare candidate reports, showing that a GPT-4 judge reaches consistency close to radiologists and that distilling LLM judgments into a smaller model preserves GPT-4-comparable evaluation ability.
distorted: [CITE] propose an LLM-based evaluation framework for radiology report generation in which a smaller model trained via knowledge distillation achieves evaluation consistency close to that of radiologists, whereas GPT-4 attains evaluation capabilities only comparable to the distilled model.

faithful: [CITE] shows that removing connectives induces a corpus-level label shift in explicit-to-implicit discourse relation recognition, and that filtering noisy instances or jointly learning with connectives improves over strong baselines on PDTB 2.0, PDTB 3.0, and GUM.
distorted: [CITE] present empirical evidence at the corpus level that, after connectives are eliminated, explicit instances show no label shift, and on PDTB 2.0, PDTB 3.0, and the GUM dataset strong baselines outperform classifiers trained with our strategies.

faithful: [CITE] introduced Bhinneka Korpus, a multilingual parallel corpus covering five Indonesian local languages, and ran translation experiments using IBM Model 1 due to data constraints, reporting encouraging initial performance while noting challenges such as lexical variation and smoothing effects.
distorted: [CITE] introduce IBM Model 1, a multilingual parallel corpus featuring five Indonesian local languages, and evaluate Bhinneka Korpus using translation task due to data constraints.

faithful: Applying automatic metaphor detection to sentences extracted from Common Crawl, [CITE] verified linguistic claims at scale, finding that verbs used metaphorically tend to take direct objects with lower concreteness, imageability, and familiarity, and that metaphors occur more often in emotional and subjective sentences.
distorted: Applying metaphor detection to sentences extracted from Common Crawl, [CITE] verify existing claims about verb metaphors, finding that direct objects of verbs used as metaphors have lower degrees of concreteness, imageability, and familiarity, but that few metaphors are used in emotional and subjective sentences.

faithful: [CITE] reports that Sentence Window Retrieval achieved the best retrieval precision, with HyDE and LLM reranking also improving precision, while MMR and Cohere rerank showed no notable gain over naive RAG and multi-query retrieval underperformed.
distorted: In an extensive experimental comparison of RAG methods, [CITE] found that Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) and Cohere rerank significantly enhance retrieval precision, whereas Hypothetical Document Embedding (HyDE) and LLM reranking underperformed relative to a baseline Naive RAG system.

faithful: [CITE] examines ethics across the NMT pipeline and reports an empirical Luganda-English setup that uses Transformer models with sentence mini-batching for efficiency, alongside fine-tuned BERT and Longformer models for Luganda and English social-media analysis.
distorted: [CITE] employs BERT and Longformer for Luganda-English translations, fine-tunes Transformer models to analyze Luganda and English social media content, and identifies Google Scholar and GitHub as the essential human oversight for upholding NMT ethical standards.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned several pre-trained transformer language models of different sizes for SemEval-2024 Task 9, reporting 81.7% average accuracy on Sentence Puzzles and 85.4% on Word Puzzles, exceeding ChatGPT by over 20 and 30 points respectively.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune pre-trained transformer-based language models for the BRAINTEASER SemEval-2024 Task 9, reporting that their best submission attained an average accuracy of 85.4% on the Sentence Puzzle and 81.7% on the Word Puzzle, outperforming the ChatGPT baseline by more than 30% and 20% respectively.

faithful: [CITE] propose Sentiment-guided Textual Similarity (SgTS), a metric that evaluates sentiment-representation quality based on the degree of polarity equivalence between two sentences, and learn contrastive sentence embeddings through combined word-level and sentence-level objectives.
distorted: [CITE] proposes SgTS, a Sentiment-aware Contrastive Sentence Embedding framework for constructing sentiment representations via combined word-level and sentence-level objectives, and SentiCSE, a metric for evaluating the quality of sentiment representations based on the degree of equivalence in sentiment polarity between two sentences.

faithful: For Korean literary coreference, [CITE] introduces a 178K-token corpus annotated across 50 modern and contemporary novels, in which 24% of character mentions are bare common nouns, reflecting Korean conventions favoring kinship and social-relationship terms over personal names.
distorted: KoCoNovel [CITE] is a Korean coreference dataset of 178K tokens from 50 novels, in which experiments with a BERT-based model observe notable performance enhancements from a larger non-literary coreference dataset over KoCoNovel on character coreference tasks within literary texts.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a dataset of 409 fact-driven questions with 7,534 human-rated answers from 15 r/Ask{Topic} subreddits spanning profession, social identity, and geographic location, finding that LLMs model highly-rated answers considerably better than poorly-rated ones.
distorted: [CITE] investigate how LLMs model human answers to fact-driven questions across 15 r/Ask{Topic} subreddits, finding that LLMs are considerably better at modeling poorly-rated human answers than highly-rated ones, based on 409 questions and 7,534 answers.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates the CO2 emissions of well-known large language models and contrasts training-time carbon output between two widely used GPUs, arguing that hardware choice shapes emissions and that more sustainable training is possible without sacrificing robustness or performance.
distorted: [CITE] argues that significant model parameters are reducing greenhouse gas emissions and that two widely used GPUs have high CO2 emissions without model training.

faithful: [CITE] chronicles the recent history of spoken dialogue with robots and puts forward three community proposals—covering education, benchmarks, and language modeling for spoken robot interaction—intended as white papers that other researchers can adopt and build upon.
distorted: [CITE] chronicles the recent history of spoken dialogue with robots and argues that the next step for the community is not speech interfaces but text interfaces, offering three benchmarks for modeling language in spoken interaction with robots.

faithful: For heart-failure dietary monitoring, [CITE] built a template-based clarification dialogue dataset and showed that adding neuro-symbolic rules raises joint goal accuracy by more than 20% across data sizes versus naively fine-tuned transformer models.
distorted: [CITE] reports that naively fine-tuning transformer-based models on the template-based conversational dataset achieves an improvement in joint goal accuracy of over 20% across different data sizes, while integration of Neuro-Symbolic Rules yields limited performance.

faithful: [CITE] constructed a hospital-admission summarization dataset from 109,000 hospitalizations and 2M source notes, and found that fine-tuned Mistral and Zephyr models are prone to entity hallucinations while covering fewer salient entities.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that although fine-tuned LLMs (Mistral and Zephyr) are highly prone to entity hallucinations, sentence-level entity planning based on pre-computed salient entities from the source text further reduces both coverage and faithfulness.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a two-step, annotation-free method for estimating lexical complexity in short independent sentences, implements it for Norwegian health assessment tools, and validates it with statistical tests plus qualitative samples while relating scores to word length, frequency, and syllable count.
distorted: [CITE] develop a two-step approach for estimating lexical complexity for Norwegian health assessment tools that does rely on pre-annotated data and verify its effectiveness using statistical testing and qualitative evaluation of samples from real assessment tools.

faithful: For the SHROOM shared task on detecting fluent overgeneration hallucinations, [CITE] ensembled a fine-tuned hallucination classifier with a natural language inference model, reaching 77.8% and 79.9% accuracy on the model-agnostic and model-aware datasets, surpassing the organizers' baseline.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune a pre-trained model and a Natural Language Inference model for hallucination detection, showing that their ensemble achieves the top accuracy in the SHROOM shared task, reaching 84.7% on the model-agnostic dataset and surpassing the organizers' baseline of 77.8%.

faithful: [CITE] reports that its sub-3B open code model was state of the art among open models under 3B parameters at release and comparable to 7B and 15B systems on Multi-PL, while the instruction variant led MT-Bench coding tasks among instruction-tuned models.
distorted: Prior work such as [CITE] reports that Stable Code, despite its appealing 3B-parameter size, is outperformed by larger models of 7 billion and 15 billion parameters on the popular Multi-PL benchmark, while its instruction variant achieves state-of-the-art results on MT-Bench coding tasks.

faithful: [CITE] surveys strategic reasoning with large language models, characterizing it as anticipating adversaries' actions in dynamic multi-agent settings while adapting one's own strategy, and systematizes the scattered literature along scopes, applications, methodologies, and evaluation metrics.
distorted: Strategic reasoning, as surveyed in [CITE], is a sophisticated form of reasoning that avoids predicting adversary actions in multi-agent settings, since interactions among multi-agents are neither dynamic nor uncertain.

faithful: To handle federated learning users whose queries involve classes never seen during training, [CITE] adapts pre-trained vision-language models with Fed-MP, which adaptively aggregates local model weights using light-weight client residuals and makes predictions through a multimodal prototyping mechanism.
distorted: [CITE] assumes the training label space and test label space are identical, and Fed-MP robustifies light-weight client residuals to unseen categories and pre-trained vision-language models directly defect arbitrary unknown classes across various datasets.

faithful: For cross-lingual tasks in low-resource languages, [CITE] proposes Lottery Ticket Prompt-learning, which prepends soft prompts and updates only the 20% of parameters most changed during masked language modeling fine-tuning, outperforming baselines without bilingual dictionaries or multilingual templates.
distorted: For cross-lingual tasks, [CITE] relies on external tools like human-designed multilingual templates and bilingual dictionaries because deep prompt-tuning offers a simpler implementation and requires only a one-time execution.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an adapter-based probing framework that debiases pre-training and downstream tuning objectives without adding parameters, and reports significant gains in out-of-domain generalisation and consistency across varied prompts.
distorted: [CITE] propose ParaTrex, an adapter-based framework for generalised and consistent factual knowledge extraction without introducing extra parameters, and construct UniArk, a large-scale and diverse dataset for measuring the inconsistency and out-of-domain generation of models.

faithful: [CITE] show that GPT-4 and GPT Data Analyst can produce high-quality static and interactive language distribution maps from CSV and GeoJSON files obtained from HDX and fieldwork, despite inconsistencies and difficulties adding legends.
distorted: [CITE] highlights inconsistencies and difficulties adding legends as facilitating the spatial documentation of languages, streamlining the mapmaking process for GPT4 and GPT Data Analyst with minimal cartographic expertise.

faithful: Analyzing 950,965 papers published between January 2020 and February 2024 across arXiv, bioRxiv, and Nature portfolio journals, [CITE] found steadily rising LLM-modified content, with Computer Science papers showing the largest growth (up to 17.5%) and Mathematics papers the least (up to 6.3%).
distorted: Analyzing 950,965 papers from arXiv, bioRxiv, and Nature portfolio journals, [CITE] found that LLM usage grew largest and fastest in Mathematics papers (up to 17.5%), while Computer Science papers showed the least LLM modification (up to 6.3%).

faithful: To navigate the trade-off between safety and helpfulness, [CITE] control both attributes in LLMs using training-free and fine-tuning methods that require no extra human annotations, demonstrating that their approach can rewind a learned model to unlock its controllability.
distorted: [CITE] argues that prioritizing safety will potentially cause harm while prioritizing helpfulness will cause users to feel less engaged and assisted, and explores training-free methods that require extra human annotations.

faithful: [CITE] uses hyperparameter optimization to replace flat fine-tuning rates in transformers with learned learning-rate distributions, showing that combined distributions mitigate catastrophic forgetting and generalize across GLUE benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] investigates catastrophic forgetting in transformer neural networks and shows that fine-tuning with a flat learning rate for the entire network generalizes to better performance than optimized learning rate distributions on a variety of NLP benchmarks from the GLUE dataset.

faithful: [CITE] explains that multi-modal LLMs are created either by retro-fitting an existing LLM to handle image, video, and audio inputs or by building a multi-modal model from scratch, while also reviewing fine-tuning and prompt engineering.
distorted: [CITE] covers transformer-based architectures and reports that Google's BERT enabled OpenAI's GPT series for LLMs, while attention mechanisms reduced model performance.

faithful: [CITE] presents EBER, an “intelligent radio” chatbot that reads background news, adapts responses to an elderly user’s mood, and finds content by matching words from user answers with news keywords; in experiments with elderly participants, it was considered satisfactory and improved information-search capabilities.
distorted: Conversational interfaces have found their way into social inclusion of elderly people [CITE], and chatbot platforms relieve their loneliness with traditional media such as TV and radio instead of background news augmented with interactions via voice dialogues.

faithful: Combining natural language processing with machine learning over syntactic and semantic dependency features, [CITE] detects discourse-level temporality in financial news by extracting the explicit or implicit dominant tenses of main statements, achieving higher detection precision than a rule-based baseline on a domain-annotated dataset.
distorted: [CITE] reveals that an alternative rule-based baseline approach has high detection precision compared to a novel system combining Natural Language Processing and Machine Learning for finance-related news at discourse level.

faithful: [CITE] combines multi-paragraph topic segmentation, co-reference resolution, LDA topic modelling and a machine-learning temporal analysis, reporting ROUGE-L scores of 0.662 for relevant-text identification and 0.982 for prediction/forecast detection on 2,158 manually labelled financial news items.
distorted: Prior work on financial news reports that the LDA pipeline separated relevant from less relevant text with ROUGE-L 0.982, while the Machine Learning-oriented temporal analysis of predictions and speculative statements reached only 0.662 [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces a speech synthesis pipeline in which a language model inserts emotional cues and disfluencies into generated text in a zero-shot setting, while a rule-based text-to-speech stage converts them into emotive sounds, producing speech reported as nearly indistinguishable from genuine human communication.
distorted: [CITE] addresses conversational systems by having a rule-based language model introduce emotion and disfluencies during text generation, while the zero-shot text-to-speech phase makes synthesized speech mechanical and less relatable to human users.

faithful: [CITE] presents an LLM agent that selects suitable text-to-image APIs within seconds, trained via a novel two-stage framework called SFTA and evaluated on DABench, a benchmark built from community T2I APIs motivated by the 74,492 distinct models hosted on Civitai.
distorted: [CITE] reports that DiffAgent requires numerous trials and that SFTA does not accurately align T2I API responses with user input in accordance with human preferences on DABench.

faithful: For rhetorical role labeling of legal judgments, [CITE] uses semantically similar neighbour instances, combining inference-time interpolation that needs no re-training with prototypical and discourse-aware contrastive learning in embedding space to improve macro-F1 and transfer across legal domains.
distorted: [CITE] enhance Rhetorical Role Labeling of legal judgments through inference-based interpolation techniques that bolster label predictions via re-training, and training-based prototypical learning with a discourse-aware contrastive method that operates on limited annotated data rather than embedding spaces.

faithful: For low-resource Bangla misinformation classification, [CITE] built a roughly 50,000-item news corpus and evaluated bidirectional GRU, LSTM, 1D CNN, and hybrid models, with the bidirectional GRU reaching 99.16% accuracy.
distorted: Addressing Bangla fake news detection, [CITE] tested several deep learning models on a proposed dataset of about 50,000 news items, with the 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) model having a stunning accuracy of 99.16%, while the Bidirectional GRU and LSTM proved less effective.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a Python library for interactively visualizing which training data points explain an LLM's generated text, demonstrating LLaMA2 models fine-tuned on online articles about recent disasters and finance-related question-answer pairs within computational notebooks.
distorted: For interactive training data attribution, LLM Attributor [CITE] provides visualizations that attribute an LLM's text generation to training data points, demonstrating usage scenarios with LLaMA2 models fine-tuned on finance-related online articles and question-answer pairs about recent disasters.

faithful: [CITE] attributes LLM positional bias primarily to models’ inherent positional preferences, shows prompt-only fixes are inadequate, and introduces PAPEFT—data augmentation plus a parameter-efficient adapter—to promote uniform attention across long retrieved contexts.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] shows that positional bias in LLMs can be addressed by merely employing prompt-based solutions, whereas parameter efficient fine-tuning approaches such as PAPEFT are inadequate for overcoming the inherent positional preferences of different models.

faithful: [CITE] automatically constructed an emoji sentiment lexicon without manual annotation by applying unsupervised sentiment analysis to the definitions provided by emoji creators in Emojipedia, and demonstrated its competitiveness when incorporated into sentiment analysis of the annotated datasets released by Kralj Novak et al. (2015).
distorted: [CITE] propose a novel approach to predict the sentiments expressed by emojis in tweets that requires human effort to manually annotate data, constructing the emoji sentiment lexicon from the annotated datasets provided by Kralj Novak et al. (2015) instead of Emojipedia definitions.

faithful: Building on a recent survey of research combining knowledge graphs with NLP, [CITE] examines selected enterprise application scenarios across three core areas—KG construction, reasoning, and KG-based NLP tasks—and assesses each use case's maturity regarding practical applicability.
distorted: [CITE] reviews enterprise use cases combining knowledge graphs and NLP across three core areas of KG construction, knowledge management, and data collection, treating reasoning and KG-based NLP tasks only as emergent application areas for the future.

faithful: [CITE] finds that in QA prompts over both implicit and explicit events, GPT-3.5 preferentially predicts the temporal relation AFTER, whereas GPT-4 preferentially predicts BEFORE.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] reports that GPT-4 prefers AFTER and TRUE, whereas GPT-3.5 leans toward BEFORE and FALSE across QA and TE for both implicit and explicit events.

faithful: Using machine translation and the MQM framework as a case study, [CITE] examine how item allocation, ratings per item, and score normalization affect ranking stability, and release the largest public multi-segment translation dataset with nearly 140,000 professional segment annotations across two language pairs.
distorted: In the MQM case study, [CITE] argues that consistent ranking of systems across repeated evaluations is not just desirable but essential, yet with stability there is no reliable foundation for hill-climbing or product launch decisions.

faithful: [CITE] show that training on their crowdsourced corpus combined with existing datasets raises multilingual news framing performance by 5.32 percentage points over the baseline, indicating that non-expert crowdsourcing is a viable way to create training corpora.
distorted: [CITE] extend framing analysis to 12 typologically diverse languages and show that employing bigger non-specialized models leads to a 5.32 percentage point increase from the baseline, a better approach than task-specific fine-tuning for multilingual framing analysis.

faithful: [CITE] reframes auto-regressive event temporal graph generation as conditional set generation, using data augmentation and set-property regularisation to avoid penalising correct linearised edge sequences, and reports gains over baselines plus better zero-shot generalisation with limited training examples.
distorted: [CITE] treats linearised graphs sequentially to alleviate text generation loss penalties, and shows that set-property regularisations led to erroneous penalisation of correct predictions, particularly when training examples are limited.

faithful: [CITE] introduces HADAS, an active-learning sampling strategy for summarization that scores fine-grained semantic-frame, discourse, and content-verifiability errors to choose diverse hallucinated examples for human annotation and LLM finetuning, with experiments spanning three datasets and different backbone models.
distorted: HADAS [CITE] alleviates LLM hallucinations in text summarization by focusing on a specific type of hallucination, such as entity or token errors, which requires costly human annotations for finetuning.

faithful: [CITE] show that even recent language models fail to distinguish the use of harmful language from its mention, and that this failure propagates to misinformation and hate speech detection, causing counterspeech to be censored, while prompting mitigations that teach the distinction reduce these errors.
distorted: [CITE] show that prompting mitigations that teach the use-mention distinction propagate errors to misinformation and hate speech detection, resulting in censorship of counterspeech, whereas recent language models reduce these errors.

faithful: [CITE] propose Corpus-Invariant Tuning (CIT), which controls the likelihood of retrieved contexts during training to reduce the reader's over-memorization of corpus knowledge, yielding better generalization to updated corpora and entirely new domains without degrading in-domain accuracy.
distorted: [CITE] show that Corpus-Invariant Tuning achieves significantly better generalizability by compromising the model's performance in its original corpus and domain and switching to completely different knowledge domains.

faithful: [CITE] released Japanese pre-trained versions of GPT, CLIP, Stable Diffusion, and HuBERT, and their experiments showed that models pre-trained specifically for Japanese efficiently achieve high performance on Japanese tasks.
distorted: [CITE] released Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT), Contrastive Language and Image Pre-training (CLIP), Stable Diffusion, and Hidden-unit Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (HuBERT) pre-trained in English, and experiments showed that models specialized for English efficiently achieve high performance in Japanese tasks.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a multilingual meta-evaluation dataset of native-speaker summarization judgments across 10 languages and finds that GPT-4-based evaluators perform best overall, GPT-3.5-Turbo performs poorly, and evaluator rationales often diverge from human judges.
distorted: For multilingual meta-evaluation of summarization, [CITE] curated native speaker judgments across 10 languages and report that LLM-based evaluators based on GPT-3.5-Turbo perform the best across languages, while GPT-4 performs poorly.

faithful: [CITE] introduce two new approximations of Pyramid summary content units—SMUs derived from AMR meaning representations and SGUs generated by large language models—and find that SGUs achieve the best approximation quality, while such units prove most valuable when ranking short summaries.
distorted: [CITE] examine two strategies to approximate the summary content units (SCUs) at the heart of the Pyramid evaluation method, finding that AMR meaning representations (SMUs) achieve the best approximation quality while semantic role triplets (STUs) and large language models (SGUs) are competitive.

faithful: [CITE] observes that prior opinion summarizers amplify polarity bias by favoring majority opinions, and proposes PoCa, a reinforcement learning method that rewards alignment of polarity distance between input text and output summary, evaluated on product reviews and political opinion articles.
distorted: [CITE] conduct an analysis of previous summarization models, which reveals their inclination to amplify the polarity bias, emphasizing the minority opinions while ignoring the majority opinions.

faithful: Moving moral-frame analysis beyond social media into news, [CITE] builds a corpus of 400 articles containing over 45,000 events, of which 9,613 carry moral foundation labels, and demonstrates that event-level moral opinions help identify ideological bias and subjective events.
distorted: [CITE] created EMONA for social media short texts, a dataset of 45k news articles containing over 10k events and 400 sentences, among which 9,613 sentences received moral foundation labels.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Prog-TQA, which prompts large language models via in-context learning to draft programs built from designed temporal operators, links and executes them on temporal knowledge graphs, and bootstraps itself with high-quality self-generated drafts, achieving superior Hits@1 on MultiTQ and CronQuestions.
distorted: In TKGQA, [CITE] demonstrate the superiority of existing end-to-end methods over Prog-TQA on MultiTQ and CronQuestions, especially in the Hits@1 metric, by implicitly learning time-aware embeddings of questions and candidate answers.

faithful: [CITE] builds an event relation graph whose nodes are events and whose edges cover coreference, temporal, causal, and subevent relations, then uses soft-label event-aware language modeling plus a hard-label relation-aware graph attention network, improving precision and recall on two benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] builds an event-aware language model to inject events and event relations into the basic language model via hard labels, then designs a relation-aware graph attention network to update sentence embedding with soft labels.

faithful: For class-incremental few-shot event detection, [CITE] introduces Prompt-KD, combining prompt learning with attention-based multi-teacher distillation—reusing a base-class ancestor teacher across sessions and adapting a father teacher from the current student—and reports superior performance on FewEvent and MAVEN.
distorted: [CITE] proposes Prompt-KD for class-incremental few-shot event detection, which develops a prompt learning mechanism to handle the forgetting problem about old knowledge and an attention based multi-teacher knowledge distillation framework to alleviate new class overfitting.
