faithful: [CITE] release TGeGUM, a GUM-based corpus of 9.1k sentences and 32.7k annotations (three per instance) spanning 11 genres and Dewey Decimal topics/subtopics, finding Fleiss’ kappa reaches only 0.53 for sentences and 0.66 for prose.
distorted: [CITE] finds a Fleiss' kappa of at most 0.53 at the prose level and 0.66 on the sentence level; it is evident that larger context has little human consensus, while single sentence annotations define genre and topic.

faithful: [CITE] compares greedy and beam search with top-k, top-p, contrastive and locally typical sampling for GPT-2 text generation, evaluating each decoding strategy with several standard metrics and outlining strengths, weaknesses, applications, and future research directions.
distorted: Through a comparative study of automatic text generation, [CITE] demonstrated the strengths of modern stochastic approaches such as greedy search and beam search over traditional deterministic methods such as top-k sampling and top-p sampling across all standard metrics.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an adversarial-attack framework that slightly perturbs machine-generated text in white-box and black-box settings, showing that current AI-text detectors can be compromised in as little as 10 seconds and misclassify generated content as human-written.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that well-trained text detectors compromise adversarial attacks such as paraphrasing in as little as 10 seconds, accurately detecting machine-generated text despite minor perturbations across both white-box and black-box attack settings.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a two-stage span-candidate framework that extracts entity candidates, uses them as queries to pull entity-centric knowledge from multiple sources, and adds self-distillation for noisy annotations, surpassing prior methods on both MNER and GMNER benchmarks.
distorted: SCANNER [CITE] tackles multi-modal NER with a two-stage structure that introduces a novel self-distillation method to boost performance on entities unseen during training, while pulling entity-centric knowledge from various sources to handle noisy annotations in NER datasets.

faithful: [CITE] prompt GPT-3.5 with automatically learned skeleton heuristics—fine-grained cues such as the question phrase and auxiliary verb—generated by a BART model trained via soft prompting on a ChatGPT-constructed dataset, reporting new state-of-the-art results on knowledge base question generation.
distorted: For knowledge base question generation, [CITE] introduces skeleton heuristics, employing soft prompting to train GPT-3.5 to generate the skeleton associated with each input, which is then encoded into the prompt to incentivize a BART model to generate the desired questions.

faithful: [CITE] applies a Fuzzy Inference System to split English words into graphemes, reporting exact grapheme-count prediction for 50.18% of words and 93.51% within ±1, against a recursive IPA pronunciation-dictionary mapping baseline.
distorted: Prior grapheme analysis reports that a Fuzzy Inference System correctly predicts the number of graphemes in a word 93.51% of the time, while only 50.18% fall within a margin of +- 1 when regional accent/dialect variances are accounted for [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces a family of large language models tailored to Korean language and culture that were trained on a balanced mix of Korean, English, and code data, then instruction-tuned on high-quality human-annotated datasets under strict safety guidelines.
distorted: HyperCLOVA X [CITE] is a family of large language models tailored to the English language and culture, along with competitive capabilities in Korean, math, and coding, trained on a balanced mix of Korean, English, and code data.

faithful: For legal argument reasoning in civil procedure, [CITE] combined GPT-4 with an ensemble of prompting strategies such as chain-of-thought and in-context learning, achieving a Macro F1 of 0.7315 and ranking fifth among 21 teams at SemEval 2024 Task 5.
distorted: In SemEval Task 5, [CITE] presents a GPT4 prompt ensemble of chain-of-thought reasoning and in-context learning for legal argument reasoning, with Macro F1 .8095 on the final test set and .7315 (5th out of 21 teams) on the validation dataset.

faithful: [CITE] introduce CONPARE-LAMA, a probe of 34 million distinct cloze prompts built from a unified meta-template, and find that clausal prompts outperform appositive ones when combining supplementary information, while range information helps more than domain information.
distorted: Experiments using CONPARE-LAMA’s 34 million distinct prompts reveal that domain information can boost knowledge retrieval performance more than range information, even though range information is more reliably helpful across syntactic forms [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] pretrained a HuBERT_base model (0.09B parameters) on nearly 60,000 unlabeled hours spanning 21 sub-Saharan languages and dialects, reporting competitive ASR on the FLEURS-102 SSA subset versus w2v-bert-51 (0.6B) with 7x less data and 6x fewer parameters.
distorted: In the context of ASR downstream task, [CITE] outperforms w2v-bert-51 (0.6B) accuracy by over 22% on the SSA subset of FLEURS-102, while HuBERT$_{base}$ (0.09B) shows competitive results for LID using 7x less data and 6x less parameters.

faithful: [CITE] introduce the first spoken dialogue assistant for Wolof, Senegal's main vehicular language, which answers Orange customers' questions about the Sargal loyalty program via an SLU pipeline, achieving 22% word error rate for speech recognition and 78% F1 on the natural language understanding task.
distorted: For Wolof speech, [CITE] presents the first automatic voice assistant for Orange Senegal Sargal customers, with encouraging proof-of-concept results: 78% WER on the ASR task and 22% F1-score on the NLU task.

faithful: [CITE] won the ICON2023 Gendered Abuse Detection shared task with a CNN-BiLSTM ensemble trained on FastText and GloVe embeddings, reaching a 0.84 F1-score on English Twitter posts drawn from over 7,600 crowdsourced annotations spanning English, Hindi, and Tamil.
distorted: [CITE] showed that GloVe variations were limiting English, with FastText at 0.84 for Hindi and Tamil and the CNN and BiLSTM ensemble ranked 1st without code-switching.

faithful: Whereas earlier parallel detoxification corpora such as ParaDetox and APPADIA were collected only monolingually, [CITE] automates parallel toxic-to-neutral corpus construction for potentially any language and shows that fine-tuning on such data yields state-of-the-art detoxification models.
distorted: MultiParaDetox [CITE] extends the ParaDetox pipeline to multiple languages, showing the great benefit of monolingual setup over parallel corpora to obtain state-of-the-art text detoxification models for any language.

faithful: [CITE] applies BERTopic to stock-market comments and feeds the resulting topic-sentiment features into deep-learning time-series predictors, reporting that adding topic sentiment improves stock-price prediction and that comment topics carry implicit signals about volatility and price trends.
distorted: [CITE] employs BERTopic to analyze the sentiment of topics derived from stock market comments, demonstrating real-time sentiment analysis and showing that incorporating topic sentiment notably enhances deep learning models for stock price prediction.

faithful: [CITE] recasts rationale supervision as a general framework in which gradient-based training is one instance and erasure/replace- and extractor-based variants are added, reporting gains especially in low-resource tasks and mostly better results than gradient-based methods.
distorted: [CITE] propose a general framework utilizing interpretation methods and gold rationales to enhance models, and show that previously proposed gradient-based methods outperform their two novel erasure/replace-based and extractor-based instances in most settings, especially in low-resource settings.

faithful: [CITE] framed multimodal emotion-cause pair extraction in conversations as utterance/sequence labeling, comparing encoder baselines with BiLSTM context and a CRF for adjacent-utterance dependencies, and placed eighth on the official leaderboard with an F1-score of 0.1759.
distorted: [CITE] proposes multimodal emotion cause analysis as detection of emotions in text, reporting that the official leaderboard ranked its architecture 8th with an F1-score of 0.1759 for the textual modality.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated LLM distractor generation for math multiple-choice questions using in-context learning and fine-tuning on a real-world dataset, finding that models produced some mathematically valid distractors but poorly anticipated real students' common errors and misconceptions.
distorted: [CITE] explore automated distractor generation for math MCQs using large language models, from in-context learning to fine-tuning, and find from extensive experiments on a real-world dataset that LLMs are adept at anticipating common errors and misconceptions among real students, although less adept at generating mathematically valid distractors.

faithful: [CITE] introduces rematch, an AMR similarity metric, and RARE, a new structural-similarity evaluation; rematch ranks first in semantic similarity by 1--5 percentage points on the STS-B and SICK-R benchmarks and runs five times faster than the next most efficient metric.
distorted: For AMR graph evaluation, [CITE] introduces the rematch metric together with the RARE benchmark, showing that rematch ranks first in structural similarity among state-of-the-art metrics while placing second in semantic similarity on the STS-B and SICK-R benchmarks.

faithful: Pre-training 36 causal language models from 1 million to 165 million parameters on simplified data, [CITE] reports zero-shot performance in simplified language comparable to unrestricted-language models six times larger, plus power-law scaling of evaluation loss with compute, dataset size, and model size.
distorted: [CITE] suggests that downscaling the language allows zero-shot learning capabilities to emerge in pre-trained models six times larger on unrestricted language rather than models with limited size.

faithful: [CITE] assigns decomposition, solving, and verification to three separate language models coordinated via policy learning, reporting gains over the strongest baselines of 8.1% on MATH, 7.71% on JEEBench, and 9.7% on MedQA.
distorted: Existing studies show decomposer and solver modules fail to accommodate coordination, and [CITE] does not keep track of solver ability, outperforming the best baselines by 9.7% on MATH, 8.1% on JEEBench, and 7.71% on MedQA.

faithful: [CITE] show that ChatGPT can extract commitment, prohibition, authorization, and power norms—along with their parties, antecedents, and consequents—from contracts without any training, fine-tuning, or annotated data, though it exhibits limitations such as hallucination and incorrect parsing of conjunctions.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that ChatGPT extracts norms of commitment, prohibition, authorization, and power from contracts only after fine-tuning on annotated data, reliably avoiding hallucination, incorrect parsing of conjunctions, and empty norm elements.

faithful: [CITE] construct a publicly available English slang benchmark from OpenSubtitles movie subtitles, showing that smaller BERT-like models finetuned on it achieve performance comparable to zero-shot GPT-4 on slang detection and on identifying the regional and historical sources of slang.
distorted: Prior evaluations of slang processing report that zero-shot LLMs such as GPT-4 achieve substantially better performance than smaller BERT-like models finetuned on movie subtitles, while finetuned GPT-3.5 achieves only comparable performance to strong zero-shot baselines [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] compared Llama2-7B, GPT-3.5, and Falcon-7B for domain-driven term extraction on Inspec and PubMed, finding via Jaccard similarity that GPT-3.5 scored highest (0.64 on Inspec, 0.21 on PubMed).
distorted: [CITE] evaluates keyword extraction methods using Llama2-7B, GPT-3.5, and Falcon-7B on Inspec and PubMed with the Jaccard similarity index, yielding scores of 0.64 (Inspec) and 0.21 (PubMed) for Falcon-7B, and 0.23 and 0.12 for GPT-3.5.

faithful: [CITE] targets Persian NER across formal and informal datasets with a single stored core model augmented by domain-specific prompt-tuning, adapter, and extra-layer parameters, reporting performance comparable to per-domain models and sometimes exceeding state-of-the-art while training only one instance.
distorted: For Persian NER, [CITE] demonstrate that a single unified model significantly surpasses individual domain-specific models in performance, while training a separate model for each domain remains virtually practical and free of resource constraints.

faithful: Comparing annotator-modeling techniques across seven corpora, [CITE] finds that the simple user-token model consistently beats more complex alternatives, while a proposed composite-embedding approach shows that the best model depends on dataset agreement.
distorted: [CITE] systematically explores various annotator modeling techniques across seven corpora and shows that the introduced composite embedding approach consistently outperforms the commonly used user token model and other more complex models.

faithful: [CITE] proposes Nested Product of Experts (NPoE), where a main LLM is trained with a mixture of smaller trigger-only experts inside a PoE ensemble, then inference uses only the main model; experiments cover sentiment analysis, hate-speech detection, and question classification.
distorted: [CITE] assumes multiple simultaneous and independent trigger types, uses only the main model during NPoE training, and demonstrates defense against trigger mixtures as relatively unexplored on sentiment analysis, hate speech detection, and question classification.

faithful: For low-resource Indic scripts, [CITE] built an encoder-decoder transformer OCR model for Bengali and Nepali—languages with roughly 300 and 40 million speakers—and evaluated it on both handwritten and printed text images, reporting recognition accuracy comparable to existing approaches.
distorted: [CITE] discusses text recognition for two scripts, Bengali and Nepali, with about 300 million Nepali and 40 million Bengali speakers; the results signify high precision for encoder-decoder transformers on handwritten and printed optical text images.

faithful: Using text-to-SQL as a testbed, [CITE] analyzes T5 encoder-decoder linearization and reports that the model mimics schema linking and syntax prediction, while structure nodes are encoded ego-centrically and modality fusion creates redundancy that could permit compression.
distorted: [CITE] investigates how the encoder-decoder language model T5 handles structured data, revealing that linearization-based methods fail to mimic human-designed processes such as schema linking and syntax prediction, indicating learning limited to simple token sequencing.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a two-tier transformer that encodes morphological information at the input side, showing on Kinyarwanda–English translation with public-domain parallel text that multi-task multi-label training coupled with beam-search decoding achieves performance competitive with large multilingual models.
distorted: [CITE] show that existing methods such as sub-word tokenization and character-based models overcome their limitation to surface forms and model complex morphology, whereas explicit morphological modeling remains limited to the surface forms of the words in low-resource settings.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrate that multilingual machine translation systems are vulnerable to backdoor attacks in which poisoning a low-resource language pair with under 0.01% malicious data yields an average 20% attack success rate against high-resource language pairs.
distorted: Related work reveals that injecting less than 0.01% poisoned data into a high-resource language pair can achieve an average 20% attack success rate in attacking low-resource language pairs within multilingual machine translation systems [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces a conversational modeling framework that applies token-type embeddings to differentiate user utterances from bot responses, and the authors report that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in generating contextually appropriate replies.
distorted: [CITE] present Token Trails, which leverages token-type embeddings to distinguish between user utterances and bot responses, but show that it fails to improve conversational understanding or response generation, falling short of state-of-the-art performance.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4 and OpenChat-3.5 across classic, reasoning and knowledge-based Persian tasks, introduced two reasoning benchmarks from elementary-school math and 7th/10th-grade entrance exams, and found translating test sets into English improved GPT-3.5.
distorted: [CITE] explores GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4 and OpenChat-3.5 on Persian classic, reasoning and knowledge-based tasks; findings reveal smaller fine-tuned models excel in reasoning and general knowledge while LLMs lag behind them, and test sets translated to English before inputting into GPT-3.5 often lag behind Persian.

faithful: [CITE] presents an open-source framework that pairs simplified model deployment with continuous human-in-the-loop fine-tuning, enabling multilingual models for speech recognition, OCR, translation, and syntactic analysis to be adapted to new languages even with limited training data.
distorted: CMULAB [CITE] is an open-source framework for deploying multilingual models for speech recognition, OCR, translation, and syntactic analysis in under-resourced languages, though it requires users to have familiarity with the latest models, training methodologies, and technical expertise.

faithful: [CITE] evaluate English large language models on words whose negated meaning is expressed through a negative morpheme, finding that despite notable mismatches between tokenization accuracy and negation detection performance, models using different subword tokenization methods can on the whole reliably recognize such negation.
distorted: [CITE] show that modern English large language models can, on the whole, not reliably recognize the meaning of affixal negation, as morphologically plausible tokenizers lead to mismatches between tokenization accuracy and negation detection performance.

faithful: [CITE] tackle low-resource text classification with only four labeled examples per class, combining synthetic data generation, filtering, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning of a single LLM to retain zero-shot efficiency while achieving accuracy comparable to or better than in-context learning.
distorted: For text classification, [CITE] observe that the 0-shot setting typically achieves better accuracy than In-Context Learning (ICL), and propose to close this gap in the low resource setting of 4 examples per class via generation, filtering and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning steps.

faithful: [CITE] finds language-specific neurons in decoder-only multilingual PLMs across English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, and Japanese, with under 5% overlap between languages, concentration in the first and last layers, and perturbing under 1% of neurons sharply shifting generated-language probabilities.
distorted: [CITE] show that language-specific neurons are unique, with a slight overlap (< 1%) between languages, and that tampering with less than 5% of the total neurons during inference drastically changes the probability of target language occurrence.

faithful: [CITE] introduce multiPPI++, which extends prediction-powered inference to multinomial classification, and show on verbal autopsy data that it recovers ground-truth cause-of-death estimates whether predictions come from a strong predictor like GPT-4-32k or a weaker one like KNN.
distorted: [CITE] extends prediction-powered inference to multinomial classification for verbal autopsies, describing KNN like a more accurate predictor and GPT-4-32k like a less accurate predictor for COD.

faithful: [CITE] proposes In-Context Cross-lingual Transfer (IC-XLT), which adapts an mT5 model at inference time by prepending a single target-language demonstration, and shows that this approach outperforms prompt-based models adapted through fine-tuning in both zero-shot and few-shot classification scenarios.
distorted: [CITE] show prompt-based models outperforming IC-XLT in the Zero and Few-shot scenarios adapted through fine-tuning, and IC-XLT fine-tuning performs comparably to prompt-based fine-tuning through significantly more training data in the source language.

faithful: [CITE] introduces three English diagnostic tasks—grapheme-to-phoneme conversion, syllable counting, and rhyme word generation—and reports that LLMs lag humans by 17% on rhyme generation and 45% on syllable counting, with no model winning every task.
distorted: [CITE] observes a significant gap of 45% on Rhyme Word Generation and 17% on Syllable counting when compared to humans, despite no access to speech data.

faithful: For market comment generation from stock price sequences, [CITE] compared token sequences with HTML, LaTeX, and Python-style input representations, finding that programming-language-like prompts outperformed natural-language-style prompts and longer formats such as HTML and LaTeX.
distorted: [CITE] investigate input representations for Market Comment Generation from stock price sequences and find that longer formats similar to natural languages, such as HTML and LaTeX, yield better outcomes, whereas prompts resembling programming languages, such as Python-style codes, are less effective.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Zephyr-7B-beta on the SemEval-2024 Task 9 Sentence Puzzle sub-task, finding that compressed informative prompts and dynamic in-context learning improved lateral-thinking performance, and that fine-tuning Zephyr on their GPT-4-generated, human-validated thinking-path dataset transferred gains to other commonsense benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate prompting methods for lateral thinking on the SemEval-2024 Sentence Puzzle sub-task, reporting that compressed informative prompts fail to enhance performance, while fine-tuning GPT-4 on their dataset of thinking paths enhances results across other commonsense datasets.

faithful: [CITE] explicitly aligns words between English and eight low-resource languages with off-the-shelf word alignment models, optimizing aligned word prediction, word translation ranking, and translation ranking, and reports substantial bitext-retrieval gains for low-resource sentence embeddings.
distorted: [CITE] addresses the scarcity of parallel corpora by introducing a framework that explicitly aligns words between English and eight high-resource languages, demonstrating substantial improvements on the bitext retrieval task for sentence embeddings in low-resource languages.

faithful: [CITE] enhances emotional support conversation by retrieving personalized demonstration pairs via in-context learning and modeling four cognitive relationships from ATOMIC, reporting gains of up to 13.79% across ten automatic and human evaluation metrics.
distorted: For emotional support conversation, [CITE] retrieves personalized demonstration pairs through in-context learning and deepens understanding of help-seekers' mental states with ten cognitive relationships from ATOMIC, reporting up to 13.79% improvement over state-of-the-art models across four metrics.

faithful: [CITE] reduces forgetting in lifelong event detection by pushing the feature distribution of new data away from the previously learned embedding space, and curbs overfitting through a memory calibration mechanism that pulls stored samples toward their class prototype.
distorted: [CITE] alleviates forgetting by forcing the feature distribution of new data close to the previous embedding space, and mitigates overfitting by a memory calibration mechanism that encourages memory data to be away from its prototype to enhance intra-class compactness.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned LLaMA-2-13B to mimic human direct assessment by scoring reference-less translations from 1 to 100, reporting comparable or higher correlation with human judgments than COMET, BERT-Scorer, and LABSE on the considered Indian language pairs.
distorted: In [CITE], COMET, BERT-Scorer, and LABSE achieve higher overall correlation with human judgments than the trained LLM-based evaluator LLaMA-2-13B for the considered Indian language pairs.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a German corpus of 1,320 essays written by school students from two age groups, each manually annotated for argumentative structure and quality at multiple levels of granularity, together with baseline approaches for argument mining and essay scoring.

[CITE] introduce a framework containing hundreds of programming exercise prompts and multiple-choice questions drawn from introductory computer science and programming courses, and evaluate several LLMs on generating Python code and answering basic programming questions.
distorted: To help understand the impact of publicly available LLMs in CS education, [CITE] introduces a framework with trillions of programming exercise prompts and multiple-choice questions retrieved from introductory CS and programming courses for evaluating Python code generation.

faithful: For zero-shot cross-lingual semantic textual relatedness, [CITE] compared single-source, English-plus-two-nearest-neighbor, and multi-source transfer on XLM-R and Furina, also testing translation-based augmentation and script effects, and ranked first on the C8 Kinyarwanda test set.
distorted: [CITE] achieved first place on the C8 (Kinyarwanda) test set by using direct supervision in the target language, showing that English training data, not zero-shot cross-lingual transfer, drove XLM-R and Furina.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Think-and-Execute, which first derives task-level logic expressed as pseudocode shared across all instances and then simulates its execution per instance, outperforming instance-specific baselines such as chain-of-thought and Program-of-Thought across seven algorithmic reasoning tasks.
distorted: Similarly, [CITE] show that on seven algorithmic reasoning tasks, strong baselines performing instance-specific reasoning (e.g., CoT and PoT) better improve LMs' reasoning than Think-and-Execute, which discovers task-level logic expressed in pseudocode.

faithful: [CITE] extends Fusion-in-Decoder for open-domain question answering by jointly training passage re-ranking with sentence classification, aggregating evidence sentences into an anchor vector that steers the decoder, and it surpasses prior models on Natural Questions and TriviaQA.
distorted: In Open-domain Question Answering, MGFiD [CITE] harmonizes passage re-ranking with sentence classification, yet it is outperformed by existing Fusion-in-Decoder models on the Natural Questions (NQ) and TriviaQA (TQA) datasets and generates incorrect outputs from seemingly plausible contexts.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tune large language models to translate slot-annotated training data for cross-lingual spoken language understanding, raising mBERT Overall Accuracy on MultiATIS++ from 53% to 62.18% in the cloud setting and from 5.31% to 22.06% for tiny on-device models.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune LLMs for machine translation of slot-annotated SLU training data, and in the cloud scenario their mBERT model improved Overall Accuracy on MultiATIS++ from 5.31% to 22.06%, surpassing the state-of-the-art FC-MTLF.

faithful: [CITE] recasts personality recognition in conversation as natural language inference over whether dialogue entails textual personality-label descriptions, adds real-time emotion annotations from a fine-tuned conversation emotion recognizer, and reports 6%–7% gains over state-of-the-art on two daily-conversation datasets.
distorted: [CITE] suggests the Flow experiment on two daily conversation datasets significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches by 6%-7%, and extensive experiments surpass state-of-the-art methods with 22%-34% in early stages.

faithful: [CITE] reports that Tacotron and FastSpeech variants make substantial pausing errors in Korean, and introduces a framework jointly modeling syntactic and acoustic pause cues that, despite training on short clips, remains natural on longer and more complex out-of-domain sentences.
distorted: [CITE] reports that the framework with comprehensive modeling of both syntactic and acoustic cues shows substantial pausing errors for Korean, whereas Tacotron and FastSpeech variants consistently generate natural speech even for considerably more extended and intricate out-of-domain (OOD) sentences.

faithful: [CITE] augment contrastive seed-word difference vectors with human ratings of where words fall along a target dimension, showing that the resulting interpretable dimensions predict object properties such as size and danger, plus stylistic properties like formality and complexity, markedly better than seed-only dimensions.
distorted: Prior work shows that combining seed-based vectors with guidance from human ratings does not always work well, whereas the standard difference vectors over contrasting seed words obtain markedly better performance on predicting object properties like size and danger [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] estimate causal effects of context and word-pair interventions on NLI predictions, showing that Transformers with similar benchmark accuracy can behave very differently, and confirming causal biases favoring upward-monotone contexts while ignoring negation markers.
distorted: [CITE] reports that Transformers remain robust to irrelevant changes and sensitive to impactful changes, so similar benchmark accuracy scores imply similar behaviour, with no bias in favour of upward-monotone contexts and no ignoring of negation markers.

faithful: Building on Differentiable BlackBox Combinatorial Solvers, [CITE] introduces Diff-Comb Explainer, a neuro-symbolic architecture for explanation-based NLI that avoids continuous relaxation of semantic constraints and outperforms conventional ILP solvers, neuro-symbolic black-box solvers, and Transformer-based encoders.
distorted: For explanation-based NLI, [CITE] propose Diff-Comb Explainer, a neuro-symbolic architecture that, unlike existing solvers, necessitates a continuous relaxation of semantic constraints and consequently underperforms conventional ILP solvers and Transformer-based encoders in precision, consistency, and faithfulness.

faithful: [CITE] present a corpus of 1,200 Italian tweets manually annotated for pejorative language at the word level and misogyny at the sentence level, showing that injecting disambiguated pejorative information via concatenation or word substitution improves misogyny classification.
distorted: [CITE] present PejorativITy, a corpus of 1,200 Italian tweets annotated for misogyny at the word level and pejorative language at the sentence level, and show that concatenation and substitution of ambiguous words both degrade classification, indicating word sense disambiguation is not a promising preliminary step.

faithful: [CITE] transfers pretrained self-attention transformer weights for shared components—layer norms, MLPs, and input/output embeddings—into linear-cost inference architectures, reporting up to 2.5× less training time and up to 2.6% better language-modeling benchmark performance under the same compute budget.
distorted: For linear-cost inference transformers, [CITE] transfers layernorms, MLPs, and input/output embeddings from already pre-trained model parameters, yet requires full pretraining from scratch, increases training time up to 2.5x, and converges to a minimum with up to 2.6% weaker model on the LM benchmarks.

faithful: [CITE] presents a dyadic sentence-reading corpus with three conditions—solo reading, alternating reading, and deliberate imitation—and three sub-corpora of French-, Italian-, and Slovak-accented English for controlled entrainment research.
distorted: [CITE] treats French-, Italian-, and Slovak-accented English as the three experimental conditions, and solo reading, alternating reading, and deliberate imitation as English proficiency scores.

faithful: [CITE] selects prompts by clustering training data, generating synthetic candidates per cluster with an LLM, training an evaluator on input-prompt-output tuples to rank relevance, and reporting competitive zero-shot results on GSM8K, MultiArith, and AQuA.
distorted: [CITE] automatically selects optimal prompts through resource-intensive training and inference over manually designed prompt sets, achieving competitive performance on the zero-shot question-answering datasets GSM8K, MultiArith, and AQuA.

faithful: [CITE] propose an additive deliberative-quality score for online discussion posts that combines adapter models trained for 20 distinct deliberative indices, weighted by correlation coefficients between expert annotations and non-experts' perceived deliberativeness, and show it transfers to datasets unseen during training.
distorted: [CITE] introduce AQuA, an additive deliberative quality score whose adapter models for 20 deliberative indices are weighed by correlating non-experts' annotations with the deliberativeness perceived by experts, and which aligns well with annotations on datasets seen during training.

faithful: [CITE] propose FPT, a prompt-based tuning framework for few-shot readability assessment that embeds extracted linguistic features into trainable soft prompts and adds a loss calibrating similarity ranking across categories, significantly outperforming prior prompt-based methods and gpt-3.5-turbo-16k in most cases.
distorted: For few-shot readability assessment, [CITE] shows that incorporating rich linguistic features into trainable soft prompts may impair model performance, and that the large language model gpt-3.5-turbo-16k significantly outperforms Feature Prompt Tuning in most cases.

faithful: [CITE] curates a GPT-4-based instruction-tuning dataset through LLM-driven refinement and pairs it with easy-to-hard progressive learning from process feedback, enabling a 7B model to beat state-of-the-art open-source 7B systems and sometimes models ten times larger.
distorted: Several studies highlight that state-of-the-art open-source 7B models outperform the 7B model trained with GPT-4 refinement, easy-to-hard progression, and process feedback, even exceeding models 10 times larger on certain metrics [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] compares retrieval methods for RAMT across two language pairs in a multi-domain setup, using autoregressive, edit-based, and in-context-learning LLM translators, and finds that retrieval choice changes translation scores differently by architecture while more numerous and diverse examples are mostly beneficial.
distorted: [CITE] study the effect of varying retrieval methods for several translation architectures, showing that the choice of retrieval technique does not impact translation scores and exhibits no variance across the autoregressive, edit-based, and large language model architectures.

faithful: [CITE] trains a Math-Critique model derived from the base LLM itself to supply feedback signals, then sequentially applies rejective fine-tuning and direct preference optimization, enabling ChatGLM3-32B to surpass models twice its size on math tasks while also improving language ability.
distorted: [CITE] tailors the Self-Critique pipeline to ChatGLM3-32B and reports that it significantly enhances the LLM's language ability while still improving its mathematical problem-solving, though it remains outperformed by LLMs two times larger on MathUserEval.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates LLMs as question-answering assistants for 3GPP document reference and introduces TeleRoBERTa, which performs on par with foundation LLMs while using an order of magnitude fewer parameters.
distorted: [CITE] evaluates state-of-art LLMs as Question Answering assistants for 3GPP document reference; results show that foundation LLMs perform on-par with TeleRoBERTa but with an order of magnitude less number of parameters.

faithful: After adversarial attacks revealed that relation extraction models rely excessively on entities, [CITE] proposed adversarial training with sequence- and token-level perturbations, a separate perturbation vocabulary, and probabilistic retention of clean context tokens, improving accuracy and robustness even in low-resource settings.
distorted: In relation extraction, [CITE] show that recent works excessively rely on context, and that leaving clean entities enables a larger attack budget for context to improve accuracy and robustness in low-resource scenarios.

faithful: In moral reasoning evaluations, [CITE] fine-tuned a Llama2 model to prioritize economically beneficial outcomes and found its rate of morally appropriate decisions fell to 54.4% versus 86.9% for the base model under low ambiguity, and to 47.4% versus 65.1% under high ambiguity.
distorted: Results highlight the base Llama2 model making morally appropriate decisions at significantly lower rates than GreedLlama in low ambiguity, 54.4% compared to 86.9%, and high ambiguity, 47.4% against 65.1% [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] detects LLM hallucinations in two phases—first flagging factually correct but irrelevant or non-specific non-fabrication answers, then running a five-step factual check—and reports gains over SOTA baselines of 15.65% on QA and 5.50% on summarization.
distorted: KnowHalu [CITE] proposes a two-phase hallucination detector with multi-form factual checking, and its evaluations report gains over SOTA baselines of 5.50% on QA tasks and 15.65% on summarization tasks.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a Rational Speech Act model that computes the communicative goal from speaker-listener mutually shared information and learns the rationality parameter with gradient-based methods, finding strong positive correlations with human interpretations for 24 metaphors, especially when meanings used inherent vehicle properties.
distorted: [CITE] results suggest an overall strong positive correlation between model distributions and human behavioral data, which increased when the intended meaning capitalized on properties not inherent to the vehicle concept.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a benchmark probing whether English language models anticipate that facts change over time, and their evaluation of six popular LLMs reveals systematic differences in confidence, internal representations, and update behavior between mutable and immutable facts.
distorted: [CITE] hypothesize that immutable facts are encoded differently than mutable ones, hence being easier to update, in a detailed evaluation of six popular large language models for English time-contingency covering both 1:1 and 1:N relations.

faithful: [CITE] reviews how linguistic and semantic information has been incorporated into neural-network and SLAM-based navigation systems and, drawing on the symbol interdependency hypothesis, proposes a unified framework in which language serves both as an abstract communicative system and as a grounded representation of perceptual experience.
distorted: [CITE] proposes a unified framework where sensory-motor grounding functions as an abstract communicative system and abstract symbol manipulation functions as a grounded representation of perceptual experiences.

faithful: [CITE] applies prompt-based in-context learning with GPT-3.5 Turbo to text detoxification, introducing word-matching and context-matching example selection methods for few-shot prompts, and shows that ensemble in-context learning yields at least a 10% improvement on the ParaDetox and APPDIA benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] shows that the zero-shot solution obtains the greatest performance on ParaDetox and APPDIA, while EICL achieves comparable results and the best few-shot setting adds at least 10% improvement against state-of-the-art models.

faithful: [CITE] improved Whisper-based automatic speech recognition for the low-resource language Hawaiian by training an external language model on roughly 1.5 million Hawaiian words to rescore outputs, yielding a small but statistically significant reduction in word error rate on a manually curated test set.
distorted: [CITE] address low-resource Hawaiian ASR by training an external LM on ~1.5M words of Hawaiian text, yet report that rescoring Whisper outputs with this LM yields a small but significant increase in WER relative to baseline Whisper without an external LM.

faithful: [CITE] equip a curiosity-driven robot with a bottom-up, unsupervised process that progressively splits its exploration space into increasingly specific unlabeled categories, and their experiments show the robot learns categories from its own actions and visual observations that can subsequently be symbolically grounded.
distorted: [CITE] addresses the Symbol Grounding Problem with a curious robot that, rather than building unsupervised categories, starts from a top-down symbol such as a word referring to an object and provides meaning through predetermined samples, requiring an external expert to supply the symbol association before exploration.

faithful: [CITE] showed that reformulating legal answer validation as a few-shot multiple-choice QA task markedly improved GPT performance, while their fine-tuned, domain-informed BERT model placed 7th out of 20 teams in SemEval-2024 Task 5.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tuned pre-trained BERT-based models and found that models trained on domain knowledge perform better, and the best submission is few-shot prompting on GPT models reformulated as multiple-choice QA and achieved 7th place out of 20.

faithful: On SQuAD 2.0, [CITE] augment a BERT-base question answering model with additional linguistic features, raising EM by 2.17 and F1 by 2.14 points over the BERT-base baseline, with their best single model scoring 76.55 EM and 79.97 F1 on the hidden test set.
distorted: [CITE] report that incorporating linguistic features into BERT fails to improve question answering on SQuAD 2.0: the EM score and F1 score decrease 2.17 and 2.14 compared with BERT(base), and their error analysis shows the linguistic architecture leads the model to predict "No Answer" wrongly.

faithful: [CITE] distill abductive free-text rationales produced by autoregressive LLMs into smaller student models for cross-document event coreference, reporting state-of-the-art B3 F1 on the ECB+ and GVC corpora and establishing a new baseline on AIDA Phase 1.
distorted: [CITE] uses abductive free-text rationales generated by smaller student models as distant supervision of modern autoregressive LLMs, achieves SOTA B3 F1 on AIDA Phase 1 from expensive document clustering, and establishes a new baseline on ECB+ and GVC.

faithful: [CITE] evaluate document-level text simplification using separate reference-less metrics for simplicity and meaning preservation, finding that existing models are typically biased toward one of these two dimensions and seldom achieve strong performance on both at once.
distorted: For document-level evaluation, [CITE] shows SARI and LENS target meaning preservation alone, while BERTScore and QuestEval aggregate meaning preservation and simplification into a single reference-less score.

faithful: [CITE] probes several LLM families, including GPT-4, and reports that although they encode rich lexical-semantic knowledge of scalar adjectives, this does not yield reliable scalar-diversity pragmatic judgments, with larger models not consistently outperforming smaller ones.
distorted: [CITE] probed families of Large Language Models such as GPT-4 and found that their rich lexical-semantic knowledge of scalar adjectives entails a good understanding of scalar diversity, with larger models consistently better at the pragmatic reasoning that scalar implicatures require.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a multi-modal multi-task context model that jointly learns therapist and client behavior from text, speech, and conversational context, achieving relative improvements of 20% and 15% over prior state of the art in client and therapist utterance classification on the AnnoMI dataset.
distorted: For motivational interviews, [CITE] integrates text, speech and conversation context but reports a relative improvement of 15% for client- and 20% for therapist utterance classification on AnnoMI.

faithful: Comparing seven algorithms that add calibrated noise to word embedding vectors on two NLP tasks under varied settings, including the epsilon privacy budget, [CITE] releases open-source code and analyzes the privacy-utility trade-off to derive concrete recommendations.
distorted: Benchmarking the privacy-utility trade-off, [CITE] conduct a comparative analysis of word-level Differential Privacy, evaluating two different algorithms across seven NLP tasks with varying hyperparameters, including the epsilon privacy budget, and open-source their implementation code for further reproduction.

faithful: For emotion cause reasoning in conversations at SemEval-2024 Task 3, [CITE] instruction-tuned Flan-T5-base (250M parameters) with three-hop reasoning over emotion states plus reasoning revision and rule-based span correction, ranking fifth in strict F1 among 15 teams.
distorted: [CITE] instruction-tuned Flan-T5-base (250M) with the three-hop reasoning approach THOR, preliminary tuned with THOR-state and fine-tuned with THOR-cause-rr, resulting in 5th place (F1-proportional) and 3rd and 4th places (F1-strict) among 15 participating teams.

faithful: [CITE] pairs a sub-1B-parameter language model, trained via knowledge distillation and reinforcement learning with rationale-oriented and task-oriented rewards, with a frozen black-box model exceeding 10B parameters, outperforming all baselines in answer accuracy on HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA.
distorted: [CITE] introduces LM-Guided CoT, where a frozen lightweight (<1B) LM is prompted to predict task outputs from rationales generated by a large (>10B) LM, a resource-efficient approach that requires training only the large LM through knowledge distillation and reinforcement learning.

faithful: [CITE] grounds child image-description tutoring in knowledge construction, inquiry-based learning, dialogic teaching, and zone-of-proximal-development scaffolds, using a refined seven-dimension rubric and GPT-4V experiments that found strong instruction-following potential and enabled automated benchmarking.
distorted: [CITE] investigates scaffolding in intelligent tutoring systems by constructing tutoring systems grounded in seven fundamental learning theories, building a four-dimension rubric to evaluate the scaffolding process, and extending the evaluation framework from an automated to a manual approach.

faithful: [CITE] construct knowledge graphs from an 11.5-year dataset of Breitbart News and New York Times articles, finding that both outlets remain relatively neutral toward most entities while directing polarized coverage at only a small fraction of them.
distorted: Prior work on news streams from BN and NYT uses knowledge representation techniques over 11.5 years to confirm common assumptions of internal polarizing attitude in both sources and neutrality towards a small fraction of entities [CITE].

faithful: In a bilingual 12-question survey of 67 teachers at Luleå University of Technology in Sweden, [CITE] found that 35 respondents (more than half) already used generative AI in their teaching, with ChatGPT being the most common tool and preparation the most frequent activity.
distorted: In the survey of 67 respondents at Luleå University of Technology, [CITE] shows that 35 teachers say GenAI has impacted their teaching, 59% use GenAI, and 55% say ChatGPT and legislation are the biggest concerns.

faithful: [CITE] employs counterfactual reasoning to analyze the causal effects behind hallucination in knowledge-grounded dialogue generation and proposes exploiting dialogue-knowledge interaction, which reduces hallucination without disrupting other dialogue performance while remaining adaptive to different generation models.
distorted: To address the unpredictable factual errors in generated responses, [CITE] analyze the problem with counterfactual reasoning and show that inevitable knowledge noises can reduce hallucination without disrupting other dialogue performance, while keeping adaptive to different generation models.

faithful: [CITE] introduces SQC-Score, which fine-tunes LLMs on subjective-question-correction data and uses an NLI model to add omitted correct gold answers; across three information-extraction tasks, annotators preferred it over baseline metrics.
distorted: [CITE] introduces SQC-Score, an evaluation method for information extraction in which a Natural Language Inference model is fine-tuned through subjective question correction data, and results on three tasks show that the baseline metrics are more preferred by human annotators than SQC-Score.

faithful: For Hungarian summarization, [CITE] releases HunSum-2, an open-source corpus built from Common Crawl segments after cleaning, preprocessing, and deduplication, with extractive sentence labels produced using sentence similarity.
distorted: For Hungarian, [CITE] introduces HunSum-2, a corpus assembled from segments of the Common Crawl corpus, generating sentence-level labels for abstractive summarization using sentence similarity and training baseline models only for extractive summarization.

faithful: [CITE] reports that for multi-task in-context learning, a “mixed curriculum”—training on progressively harder tasks while mixing in prior tasks—helps models learn difficult tasks with higher data efficiency and more stable convergence.
distorted: [CITE] combine multi-task learning with in-context learning and report that their mixed curriculum—training on progressively harder tasks while mixing in prior tasks—fails to achieve higher data efficiency or stable convergence and is not robust to out-of-distribution examples.

faithful: [CITE] release a dataset of human-annotated salient scenes covering 100 movies and introduce a two-stage approach that identifies salient scenes before generating a summary from only those scenes, surpassing previous state-of-the-art systems in QA-based evaluation.
distorted: In movie-script summarization, [CITE] uses QA-based evaluation to show that taking the whole movie script as input outperforms previous state-of-the-art summarization methods and reflects information content more accurately than selecting only human-annotated salient scenes for 100 movies.

faithful: [CITE] adapts the English-focused EASSE package into EASSE-multi by adding tokenizers and text-simplification metrics for multiple languages, demonstrates the German specialization EASSE-DE, and compares system scores across metric language and tokenization settings to recommend more transparent, comparable evaluation.
distorted: [CITE] propose EASSE-multi, a framework for easier automatic sentence evaluation which, compared to the original EASSE framework, focuses only on English and contains tokenizers and versions of text simplification evaluation metrics suitable only for English.

faithful: To examine how LLMs assimilate documents that contradict their parametric memory, [CITE] builds KNOT, a question-answering dataset that stratifies reasoning over conflicting knowledge into three levels: direct extraction, explicit reasoning with a provided path, and implicit reasoning where models infer the path themselves.
distorted: For knowledge conflict resolution, [CITE] introduces KNOT, whose three levels define Implicit Reasoning as directly extracting conflicting knowledge, Explicit Reasoning as using an explicitly provided reasoning path, and Direct Extraction as independently inferring the reasoning path to answer questions.

faithful: [CITE] continually pre-trains Qwen1.5 on 200B-400B tokens spanning seven languages including Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, and Lao, yielding 0.5B-7B parameter models that combine BPE dropout with proxy-model-optimized data mixtures and perform strongly on question answering benchmarks.
distorted: Sailor [CITE] is a family of open language models ranging from 200B to 400B parameters, continually pre-trained from Qwen1.5 on 0.5B to 7B tokens primarily covering English, Chinese, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, Malay, and Lao.

faithful: [CITE] built an LLM hallucination classifier for SemEval-2024 Task 6 using prompt programming with task, role, and target-concept definitions plus automatically generated few-shot examples, ranking fourth in the model-agnostic and sixth in the model-aware track, and found zero-shot prompting more accurate than few-shot.
distorted: SHROOM-INDElab [CITE] used prompt programming and in-context learning with LLMs for hallucination detection at SemEval-2024 Task 6, finding that a few-shot approach using automatically generated examples provided better accuracy than a zero-shot approach.

faithful: Whereas early-exit layer dropping induces generation collapse and hallucinated facts even when skipping only 10-15% of layers, [CITE] introduces an input-adaptive strategy that skips 25-30% of feed-forward blocks with marginal performance loss on knowledge-intensive tasks, without requiring any KV-cache handling.
distorted: [CITE] attributes generation collapse and hallucination of wrong facts to FFN-SkipLLM and reports that skipping 25-30% of FFN blocks requires state copying of the KV cache with noticeable performance drop on MT-Bench and Factoid-QA.

faithful: For zero-shot topic classification in the low-resource language Luxembourgish, [CITE] constructed two topic relevance datasets from a dictionary providing synonyms, word translations, and example sentences, and showed that models trained on this dictionary-based data outperform models following the NLI-based approach.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tune a language model on a Natural Language Inference dataset and show that the NLI-based approach outperforms dictionary-based trained models for zero-shot topic classification in Luxembourgish, a low-resource language, on two topic classification tasks.

faithful: For SemEval-2024 Task 2 clinical-trial NLI, [CITE] compared finetuned/ensembled masked language models with template-prompted LLMs using Chain-of-Thought and Contrastive Chain-of-Thought, finding 2-shot Flan-T5-large best at 0.57 F1, 0.64 Faithfulness and 0.56 Consistency.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate Natural Language Inference for Clinical Trial Reports on NLI4CT and find that finetuning and ensembling Masked Language Models outperforms prompting Flan-T5-large with Chain-Of-Thought and Contrastive Chain-Of-Thought, achieving the best system with 0.57 F1 score.

faithful: [CITE] preregistered few-shot cross-topic stance experiments with RoBERTa using 100-example shots from seven datasets, finding that cross-encoding generally beat bi-encoding and adding NLI training often helped considerably, though inconsistently across datasets.
distorted: For few-shot stance detection across different topics with pre-trained RoBERTa models trained on shots of 100 examples from 7 datasets, [CITE] reports that in general bi-encoding out-performs cross-encoding, while adding Natural Language Inference knowledge gives no considerable improvement and is consistent across all datasets.

faithful: [CITE] presents the first multi-task corpus of 1,665 real-world business documents sourced from US state government websites, densely annotated for document classification, key entity extraction, and visual question answering, with baselines covering textual, multi-modal, and large language model approaches.
distorted: BuDDIE [CITE] is a multi-task dataset of 1,665 real-world invoices and receipts from US state government websites, with sparse annotations that support one or two co-related tasks such as entity extraction and entity linking.

faithful: [CITE] trained Random Forest classifiers on Norton Anthology, Penguin Classics, and Open Syllabus titles contrasted with bestsellers, Nobel laureates, and award winners, reaching up to 77% F1 and finding quality categories easier to separate from controls than from one another.
distorted: [CITE] apply Random Forest to titles from Norton Anthology, Penguin Classics and Open Syllabus, achieving up to 77% F1 scores, and find quality categories easier to distinguish from other quality categories than from control groups.

faithful: For German compounds built from personal names, [CITE] models 321 such forms alongside full names and finds that valence norms and pretrained language models capture evaluative shifts, with regressions implicating compound and modifier valence, domain, and party membership.
distorted: [CITE] model 321 corresponding full names at discourse level and show that personal full names, as compared to PNCs, bear the evaluative nature, and compound and modifier valence, domain, and political party membership influence Angela Merkel.

faithful: [CITE] crowdsource a filtered, balanced Wikipedia-based set of English events with automatically perturbed pseudo-implausible variants, and their quantitative analysis reports that annotators favor plausibility while disagreeing more on implausible events.
distorted: Prior work on event plausibility has largely ignored abstractness; [CITE] addresses this gap with a crowd-sourced English dataset of plausible and pseudo-implausible events, finding that annotators disagree more on implausible events and that more abstract event participants trigger a perception of implausibility.

faithful: [CITE] manually annotated 1,837 texts produced by multiple models in the politics domain of the ToTTo dataset and demonstrated that correcting problematic table inputs reduces factual errors by 52% to 76%, depending on the model.
distorted: [CITE] observes that models struggle in processing tabular inputs that are structured in a non-standard way, particularly when the input lacks distinct row and column values or when the column headers are correctly mapped to corresponding values.

faithful: By scoring alternative statements for each relational fact and checking whether the correct one receives the highest log-likelihood, [CITE] probes 22 masked and causal LMs on 7,731 instances (40,916 in a larger variant).
distorted: BEAR [CITE] probes relational knowledge by relying on the objective function used in pre-training, which restricts its applicability to either masked or causal LMs and makes comparing different types of LMs impossible.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the AI Partner, AI Mentor framework, which leverages large language models to make social skill training more accessible by merging experiential learning with realistic practice and tailored feedback, drawing on interdisciplinary research from communication and psychology.
distorted: [CITE] leverages people to make social skill training more available for large language models, which rely on social skills like conflict resolution to communicate effectively and to thrive in both work and personal life.

faithful: Evaluating eight parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods across 15 architectures for low-resource neural machine translation, [CITE] found that six architectures surpassed the baseline on both in-domain and out-of-domain SacreBLEU tests, with the Houlsby+Inversion adapter achieving the best overall performance.
distorted: [CITE] showed that 6 PEFT architectures outperform the baseline for both in-domain and out-domain tests and the Houlsby+Inversion adapter has minimal performance overall, proving the effectiveness of PEFT methods.

faithful: [CITE] incorporate additional lexical information into a retrieve-and-rank bilingual lexicon induction model, reporting that this enrichment improves over the previous state of the art by an average of 2% across all language pairs of the XLING benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates on XLING the previous state of the art improving over the proposed retrieve-and-rank approach by an average of 2% across all language pairs.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned Google's BERT to infer six political-leaning labels from YouTube titles alone, training on a public corpus of 10 million titles and reporting the best accuracy (75%) and F1 (77%) among compared alternatives.
distorted: [CITE] propose a classifier based on Bert that classifies YouTube videos merely based on their titles into six categories, achieving the highest accuracy (77%) and the highest F1 score (75%) among alternatives trained on the same dataset.

faithful: Analyzing translations of the semantically difficult biblical story of Cain and Abel, [CITE] develops a typology of the most frequent errors made by Google Translate and DeepL and argues that cultural texts require a revised translation theory.
distorted: In a related study, [CITE] observes the language pairs and interfaces offered by Google Translate and DeepL for the biblical story of Caïn and Abel, concluding that AI based automatic translators can fully capture its semantic difficulty.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked machine-learning pipelines for depression detection on the DAIC-WOZ corpus, reporting that Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers reached roughly 84% accuracy, markedly exceeding the 72% accuracy reported for an SVM model in comparable literature.
distorted: [CITE] assessed ML classifiers and NLP techniques for depression detection on the DAIC-WOZ dataset, reporting that the SVM model achieved accuracy levels around 84%, significantly higher than the 72% accuracy obtained with Random Forest and XGBoost models in their case study.

faithful: [CITE] presents an end-to-end platform whose customizable pipeline transforms users' uploaded private files and legally compliant public datasets into both agent-tuning and general instruction-tuning data, enabling one-click fine-tuning of personalized agents.
distorted: As reported in [CITE], without specific agent tuning, GPT-4 currently struggles to match the efficiency of open-source models like LLaMA, particularly given the scarcity of agent-tuning datasets for fine-tuning.

faithful: [CITE] applies conformal prediction to RAG retrieval by calibrating a similarity cutoff from answerable questions at a user-chosen error rate α, then retrieving every chunk above that threshold so the true answer is included with 1−α confidence, packaged as an LLM-only Python workflow.
distorted: [CITE] retrieved all chunks with similarity not exceeding the α threshold, ensuring the true answer is captured in the context with an α confidence level.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates fallacy comprehension with five tasks spanning WHAT, WHY, and HOW, introduces the GPT-4-generated LFUD dataset built with little human effort, and reports that LFUD fine-tuning significantly boosts logical reasoning.
distorted: [CITE] propose five logical fallacy understanding tasks spanning three cognitive dimensions (WHAT, WHY, HOW) and introduce LFUD, a dataset constructed with GPT-4, demonstrating that fine-tuning LLMs on LFUD significantly degrades rather than enhances their performance on logical reasoning.

faithful: [CITE] replaces independently trained Transducer decoder embeddings with pronunciation-aware embeddings that share components among text tokens with identical or similar pronunciations, reporting consistent accuracy gains on multiple Mandarin Chinese and Korean datasets and fewer chained errors after an initial mistake.
distorted: With experiments in Mandarin Chinese and Korean, [CITE] show that conventional Transducers consistently improve speech recognition accuracy compared to PET models and effectively mitigate error chain reactions by substantially reducing the likelihood of the model generating additional errors following a prior one.

faithful: For legal question answering, [CITE] embeds the retrieval stage, indexing vocabulary, and similarity knowledge containers of the case-based reasoning cycle into retrieval-augmented generation, showing that general and domain-specific embeddings compared via inter, intra, and hybrid similarity significantly improve generated answer quality.
distorted: For legal question-answering, [CITE] presents inter, intra and hybrid similarity as representations and general and domain-specific embeddings as methods of comparison in CBR-RAG.

faithful: For entity-level sentiment in political news, [CITE] reports that LLMs beat fine-tuned BERT, with in-context learning significantly improving performance and self-consistency stabilizing predictions, while rationale-augmented chain-of-thought few-shot prompting helped inconsistently.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that fine-tuned BERT models outperform LLMs in capturing entity-specific sentiment from political news articles, and that the chain-of-thought (COT) prompting method enhances consistency in sentiment prediction.

faithful: [CITE] construct a few-shot relation extraction meta-dataset from NYT29, WIKIDATA, and a few-shot version of TACRED, and their evaluation of six recent methods under realistic conditions found no clear winner, with overall performance remaining low.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a meta dataset: NYT29 is a few-shot form of TACRED, WIKIDATA is derived from NYT29, and a recent few-shot relation extraction method comes out as a clear winner.

faithful: For low-resource Kazakh, [CITE] introduces an open-domain QA dataset of nearly 6,000 questions sourced from translated Natural Questions items and the Kazakh Unified National Testing exam, where baseline retriever-reader pipelines reach only EM = 17.8 and F1 = 28.7 in the full ODQA setting.
distorted: For Kazakh open-domain question answering, [CITE] introduce baseline retrievers and readers that achieve NDCG@10 = 0.389 and MRR = 0.382 in full ODQA, and EM = 17.8 and F1 = 28.7 in reading comprehension.

faithful: [CITE] compared pre-trained language models, GPT-3.5, and Gemini Pro in zero-shot settings using retrieval-augmented generation with various reasoning chains for NLI over breast cancer clinical trial reports, achieving an F1 of 0.69, consistency of 0.71, and faithfulness of 0.90 on the test set.
distorted: [CITE] yields an F1 score of 0.71, consistency of 0.90, and a faithfulness score of 0.69 on the test dataset for breast cancer Clinical Trial Reports under zero-shot settings using Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

faithful: For SemEval-2024 Task 1 on semantic textual relatedness across 14 languages, [CITE] combined BERT-based contrastive learning with a similarity metric for the supervised track while exploring autoencoders for the unsupervised track, additionally constructing a bigram relatedness corpus via negative sampling to refine word embeddings.
distorted: [CITE] focuses on autoencoders primarily for Track A: supervised, while exploring BERT-based contrastive learning and similarity metric based approach for Track B: unsupervised in SemEval-2024 Task 1 with 14 languages.

faithful: [CITE] propose VTPrompt, which extracts key concepts from questions and uses a detection model to highlight relevant objects as visual prompts, raising GPT-4V's MME score by up to 183.5 points and improving MMB performance by 8.17% for GPT-4V and 15.69% for Gemini Pro.
distorted: Experiments demonstrate VTPrompt enhanced MMB performance by 15.69% for GPT-4V and 8.17% for Gemini Pro, with score improvement up to 183.5 for Gemini Pro on POPE [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] combined Class Definition Prediction with hyperbolic embeddings, HypEmo hierarchical label embeddings, and multi-task emotion prediction for SemEval-2024 Task 4, reporting hierarchical F1-scores of 0.60, 0.67, and 0.48 on its three subtasks.
distorted: [CITE] address the SemEval 2024 Task 4 sub-tasks with an ensemble of Class Definition Prediction and hyperbolic embeddings, reporting a hierarchical F1-score of 0.67 using only textual content of the meme, compared to 0.60 when integrating both textual and visual content.

faithful: Q-PEFT [CITE] conditions prompt tuning on the query by extracting the top-k tokens from concatenated documents as contextual clues, and an end-to-end variant replaces this retrieval step with a multi-head attention layer, with experiments on four public datasets demonstrating its reranking effectiveness.
distorted: [CITE] introduces Q-PEFT, a query-dependent parameter efficient fine-tuning approach for text reranking that substitutes the multi-head attention layer with a retrieval mechanism and keeps the learned prompt fixed for different documents, demonstrating effectiveness on four public datasets.

faithful: [CITE] tackled SemEval-2024 Task 10 by coupling a masked-memory network with speaker participation for emotion recognition and a transformer-based speaker-centric model for flip reasoning, reporting a 5.9 F1 improvement over the task baseline on sub-task 3.
distorted: [CITE] utilizes a transformer-based speaker-centric model for Emotion Recognition in Conversations and a masked-memory network with speaker participation for Emotion Flip Reasoning; the ERC task achieves a 5.9 F1 score improvement over the task baseline for sub-task 3.

faithful: Using a field-theory framework to examine the gradient vector field of the DPO loss, [CITE] shows that DPO decreases the likelihood of human-dispreferred outputs faster than it increases that of preferred outputs, theoretically explaining its reliance on strong SFT.
distorted: [CITE] analyze the gradient vector field of the DPO loss function using field theory and find that DPO increases the probability of producing preferred data at a faster rate than it decreases the probability of producing human dispreferred data.

faithful: For parameter-efficient speaker adaptation in text-to-speech, [CITE] introduces a small learnable hypernetwork that generates Adapter block parameters conditioned on speaker representations, achieving state-of-the-art performance in the parameter-efficient regime across two domain adaptation settings.
distorted: Domain adaptation on a new set of speakers [CITE] can be solved by fine-tuning the whole model for each new domain, making Adapters, hypernetworks and dynamic speaker representations parameter-inefficient for out-of-domain speaker performance and domain-generic multi-speaker TTS.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CLiKA, which evaluates cross-lingual knowledge alignment at Performance, Consistency, and Conductivity levels, finding that continued pretraining boosts the target language while hurting others, whereas mixed pretraining is gentler, yet conductivity stays weak.
distorted: [CITE] propose CLiKA, a systematic framework to assess cross-lingual knowledge alignment at the Performance, Consistency, and Conductivity levels, and show that continued pretraining affects other languages less, while mixed pretraining improves alignment of the target language at the cost of other languages.

faithful: [CITE] compares order-as-supervision transformer pre-training objectives—Permutation Classification, Embedding Regression, and Skip-Clip—on recipes, reporting gains over the strongest baseline of 1.6% on NPN-Cooking and 7–9% on ProPara for entity tracking.
distorted: [CITE] compares Permutation Classification, Embedding Regression, and Skip-Clip for recipes and shows that order as-supervision pretraining improves over the best baseline by 7-9% on NPN-Cooking and 1.6% on ProPara across metrics.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a white-box polygraph that detects and forecasts LLM hallucinations by fitting tractable probabilistic models to internal state transitions during generation, reporting more than a 20% AUC-ROC gain over state-of-the-art methods on benchmarks such as TruthfulQA.
distorted: PoLLMgraph [CITE] detects hallucination in large language models through black-box evaluations, outperforming state-of-the-art white-box detection methods by a considerable margin with over 20% improvement in AUC-ROC on common benchmarking datasets like TruthfulQA.

faithful: [CITE] applied pruning, knowledge distillation, and quantization to AfriBERTa, a small-data model for low-resource languages, and found that compression improved efficiency and effectiveness across metrics beyond accuracy, mirroring effects previously observed in large, heavily parameterized models.
distorted: Applying pruning, knowledge distillation, and quantization to the low-resource model AfriBERTa, [CITE] show that compression techniques fail to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of small-data language models, contradicting prevailing beliefs regarding the effects of compression on large, heavily parameterized models.

faithful: [CITE] automatically produces both uncontextualized and context-grounded questions for document-level event argument extraction without human involvement, finding that combining the two question types helps most when event triggers and their arguments occur in different sentences, and that the corpus-agnostic strategies transfer across datasets.
distorted: [CITE] present question generation strategies for document-level event argument extraction that require human involvement, showing that combining uncontextualized and contextualized questions is not beneficial and that their corpus-specific components do not transfer across corpora.

faithful: [CITE] converts response-level feedback into sentence-level pseudo-labels by combining multiple instance learning and learning from label proportions with priors such as document-sentence cosine similarity, reporting gains over baselines on six datasets spanning retrieval, question answering, summarization, and math reasoning.
distorted: [CITE] aggregates sentence-level labels into response-level scores using multiple instance learning and learning from label proportions, reporting improved performance over models trained on fine-grained human annotated labels across six datasets and four tasks.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated hallucination detection across the Machine Translation, Definition Modeling, and Paraphrase Generation subtasks of SemEval-2024 Task 6, finding that semantic similarity to factual references yielded only moderate accuracy and correlation on trial data, while an ensemble of mutually judging language models fell short of expectations.
distorted: On SemEval-2024 Task 6, [CITE] show that an ensemble of language models that judge each other's outputs achieves moderate accuracy and correlation scores, while semantic similarity between the generated text and factual references falls short of expectations.

faithful: [CITE] profiles residual connections in deep LLMs and reports that the residual blocks of OPT-66B contribute a median of only 5% to the model's output, motivating token-level routing that skips entire layers via a trained router module.
distorted: [CITE] establish that static methods improve over dynamic sparsity by exploiting variance across individual inputs, and OPT-66B residual blocks have a median contribution of 5% to training data.

faithful: [CITE] organizes research on multilingual large language models around multilingual alignment and, as a resource contribution, compiles open-source papers, data corpora, and leaderboards while also proposing a unified taxonomy and discussing emerging frontiers.
distorted: [CITE] presents a thorough review of existing comprehensive surveys of multilingual large language models (MLLMs), summarizing their recent progress, unified taxonomy, emerging frontiers, and abundant open-source resources according to multi-lingual alignment.

faithful: [CITE] show that reward models trained with the conventional ranking objective on human preference data often fail to distinguish more favorable from less favorable responses, and that incorporating estimated preference-margin values—without requiring exhaustive annotator labels—significantly improves reward prediction accuracy.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that reward models trained with the traditional ranking objective based on human preference data effectively distinguish between more or less favorable responses in real-world scenarios, and that their novel method to estimate preference differences needs detailed, exhaustive labels from human annotators.

faithful: [CITE] proposes Adaptive Semantic Space Learning, which adaptively reorganizes data distributions in semantic space for multi-expert selection, and reports that the resulting Chinese financial multi-task LLM matches near-full-data performance using only 10% of the training data.

[CITE] introduces two-dimensional feature engineering for table-filling relation extraction, injecting prior knowledge into word-pair representations to handle overlapping relations and achieving state-of-the-art results on ACE05 Chinese, ACE05 English, and SanWen.
distorted: [CITE] directly transforms the two-dimensional sentence representation from a raw input for relation extraction, arguing that two-dimensional feature engineering is weak to utilize prior knowledge, and reports state-of-the-art performance on ACE05 Chinese, ACE05 English, and SanWen.

faithful: [CITE] introduced NLI4CT-P, a perturbed natural language inference dataset for clinical trials designed to probe interventional and causal reasoning, and their shared task attracted 106 registered participants who made over 1200 submissions and wrote 25 system overview papers.
distorted: For clinical trials, [CITE] presents NLI4CT-P and reports 25 participants registered, 106 system overview papers, and LLMs that no longer fall short in shortcut learning, factual inconsistency, and vulnerability to adversarial inputs.

faithful: [CITE] systematically perturbed inputs for zero-shot and few-shot NER on two datasets, finding via automatic and human evaluation that ChatGPT was more brittle to rare Drug or Disease replacements than Person or Location perturbations and overconfident on most incorrect predictions.
distorted: In their systematic analysis, [CITE] assess the robustness of ChatGPT under input perturbations for Named Entity Recognition and find that ChatGPT is more brittle on widely known Person or Location entities compared to perturbations on rare Drug or Disease replacements.

faithful: To shrink the memory and compute demands of pre-trained Mixture-of-Experts models, [CITE] prunes experts guided by heavy-hitters counting and then applies regularization-based fine-tuning that restores accuracy while lowering the number of experts activated during inference.
distorted: SEER-MoE [CITE] introduces a two-stage framework: the first stage employs a regularization-based fine-tuning strategy for pruning the total number of experts, while the second stage uses heavy-hitters counting guidance to recover accuracy loss and reduce the number of activated experts during inference.

faithful: [CITE] tunes only prompt embeddings—trained with a small discriminator language model on as few as a few hundred examples—to steer generation, reporting control across SST-5, Yelp, GYAFC, and JIGSAW and reduced toxic or biased outputs.
distorted: [CITE] introduce Prompt Tuning for controlled language generation, training prompt embeddings with a large language model used as the discriminator, and evaluate on four datasets including GYAFC for toxic language and JIGSAW for formality.

faithful: Using records and physician assessments from a cardiology center, [CITE] found Mistral-7B to be the standout among evaluated LLMs, producing discharge notes that medical experts rated highly for clinical relevance, completeness, readability, and care-planning support.
