distorted: For cardiac discharge documentation, [CITE] reports that manual creation surpassed Mistral-7B, with generated notes receiving low marks for clinical relevance, completeness, readability, and little contribution to informed decision-making or care planning.

faithful: Comparing BERT-on-BERT, PWWS, and Fraud Bargain’s Attack against a BERT victim on IMDB, AG News, and SST2, [CITE] reports that PWWS was strongest, with lower runtime, higher accuracy, and better semantic similarity.
distorted: Three distinct adversarial attack mechanisms on the BERT classifier are assessed in [CITE], which finds that the BERT-on-BERT attack consistently outperforms PWWS and Fraud Bargain's Attack (FBA) across IMDB, AG News, and SST2, demonstrating lower runtime, higher accuracy, and favorable semantic similarity scores.

faithful: Exploiting the observation that language impairment can emerge in the prodromal phase before motor symptoms appear, [CITE] applied state-of-the-art large language models to spontaneous speech and achieved up to 73% accuracy in automatically detecting Parkinson's disease.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that motor symptoms can present in the prodromal phase and precede language impairment, and that large language models detect Parkinsons disease automatically from spontaneous speech with up to 73% accuracy.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a multi-encoder-decoder opinion summarizer trained through a synthetic dataset creation strategy that selects one review as a pseudo-summary, reporting an average 14.5% ROUGE-1 F1 improvement over prior state-of-the-art across nine test sets.
distorted: For opinion summarization, [CITE] extends Amazon, Oposum+, and Flipkart test sets and leverages ChatGPT to annotate summaries; experiments demonstrate that the SOTA achieves on average a 14.5% ROUGE-1 F1 improvement over the SDC and MEDOS combination across nine test sets.

faithful: [CITE] detects aspect categories in reviews by coupling a deep neural network with gradual machine learning, encoding similar or opposite instance relations mined from the DNN's latent space as binary factor-graph features, and consistently outperforms pure DNN baselines on real benchmark datasets.
distorted: For multi-label Aspect Category Detection in a given review sentence, [CITE] demonstrates that pure DNN solutions consistently outperform the GML approach in collaboration with DNNs for feature extraction on real benchmark datasets.

faithful: For interpretive reading comprehension, [CITE] releases the first dataset of educational narratives with well-edited theme texts and human-annotated theme keywords at multiple granularities across genres and cultural origins, showing state-of-the-art methods still find theme inference challenging.
distorted: [CITE] centered on literal comprehension of educational narratives and, after extensive experiments with state-of-the-art methods, found the task challenging and significant for surface-level understanding of content.

faithful: [CITE] jointly trained financial text classifiers for sentiment, objectivity, forward-looking sentence prediction and ESG-content detection, finding that explicitly feeding auxiliary-task predictions as features for the final target task performed best before extracting FTSE350 annual-report features.
distorted: [CITE] highlights the positive effect of explicitly adding final target task predictions as features for the auxiliary task during multi-task training for financial sentiment, objectivity, forward-looking sentence prediction and ESG-content detection.

faithful: [CITE] proposes the Social Tasks in Sandbox Simulation (STSS) benchmark, which scores language agents objectively at the action level via goal achievement in multi-agent simulations, and finds it challenging for state-of-the-art agents while still discriminating between distinct ones.
distorted: Related work [CITE] introduces STSS to stay at the language level and use subjective metrics, while conversation scenarios for the language-level benchmark objectively scrutinize goal achievements within multi-agent simulation at the action level.

faithful: [CITE] measures factual knowledge storage in bits and finds that language models can store exactly 2 bits of knowledge per parameter, even under int8 quantization, implying a 7B-parameter model holds 14B bits, exceeding their estimate of English Wikipedia and textbooks combined.
distorted: [CITE] establishes that LLaMA/Mistral with GatedMLP match or even surpass GPT-2 with rotary embedding in knowledge storage, particularly over shorter training durations, because rotary embedding is less stable and harder to train.

faithful: For Persian conversational question answering, [CITE] augments a large language model with keywords extracted from the conversational flow, reporting gains of up to 8% over existing methods and an LLM-only baseline.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate Persian conversational question answering and report that the LLM-only baseline outperformed their combined contextual keyword extraction approach by up to 8% on the evaluation benchmarks compared to existing methods.

faithful: Using a proposed semantic drift score on Wikipedia-style biographies, [CITE] shows that LLMs tend to generate correct facts before drifting into incorrect ones, and that early stopping combined with semantic-similarity reranking substantially improves factual accuracy.
distorted: [CITE] show that modern LLMs tend to generate incorrect facts first, then drift away and generate correct facts later, and further show that calling an external API can improve factuality by a large margin, but early stopping methods do not get positive results.

faithful: For Croatian, Serbian, Bosnian and Montenegrin, [CITE] reports that additionally pretraining existing multilingual encoders with limited computation matches dedicated from-scratch models on a new benchmark, and adding Slovenian to pretraining causes little to no performance loss.
distorted: For the closely related languages Croatian, Serbian, Bosnian and Montenegrin, [CITE] show that comparable performance to dedicated from-scratch models cannot be obtained via additional pretraining of existing multilingual models, and that including the neighboring language Slovenian brings substantial loss in the performance of the final model.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates extremely long-context understanding across Fiction Reading, Paper Reading, and Law Reading with 27 English/Chinese subtasks, averaging over 100K English words or 200K Chinese characters, and finds six leading LLMs remain well below human performance.
distorted: [CITE] reports that human levels significantly lag behind six leading LLMs across Memory Retrieval, Detailed Understanding, Overall Understanding, and Open-ended Generation in English and Chinese.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an expert-annotated Persian offensive-language dataset, quality-checked through a three-stage labeling process with kappa agreement, alongside a larger crawled unlabeled corpus, reporting XLM-RoBERTa F1-scores of 76.9% three-class and 89.9% two-class.
distorted: For Persian offensive social media, [CITE] reports XLM-RoBERTa F1-scores of 89.9% for the three-class and 76.9% for the two-class versions of the dataset.

faithful: [CITE] augments BABERT by feeding supervised high-quality boundary information into pre-training, and its proposed Boundary Information Metric compares PLMs' boundary awareness without task-specific fine-tuning, with the enhanced variant beating vanilla BABERT on Chinese sequence labeling and broader NLU tasks.
distorted: Prior work on Chinese sequence labeling shows that BABERT incorporates supervised high-quality boundary information into pre-training, and that extending it with unsupervised statistical boundary information produces a variant that outperforms the vanilla version across Chinese natural language understanding tasks [CITE].

faithful: Participating in the SOMD shared task on software mention disambiguation, [CITE] combined retrieval-augmented generation with the in-context learning of generative LLMs, framing NER and Attributive NER as single-choice question answering to extract software entities and attributes such as distributive information.
distorted: [CITE] uses single-choice question-answering to replace generative Large Language Models, prioritising Retrieval-Augmented Generation over in-context learning for Named Entity Recognition and Attributive NER.

faithful: To close the train–inference distribution gap in neural codec language models, [CITE] iteratively builds a preference dataset pairing golden codec tokens with synthetic ones and applies preference optimization, yielding steady self-improvement that also generalizes to smaller models.
distorted: [CITE] introduces SpeechAlign, an iterative self-improvement strategy in which preference optimization over golden and synthetic codec tokens leads to discrepancies between the training and inference phases, steadily converting strong models to weak ones and negatively affecting smaller models.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an entity-centric data labeling methodology that produces representative, reusable benchmark datasets without complex sampling schemes, supports estimation of cluster and pairwise precision and recall, and is validated on inventor name disambiguation and simulation studies.
distorted: [CITE] propose an entity-centric data labeling methodology that necessitates sophisticated, application-specific sampling schemes to find matching pairs of records among an immense number of non-matches.

faithful: [CITE] reports that pairing cost-effective GPT-3.5 with training-free in-context learning and a context-aware entity-marking generation step lifts CoNLL03 named-entity F1 from 85.9% to 91.9%, nearly matching supervised fine-tuning.
distorted: [CITE] introduced LTNER, a NER processing framework whose Contextualized Entity Marking with the cost-effective GPT-3.5 requires additional supervised training, improving the F1 score on the CoNLL03 dataset from the initial 91.9% to 85.9%.

faithful: For extracting fields such as street, postal code, and country from free-text payment messages, [CITE] found that a Transformer fine-tuned with early stopping significantly outperforms alternative approaches, while generative LLMs still achieved strong zero-shot performance on noisy real-world transactional data.
distorted: [CITE] suggests generative LLMs significantly outperform a well fine-tuned Transformer model using early-stopping for address parsing in payment data, and Transformer models warrant further investigations with SWIFT ISO 20022.

faithful: For the nuclear power domain, [CITE] combined a deep-learning causal relation detector with a knowledge-based cause-effect extractor, supported by an interactive pair-labeling tool and a newly compiled licensee event report corpus of 20,129 text samples.
distorted: For causality extraction from nuclear licensee event reports, [CITE] proposed a hybrid framework in which a knowledge based approach performs causal relation detection while a deep-learning-based approach handles cause-effect extraction, supported by an interactive labeling tool and an LER corpus of 20,129 text samples.

faithful: [CITE] reports that naively finetuned summarizers become highly language-specific in outputs and internal representations, and introduces query-key (QK) finetuning plus a balanced adversarial language classifier after linking removal of source-language identity to zero-shot summarization performance.
distorted: In zero-shot summarization, [CITE] show naively finetuned models are language-agnostic in output behavior and internal representations, and the standard adversarial language classifier more directly enforces language-independent representations.

faithful: CodecLM [CITE] treats LLMs as codecs that encode seed instructions into on-the-fly keyword metadata capturing the target instruction distribution and decode them into tailored instructions, with Self-Rubrics and Contrastive Filtering improving data efficiency on four open-domain instruction-following benchmarks.
distorted: CodecLM [CITE] uses LLMs as codecs to first decode seed instructions into metadata and then encode metadata to create tailored instructions, with extensive experiments on four open-domain instruction following benchmarks validating the effectiveness of current state-of-the-arts over CodecLM.

faithful: [CITE] populates a black-box LLM prompt with prior-run demonstrations selected by a differentiable ranking model and synthesized instructions, reporting state-of-the-art WebVoyager results that beat text-only models by 8% overall and up to 36% on certain websites.
distorted: [CITE] achieves state-of-the-art results on the WebVoyager benchmark, beating strong multi-modal models by 8% overall and up to 36% on certain websites, while remaining within 5% of text-only models despite only receiving textual inputs.

faithful: [CITE] introduce an open leaderboard that quantitatively compares how prone large language models are to hallucination, benchmarking both factuality and faithfulness across tasks such as question answering, summarisation, and reading comprehension.

Examining 55 languages (36 African and 19 European), [CITE] shows that jointly learning diacritization with machine translation doubles or triples translation performance for some low-resource languages but degrades it in high-resource settings, while retaining or removing diacritics leaves MT quality largely unchanged.
distorted: Results show that diacritization significantly benefits MT in the HR scenario, doubling or even tripling performance for some languages, but harms MT in the LR scenario across 55 languages [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] presents a multimodal web-page benchmark covering seven tasks and 1.5K human-curated instances from 139 real websites across 87 sub-domains, where evaluating 14 open-source MLLMs alongside Gemini Pro, Claude-3, and GPT-4V exposes weak text-rich grounding and poor low-resolution performance.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a multimodal benchmark with seven tasks, comprising 139 human-curated instances from 1.5K real websites covering 87 sub-domains, and reveals current MLLMs with no significant challenges or performance gaps in OCR, understanding, grounding, text-rich environments, and low-resolution image inputs.

faithful: [CITE] optimizes retrieval for personalized LLM generation with reinforcement learning using any task metric as reward and knowledge distillation from the downstream LLM, plus pre-/post-generation retriever selection, reporting statistically significant gains on six of seven LaMP datasets.
distorted: [CITE] propose knowledge distillation from the retrieval model to the downstream LLM and a reinforcement learning reward function defined using retriever selection, revealing statistically significant improvements in seven out of six LaMP datasets.

faithful: [CITE] improves dual-encoder retrieval by pairing contrastive learning with pairwise learning and adding a document-encoder decoder that uses prompt-tuning to generatively extract event triplets, while that decoder is discarded at inference.
distorted: [CITE] incorporates pairwise learning to accompany contrastive learning for encoder optimization and includes a decoder module after the query encoder, which is crucial during inference for real-time retrieval.

faithful: [CITE] systematically organizes methods for protecting privacy during in-context learning and prompting, a paradigm in which large language models perform tasks from demonstration examples without any parameter updates, and compares these defenses while cataloging available resources and open challenges.
distorted: Recent work [CITE] demonstrates that in-context learning (ICL) allows large language models (LLMs) to be utilized through the presentation of demonstration examples with modifications to the model parameters, alleviating the privacy risks of prompting.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a modular evaluation framework whose meta-evaluation modules combine human evaluation with data-contamination detection, and whose distributed computation and caching infrastructure supports large-scale assessment of open-source and proprietary LLMs across multi-node, multi-GPU clusters.
distorted: FreeEval [CITE] is a modular framework in which distributed computation and caching strategies enhance the fairness of evaluation outcomes, while meta-evaluation techniques like human evaluation and data contamination detection enable extensive evaluations across multi-node, multi-GPU clusters.

faithful: [CITE] detect shopping product questions by combining purchase-history features that capture latent shopping behavior within a Mixture-of-Experts model, reaching an F1 score of 0.91 and producing significantly more shopping-list additions than prompts issued after random product questions.
distorted: For proactive recommendations in voice assistants, [CITE] demonstrate that Shopping Product Questions can be identified from question text alone with F1=0.91, and that prompting users after random PQs leads to a significantly higher rate of added products than prompting after SPQs.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned Google’s open-source Tesseract 5.0 OCR from the Arabic base model on 1,233 transcribed line images from pre-1950 Kurdish documents at the Zheen Center, reporting 0.755% CER with lstmeval and 84.02% average character accuracy with Ocreval.
distorted: For historical Kurdish documents printed before 1950, [CITE] fine-tunes Google Tesseract 5.0 from the Arabic model and reports that Ocreval gives a Character Error Rate of 0.755%, while lstmeval shows average character accuracy of 84.02% on 1233 line images.

faithful: Using Tang et al. (2022)'s universal multimodal machine translation framework and probing tasks on authentic translation data, [CITE] reports that images help most real-world datasets, with gains governed by text-visual alignment and coherence, while visual input remains supplementary and substitutable.
distorted: [CITE] adhere to the universal multimodal machine translation framework proposed by Tang et al. (2022) and find through probing tasks on real-world translation datasets that the visual modality is dispensable or offers only marginal advantages for the majority of authentic translation datasets.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned PubMedBERT to detect biomedical fields of application, comparing title-plus-abstract input with only argumentative elements and reporting top F1 scores from 0.22 to 0.84 across fields, with conclusion and background labels performing best.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tuned PubMedBERT on a specific corpus and compared title and abstract to argumentative elements: the best argumentative labels were the claims from the authors instead of the ones related to the conclusion and background sections, with F1 scores from 0.22 to 0.84.

faithful: [CITE] approached SemEval-2024 hallucination detection by fine-tuning pre-trained encoders, ensembling high-performing models, and augmenting training with synthetic samples generated from the unlabeled subset, with their best system ranking 9th in the model-agnostic track and 17th in the model-aware track.
distorted: [CITE] present systems for the SemEval-2024 hallucination detection task, where their premier method, utilizing supervised refinement of pre-trained encoders, ensemble approaches, and additional training samples, achieved 9th place in the model-aware track and 17th place in the model-agnostic track.

faithful: [CITE] reports that on classical Latin verse encoded with sonic and metrical features, CNNs matched LSTM authorship-classification accuracy while training faster and offering potentially better interpretability, with simple trainable embeddings beating domain-specific schemes.
distorted: For poetry, [CITE] reports that LSTMs are better choices than CNNs: they train more quickly, have equivalent accuracy, and potentially offer better interpretability about authorial style in classical Latin verse.

faithful: [CITE] builds educational crossword data by pulling Wikipedia context for keywords and prompting LLMs to write pedagogical clues, yielding 44,075 unique examples in which each text–keyword pair is paired with three distinct clues.
distorted: [CITE] created clue-instruct, a dataset containing three unique examples with 44,075 distinct crossword clues associated with text-keyword pairs, and confirmed human evaluations missing despite automatic evaluations of traditional databases.

faithful: For textual out-of-distribution detection with Transformers, [CITE] argues that representations learned by maximizing the conditional likelihood p(y|x) are biased, and instead proposes a variational inference framework that maximizes the joint likelihood p(x, y), demonstrating effectiveness across various text classification tasks.
distorted: VI-OOD [CITE] delves into textual OOD detection with Transformers by maximizing the conditional likelihood p(y|x) instead of the joint distribution p(x, y), demonstrating effectiveness and wide applicability on various text classification tasks.

faithful: [CITE] introduces OxfordEval, an automatic win-rate metric against Oxford Dictionary sentences that aligns with human judgments, and reports that FM-MLM, using masked language models to select meaning-exemplifying sentences, reaches 85.1% versus 39.8% for prior model-generated sentences.
distorted: For low-cost generation and evaluation of sentences illustrating word usage, [CITE] reports that OxfordEval gives FM-MLM only a 39.8% win rate against Oxford baseline sentences, whereas prior model-generated sentences exceed 85.1%.

faithful: For Polish, [CITE] introduces a freely licensed (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) emotional-speech corpus containing over three hours from nine actors portraying anger, fear, happiness, sadness, surprise, and neutral states, with text chosen to cover Polish phonetics.
distorted: Addressing the scarcity of emotional speech datasets for Slavic languages, the nEMO corpus [CITE] provides over nine hours of Polish recordings by three actors portraying six emotional states, including anger, fear, happiness, sadness, and surprise, released under a Creative Commons license.

faithful: [CITE] proposes an ensemble that combines Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Decision Tree classifiers to detect fake reviews on e-commerce platforms, reporting that the hybrid architecture yields higher predictive accuracy and robustness than traditional single-model approaches.
distorted: [CITE] propose an ensemble of Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Decision Tree classifiers for finding fake reviews, yet their metrics demonstrate that traditional single-model approaches achieve superior accuracy and robustness against the proposed ensemble method.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned sarcasm detectors on four datasets differing in label source, domain, and mocking style, finding intra-dataset performance was consistently higher with third-party than author labels, while most cross-dataset transfers generalized poorly and their newly released dataset transferred best.
distorted: Prior robustness studies of sarcasm detection found that, for intra-dataset predictions, models consistently performed better when fine-tuned with author labels rather than with third-party labels, suggesting self-reported sarcasm annotations yield superior same-dataset performance [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduces a conversational assistant for literature review that unifies three modules—Knowledge Management to organize papers, Recommendation to discover relevant work, and Query Answering for deeper engagement—in a personalized platform.
distorted: SurveyAgent [CITE] integrates three key modules: Knowledge Management for discovering relevant literature, Recommendation for engaging with content on a deeper level, and Query Answering for organizing papers, all within a unified conversational platform.

faithful: For Spanish medical entity linking, [CITE] pairs a SapBERT-based bi-encoder for candidate retrieval with a cross-encoder re-ranker trained via contrastive learning, surpassing prior benchmarks by 40 points on DisTEMIST and 43 points on MedProcNER when normalizing mentions to SNOMED-CT codes.
distorted: [CITE] presents ClinLinker, a two-phase pipeline pairing a SapBERT-based bi-encoder with a cross-encoder for medical entity linking in Spanish, outperforming previous benchmarks by 43 points in DisTEMIST and 40 points in MedProcNER, both normalized to SNOMED-CT codes.

faithful: [CITE] proposes LD-Align, an annotation-free alignment method that reconstructs samples to build an auto-encoding-like latent space and uses distances between sample pairs there to steer DPO-based training toward a high-quality supervised fine-tuning dataset.
distorted: LD-Align [CITE] achieves annotation-free alignment by replacing DPO-based training with RLHF and extensive human annotation, while ignoring the latent space, sample reconstruction, and the high-quality supervised fine-tune dataset.

faithful: [CITE] introduces EusIE, a Basque event extraction dataset following MEE, and across 72 language pairs finds that shared script and morphology help token-level trigger/entity identification, whereas common word order matters most for argument extraction.
distorted: For Basque event extraction, [CITE] reports that across 72 language pairs common word order produces higher quality cross-lingual transfer for entity and event trigger identification, while common writing script and morphological features are most relevant for argument extraction.

faithful: To enable precise length-controllable evaluation, [CITE] introduces two challenging subsets, TSort and BestAnswer, whose test cases can be manipulated to reach 128k tokens, and evaluates four closed-source API models plus six open-source models, revealing clear limitations in ultra-long-context settings.
distorted: [CITE] introduce L-Eval and LongBench as length-adaptable benchmarks that produce text samples up to 128k tokens; Ada-LEval includes test samples from 2k to 32k+ entangled together.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated three conversational LLMs on a subset of a public media-bias dataset with a news-editor checklist, finding none debiased perfectly and that ChatGPT sometimes made unnecessary edits risking authorial-style changes and misinformation.
distorted: [CITE] design an evaluation checklist tailored to news editors' perspectives and show that three popular conversational models, including ChatGPT, perform as proficiently as domain experts in evaluating the quality of debiased outputs without unnecessary changes.

faithful: Comparing independent versus joint generation of SOAP note sections with PEGASUS-X, [CITE] found ROUGE scores differing by under 1% between the two designs, while showing that Llama2 can assess note consistency with human-level agreement (Cohen's kappa of 0.79 for age and 1.00 for gender).
distorted: [CITE] compare independent and joint SOAP note generation with PEGASUS-X Transformers, finding that clinical note consistency improves when each section is generated independently rather than conditioned on all previously generated sections.

faithful: [CITE] shows that cleaning the AlignScore training corpus, adding robustness-enhanced samples, and training on only a 10% subset yields LIM-RA, which achieves the best factual-consistency score on 24 of 33 test datasets, surpassing both AlignScore and ChatGPT across four benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] experiments show AlignScore achieves the highest score on 24 of the 33 test datasets, consistently outperforming LIM-RA and ChatGPT across four benchmarks while staying competitive on the rest.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a counterfactual-pair evaluation that grounds both continuations in the same demographic group and accounts for generation sampling variability, and its qualitative analysis of several generative models found a tendency to discuss family and hobbies when referring to women.
distorted: FairPair [CITE] is an evaluation framework for language models that captures differential treatment appearing only in extreme, rare cases rather than the biases that occur during ordinary usage.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates gender bias in monolingual masked language models for Chinese, English, German, Portuguese, and Spanish, introducing a model-based sentence-pair generation method and showing that bias conclusions often flip when different scoring metrics are applied to the same dataset.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate gender bias in multilingual masked language models for 5 languages, showing that the traditional lexicon-based method enables a more robust analysis than their model-based method, with results remaining stable across one existing and 3 new scoring metrics.

faithful: [CITE] presents a Persian-language benchmark of 20,192 four-choice questions drawn from 38 exam-derived tasks, using original non-translated items with metadata such as human response rates and difficulty levels.
distorted: [CITE] addresses non-English LLM evaluation by introducing a meticulously curated Persian benchmark comprising 38 four-choice questions sourced from 20,192 diverse tasks extracted from Persian examinations, spanning subjects from lower primary school to upper secondary school.

faithful: In a cooking-domain conversational task assistant, [CITE] trained an 82% F1 classifier to select relevant interesting facts and, in live tests on a leading multimodal voice assistant, found 66% positive fact reception with 40% higher satisfaction and 37% longer conversations.
distorted: [CITE] train a high-performing classifier with 66% F1-score to identify relevant and interesting facts for cooking, and live testing on a leading multi-modal voice assistant shows 82% of the presented facts were received positively.

faithful: Through one-hour human-AI collaborative red-teaming workshops, [CITE] produced CULTURALBENCH-V0.1, a compact multicultural knowledge benchmark on which different families of modern LLMs achieved accuracies ranging from only 37.7% to 72.2%, exposing substantial gaps in cultural proficiency.
distorted: CulturalTeaming [CITE] reveals that a decreased level of AI assistance, such as LLM-generated revision hints, empowers users to create more difficult cultural questions with enhanced perceived creativity, as gathered through 1-hour workshop sessions into CULTURALBENCH-V0.1.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a generative classifier retriever for oncology EHR records, trained on LLM-generated query-document support pairs, which outperforms proprietary counterparts such as Ada and Mistral by 30-50 F-1 points and is additionally benchmarked against a fine-tuned PubMedBERT model.
distorted: Prior EHR retrieval work [CITE] reports that propriety counterparts such as Ada and Mistral are 30-50 F-1 points better than the retriever for oncology data elements.

faithful: [CITE] integrates Llama2 semantic embeddings into the end-to-end VITS architecture, matching the naturalness of both original VITS and BERT-augmented VITS on LJSpeech while significantly improving emotive expressiveness on the EmoV_DB_bea_sem corpus.
distorted: Prior work states that [CITE] integrates semantic embeddings from Llama2 with VITS, matches the naturalness of ORI-VITS and BERT-VITS on EmoV_DB_bea_sem, and significantly enhances emotive expressiveness on LJSpeech.

faithful: [CITE] introduces PINOSE, a probe trained on offline self-consistency checks rather than human labels, which inspects internal states before response decoding and surpasses existing factuality detectors on factuality-detection and question-answering benchmarks while avoiding costly multi-output online verification.
distorted: Relatedly, [CITE] introduces PINOSE, a probing model trained on human-annotated labels with online self-consistency checking, generating multiple responses to improve transferability to out-of-distribution content while reducing the computation burden of offline verification.

faithful: [CITE] conditions dialogue generation on a continuous latent response representation used as the diffusion prior rather than a fixed Gaussian or discrete variable, inferring it through iterative denoising and reporting much more diverse yet coherent responses with high inference efficiency.
distorted: [CITE] experimental results show previous discrete or Gaussian-based continuous latent variables greatly enhance diversity, while the proposed diffusion model limited diversity and inference efficiency.

faithful: [CITE] proposes MM-ECPE, an end-to-end multitask model sharing interactions among GRU, knowledge-graph and transformer modules, plus a BERT variant with sentiment-lexicon and position-aware interaction that screens labels by knowledge-graph path length, performing especially well on position-imbalanced ECPE samples.
distorted: [CITE] proposes MM-ECPE(BERT) based on shared interaction between GRU, knowledge graph and transformer modules, and MM-ECPE based on BERT, sentiment lexicon, and position-aware interaction module layer, especially on position-imbalanced samples.

faithful: Comparing predictions on original versus simplified texts across 11 pre-trained models (including BERT and GPT-3.5) and six datasets in three languages, [CITE] found pervasive prediction inconsistencies that enable zero-iteration, model-agnostic adversarial attacks with success rates reaching 50%.
distorted: [CITE] reveals coherence across all languages and models: 11 pre-trained models, including BERT and OpenAI's GPT 3.5, maintain predictions on simplified inputs, while original inputs craft zero-iteration model-agnostic adversarial attacks with success rates of up to 50%.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a constrained decoding algorithm that equips the non-autoregressive Directed Acyclic T5 model with lexical, vocabulary, and length control, mitigating out-of-vocabulary errors and unfaithful entity-name generation while achieving strong results on the Schema Guided Dialogue and DART benchmarks.
distorted: Control-DAG [CITE] offers DA-T5 lexical, vocabulary and length control, establishing strong NAR results for Data-to-Text NLG on the Schema Guided Dialogue dataset and for Task-Oriented Dialogue on DART.

faithful: On WebNLG graph-to-text generation, [CITE] introduces a graph-guided self-attention module that injects token-level structure into pretrained language models end to end, matching state-of-the-art systems while removing extra graph-adaptation pre-training and cutting trainable parameters by over 100 million.
distorted: [CITE] reports that GraSAME outperforms SOTA models on WebNLG yet requires extra pre-training tasks to adjust graph inputs and over 100 million additional trainable parameters.

faithful: Arguing that verifying an action's correctness after seeing its output is much easier than pre-execution validation, [CITE] introduces the open-source Gorilla Execution Engine (GoEX), a runtime for autonomous LLM applications that mitigates risk through an intuitive undo feature and damage confinement.
distorted: [CITE] argues that pre-facto validation—verifying the correctness of a proposed action before seeing the output—is much easier than post-facto validation, motivating a runtime for autonomous LLM applications built around undo and damage confinement.

faithful: [CITE] proposed a meta-regressor framework built on LLMs for hallucination detection, which ranked first in the model-agnostic track and second in the model-aware track of the SemEval-2024 SHROOM shared task, achieving the highest leaderboard scores.
distorted: For Semeval 2024 Task 6, SHROOM, [CITE] describes a winning meta-regressor framework ranked 1st in the model aware sub-task and 2nd in the model agnostic sub-task, respectively, with the highest leaderboard scores.

faithful: [CITE] skips a fixed number of intermediate layers chosen solely from the target speedup ratio, and on machine translation and text summarization this sample-independent strategy improves both inference performance and actual throughput while staying compatible with batch decoding and KV caching.
distorted: [CITE] propose a Unified Layer Skipping strategy for Large Language Models in which different samples are assigned different computational budgets and multiple contiguous layers at the bottom or top are skipped, which significantly enhances both the inference performance and the actual model throughput.

faithful: [CITE] presented a direct Ukrainian–Czech machine translation system built in spring 2022 that leverages the typological similarity of the two languages instead of pivoting through English and applies block back-translation to exploit monolingual training data efficiently.
distorted: Developed in the spring of 2022, Charles Translator [CITE] translates between Ukrainian and Czech using English as a pivot, unlike other available systems that translate directly and take advantage of the typological similarity of the two languages.

faithful: [CITE] extends XNLI to Basque by machine translating the English corpus and then manually post-editing it, finding post-edition necessary and translate-train best overall, though its advantage shrinks on natively constructed data.
distorted: [CITE] expands XNLI to include English by first machine-translating the Basque XNLI corpus into English, and the results show that professional post-edition is necessary, although the translate-train cross-lingual strategy obtains better results overall when the gain is lower in a dataset built natively from scratch.

faithful: [CITE] proposes Event Grounded Generation (EGG), which uses LLMs to extract fine-grained legal events from case facts without massive annotated event data, merges these events with the facts to generate court views, and includes an LLM-free variant that removes LLM-based extraction during inference.
distorted: Prior work on criminal court view generation [CITE] shows that coarse-grained approaches partitioning case facts into broad verdict-related segments effectively capture complex details such as criminal elements and legal events, while introducing fine-grained event information fails to improve generation.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an open-source interactive toolkit that traces a Transformer language model’s full prediction process from the top-layer representation to individual attention heads and feed-forward neurons, ranking component importance at each step so only prediction-relevant components are inspected.
distorted: In contrast to previously existing tools that make the entire prediction process transparent, the LM Transparency Tool [CITE] focuses on isolated parts of the decision-making process, attributing changes only to individual attention heads rather than the whole input-to-output information flow.

faithful: Adapting an English dehumanisation-detection approach via zero-shot cross-lingual valence and arousal detection, [CITE] analysed Slovene newspaper discourse and found it grew more negative and intense between the 2015-16 and 2022-23 periods, yet was less dehumanising toward Ukrainian migrants specifically.
distorted: [CITE] adapts an English approach with a sentiment resource, zero-shot cross-lingual valence and arousal detection, and statistical significance testing, finding Slovene migration discourse became less negative and less intense between 2015-16 Syria and 2022-23 Ukraine, and more dehumanising when addressing Ukrainian migrants compared to others.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated sentence-level groundedness in retrieval-augmented long-form question answering across 3 datasets and 4 model families, finding that a significant fraction of generated sentences remained ungrounded even when they contained correct ground-truth answers, although larger models grounded their outputs more effectively.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] evaluates groundedness in retrieval-augmented LFQA across 4 datasets and 3 model families, finding that smaller models tend to ground their outputs more effectively and that correct ground-truth answers are rarely compromised by hallucinations.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Dynamic Personality Generation (DPG), a Hypernetworks-based method that embeds Big Five theory into GPT-4 to score dialogue personalities, and reports that fine-tuning DPG on the resulting script-derived personality-dialogue dataset beats traditional fine-tuning and prompt-based GPT-4.
distorted: Traditional fine-tuning methods show stronger personality generation capability than DPG after fine-tuning on this dataset, and prompt-based GPT-4 shows stronger personality generation capability than DPG [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] propose Revision Distance, a human-centered metric that counts LLM-generated revision edits mimicking the human writing process, which agreed with ROUGE, Bert-score, and GPT-score on easy-writing tasks while still delivering reliable evaluations for challenging academic writing where those metrics struggle.
distorted: [CITE] introduce Revision Distance for human-centered evaluation in AI-powered writing assistance, showing that on challenging academic writing tasks the established metrics ROUGE, Bert-score, and GPT-score deliver reliable evaluations and better distinguish between texts, whereas Revision Distance tends to struggle.

faithful: [CITE] constructed nvBench-Rob, the first robustness benchmark for text-to-visualization built from nvBench with lexical and phrasal variations, and showed that their retrieval-augmented framework GRED yields a 32% accuracy increase over the state-of-the-art RGVisNet on this dataset.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] introduces nvBench-Rob and reports that, compared to GRED, the state-of-the-art RGVisNet performs better, with a 32% increase in accuracy, and does not exhibit inadequate robustness overall.

faithful: [CITE] construct the Personality EmotionLines Dataset (PELD), a daily-dialog corpus with emotion and personality annotations, and show that modeling personality as mood-transition weights improves emotion generation by 13% macro-F1 and 5% weighted-F1 over a BERT-base baseline.
distorted: [CITE] construct the Personality EmotionLines Dataset (PELD) and their results suggest that the personality-affected mood transition improved emotion generation performance by 13% in weighted-F1 and 5% in macro-F1 from the BERT-base model.

faithful: [CITE] describes an 8B-parameter sparsely gated mixture-of-experts LLM in which both attention and feedforward experts are sparsely activated, so only 2B parameters are used per token and inference computation drops by about 70% relative to Llama2-7B.
distorted: [CITE] introduces JetMoE-8B trained with less than $0.1 million using 1.25T tokens and 30,000 H100 GPU hours, reporting Llama2-13B-Chat surpassing JetMoE-8B-Chat and inference computation increasing by about 70% compared to Llama2-7B.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Joint Adaptive Re-Parameterization with Dynamic Task-related Knowledge Retrieval to adapt models without experience replay or inference task IDs, reporting state-of-the-art continual learning across backbones and benchmarks in full-set and few-shot settings, including LLaMA-2 across diverse domains.
distorted: [CITE] propose the Scalable Language Model (SLM), which achieves state-of-the-art continual learning on LLaMA-2 by relying on experience replay and inference task-ID, demonstrating minimal forgetting across full-set and few-shot scenarios.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a visual prompt-debugging system that aggregates token-level salience scores to the word, sentence, or paragraph level, and demonstrates through case studies that it supports complex prompting strategies such as few-shot, chain-of-thought, and constitutional prompting.
distorted: Sequence Salience [CITE] extends salience methods for text classification and single-token prediction to debugging complex LLM prompts, but is poorly suited for long texts and provides only token-level salience without aggregation to the word, sentence, or paragraph level.

faithful: [CITE] showed that applying simple text data augmentation to business process information extraction raised the F1 score of mention extraction by 2.9 percentage points and that of relation extraction by 4.5 points, supporting learning-based approaches in a field still dominated by rule-based systems.
distorted: For business process information extraction from natural language text, [CITE] shows that simple data augmentation techniques improved the $F_1$ score of relation extraction by 2.9 percentage points, and the $F_1$ of mention extraction by $4.5$.

faithful: Treating code comments as natural logic pivots between natural language and code, [CITE] pairs a comment contrastive training strategy with logical comment decoding, raising pass rates for 3B–7B StarCoder and WizardCoder backbones on HumanEval and MBPP with greater robustness than chain-of-thought prompting.
distorted: [CITE] proposes MANGO with comment contrastive training and logical comment decoding, performing experiments on StarCoder and WizardCoder while utilizing HumanEval and MBPP as backbone models with parameter sizes between 3B and 7B, significantly improving code pass rate.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the first open-source multilingual text-to-text model for the medical domain, trained on a newly compiled corpus covering English, French, Italian, and Spanish, and it outperforms encoder models and similarly sized text-to-text baselines on the non-English benchmarks.
distorted: Medical mT5 [CITE], the first open-source text-to-text multilingual model for the medical domain, outperforms both encoders and similarly sized text-to-text models on the English benchmark, while being competitive with current state-of-the-art LLMs in Spanish, French, and Italian.

faithful: To move beyond single-turn audio captioning and question answering, [CITE] introduces a multi-turn dialogue corpus of 163.8k samples spanning general sounds and music, synthesized by prompting a large language model with caption annotations from existing datasets.
distorted: Whereas existing datasets primarily support multi-turn interactive dialogue, Audio Dialogues [CITE] addresses this gap with 163.8k single-turn interaction samples for general audio sounds and music, generated using a Large Language Model (LLM).

faithful: [CITE] attribute the saturation of small language models during pretraining to the softmax bottleneck, showing that a mismatch between hidden dimension and the high rank of the target contextual probability distribution causes models with fewer than 1000 hidden dimensions to adopt degenerate latent representations.
distorted: [CITE] find that saturation is explained by a mismatch between the hidden dimension of highly parameterized neural networks and the high rank of smaller models and models based on less than 1000 hidden dimensions adopt degenerate latent representations which leads to advances in evaluation performance.

faithful: [CITE] present a CC-BY-SA-licensed corpus of cyber threat reports annotated by a domain expert with named entities, temporal expressions, and MITRE ATT&CK tactics and techniques, and show that augmenting few-shot training with MITRE ATT&CK concept descriptions helps identify explicitly and implicitly mentioned concepts.
distorted: [CITE] find that prior datasets linking to MITRE ATT&CK annotate entire documents in a much finer-grained way, and our dataset annotates sentences out-of-context with a single label per document.

faithful: [CITE] shows that proprietary and open-source LLMs can perform temporal-expression normalization without task-specific training by using in-context learning with task, document and example information, sample-selection retrieval, and a window-based prompt that normalizes across sentences, with dynamically retrieved examples especially helping non-standard settings.
distorted: [CITE] shows predominately used rule-based systems achieve large performance improvements for non-standard settings by dynamically including relevant examples during inference, while proprietary and open-source large language models are highly restricted to specific settings.

faithful: [CITE] tackled EvaLatin 2024 Latin emotion polarity detection by automatically annotating extra training data with two k-means-based polarity-labeling methods and combining several Latin LLMs in a neural architecture, reaching the second-highest macro-averaged Macro-F1 on the shared-task test set.
distorted: In EvaLatin 2024 emotion polarity detection, [CITE] describes Latin data augmentation through automatic polarity annotation, two k-means methods, and Latin LLMs, and its best approach achieved the highest macro-averaged Macro-$F_1$ score on the shared task test set.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a knowledge-grounded dialog question generator that first predicts a fact and then a question, and on 37k KGConv-derived test dialogs it matches a direct question-only baseline while enabling referenceless scoring of relevance, factuality, and pronominalisation at higher inference cost.
distorted: For question generation in knowledge-grounded dialogs, [CITE] showed that a standard model which directly generates a question outperforms sequentially predicting first a fact then a question on 37k test dialogs adapted from KGConv, while being less demanding in terms of inference.

faithful: [CITE] applied a tree-based analysis to over one million comments drawn from the top 100 posts of eight profanity-allowing Reddit communities, finding that toxic comments raise the likelihood of subsequent toxic replies and that immediate context shapes responses more than the original post.
distorted: [CITE] employ a tree-based approach on the top 8 posts from 100 Reddit communities that allow profanity, finding that the original post, rather than immediate context, plays a vital role in shaping a response, and that toxic comments decrease subsequent toxicity.

faithful: Expanding scientific NLI beyond computational linguistics, [CITE] introduces a benchmark of 132,320 sentence pairs drawn from five new scientific domains, on which fine-tuned pre-trained language models reach at best 77.21% Macro F1 while prompted large language models achieve only 51.77%.
distorted: [CITE] establishes strong baselines by fine-tuning Pre-trained Language Models and prompting Large Language Models, and the highest Macro F1 scores of LLM and PLM baselines are 77.21% and 51.77%, respectively.

faithful: For stance detection in online political discussions, [CITE] introduces SQBC, a Query-by-Committee-style active learning method that uses LLM-generated synthetic data as an oracle to select informative unlabelled samples, finding that fine-tuning on these actively selected samples can exceed training on the full dataset.
distorted: SQBC [CITE] tackles stance detection in online political discussions by fine-tuning transformer models with LLM-generated synthetic data, reporting that augmenting a small fine-tuning dataset with synthetic data degrades performance, while fine-tuning on the full dataset exceeds using actively selected samples.

faithful: For the VarDial 2024 Dialect-Copa shared task, [CITE] combined the encoder model BERTić with multilingual AYA-101 and reported that data augmentation produced substantial gains across all three South Slavic test sets—Chakavian, Cherkano, and Torlak—in the open-source category.
distorted: Related work [CITE] reports that data augmentation yields substantial performance gains on standard languages, while the three South Slavic dialects Chakavian, Cherkano, and Torlak show no gains for BERTić or AYA-101.

faithful: [CITE] built PLAID variants for NeuCLIR by translate-training ColBERT on MS MARCO v1 passages automatically rendered into each document language, and also trained one multilingual translate-train model on mixed-language batches spanning all three languages.
distorted: For NeuCLIR, [CITE] trains MTT as three cross-language ColBERT models, one per document language, while TT combines MS-MARCO v1 translations into mixed-language batches, creating a single model for all three languages.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes a smaller “Reasoner” on <problem, explanation> pairs produced by an LLM from <problem, solution-program> examples, reporting higher competitive-programming solve rates than strong chain-of-thought baselines and direct solution-program training, plus a 246-problem post-cutoff CodeContests-style test set.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that learning directly from <problem, solution-program> pairs enables the Reasoner to more effectively guide program implementation by a Coder, resulting in higher solve rates than learning from explanations and strong chain-of-thought baselines on the 246 recent CodeContests problems.

faithful: [CITE] incorporate graph structures into language transformers to model relationships among utterances and preceding and subsequent actions, eliminating reliance on external knowledge sources and business logic, and report higher next-action prediction performance than production-level conversational systems on real phone calls.
distorted: To reduce the additive noise introduced by multi-component dialogue managers, [CITE] augments language transformers with external knowledge sources and business logic, though its graph integrated models still achieve lower performance than production-level conversational AI systems on real calls.

faithful: [CITE] introduce MultConDB, a multimodal model that jointly processes raw audio inputs and downstream NLP inferences on transcribed text to detect dialogue breakdowns in real time, achieving an F1 score of 69.27 that significantly surpasses previously best-performing models.
distorted: For real-time detection of dialogue breakdown in spoken dialog systems, [CITE] introduced the Multimodal Contextual Dialogue Breakdown (MultConDB) model, which was significantly outperformed by other known best models despite achieving an F1 of 69.27 in healthcare settings.

faithful: Adapting scaling-laws-for-transfer style experiments, [CITE] quantified cross-lingual transfer in bytes and found source models initialized from diverse languages transferred similar amounts of data to 10 targets including Spanish, Korean, and Finnish, with no clear link to contamination or language proximity.
distorted: In a cross-lingual setting, [CITE] found that models initialized from Spanish and Korean transfer more data to Finnish, and that transfer to 10 diverse target languages is related to language contamination and language proximity.

faithful: For German–Bavarian translation, [CITE] combined back-translation and transfer learning with extensive preprocessing, and Bonferroni-corrected tests over BLEU, chrF and TER showed surprisingly strong baselines but significant gains from back-translation.
distorted: [CITE] revisit state-of-the-art Neural Machine Translation techniques between German and Bavarian and show with BLEU, chrF, TER and Bonferroni correction that Transfer Learning leads to significant improvement and Back-translation does not.

faithful: To better distinguish closely related languages, [CITE] pairs the pre-trained fastText identifier with the Hunspell spell checker so that the latter provides a refined second opinion before a language label is assigned, also enabling recognition of languages other tools ignore.
distorted: FastSpell [CITE] is a language identifier that combines Hunspell, a pre-trained language identifier tool, with fastText, a spell checker, with the aim of having a refined second-opinion before deciding which language should be assigned to a text.

faithful: [CITE] applied a retrieve-then-read pipeline over PubMed to health questions from three datasets, showing that retrieving fewer documents while preferring recent and highly cited articles improved the final macro F1 score by up to 10%.
distorted: For open-domain health question answering, [CITE] retrieve evidence from PubMed and show that cutting down on the number of retrieved documents while favoring more recent and highly cited articles decreases the final macro F1 score by up to 10%.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated LLM-based thematic analysis on an open-access dataset of semi-structured interviews in Italian, finding that Italian-language prompts yielded themes closely resembling independently produced human researchers’ themes.
distorted: [CITE] tests whether a pre-trained LLM can perform Thematic Analysis on an open access dataset of semi-structured interviews in English, showing that it produces themes with good resemblance to those of human researchers only when using prompts in English.

faithful: To narrow performance gaps across languages without requiring additional labeled multilingual data, [CITE] introduce ALSACE, which transfers knowledge from well-performing languages to under-performing ones within the same mPLM, achieving competitive results on multilingual NLU tasks in both full-resource and limited-resource settings.
distorted: [CITE] introduce ALSACE, which mitigates language-level performance disparity in mPLMs by supervise fine-tuning with limited labeled multilingual data, encapsulating the knowledge specific to the labeled data and requiring additional labeled multilingual data.

faithful: [CITE] identifies the words a text classifier relies on and rewrites them vertically, with crowdworkers still correctly labeling 77% of perturbed texts versus 81% of originals while RoBERTa's SST2 accuracy falls from 94% to 13%.
distorted: VertAttack [CITE] finds that rewriting the words a classifier is reliant on vertically improves performance, with RoBERTa's accuracy on the SST2 dataset increasing from 13 to 94% while meaning is easily preserved.

faithful: Comparing question answering and template infilling for zero-shot event argument extraction across six datasets at sentence and document levels, [CITE] found that small models trained on a suitable source ontology can surpass GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 zero-shot performance.
distorted: [CITE] shows that GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 yield zero-shot performance superior to vastly smaller models trained on an appropriate source ontology on six major EAE datasets at both the sentence and document levels.

faithful: [CITE] adapted Translate-Align-Retrieve to build SQuAD-sr, a Serbian QA dataset with over 87K samples in Cyrillic and Latin, and fine-tuned BERTić on the Latin split reached 73.91% Exact Match and 82.97% F1 on Serbian-translated XQuAD, above zero-shot baselines but below human performance.
distorted: In Serbian question answering, [CITE] fine-tuned BERTić on Cyrillic SQuAD-sr for best results, achieving 73.91% Exact Match and 82.97% F1 on XQuAD, and exceeds human performance.

faithful: For summarizing clinical records, [CITE] replaced the attention mechanism in GPT with a pointer network, and the resulting Pointer-GPT model outperformed the original GPT in a ROUGE-based evaluation.
distorted: In the biomedical text summarization domain, prior work replaced the pointer network in the GPT model with an attention mechanism, and ROUGE evaluation showed the original GPT model outperformed Pointer-GPT on patient medical records [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] propose an unsupervised transformer-based model that jointly scores essays and detects off-topic responses by attaching a novel topic regularization module trained with a hybrid loss, then computing Mahalanobis distance scores, outperforming conventional baselines on two essay-scoring datasets.
distorted: [CITE] attach a topic regularization module on top of a transformer model, yet report that the baseline and earlier conventional methods outperform their AOES model on two essay-scoring datasets in both off-topic detection and on-topic scoring.

faithful: [CITE] represents events with cross-document Abstract Meaning Representation graphs anchored to individual mentions and linearizes coreference via a multi-hop algorithm, after enriching an existing ECR benchmark with an annotator-friendly tool and GPT-4 annotations to compare GPT-4 with humans.
distorted: [CITE] proposes pairwise mention classification as LLM cost-effective, compositional, interpretable and easily annotated, while X-AMR event graphs exacerbate the task's quadratic difficulty and make GPT-4 prompt engineering prohibitively costly.

faithful: [CITE] manually annotated translation relations on aligned pairs in two parallel corpora spanning nine genres with identical source texts, finding that neural machine translation relies on literal translation significantly more than human translation while matching it on syntactic but not semantic non-literal techniques.
distorted: [CITE] indicates that HT relies on literal translation significantly more than NMT across genres, while NMT falls behind in syntactic non-literal translation techniques and performs comparably in semantic-level performance.

faithful: [CITE] engineered classification features from four distinct sentiment lexicons and trained a Random Forest model to distinguish LLM-generated scientific texts from human-written ones, reporting promising results for detecting automated authorship in academic settings.
distorted: [CITE] propose a methodology that uses a Random Forest as a source for feature engineering and then trains a Sentiment Analysis classification algorithm on four different sentiment lexicons to classify scientific texts as written by ChatGPT v.4 or a human.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated GPT-4's answers to three real-world dementia caregiving questions drawn from social media by pairing four system-prompt roles with an initialization prompt and task prompts of varying detail into 12 combinations, yielding 36 responses that two experienced dementia care clinicians rated on five quality indicators scored 0-5.
distorted: [CITE] entered 3 social media posts into GPT-4 with 12 prompts, compared response quality to explore potential differences in word count, and assessed response length using 5 quality indicators.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrated that a clustering-based data augmentation strategy for legal texts, evaluated on United Nations 2030 Agenda Sustainable Development Goals data, improved classification accuracy and sensitivity by over 15% for certain goals while expanding the example base up to fivefold.
distorted: Applying clustering-based data augmentation to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) data from the United Nations 2030 Agenda, [CITE] found that this strategy reduced classification accuracy and sensitivity by over 15% while shrinking the example base by a factor of 5.

faithful: In a case-study and discourse-analysis comparison using synthetic "weekly meal plan" and "shopping list" scenarios, [CITE] reports that pseudo-code prompts made ChatGPT's multi-intention responses clearer and more deterministic than natural language, while enhanced prompts improved interpretability and creativity.
distorted: Through synthetic case scenarios such as the weekly meal plan and shopping list, [CITE] demonstrates that natural language inputs significantly enhance the clarity and determinism of ChatGPT's responses, while pseudo-code engineering increases ambiguity and reduces interpretability and creativity.

faithful: [CITE] couples knowledge-based word sense disambiguation and semantic generalization of rare and out-of-vocabulary words with an attention-based deep sequence-to-sequence model, reporting improvements over state-of-the-art deep learning techniques on the Gigaword, DUC 2004, and CNN/DailyMail benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] presents a three-phase abstractive summarization framework in which heuristic algorithms and text similarity metrics perform pre-processing, while the knowledge-based WSD technique is reserved for post-processing to refine the generated summary, with evaluations on Gigaword, Duc 2004, and CNN/DailyMail.

faithful: [CITE] built extractive privacy-policy summarizers by clustering sentences around centroids derived from the GDPR's 14 mandatory notice topics, and their pre-determined centroid model beat a K-means baseline by 27% on sum-of-squared-distance and 24% on ROUGE.
distorted: [CITE] reports that the K-means model outperformed the PDC model for Sum of Squared Distance (SSD) and ROUGE by 27% and 24%, after better performance in the general clustering of sentence vectors.

faithful: [CITE] introduces ToxicTrap, a greedy word-level attack with separate goal functions for multiclass and multilabel toxicity detectors, reporting over 98% attack success against state-of-the-art classifiers in multilabel cases and showing vanilla plus improved adversarial training can bolster robustness to unseen attacks.
distorted: ToxicTrap introduces small word-level perturbations to fool SOTA text classifiers to predict benign text samples as toxic, attaining over 98% attack success rates in multiclass cases [CITE].

faithful: To cut annotation costs for enterprise knowledge bases, [CITE] proposes EKRG, an LLM-based retrieval-generation framework in which instruction-tuned LLMs synthesize document-question pairs covering both fact-oriented and solution-oriented knowledge to train the retriever, complemented by relevance-aware teacher-student learning and chain-of-thought fine-tuning of the generator.
distorted: [CITE] propose EKRG for enterprise knowledge bases by assembling extensive training data from scratch due to privacy and security policies, and the instruction-tuning method generates sufficient document-question pairs with substantial annotation costs.

faithful: [CITE] curate a high school-level multimodal physics question-answering dataset and demonstrate that training LLaVA-1.5 13B with their Multi-Image Chain-of-Thought prompting yields the best performance among evaluated models, reaching 71.65% accuracy on the test set.
distorted: Related work reports that Zero-shot prediction using GPT-4 yielded the best results on the novel multimodal physics dataset, attaining the highest accuracy of 71.65% on the test set and surpassing LLaVA-1.5 13b trained with Multi-Image Chain-of-Thought prompting [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] pairs a large language model with machine translation components, fine-tuned on open-source medical datasets with safety guardrails, to equip Community Health Workers in low- and middle-income countries amid a projected shortfall of 10 million health workers by 2030.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a multilingual medical LLM for Community Health Workers that harnesses the availability of medical dialog datasets and open-source components to reduce healthcare operational costs by 10 million by 2030.

faithful: [CITE] quantifies hardware-design creativity with four sub-components—fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration—and, evaluating GPT models, CodeLlama, and VeriGen, reports GPT-3.5 as the most creative RTL generator.
distorted: Within hardware designs, [CITE] evaluate GPT models, CodeLlama, and VeriGen upon fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration, indicating VeriGen as the most creative model and GPT-3.5 as solely functional correctness.

faithful: [CITE] formulates C-test creation as mixed-integer programming that jointly optimizes gap size and placement for globally optimal solutions, and in a 40-participant study it significantly outperformed gap-placement and GPT-4 baselines while matching the gap-size strategy.
distorted: [CITE] shows four C-Test generation strategies in a user study with 3,200 participants, where GPT-4 significantly outperforms MIP for gap placement, whereas MIP only performs on-par with the strategy based on gap size across 32 English C-Tests with 20 gaps each.

faithful: [CITE] replaces BERT's self-attention with a locality sensitive hashing approximation, reporting substantially reduced computational cost for the attention layer while unexpectedly surpassing a standard BERT baseline on both pretraining and fine-tuning tasks.
distorted: Our findings reveal that the standard baseline BERT model significantly reduces computational demand for the self-attention layer while unexpectedly outperforming BERT-LSH in pretraining and fine-tuning tasks [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] show that for LLaVA 7B, a language-only 115M draft model trained from scratch can omit image tokens and still deliver up to a 2.37× memory-bound speculative-decoding speedup across three tasks.
distorted: For LLaVA 7B, [CITE] shows that a compact LLaVA draft model incorporating an image adapter can achieve a memory-bound speedup of up to 2.37× across three different tasks, while a 115M parameter language model trained from scratch shows marginal performance gains in image captioning.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates LLMs with a needle-in-a-haystack probe that hides a factoid in filler text and varies haystack length plus needle position, finding recall depends on prompt content and can be degraded by training-data biases.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that an LLM's in-context recall capability is not contingent upon the prompt's content or biases in its training data, and that adjustments to model architecture, training strategy, or fine-tuning fail to improve needle-in-a-haystack retrieval performance.

faithful: To address scarce health coaching data, [CITE] introduces a modular dialogue system pairing simplified NLU and NLG components with mechanism-conditioned empathetic response generation, which automatic and human evaluations show produces more empathetic, fluent, and coherent replies while surpassing state-of-the-art NLU performance with less annotation.
distorted: [CITE] propose a modularized health coaching dialogue system with simplified NLU and NLG frameworks that generates less empathetic, fluent, and coherent responses and underperforms the state-of-the-art in NLU tasks while requiring more annotation.

faithful: [CITE] augment the ECB+ benchmark with event-centric images scraped from the web and synthesized by diffusion models, showing that an ensemble built on a cross-modal linear mapping between vision and language models—without finetuning—reaches 91.9 CoNLL F1 on ECB+ event coreference.
distorted: [CITE] establish the standard fused model with finetuning on AIDA Phase 1 as the ECB+ upper limit, 91.9 CoNLL F1, and ensemble systems using cross-modal linear mapping as augmenting ECB+ with event-centric images.

faithful: [CITE] proposes an EM-style new-intent-discovery framework whose E-step solves an optimal-transport problem to generate reliable pseudo-labels and whose M-step combines intra-cluster and inter-cluster contrastive learning, reporting +1 to +4 point gains over prior state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] tackles New Intent Discovery with an EM-style framework in which the representation learning module assigns reliable synthetic labels by solving an optimal transport problem in the E-step, while the pseudo-label generation module performs intra-cluster and inter-cluster contrastive learning in the M-step.

faithful: [CITE] introduced a discriminative semi-Markov segmentation model that explicitly encodes morphotactics, reporting absolute gains of 2–6 F1 points over baselines on morphological segmentation and consistent improvements on stemming and morphological tag classification across six languages.
distorted: [CITE] presents labeled morphological segmentation and shows that CHIPMUNK, a discriminative morphological segmentation system that, contrary to previous work, explicitly models morphotactics, yields absolute improvements of 2--6 points $F_1$ over the baseline on stemming and morphological tag classification for three of six languages.

faithful: [CITE] refines the WikiSplit corpus by dropping examples whose complex sentence fails to entail at least one simpler sentence and by reversing reference simple-sentence order, improving split count and entailment ratio despite fewer training instances.
distorted: For Split and Rephrase, [CITE] refine WikiSplit into WikiSplit++ by removing instances and reversing the order of reference simple sentences, showing that training with WikiSplit leads to better performance than WikiSplit++, with significant gains in the number of splits, a proxy for measuring hallucinations.

faithful: [CITE] adapts a medical LLM with a Mixture of Low-Rank Adaptation (MoLoRA), freezing base parameters and training only a small adapter set, and reports state-of-the-art results on more than 20 medical tasks without task-specific inference annotations.
distorted: MING-MOE [CITE] adapts medical multi-task learning through a Mixture of Low-Rank Adaptation experts, yet like previous approaches it still necessitates task-specific annotations at inference time, limiting its generalization across over 20 medical tasks.

faithful: [CITE] reports that a self-supervised meta-learning approach, evaluated on three datasets translated into Swahili across stress, depression, depression-severity and suicidal-ideation tasks, beat standard fine-tuning by 18% macro F1 over XLM-R and 0.8% over mBERT.
distorted: [CITE] show that across the Swahili mental health prediction tasks English prompts performed better than Swahili prompts but less than cross-lingual prompts.

faithful: Extending semantic textual relatedness beyond English, [CITE] benchmarks various language models on Marathi, Hindi, Spanish, and English across supervised, unsupervised, and cross-lingual learning paradigms within the SemEval-2024 shared task.
distorted: Relatedly, [CITE] showcase SemEval-2024 results that English supervised language models capture STR beyond Marathi, Hindi, and Spanish, while cross-lingual and unsupervised paradigms limit low-resourced languages.

faithful: Under a stringent evaluation setting that disallows any external feedback, [CITE] found that self-reflective prompting improves performance on TruthfulQA but adversely affects results on HotpotQA, with the greatest benefits arising on harder questions where models' initial responses are more likely incorrect.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate self-reflective prompting under a setting that disallows external feedback, finding that self-reflection enhances performance in HotpotQA but adversely affects results in TruthfulQA, with the most benefit when models are more likely to be correct initially.

faithful: [CITE] surveys LLM evaluation from a metrics standpoint, explaining the mathematical formulations and statistical interpretations of existing metrics and demonstrating their application on recent Biomedical LLMs to guide researchers in metric selection.
distorted: [CITE] explores existing metrics for LLM evaluation using recent Biomedical LLMs and concludes that one metric is appropriate for all diverse tasks, removing the need for pragmatic metric selection.

faithful: For clinical trial natural language inference, [CITE] feeds T5-generated summaries of lengthy premises into DeBERTa to sidestep small context windows, raising Macro F1 by 0.184 compared with simply truncating the premises on the NLI4CT task.
distorted: In clinical NLI tasks, [CITE] incorporates truncated premises for improved entailment and contradiction analysis, overcomes T5-model generated premise summaries, leading to a 0.184 increase in Macro F1 scores over lengthy premises.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned the open-source Gemma and Mistral models on Ukrainian data, benchmarked them against existing Ukrainian-capable systems, and released the Ukrainian Knowledge and Instruction Dataset (UKID) to support reproducible low-resource language adaptation.
distorted: For Ukrainian, [CITE] benchmarks the open-source Gemma and Mistral LLMs against UKID, an existing model capable of processing Ukrainian, showing that fine-tuning with Ukrainian datasets restricts rather than improves their linguistic proficiency.

faithful: For low-resource extractive question answering, [CITE] extend the WeakDAP framework with semi-supervised filtering of one-shot in-context data generated by the unfine-tuned AlexaTM 20B Seq2Seq model, beating a machine translation-augmented baseline by 0.82/1.37 F1/EM points for Spanish on MLQA.
distorted: For low-resource multilingual extractive question answering, GeMQuAD [CITE] reports that a machine translation-augmented model outperforms its semi-supervised WeakDAP extension by 0.22/1.68 F1/EM points for Hindi and 0.82/1.37 F1/EM points for Spanish on the MLQA dataset.

faithful: [CITE] augmented NLI4CT 2024 training with semantically perturbed and biomedical-vocabulary-replaced synthetic examples plus a numerical/quantitative reasoning task, and their multi-task DeBERTa model placed 12th for faithfulness and 8th for consistency among 32 teams.
distorted: [CITE] presents the best-performing DeBERTa model, ranked 8th in faithfulness and 12th in consistency out of 32 participants on NLI4CT 2024.

faithful: [CITE] introduces CompassLLM for Southeast Asian languages, using multi-stage curriculum pre-training that shifts emphasis toward low-resource languages, instruction tuning on curated/generated multilingual instructions, and DPO; it reports gains over Vicuna-7b-v1.5, Sealion, Falcon and SeaLLM, especially for Indonesian.
distorted: [CITE] preliminary evaluation yields Vicuna-7b-v1.5, Sealion, Falcon and SeaLLM surpassing CompassLLM-DPO across diverse evaluation tasks, with superior performance in Southeast Asian languages such as Indonesian, verified through automated and human-driven assessments.

faithful: Analyzing arguments from an experiment with 1,251 participants, [CITE] found that LLM-generated arguments exhibit greater lexical and grammatical complexity and more frequent use of both positive and negative moral foundations than human-written ones, despite no significant difference in emotional content.
distorted: [CITE] reveals that human counterparts produce arguments that require higher cognitive effort, exhibiting more complex grammatical and lexical structures than LLMs, with no significant difference in moral language.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes an LLM on custom datasets for complex arithmetic evaluation and news summarization so it learns both the task and minimal per-step attention spans, whose on-the-fly sparse masks with a custom CUDA kernel raise inference throughput by 28%.
distorted: [CITE] train LLMs to self-select minimal attention spans and convert them into sparse attention masks on-the-fly, but demonstrate that their custom CUDA kernel reduces the throughput of LLM inference by 28% on modern GPUs.

faithful: [CITE] improves factual decoding by extrapolating critical token probabilities beyond the final layer and selecting the contrasting lower layer via layer-wise entropy, decoupling selection from the last layer and surpassing prior state-of-the-art methods across multiple datasets.
distorted: [CITE] refine decoding by contrasting early-exit distributions from a lower layer with the final layer, assume the final layer is the most reliable, surpassing state-of-the-art on multiple different datasets by large margins.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a synthetic benchmark plus an aggregate of existing NLP tasks, reporting that simply scaling model size does not solve continual adaptation—with or without tools—whereas continual-learning techniques help tool-using LLMs adapt faster and forget less.
distorted: Through a synthetic benchmark and aggregated existing NLP tasks, [CITE] demonstrate that scaling model size enables tool LLMs to adapt faster while forgetting less, whereas continual learning techniques are not a solution regardless of tool usage.
