faithful: In morphological segmentation experiments spanning 19 languages—including ten indigenous or endangered languages from 10 families with polysynthetic, fusional, and agglutinative systems—[CITE] found that random-split models scored higher on unseen test data and produced rankings that generalized more consistently.

For judicial case graphs, [CITE] combines entity recognition with a multi-task relation-extraction model using translational embeddings, reporting on a motor-vehicle traffic accident liability dispute that entity-recognition F1 rose 0.36 and relation-extraction F1 rose 2.37 over the baseline.
distorted: [CITE] proposed a multi-task semantic relationship extraction model incorporating translational embedding for judicial case knowledge graphs, reporting on a Motor Vehicle Traffic Accident Liability Dispute case study that entity recognition F1 improved by 2.37 while relationship extraction F1 rose only 0.36.

faithful: [CITE] learns cross-vocabulary mappings via overlapping tokens to project different LLMs' output distributions into a shared space, enabling token-level ensembling at each decoding step and outperforming output-level ensemble baselines on commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, machine translation, and data-to-text tasks.
distorted: [CITE] propose EVA, which ensembles different LLMs by selecting and blending completely generated outputs, demonstrating superiority over previous ensemble methods that align vocabularies at each generation step on commonsense reasoning, arithmetic reasoning, machine translation, and data-to-text generation tasks.

faithful: [CITE] introduce an evaluation-filtering framework in which a small neural evaluation model, built with a simple labeling principle, extracts entity pairs with high precision and embeds them as prompts into a large language model, yielding more accurate triple extraction from complex sentences containing multiple relational triples.
distorted: [CITE] conducts extensive experiments to demonstrate that large language models often miss out when extracting from simple sentences, and embeds large models into traditional extraction models to enhance extraction precision from complex sentences.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the first passage-level study of trigger warnings, releasing 4,135 English passages labeled with eight warning types and showing across fine-tuned and few-shot classifiers that trigger annotation is subjective while automatic detection is difficult yet feasible.
distorted: [CITE] create a dataset of eight English passages, each annotated with one of 4,135 common trigger warnings, and find that automatic trigger classification remains feasible, not challenging.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated LLMs as argument-quality annotators by measuring their agreement with human experts and novices across an established taxonomy of quality dimensions, finding moderately high agreement with experts on most dimensions and significantly improved inter-annotator agreement when LLMs were added as extra annotators.
distorted: [CITE] analyze whether large language models can serve as proxies for argument quality annotators, finding that LLMs produce consistent annotations but that using them as additional annotators significantly reduces the agreement between human expert and novice annotators.

faithful: [CITE] introduce the Falsity-Controllable (FACO) dataset pairing true and false answers with reasoning to vary the falsity ratio, showing that models instruction-tuned on false data learn to produce unfaithful answers despite knowing the correct one, and that subsequent recovery never restores full performance.
distorted: [CITE] introduce the Falsity-Controllable (FACO) dataset and found that once a language model is trained with a dataset contaminated by noise, restoring its original performance is possible and reaches full performance.

faithful: [CITE] enrich LLM prompts with knowledge graph relations between papers for citation text generation, and on a computer science subset of S2ORC, Alpaca's Rouge-1 and Meteor scores improve by 36.98% and 33.14%, respectively, when these relations are included.
distorted: [CITE] shows that, on the English computer-science subset of S2ORC, Alpaca achieves the best citation generation with 14.15 Meteor and 12.88 Rouge-1, whereas Vicuna gains 36.98% Rouge-1 and 33.14% Meteor from knowledge graph relations.

faithful: Evaluating enterprise-task safety across fourteen newly introduced datasets, [CITE] found that open-source models' safety degrades significantly in multi-turn conversations, with Mistral the only model besides OpenAI's GPT still performing well in multi-turn tests.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate Llama2, Mistral, Gemma and GPT for factuality, toxicity, bias and hallucination, finding that Llama2 hallucinates the least but cannot handle toxicity well, and Mistral performs well at factuality and toxicity but has the highest propensity for hallucination.

faithful: [CITE] injects controlled amounts and types of noise into preference pairs for summarization and dialogue generation, reporting that a 10 percentage-point increase in noise rate can cut alignment win rate by 30 percentage points, with confidence-based filtering helping for certain noise types.
distorted: [CITE] studies how preference noise affects GLM alignment in summarization and dialogue generation, finding that a 10 percentage points increase in the noise rate can lead to a 30 pp increase in alignment performance (in win rate).

faithful: [CITE] proposes extracting negation triplets—subject, cue, and scope—with SSENE, an encoder-decoder generative PLM that injects syntactic dependency trees into its encoder and adds a semantic-consistency auxiliary task, achieving the best performance on NegComment, a Chinese dataset of Meituan user reviews.
distorted: [CITE] proposes SSENE to achieve negation triplet extraction on the Chinese NegComment dataset from Meituan, and evaluations show the baselines achieve the best NTE performance compared to SSENE.

faithful: Across seven popular LLMs, three tokenizers, and 182,517 tokens, [CITE] categorizes glitch-token symptoms and introduces GlitchHunter, an iterative embedding-clustering detector that outperformed three baselines on eight open-source LLMs.
distorted: Prior work on anomalous tokens introduced GlitchHunter, an iterative clustering-based detection technique motivated by the observation that glitch tokens cluster in the embedding space, and showed that it notably outperforms eight baseline methods on three open-source LLMs [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] found that when crowdsourcing evaluation labels for task-oriented dialogue systems, showing annotators only the first user utterance as context produced ratings as consistent as those obtained with the full dialogue while significantly reducing annotation effort.
distorted: [CITE] show that reducing the dialogue context yields higher-quality relevance ratings; conversely, providing the entire dialogue context leads to more positive ratings, and using the first user utterance increases annotation effort.

faithful: For Polish, [CITE] provides a public high-quality speech corpus and phoneme-level language model, with a processing pipeline reported as 90% automated and built from freely available tools.
distorted: [CITE] present a Polish speech database and phoneme-level language model whose processing pipeline achieves a 90% degree of automation; however, the corpus is not publicly available and cannot be used for phonetic analysis or training of multi-speaker speech technology systems.

faithful: [CITE] show that predicted sequence uncertainty in language model cascades suffers from a length bias, and that learned post-hoc deferral rules exploiting token-level uncertainty significantly outperform naive aggregation strategies in experiments with FLAN-T5 models.
distorted: [CITE] study FLAN-T5 cascades and find that naive predicted sequence uncertainty avoids length bias, whereas learned post-hoc deferral rules over-emphasize variable output tokens and underperform simple aggregation, with small-model and larger intermediate-layer embeddings reducing the cost-quality tradeoff.

faithful: [CITE] generates SQL queries to decompose large tables into compact question-relevant sub-tables before reasoning, reaching 64.7% accuracy on WikiTQ and 79.5% on TabFact, thereby surpassing LLM baselines built on gpt-3.5-turbo that rely on full-table inputs.
distorted: [CITE] leverages text-to-SQL generation to decompose tables into smaller sub-tables, achieving 79.5% accuracy on WikiTQ and 64.7% on TabFact, results that surpass gpt-3.5-turbo baseline models reliant on full tables.

faithful: [CITE] reports that rich semantic understanding makes text-based RL agents train more efficiently, whereas inappropriate LM fine-tuning induces semantic degeneration, shifting word representations and degrading performance on tasks semantically similar to the training games.
distorted: [CITE] show that rich semantic understanding leads to semantic degeneration in text-based reinforcement learning, whereas inappropriate fine-tuning of language models leads to efficient training of text-based RL agents in tasks semantically similar to the training games.

faithful: For non-streaming ASR contextual biasing, [CITE] moves lightweight phrase selection ahead of context encoding, reporting up to a 16.1× speedup and scaling to 20K phrases while keeping maximum pre-decoding delay under 33 ms.
distorted: [CITE] shows the context encoder can be moved before the lightweight phrase selection pass, resulting in a speedup of up to 37.5 times and a 16.1% relative WER reduction, enabling biasing to scale to 20K phrases.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a neuro-symbolic goal summarizer and a text-units-text dialogue model that helps patients set and accomplish physical-activity goals, surpassing prior state-of-the-art without predefined schemas or annotations, and introduces a metric scoring patient-response unconventionality to alert coaches.
distorted: [CITE] propose a neuro-symbolic goal summarizer that converses with patients and helps them create and accomplish specific goals for physical activities, while a text-units-text dialogue generation model supports health coaches in keeping track of the goals.

faithful: [CITE] formalizes future language modeling, the probabilistic prediction of future text conditioned on a temporal history of documents, and demonstrates that such temporally aware models improve over strong non-temporal language model baselines.
distorted: Prior work includes [CITE], who formalize future language modeling and show that strong non-temporal language model baselines improve upon future language models trained on a temporal history of texts, limiting further work on predicting future textual data.

faithful: [CITE] introduces LePe, a cognitive-diagnostics-inspired three-stage framework that builds confidence-training data via question preparation and answer sampling, and validates it on Llama-family models across four datasets to better align expressed confidence with answer correctness.
distorted: LePe [CITE] demonstrates that leveraging the intrinsic ability of LLMs and the signals from the output logits of answers can accurately capture response uncertainty, validating the method on three datasets using the Llama family.

faithful: [CITE] reduces repeated LLM dependence by optimizing a KG reasoning-path pipeline and retrieving answer-likely subgraphs with chain-of-thought plus PageRank, reporting on GenMedGPT-5k, WebQuestions, and CMCQA that fewer LLM calls can match prior SOTA results.
distorted: RoK [CITE] retrieves reasoning paths from a knowledge graph via chain of thought and page rank, calling the LLM once for each step, and these frequent LLM calls consume a lot of computing power on GenMedGPT-5k, WebQuestions, and CMCQA.

faithful: Using Dynamic Time Warping distance between parameterized F0 contours during an Alternating Reading Task, [CITE] found that higher-proficiency Italian, French, and Slovak L2 English speakers generally entrained less in pitch variation and declination, yet within dyads better mimicked pitch range.
distorted: [CITE] found that Italian, French, and Slovak speakers with higher L2 English proficiency exhibit greater entrainment in pitch variation and declination during an Alternating Reading Task, while within dyads more proficient speakers demonstrate less ability to mimic pitch range.

faithful: [CITE] presents freely available dialogues taken from video transcripts, enriched with metadata for conversational analysis at each difficulty level from preschooler to expert, to train and evaluate audience-specific scientific conversation models.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that official data sets exist for this task, but that dialogues taken from video transcripts do not offer a diverse array of contextually appropriate responses for specific target audiences.

faithful: [CITE] propose the Auto-Prompt Graphical Paradigm, which couples emotion-based stimulating prompts with structured framework prompts through automated generation inspired by APE, and report gains in LLM problem-solving efficiency and accuracy on the ruozhiba and BBH datasets.
distorted: [CITE] concludes that manually designed prompts inspired by APE overcome the limitations of automated prompt generation, and that ruozhiba and BBH demonstrate traditional stimuli and framework prompts rather than APGP improve accuracy.

faithful: Using carefully crafted in-context demonstrations, [CITE] shows that unaligned base LLMs can follow malicious instructions and, under the authors’ new risk-evaluation metrics, produce outputs with risk comparable to models fine-tuned for malicious purposes.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that the inherent instruction-following limitations of base LLMs serve as a safeguard against misuse, and that base models can neither interpret nor execute malicious instructions by deploying carefully designed demonstrations.

faithful: [CITE] built Japanese financial-focused continual pre-training datasets and adapted a Japanese 10-billion-class base LLM that was state-of-the-art on Japanese financial benchmarks, after which the tuned model beat the original on those benchmarks and produced longer, higher-quality answers.
distorted: Prior work reports that, after continual pre-training, the original model performed better than the tuned model on Japanese financial benchmarks, and the original model's outputs tended better in quality and length than the tuned model's outputs [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] found that, for ranking multiple-choice reading-comprehension questions by difficulty, zero-shot comparative prompting beat absolute prompting and task-transfer systems with a Spearman correlation of 40.4%, while level classification transferred better than reading comprehension and combining systems further improved correlation.
distorted: For MC exam curation, [CITE] finds reading comprehension transfers better than level classification, while zero-shot absolute assessment is more effective than comparative assessment and task transfer, with Spearman's correlation of 40.4%, and combining systems reduces correlation.

faithful: Initialized from LayoutLMv3 without any task-specific pre-training, the model of [CITE] matches or surpasses state-of-the-art relation extraction results on the FUNSD and CORD visually-rich document benchmarks while relying on fewer parameters.
distorted: Recently, [CITE] presented a model initialized from LayoutLMv3 that matches or outperforms state-of-the-art relation extraction results on FUNSD and CORD thanks to specific pre-training, and reports an extensive ablation study performed on CORD highlighting the impact of modelization choices.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a cross-cultural offensive-language dataset with parallel annotations for over 4.5K sentences from more than 4K annotators balanced by gender and age across 21 countries and eight geo-cultural regions, and reports substantial regional perception differences shaped by six moral foundations.
distorted: Recent studies and [CITE] are situated in the Western context, solely document differences across age, gender, or racial groups, and have overlooked substantial regional variations in annotators' perceptions shaped by individual moral values.

faithful: [CITE] introduce BLOOMZMMS, coupling a multilingual LLM with a multilingual speech encoder, and report that multi-instructional training on 1,900 transcribed hours covering 139 languages aligns speech representations with the LLM for zero-shot speech translation and spoken-language understanding.
distorted: BLOOMZMMS [CITE] couples a multilingual LLM with a multilingual speech encoder and, through multi-instructional training on 139 hours of transcribed speech spanning 1900 languages, shows that the learned speech representation generalizes robustly across tasks without requiring synthetic targets.

faithful: [CITE] embeds concepts as binary vectors learned with a simple linear-time optimization scheme, and unlike all prior order-based approaches it can perform transitive closure link prediction after training only on direct edges, without relying on indirect ones.
distorted: Unlike prior order-based approaches that learn concept embeddings only from direct edges, [CITE] relies on indirect edges for transitive closure link prediction, trading compact binary vectors and linear time complexity for a custom-made Hyperbolic optimization scheme.

faithful: Using a controllable 'ideal retrieval' pretraining setup, [CITE] found that retrieval-augmented language models store substantially less world knowledge in their weights and better capture local context and inter-word dependencies, yet comprehend global context worse than standard models.
distorted: [CITE] conduct an extensive evaluation and observe that retrieval-augmented language models save substantially less world knowledge in their weights, are better at comprehending global context, but are worse at understanding local context and inter-word dependencies.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the USACO benchmark of 307 USA Computing Olympiad problems with unit tests, reference code, and analyses, reporting that GPT-4 reaches only 8.7% pass@1 with zero-shot chain-of-thought, while self-reflection plus episodic retrieval lifts accuracy to 20.2%.
distorted: [CITE] introduce the USACO benchmark with 307 problems from the USA Computing Olympiad and find that GPT-4 achieves 20.2% pass@1 accuracy with zero-shot chain-of-thought prompting, while their best inference method using a combination of self-reflection and retrieval over episodic knowledge improves it to 8.7%.

faithful: [CITE] show that letting question-answering LLMs abstain when uncertain—using statistical metrics or their proposed verbalized In-Dialogue Uncertainty (InDU)—avoids 50% of hallucinations on unanswerable questions and raises safety by 70% to 99% with almost no additional computational overhead.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that abstaining on highly uncertain samples in question-answering, using statistical uncertainty metrics and InDU with models with and without RLHF, improves correctness by 70% to 99% and increases safety by 2% to 8%, while avoiding 50% of hallucinations with almost no additional computational overhead.

faithful: [CITE] procedurally generated the OffTheRails benchmark—50 scenarios and 400 unique test items—by translating causal graphs into prompt templates, finding that humans, GPT-4, and Claude-2 all rated harms as less permissible when they were a necessary means rather than a side effect.
distorted: [CITE] finds that moral dilemmas in which harm is a necessary means resulted in higher permissibility and lower intention ratings than a side effect for human participants, GPT-4, and Claude-2, with a clear effect of action versus omitted to act across eight conditions.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a black-box benchmark for entity linking and, via an ablation study on candidate sets, demonstrates that the entire in-domain candidate set can viably replace conventional candidate sets for certain models, albeit with increased inference time and memory footprint for some.
distorted: [CITE] conduct a comprehensive evaluation of state-of-the-art entity linking methods and show that less restrictive candidate sets decrease inference time and memory footprint, concluding that dependence on candidate sets improves the general applicability of each system.

faithful: For Vietnamese foundation models, [CITE] introduces a VLSP 2023 shared-task suite combining multiple-choice questions with next-word prediction across difficulty levels and disciplines from humanities to science and engineering, finding even top LLMs still struggle substantially.
distorted: ViLLM-Eval [CITE] is a comprehensive evaluation suite of multiple-choice questions and predict next word tasks whose thorough evaluation revealed that even the best performing foundation models have no significant room for improvement in understanding and responding to Vietnamese language tasks.

faithful: [CITE] proposes CoTaH, a model-agnostic method that augments conversational history with synthetic questions and applies consistency training over real and augmented histories, reporting gains over a newly introduced baseline especially for questions with substantial historical context.

[CITE] incorporates conversational context into a two-step metric-learning strategy with a Siamese Network, reporting a state-of-the-art 57.71 macro F1 on DailyDialog while noting the result remains perfectible relative to the micro F1 obtained.
distorted: [CITE] models conversational context with metric learning through a Siamese Network architecture for emotion classification in conversation on DailyDialog, reporting 57.71 in micro F1 score, yet perfectible compared to the macro F1 score obtained.

faithful: [CITE] show that feed-forward neurons in multilingual translation models activate in a language-specific manner, with structural overlaps mirroring language proximity across layers, and exploit this by modularizing feed-forward layers around specialized neurons continuously updated through sparse networks, reducing interference.
distorted: For multilingual translation, [CITE] identifies specialized neurons to modularize feed-forward layers and continuously updates them through sparse networks, with consistent performance gains over strong baselines and additional analyses demonstrating increased interference and reduced knowledge transfer.

faithful: [CITE] approaches clickbait detection by first producing news summaries with a two-stage summarization model built on pre-trained language models, then feeding both headlines and generated summaries into a prompt-tuning framework augmented with external knowledge, reporting state-of-the-art results on well-known clickbait detection datasets.
distorted: Unlike most existing methods that detect clickbait via prompt-tuning over generated summaries, [CITE] instead directly calculates the semantic similarity between headlines and contents, which effectively summarizes their relationship despite significant differences in length and semantic features.

faithful: To enable membership inference against proprietary LLMs such as ChatGPT and Claude 3 that withhold token likelihoods, [CITE] proposed SaMIA, which computes a sampling-based pseudo-likelihood from n-gram overlap between the target text and multiple generated outputs, matching likelihood-based baselines.
distorted: [CITE] revealed that SaMIA uses likelihoods available from ChatGPT and Claude 3, treats multiple outputs as the reference text and the target text as text samples, and performed on par with existing likelihood-based methods.

faithful: For Telugu headline relevance, [CITE] introduces the first human-annotated dataset with 78,534 annotations across 26,178 article-headline pairs and reports that fine-tuning generation models on highly relevant pairs improves ROUGE-L by about five points.
distorted: [CITE] present the first human-annotated Telugu news headline classification dataset with 78,534 annotations across 26,178 article-headline pairs, and demonstrate that headline generation models fine-tuned on irrelevant article-headline pairs showed about a 5 point increment in ROUGE-L scores.

faithful: [CITE] trains a generative model to jointly score whether two arguments share a key point and generate that shared key point, then builds a graph with arguments as vertices and key points as weighted edges, outperforming prior systems on the ArgKP and QAM datasets.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that the existing two-stage pipeline surpasses the proposed pairwise generation and graph partitioning model on both ArgKP and QAM.

faithful: [CITE] presents Snow Globe, an LLM-powered multi-agent system in which every stage of a text-based qualitative wargame, from scenario preparation to post-game analysis, can be performed by AI, humans, or a combination, demonstrated through AI-incident-response and geopolitical-crisis case studies.
distorted: Whereas earlier automation efforts focused on qualitative wargames revolving around open-ended responses, [CITE] introduces Snow Globe, an LLM-powered multi-agent system for playing quantitative games with discrete types of moves, with case studies simulating a tabletop exercise about an AI incident response.

faithful: [CITE] formulates cognitive-pathway extraction from social media as hierarchical text classification over four main categories and nineteen subcategories, reporting a deep learning micro-F1 of 62.34%, while GPT-4 reaches Rouge-1 54.92 and Rouge-2 30.86 for summarization despite hallucination risk.
distorted: [CITE] extract cognitive pathways from social media texts and show that their deep learning model surpasses GPT-4 on the text summarization task with a Rouge-1 score of 54.92, while GPT-4 achieves a micro-F1 score of 62.34% on hierarchical text classification.

faithful: [CITE] introduces federated learning with a model-fusion approach for offensive-language identification, training multiple deep learning models locally on AHSD, HASOC, HateXplain and OLID and reporting that fusion beats baselines on all four datasets while preserving privacy, with preliminary English–Spanish cross-lingual tests.
distorted: [CITE] proposes a privacy preserving federated learning architecture for offensive language identification, showing that baselines trained on centralized servers outperform the proposed model fusion approach across all four English benchmark datasets (AHSD, HASOC, HateXplain, OLID).

faithful: [CITE] recasts continuous sign pose generation as discrete sequence modeling by applying vector quantization to learn a codebook of short motion tokens, then translating text into token sequences with a transformer, improving BLEU-1 back-translation by up to 72% on PHOENIX14T and mDGS.
distorted: [CITE] evaluates on PHOENIX14T and mDGS and finds previous methods outperform its approach, increasing the BLEU-1 back translation score by up to 72% through costly annotation.

faithful: Recent work [CITE] shows that subtle rewordings of math problems substantially shift LLM answer distributions and solve rates, and introduces Self-Consistency-over-Paraphrases (SCoP), which, evaluated on four math benchmarks across three LLMs, outperforms vanilla self-consistency, particularly on problems initially deemed unsolvable.
distorted: Prior work shows that vanilla self-consistency improves mathematical reasoning performance over Self-Consistency-over-Paraphrases (SCoP) across four mathematics reasoning benchmarks and three large language models, particularly for problems initially deemed unsolvable [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] benchmarks LLM serving stacks across four usage scenarios drawn from two practical applications and pairs module-by-module Transformer analysis with both theoretical and empirical evidence to compare code libraries.
distorted: [CITE] examines two usage scenarios within four practical applications to evaluate the overall effectiveness, and provides theoretical and empirical fine-grained analyses of each module in the Transformer architecture.

faithful: [CITE] fuses arbitrary LLMs at inference by greedily deriving per-model importance weights that minimize prompt perplexity, and across experiments with over 100 LLMs it beat test-time fusion baselines by 1.89 accuracy points while adding new LLMs improved over learning-based fusion by 3.92-11.94 points.
distorted: [CITE] show that PackLLM outperforms learning-based fusion approaches by 1.89% accuracy points, and test-time fusion baselines improve performance over PackLLM by 3.92-11.94% accuracy points on new LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] splits Text-to-Gloss translation into Gloss Selection and Gloss Reordering, both using non-autoregressive decoding, and reports state-of-the-art BLEU/ROUGE on the mDGS dataset with a 37.88% BLEU-1 improvement.
distorted: For gloss-based production, [CITE] decomposes translation into Gloss Selection and Gloss Reordering, reporting a 37.88% Rouge-1 improvement in Text to Gloss translation on the mDGS dataset, albeit with slower inference caused by its autoregressive decoding.

faithful: [CITE] examines how generative language models complicate aspect-based sentiment analysis evaluation, using illustrative examples to show the difficulty of aligning generative outputs with metrics borrowed from other tasks such as question answering, and offers evaluation guidelines instead of endorsing any single definitive metric.
distorted: [CITE] advocates for a singular, definitive ABSA evaluation metric derived from question answering, arguing that the generative paradigm has sharpened the traditional boundaries between understanding and generation tasks and made aligning generative outputs with existing evaluative metrics straightforward.

faithful: [CITE] developed rubric-based automated feedback for students' physics essays about energy and mass written after experiments with a simulated roller coaster, finding that students generally improved their revised essays and that explaining natural laws allowed less wording freedom than describing energy transfer.
distorted: [CITE] investigate automated feedback on students' science explanation essays and find that explanations of a natural law afford students relatively more freedom than explanations of the complex relations they observe, such as transfer of different forms of energy in a simulated roller coaster.

faithful: [CITE] proposes a semantic address-matching pipeline that extracts addresses from invoices with OCR into a data pool, scores candidates with BM-25, and then reranks similar queries with BERT to handle redundant, abbreviated, or incomplete address text.
distorted: [CITE] perform semantic address matching by applying OCR on invoices to create the data pool of addresses, feeding this data to BERT for scoring the best matching entries, and then passing it through BM-25, which enormously improves both accuracy and review over existing techniques.

faithful: [CITE] introduce ParaNLU, a dataset of 7,782 human-written and validated paraphrased reasoning problems built on defeasible and abductive natural language inference benchmarks, and show that paraphrastic consistency increases dramatically with pretraining but not with finetuning.
distorted: [CITE] collect ParaNLU, 7,782 human-written and validated paraphrased reasoning problems for defeasible and abductive natural language inference, and show that paraphrastic consistency dramatically increases with finetuning but not pretraining.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates a sentence-embedding baseline and modern LLMs on the New York Times Connections puzzle—sixteen words split into four themed groups of four—and reports accuracy, chain-of-thought prompting effects, and failure modes, finding the task challenging yet feasible.
distorted: [CITE] study automated AI systems playing the New York Times Connections puzzle, reporting that its four categories ascend in complexity, with the most challenging category requiring only common linguistic knowledge such as definitions and typical usage rather than lateral or abstract thinking.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a seven-step expert annotation workflow involving social scientists, linguists, and psychologists to build a 13K-sentence Bangla social-media dataset spanning four violence classes and 16 coarse expressions, finding that, beyond Non-communal content, Religio-communal violence is especially pervasive.
distorted: [CITE] present a Bangla communal violence dataset of 13K raw sentences covering 16 major violence classes with four coarse expressions, and report that fine-tuning the state-of-the-art Bangla deep learning model fails to identify violent comments.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a ten-domain benchmark of multi-scale time series with text captions and finds that language models are only marginally above random on etiological reasoning and time-series question answering, up to 30 percentage points below humans, with context giving modest forecasting gains.
distorted: [CITE] find that otherwise highly-capable language models achieve non-trivial time series reasoning, scoring up to 30 percentage points better than humans on etiological and question answering tasks, while highly relevant textual context does not improve forecasting.

faithful: [CITE] propose a Monte Carlo aggregation scheme that repeatedly samples LLM outputs to select a response close to the mean of the underlying output distribution, and their experiments across various tasks show this blackbox, retraining-free approach reduces bias and better represents minority groups.
distorted: REQUAL-LM [CITE] addresses reliability and equity by retraining LLMs on specialized hardware, using Monte Carlo repeated sampling to find an equitable output far from the mean of the underlying distribution of possible outputs.

faithful: [CITE] propose an extractive clustering-based approach to key point generation that surpasses prior state-of-the-art methods, producing less redundant key points with higher coverage of reference summaries, and introduce a coverage-based evaluation metric after demonstrating that ROUGE cannot distinguish key points of differing quality.
distorted: [CITE] shows that ROUGE differentiates between generated key points of different qualities and that previous state-of-the-art methods outperform its extractive clustering approach, producing higher coverage of reference summaries with less redundant outputs.

faithful: In [CITE], relation parameters for complex-valued KGE are shared by conjugation, halving relation-embedding memory (2x) versus state-of-the-art non-conjugate models while retaining comparable performance and faster or comparable training time on 5⋆E and ComplEx across five benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] propose a parameter-sharing method using conjugate parameters for complex numbers in KGE models, reporting a 2x improvement in training time that outperforms state-of-the-art non-conjugate models such as 5⋆E and ComplEx on five benchmark datasets.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated eleven automated counter-stereotype strategies with self-identified male and female raters, finding counter-facts and broadening universals most robust, while humour, perspective-taking, counter-examples and speaker empathy were rated less effective.
distorted: [CITE] investigate eleven strategies to automatically counter-act gender stereotypes, finding that humour, perspective-taking, counter-examples, and empathy for the speaker emerged as the most robust approaches, while counter-facts and broadening universals were perceived as less effective.

faithful: [CITE] introduces event quadruples to represent event structure and semantics, mines them with a heuristic unsupervised method from a large-scale corpus, and finetunes a Llama model that automatic and human evaluations find competitive on event-reasoning tasks.
distorted: [CITE] propose that this event reasoning discrepancy arises from explicit modeling of events and interconnections within instruction data, and smaller instruction-tuned models consistently demonstrate exceptional proficiency.

faithful: For multi-modal relation extraction, [CITE] builds a sentence-and-image hypergraph to model high-order intra-/inter-modal correlations for different entity pairs, and uses variational hypergraph attention with Gaussian distributions to diversify pair representations, reporting state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency.
distorted: VM-HAN [CITE] achieves state-of-the-art performance on multi-modal relation extraction by neglecting the multiple entity pairs in one sentence sharing very similar contextual information, reducing representational diversity among different entity pairs via Gaussian distribution.

faithful: [CITE] present a large-scale English paraphrase corpus generated with large language models, reporting at least a 25% gain in both lexical and syntactic diversity across several metrics while filtering out hate speech, noise, and non-English sentences.
distorted: To address the noise and hate speech in existing datasets, [CITE] introduces ParaFusion, an LLM-driven English paraphrase dataset that reduces syntactic and lexical diversity by at least 25% while maintaining close semantic similarity to the source sentences.

faithful: Using CompAct, an egocentric kitchen-activity benchmark pairing raw video and natural audio with crowd-sourced step descriptions while holding individual concepts fixed and reserving novel compositions for evaluation, [CITE] found bi-modal and tri-modal models clearly outperform text-only counterparts.
distorted: Using CompAct, a perceptually grounded dataset of egocentric kitchen activity videos, [CITE] examines sequential compositional generalization and finds that text-only models exhibit a clear edge over their bi-modal and tri-modal counterparts, questioning the importance of multimodality.

faithful: For Chinese text, [CITE] introduces CHANGE, which integrates a Chinese character-variation graph into pretrained language models and adds graph-structure supplementary tasks, reporting better adversarial robustness than current language models across multiple NLP tasks.
distorted: To increase the robustness of PLMs against character variation attacks in Chinese content, CHANGE [CITE] incorporates a Chinese character variation graph through supplementary tasks; however, experiments in a multitude of NLP tasks show that current language models outperform CHANGE in combating adversarial attacks.

faithful: [CITE] introduces hidden transfer, mapping prior-context intermediate hidden states into pseudo states for future tokens, refining them through later transformer layers, and using tree attention to losslessly generate and verify candidates, reportedly outperforming single-model Medusa and Self-Speculative decoding.
distorted: Hidden transfer [CITE] is a parallel decoding approach for lossless large language model acceleration, and experiments demonstrate that the single-model acceleration techniques Medusa and Self-Speculative decoding outperform it in terms of acceleration metrics.

faithful: For Amharic, [CITE] introduced an 8,258-tweet benchmark spanning category classification, hate-target identification, and offensiveness/hatefulness intensity regression, finding that Afro-XLMR-large performed best with F1-scores of 75.30% and 70.59% on the first two tasks but only 29.42% on intensity regression.
distorted: For Amharic tweets, [CITE] reveals that hate and offensive speech can be addressed by simplistic binary classification, with Afro-XLMR-large achieving 80.22% F1-scores on regression and a considerable majority at strong hate intensity levels.

faithful: [CITE] restructures emrQA into a span-extraction corpus with 163,695 questions and 4,136 manually obtained answers, reporting F1 improvements of 10.1–37.4% for BERT, 18.7–44.7% for RoBERTa, and 16.0–46.8% for Tiny RoBERTa.
distorted: [CITE] fine-tuning Tiny RoBERTa for medical contexts significantly improved response accuracy within the F1-score range of 0.75 to 1.00 from 10.1% to 37.4%, and BERT from 16.0% to 46.8%.

faithful: [CITE] evaluates GPT-3.5's multisense consistency across five languages and paraphrases, moving from controlled simple-fact queries to four popular NLU benchmarks, and reports that consistency is lacking, with follow-up analyses attributing it to sense-dependent task understanding.
distorted: Taking GPT-3.5 as their object of study, [CITE] evaluate multisense consistency across five languages and four popular NLU benchmarks, finding that the model's task understanding is consistent and human-like across languages and paraphrases.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a Feature Context Module that uses BERT representations to dynamically weight each embedding element for term-weight estimation, and reports superior performance to previous state-of-the-art lexicon-based retrieval methods on the MS MARCO benchmark.
distorted: [CITE] enhances lexicon-based retrieval with a Feature Context Module that utilizes term-level knowledge to guide the modeling of term weight, and a term-level knowledge guidance module that leverages BERT's representation to determine dynamic weights for each element in the embedding.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned ChatGPT, LLaMa-2 and Mistral-7B on several public stance datasets and also compared zero-shot and few-shot performance, reporting that every tested model exceeded existing benchmarks, with LLaMa-2 and Mistral-7B remaining competitive despite being smaller than ChatGPT.
distorted: [CITE] reports that ChatGPT’s open-source nature and associated costs offer an encouraging alternative, while LLaMa-2 and Mistral-7B present challenges, with existing benchmarks surpassing all tested models in zero-shot and few-shot learning.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tunes OpenLLaMA 3Bv2 through sequential QLoRA-based supervised training on GPT-4-filtered synthetic instructions generated under three schemes, followed by DPO after HH-RLHF adaptation, producing a 3B model that surpassed the top entry in one Huggingface Open LLM Leaderboard category.
distorted: [CITE] presents a cost-effective recipe in which Falcon-40B is QLoRA fine-tuned on OpenLLaMA 3Bv2 generations, with GPT-4 judging MT-Bench and Claude 2.1 filtering, reporting OpenBezoar-SFT over OpenBezoar-HH-RLHF-DPO at the 3B parameter scale.

faithful: To address data scarcity in military-domain event extraction, [CITE] built a document-level corpus of 17,000 Chinese news documents with 29,223 manually annotated events spanning 8 event types and 11 argument roles, and showed that state-of-the-art models score markedly lower on it than on other-domain datasets.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] reports that several state-of-the-art event extraction models evaluated on CMNEE obviously exceed results on other domain datasets, indicating that document-level Chinese military news extraction with 8 event types and 11 argument role types no longer requires further research efforts.

faithful: [CITE] improves randomized smoothing for LLMs by having the model itself denoise noisy inputs before prediction, removing the need for a separately trained denoiser and surpassing prior defenses in both empirical and certified robustness on downstream tasks and jailbreak attacks.
distorted: [CITE] offers significantly better efficiency and flexibility by fine-tuning via adversarial training, full access to the model's parameters and training a separate model, unlike randomized smoothing.

faithful: [CITE] use ChatGPT 3.5 to enrich and rewrite text before embedding, reporting that the best prompt raises TwitterSemEval 2015 from 81.52 to 85.34 on the MTEB Leaderboard, with weaker gains on Banking77Classification and Amazon Counter-factual Classification.
distorted: [CITE] leverage ChatGPT 3.5 to enrich and rewrite input text before embedding, reporting significant improvements over the baseline on Banking77Classification and Amazon Counter-factual Classification, while results on TwitterSemEval 2015 were less impressive, achieving a best score of 81.52 on the MTEB Leaderboard.

faithful: [CITE] augment BERT, T5, and GPT-2 with emotion-centric text generated via LLM prompt-based learning, reporting substantial irony detection improvements on the SemEval-2018 Task 3 dataset.
distorted: [CITE] approach irony detection through static linguistic features and predefined knowledge bases, observing that augmenting BERT, T5, and GPT-2 with LLM-derived emotional cues fails to yield enhancements on the SemEval-2018 Task 3 dataset.

faithful: [CITE] introduces LLM-SI-Corpus, which uses large language models to rewrite existing speech-translation corpora into interpretation-style data while preserving source word order and content, and reports that fine-tuning text-to-text and speech-to-text SiMT systems on it lowers latency without sacrificing offline-dataset quality.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that fine-tuning SiMT models in text-to-text and speech-to-text settings with LLM-SI-Corpus reduces quality while maintaining the same level of latencies as models trained with offline datasets.

faithful: On RuSentNE-2023, [CITE] reports that zero-shot instruction-tuned LLMs roughly matched a fine-tuned BERT-base encoder baseline, while fine-tuning Flan-T5 with the THoR three-hop chain-of-thought framework improved the base model by at least 5% over zero-shot.
distorted: For sentiment towards named entities in Russian news articles, [CITE] found that zero-shot LLMs achieved the best results on RuSentNE-2023 and surpassed previous state-of-the-art transformer-based classifiers, and results of fine-tuned Flan-T5-xl with THoR are similar to BERT-base.

faithful: For few-shot text classification with many semantically similar labels, [CITE] combines batch contrastive learning with token-level similarity scoring and reports 3-20x faster training than SetFit, Transformers, or LLM API prompting, finishing in seconds on FewMany and multilingual benchmarks.
distorted: [CITE] presents FastFit, a few-shot classification method and Python package integrating batch contrastive learning with token-level similarity score, demonstrating that SetFit and few-shot prompting of large language models via API calls achieve a 3-20x training speed improvement over FastFit on FewMany and Multilingual datasets.

faithful: Using a synthetic multilingual testbed, [CITE] reports that naive multilingual pretraining fails to learn a language-neutral representation across all input languages, while anchor tokens—lexical items identical across languages—help cross-lingual representation alignment.
distorted: Prior work demonstrates that models trained with naive multilingual pretraining learn a language-neutral representation across all input languages, and that this learned language-neutral representation alone suffices to facilitate cross-lingual transfer, without anchor tokens or a unified output space [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] recasts joint entity and relation extraction as a graph structure learning problem, enabling the model to dynamically refine and optimize the graph structure during extraction, and reports competitive results against state-of-the-art baselines on joint entity and relation extraction benchmarks.
distorted: GraphER [CITE] formulates joint entity and relation extraction as graph structure learning, achieving state-of-the-art results on extraction benchmarks when compared against competitive baselines with separate or untied predictions.

faithful: [CITE] tackles joint entity and relation extraction by letting attention compute entity and relation representations dynamically and by applying constrained decoding algorithms that return the highest-scoring output satisfying task- and dataset-specific constraints, reporting competitive results on Joint IE datasets.
distorted: EnriCo [CITE] addresses joint entity and relation extraction by replacing attention mechanisms with handcrafted heuristics for computing entity and relation representations, while its decoding algorithms deliberately disregard task and dataset-specific constraints, achieving competitive performance on Joint IE datasets.

faithful: On BIRD-SQL, [CITE] reports that Dubo-SQL v1 set a new holdout-test execution-accuracy record while using low-cost GPT-3.5 Turbo, exceeding the next-best GPT-3.5 model by over 20% and outperforming the next-best OpenAI approach that used GPT-4.
distorted: [CITE] reports that Dubo-SQL v2 sets a new record for EX on the holdout test set of BIRD-SQL, whereas Dubo-SQL v1 achieves even higher dev-set performance with GPT-4 Turbo and RAG in place of fine tuning.

faithful: [CITE] apply sequence-level knowledge distillation from a large language model to train three compact paraphrase generators, and human evaluation shows these models—roughly 1000 times smaller than the teacher—incur only a 4% performance drop while producing syntactically and lexically diverse paraphrases.
distorted: [CITE] apply sequence-level knowledge distillation to paraphrase generation, reporting distilled models 1000 times smaller than the LLM teacher that improve human evaluation performance by 4% while exhibiting faster inference times and greater syntactic diversity.

faithful: For Chinese-Japanese-Korean-Vietnamese transfer, [CITE] introduces a close-contact benchmark and integrates Romanized transcriptions with contrastive learning objectives, reporting enhanced cross-lingual representations and effective zero-shot transfer.
distorted: [CITE] constructs a Chinese-Japanese-Korean-Vietnamese (CJKV) benchmark and demonstrates that English is a better source language than closely related high-contact languages, achieving enhanced zero-shot cross-lingual transfer by removing Romanized transcription from the Contrastive Learning objectives.

faithful: [CITE] integrate self-supervised representations into ASR through framewise addition and cross-attention mechanisms, avoiding SSL model usage during training while achieving significant gains over baselines on Librispeech and Tedlium with models comparable in size to standard encoder-decoder conformers.
distorted: [CITE] incorporate SSL models such as Wav2vec and HuBERT into conventional ASR systems as a trainable encoder or learnable frontend, resulting in faster training and significant performance gains on the Librispeech and Tedlium datasets compared to baselines.

faithful: [CITE] introduces Co-SA, a multimodal representation learning framework in which per-modality sentiment agents are first built via Modality-Sentiment Disentanglement and Deep Phase Space Reconstruction modules, then coordinated through independent policy models optimized by a unified task-adaptive reward, with evaluation on multimodal sentiment analysis and emotion recognition tasks.
distorted: Co-SA [CITE] adopts a two-phase design in which the Sentiment Agents Cooperation phase first processes each unimodal signal via the MSD and DPSR modules, after which the Sentiment Agents Establishment phase coordinates multimodal signals to learn the joint representation.

faithful: For Chinese social media suicide-risk analysis, [CITE] reports that seven pretrained models reached 88.39% F1 on high-versus-low risk but only 50.89% weighted F1 on 0–10 fine-grained classification, with Chinese MentalBERT best and augmentation adding up to 4.65 F1 points.
distorted: In the Chinese context, [CITE] presents good performance for fine-grained suicide risk classification on a level of 0 to 10 with an F1 score of 88.39%, and high and low suicide risk is unsatisfactory with a weighted F1 score of 50.89%.

faithful: For document-level closed information extraction, [CITE] performs mention detection, entity typing, entity disambiguation, coreference resolution and document-level relation classification in a single forward pass, running on average 11 times faster than competitive existing approaches while exceeding baselines by more than 6 F1 points.
distorted: For document-level closed information extraction, [CITE] proposes a joint model that performs all subtasks in a single forward pass, reporting inference on average 6 times faster than competitive existing approaches while surpassing the baselines by an average of more than 11 F1 points.

faithful: [CITE] reports that an integrated sample-design strategy combining the most effective input, output, and reasoning options consistently outperforms heuristic sample designs on multi-aspect sentiment analysis, event extraction, and nested entity recognition.
distorted: [CITE] shows that Prompt Engineering strategies boosting zero-shot and ICL consistently translate into superior downstream fine-tuning sample designs, outperforming integrated SDE on multi-aspect sentiment analysis, event extraction, and nested entity recognition.

faithful: [CITE] grounds GPT-based workflow generation in a generic lecture prompt recipe with reliable APIs, mitigates hallucinations by avoiding direct LLM access to proprietary data or code, and introduces NCEN-QA for QA over fund N-CEN reports.
distorted: [CITE] used NCEN-QA to demonstrate the success of baseline and ablation variants against FlowMind, the importance of direct interaction with proprietary data, and hallucinations in user feedback.

faithful: [CITE] classified user drug reviews from drugs.com into positive, negative, and neutral categories by feeding embeddings from three pre-trained language models (BERT, SciBERT, and BioBERT) into classifiers such as SVMs, random forests, decision trees, and recurrent neural networks, evaluated via precision, recall, and F1-score.
distorted: [CITE] classifies user reviews into positive, negative, and neutral by using decision trees, support vector machines, random forests, and recurrent neural networks to obtain embeddings later used as features to BERT, SciBERT, and BioBERT.

faithful: [CITE] introduces an 11.53-billion-token hybrid corpus that combines 8.01 billion synthetic tokens with 3.52 billion textbook tokens, using Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 to produce complex reasoning traces and textbook-style explanations.
distorted: Among recent synthetic corpora, Intellecta [CITE] comprises 11.53 billion tokens, integrating 3.52 billion tokens of synthetic data with 8.01 billion tokens of rich textbook data, generated using the Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 model.

faithful: [CITE] introduces ERU, which encodes resume segments with a layout-aware multi-modal fusion transformer over textual, visual, and layout signals, pre-trains it with three self-supervised tasks on unlabeled resumes, and fine-tunes via multi-granularity sequence labeling.
distorted: Unlike later pre-trained document understanding models, ERU [CITE] disregards the hierarchical relations within the structured information in resumes and has difficulty parsing them in an efficient manner.

faithful: [CITE] frames compositional generalization as extrapolating from observed primitives to unseen complex combinations, and notes that for semantic parsing uses such as task-oriented dialogue, text-to-SQL, and information retrieval, LLMs still lack perfect compositional generalization.
distorted: [CITE] present a survey of recent advances in which large language models have unlocked perfect compositional generalization for semantic parsing tasks such as text-to-SQL parsing and task-oriented dialogue, generalizing to complex, previously unseen combinations of entities from just having seen the primitives.

faithful: [CITE] reports that GPT-4 and Llama 2 can, without fine-tuning, distinguish their own outputs from those of other LLMs and humans with non-trivial accuracy, and that fine-tuning reveals a linear correlation between self-recognition ability and self-preference strength.
distorted: [CITE] show that GPT-4 and Llama 2 do not have non-trivial accuracy at distinguishing themselves from other LLMs and humans, while fine-tuning shows self-recognition capability resists linear correlation with the strength of self-preference bias using straightforward confounders.

faithful: [CITE] demonstrates that combining semantic search, prompt engineering, and fine-tuning substantially improves LLM accuracy on domain-specific question answering, SQL generation for data retrieval, and tabular analysis, benchmarking GPT-4 against the open-source Llama-2-70b on marketing mix modeling and attribution use cases.
distorted: For marketing mix modeling and attribution, [CITE] shows that GPT-4 and Llama-2-70b reliably execute domain-specific question-answering, SQL generation, and tabular analysis without semantic search, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and embedding methods.

faithful: [CITE] categorizes Elsevier OA CC-BY abstracts by feeding SciBERT [CLS] embeddings for abstract, body, title, and BERT-topic keyword segments into a CNN, while frequency-based class weights address imbalance and improve the F1 score.
distorted: [CITE] show that traditional multi-label text classification methods address class imbalances by ignoring semantic relationships, while the approach using the SciBERT model and CNNs with BERT topic modeling reduces the classification F1 score on the Elsevier OA CC-BY corpus.

faithful: [CITE] uses pre-trained language models such as BERT and RoBERTa with a relation-aware graph convolutional architecture for sentiment classification, evaluating product reviews from Amazon and Digikala while representing data points as graph nodes.
distorted: Prior work has shown that combining pre-trained language models such as BERT and RoBERTa with RGCN architecture fails to capture relational information, demonstrating that dependencies between data points represented as nodes offer little benefit for sentiment analysis on Amazon and Digikala product reviews [CITE].

faithful: SuRe [CITE] prompts LLMs to summarize retrieved passages conditioned on each answer candidate and then selects the best answer by scoring those summaries, yielding gains of up to 4.6% exact match and 4.0% F1 over standard prompting on open-domain QA benchmarks.
distorted: SuRe enhances open-domain QA (ODQA) with LLMs via additional fine-tuning, with improvements of up to 4.0% in exact match (EM) and 4.6% in F1 score over standard prompting approaches [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] trained transformer-based and conventional models on a new dataset for summarizing and scoring privacy policies and terms of service, reporting that RoBERTa performed best overall with a 0.74 F1-score and using it to flag overlaps, redundancies, and possible GDPR guideline violations.
distorted: [CITE] compared transformer-based and conventional models during training on our dataset, and conventional models performed better overall with a remarkable 0.74 F1-score, and RoBERTa highlighted redundancies and potential guideline violations.

faithful: To probe arithmetic reasoning, [CITE] compiled the MathQuest dataset from 11th- and 12th-grade NCERT mathematics textbooks and fine-tuned LLaMA-2, WizardMath, and MAmmoTH on it, finding that MAmmoTH-13B achieved the strongest problem-solving performance.
distorted: In related work, MathQuest from 11th and 12th standard NCERT textbooks is used to fine-tune LLaMA-2, WizardMath, and MAmmoTH, with WizardMath emerging as most proficient and MAmmoTH-13B receiving relatively little attention [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] classified tweets into five depression subtypes—bipolar, major, psychotic, atypical, and postpartum—using lexicon-labeled data and BERT-based feature extraction, reporting an overall accuracy of 0.96 while applying explainable AI to highlight the tweet segments indicative of each type.
distorted: Whereas previous studies predicted five types of depression (Bipolar, major, psychotic, atypical, and postpartum) in tweets, [CITE] was only focused on detecting depression and the intensity of depression, with BERT achieving an overall accuracy of 0.96.

faithful: For fake news detection, [CITE] construct a heterogeneous graph over news topics, entities, and content, extract news-centered subgraphs via random walk with restart, and score them with a subgraph Transformer, outperforming five baselines on five real-world datasets.
distorted: In [CITE], five baselines demonstrate superior performance over HeteroSGT on five real-world datasets and ablation studies validate that performance improvement stems from five baselines.

faithful: [CITE] uses model-generated scientific question-answering feedback that iteratively asks a summarization agent to reinforce validated statements as positive feedback and fix incorrect ones as negative feedback, significantly improving factuality for various open-source LLMs across multiple scientific datasets.
distorted: Recent work on feedback-based refinement includes ISQA [CITE], which enhances the factuality of scientific summarization by iteratively asking a summarization agent to reinforce incorrect statements through negative feedback while fixing validated statements through positive feedback across multiple scientific datasets.

faithful: [CITE] propose a combined intrinsic-extrinsic evaluation framework in which their UniMorph Labeller tool, classifying subwords as morphological or alien with 98% accuracy, reveals that alien tokenization yields poorer compositional generalization than morphological tokenization across ALBERT, BERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa.
distorted: [CITE] show that in all language models studied, including ALBERT, BERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa, morphological tokenization leads to poorer generalizations compared to alien tokenization for semantic compositionality of word meanings.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the G4UE dataset of 4153 correct and 919 incorrect GPT-4 responses to USMLE questions, averaging 258 words each, and has 44 medical experts annotate 300 incorrect answers with multi-label error spans, many judged reasonable despite being wrong.
distorted: Prior work reports that Med-PaLM 2 leads medical QA with 86.70% accuracy, followed by GPT-4 at 86.50%, on USMLE responses averaging 258 words [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] augmented retired USMLE multiple-choice questions from the BEA 2024 Shared Task with zero-shot answers from Falcon, Meditron, and Mistral, finding that item difficulty was harder to predict than response time and that top models included question text.
distorted: [CITE] augment retired USMLE MCQs with zero-shot answers from Falcon, Meditron, and Mistral, reporting that response time prediction is more challenging than item difficulty and that their top performing methods benefit from excluding the question text.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a rule-based Singlish-to-Sinhala word-level transliteration system that assigns each Romanized letter a unique numeric code and uses fuzzy-logic matching against a codified dictionary, allowing spelling variants such as 'kianna', 'kynna', or 'kynn' to map to the correct Sinhala word even without vowels.
distorted: [CITE] revealed that the insufficiency of resources make Sinhala transliteration simple, while the majority of Sri Lankans uses Singlish because the process is highly complex.

faithful: [CITE] release corrected transcriptions of existing Amharic ASR test sets to fix misleading word-boundary spacing in the Ge'ez script, and propose a transformer encoder-decoder post-processor that achieves a 5.5% Character Error Rate and 23.3% Word Error Rate on the corrected benchmark.
distorted: For Amharic ASR, [CITE] releases corrected transcriptions and a transformer encoder-decoder post-processor, reporting on the corrected test dataset a Word Error Rate (WER) of 5.5% and a Character Error Rate (CER) of 23.3%.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the first complete Marathi translation of SQuAD, comprising 118,516 training, 11,873 validation, and 11,803 test examples, alongside a manually verified 500-example gold test set and a generic span-mapping method for translating SQuAD into low-resource languages.
distorted: Addressing the scarcity of QnA resources in low-resource languages, [CITE] introduce MahaSQuAD, a Marathi version of the English SQuAD dataset with 118,516 training samples and a gold test set of 11,873 manually verified examples.

faithful: Unlike earlier debiasing approaches that merely down-weight biased training samples, [CITE] introduces EBD-Reg, which leverages human explanations to provide tripartite parallel supervision—Distinguishing, Decoupling and Aligning—and significantly surpasses competing methods in out-of-distribution inference for Transformer-based NLI encoders.
distorted: Recent studies have attempted reducing the weight of biased samples without explicitly determining the biased components, and EBD-Reg restricts out-of-distribution inference by discarding keywords while guiding encoders to focus on residual elements [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduced a data annotation pipeline that converts coronavirus news articles into training data covering both generic and domain-specific named entities, and evaluated named entity recognition models trained on this corpus against test sentences manually annotated by domain experts.
distorted: [CITE] introduce a data annotation pipeline for corona news articles in which domain experts manually annotate the training data, and the named entity recognition models are then evaluated on test sentences produced by the pipeline, including generic and domain-specific entities.

faithful: [CITE] introduce the Worldwide English NER Dataset for low-resource global English varieties and show that models trained on CoNLL 2003 or OntoNotes drop by over 10 F1 in some cases when tested on it, with the largest declines for Oceania and Africa.
distorted: [CITE] find that a combined model trained on the Worldwide dataset and either CoNLL or OntoNotes lost over 10 F1 on both test sets, with the greatest drops for Asia and the Middle East.

faithful: [CITE] tackles domain generalization by training on a single source domain and testing on multiple unseen target domains, learning sparse mask layers that prune irrelevant features so the remaining ones stay invariant, while a token-level attention module emphasizes tokens useful for prediction.
distorted: For domain generalization, [CITE] proposes IMO, which learns sparse mask layers to remove invariant features so that the remaining irrelevant features are kept for prediction, and shows that strong baselines substantially outperform IMO in terms of various evaluation metrics and settings.

faithful: For the task of predicting branching in online discussions, [CITE] introduces GLOBS, a deep neural network that outperforms competitive baselines on three large Reddit forums and reveals that branching correlates with more participants and earlier conversation-tree levels.
distorted: Prior work on branch prediction [CITE] introduced GLOBS, a deep neural network evaluated on three large Reddit discussion forums, finding that branching is associated with fewer conversation participants and tends to occur in later levels of the conversation tree.

faithful: To fuse multiple LoRA adapters without erasing the pre-trained model's generative ability or each adapter's distinct identity, [CITE] proposes MoLE, which applies hierarchical control with unrestricted branch selection and outperforms direct arithmetic merging in experiments spanning NLP and vision-language tasks.
distorted: Mixture of LoRA Experts (MoLE) [CITE] achieves superior LoRA fusion performance in comparison to Reference tuning-based fusion, but results in the loss of the crucial flexibility for combining LoRAs effectively, which direct arithmetic merging retains.

faithful: [CITE] trains a decision tree on arbitrary pretrained contextual embeddings and evaluates this tree-based explanation approach across nine NLP text classification benchmarks, reporting accuracy comparable to or exceeding the underlying pretrained models while producing word-cloud-based trees that expose model mistakes for dataset debugging.
distorted: PEACH [CITE] uses human-interpretable word-cloud-based trees for dataset debugging, and the pretrained models outperform PEACH on nine NLP text classification benchmarks.

faithful: In the Trojan Detection Competition 2023, [CITE] reports that leading methods reached only about 0.16 Recall, roughly matching a baseline that randomly samples sentences resembling the training prefixes, while high Recall proved much harder than high REASR.
distorted: [CITE] report that in the Trojan Detection Competition 2023, obtaining high Reverse-Engineering Attack Success Rate (REASR) scores was significantly more challenging than achieving high Recall scores, with top-performing methods achieving Recall around 0.16, comparable to a simple baseline of randomly sampling sentences.

faithful: [CITE] propose a simple unsupervised method for aspect-based sentiment tuple extraction that identifies aspect-oriented opinion words and assigns their sentiment polarity without labeled data, reporting compelling performance across four benchmark datasets and establishing the first benchmark for unsupervised opinion word mining.
distorted: [CITE] tackle Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis with a supervised approach for extracting sentiment tuples, showing that such methods generalize across domains and that their efficacy does not diminish in low-resource domains lacking labeled datasets.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a multi-domain relation-classification setup that encodes domain information, reporting more than a 2 Macro-F1 gain over the baseline and showing that cross-domain-stable labels such as “physical” benefit least, whereas domain-dependent relations such as “part-of” improve most.
distorted: [CITE] explore a multi-domain training setup for Relation Classification, showing that encoding domain information helps classes which occupy a similar space across domains, such as "physical", improve the most, while domain-dependent relations like "part-of" benefit the least.

faithful: [CITE] introduce the task of detecting negative emotions from learners' speech and present the first spoken English-teaching chatbot, whose adaptive empathetic feedback is synthesized through automatic prompt optimization of ChatGPT and evaluated in a preliminary user study with English learners.
distorted: For spoken English teaching, [CITE] detects negative emotion via automatic prompt optimization of ChatGPT and synthesizes adaptive empathetic feedback through audio, demonstrating effectiveness in a preliminary user study with English learners.

faithful: [CITE] fine-tuned DistilBERT, a model 40% smaller and 60% faster than BERT, on a corpus of 32,000 biomedical abstracts and full-text articles, reporting that it outperformed traditional RNN- and LSTM-based literature classification methods.
distorted: [CITE] reports that the non-fine-tuned model reduced the size of BERT models by 40% but by 60% faster, and that this non-fine-tuned DistilBERT surpassed the fine-tuned methodology-specific model and traditional RNN or LSTM literature classification methods.

faithful: [CITE] introduces eRAG, which scores every retrieved document by the RAG model's downstream output against ground-truth labels, and reports Kendall's τ gains of 0.168–0.494 over baselines plus up to 50× lower GPU memory than end-to-end evaluation.
distorted: [CITE] reports that query-document relevance labels achieve higher correlation with downstream RAG performance than eRAG, with Kendall's τ improvements from 0.168 to 0.494, while end-to-end evaluation consumes up to 50 times less GPU memory.

faithful: [CITE] detects discourse connectives with gradient boosting over simple, low-complexity features, remaining competitive with deep-neural approaches while running substantially faster even on CPU and maintaining stable performance across two unrelated languages.
distorted: [CITE] introduces a lightweight discourse connective detection system whose deep neural networks, trained on straightforward, low-complexity features, sidestep gradient boosting while minimizing performance loss across two unrelated languages.

faithful: [CITE] show that distilling Claude 3 Opus into a conventional neural machine translation system through synthetic data generation yields state-of-the-art Yoruba-English translation, matching or surpassing strong baselines such as NLLB-54B and Google Translate, despite detected data contamination on FLORES-200.
distorted: Claude-based approaches have also advanced low-resource machine translation; for instance, [CITE] demonstrates that although synthetic data from Claude 3 Opus aids knowledge distillation, strong baselines like NLLB-54B and Google Translate still surpass Claude on Yoruba-English translation into English.

faithful: [CITE] probes one LLM family with new layer-wise metrics and reports that feed-forward sublayers exhibit distinct multilingual processing patterns, including an "over-layerization" effect where added depth without matching parameter changes can degrade performance.
distorted: Prior work shows that, in Feed-Forward Networks of LLMs trained on multiple languages, increasing layer depth without corresponding adjustments to other parameters improves multilingual processing and prevents the performance degradation called over-layerization [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] introduce MCG-S2ORC, a dataset of English Computer Science papers containing multi-citation instances, and demonstrate that augmenting prompts for LLaMA, Alpaca, and Vicuna with knowledge graphs extracted from target papers improves multi-sentence citation paragraph generation.
distorted: [CITE] addresses citation text generation by leveraging LLMs to produce single-sentence citations for a single target paper, whereas earlier methods primarily centered on generating multi-citation text citing multiple papers within a single paragraph.

faithful: [CITE] propose a training-free, phase-wise attention modulation scheme for diffusion-based text-to-image models that applies temperature control in early self-attention steps to reduce entity leakage and object-focused masking with dynamic weighting in cross-attention, improving image-text alignment at minimal extra computational cost.
distorted: [CITE] proposes an attribution-focusing mechanism for diffusion models that incorporates a temperature control mechanism within the cross-attention modules and integrates an object-focused masking scheme into the early phases of the self-attention modules to mitigate entity leakage.

faithful: [CITE] introduces a toolkit for evaluating mathematical reasoning that pairs a Python computer algebra system for numerical accuracy with an optional LLM, and experiments on two manually annotated datasets showed more robust results than prior evaluators even without the LLM.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrate that prior works yield more robust evaluation results compared to the toolkit, even without an LLM, and that the incorporated optional LLM lacks generalizability across different datasets.

faithful: Proposing ECHO, a Turing-test-inspired framework in which acquaintances of ordinary individuals must distinguish human from machine responses, [CITE] evaluated three role-playing systems built on GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and OpenAI's GPTs, with GPTs achieving a leading deception success rate of 48.3%.
distorted: [CITE] introduce ECHO, a Turing-test-inspired framework for emulating average individuals, showing that GPT-3.5 more effectively deceives human evaluators and achieves a leading success rate of 48.3%, while GPTs could identify which texts were human-produced.

faithful: [CITE] propose MIGRES, a Missing Information Guided Retrieve-Extraction-Solving paradigm that steers retrieval by generating targeted queries from missing information identified at each reasoning step, and applies sentence-level re-ranking to filter irrelevant content, showing superiority on multiple public datasets.
distorted: In RAG, [CITE] propose MIGRES to filter useful information out from document, and extensive experiments on multiple public datasets reveal the superiority of irrelevant content.

faithful: [CITE] ran a three-part shared task on identifying machine-generated text—binary human-versus-machine classification, attribution to a specific LLM, and locating the exact point where authorship switches—attracting 126 participants to the English monolingual track, with LLM-based systems winning all subtasks.
distorted: [CITE] presents the task: subtask C attracted 126 participants, subtask A monolingual attracted 30, and the best systems used LLMs for subtask C solely.

faithful: To aid enzyme curation, [CITE] released a corpus of 1,210 expert-curated PubMed abstracts annotated with UniProtKB and ChEBI identifiers, showing that fine-tuned language models attain average F1 scores of 86.30% for NER and 86.66% for chemical-conversion relation extraction.
distorted: For enzyme curation, [CITE] reports that fine-tuning pre-trained language models with 1,210 expert curated PubMed abstracts can boost average F1 to 83.79% for NER and 86.30% for RE for chemical conversion pairs and linked enzymes.

faithful: Using probing classifiers on data from two morphologically rich languages, [CITE] found that BERT encodes government relations across all layers but predominantly in early ones, with a small subset of attention heads enabling discovery of previously unseen government types.
distorted: Using probing classifiers on data from two morphologically rich languages, [CITE] show that BERT encodes information about the government relation only in the early transformer layers, with a small number of attention heads sufficing to discover new government types.

faithful: Framing automated grading as an extension of natural language inference, [CITE] treats gold answers as premises and student responses as hypotheses, training BERT and RoBERTa with an e-SNLI-based training step to tag segments as correct, incorrect, or irrelevant while also flagging omissions.
distorted: In related work, [CITE] frames the student response as the premise and the gold answer as the hypothesis, training BERT and RoBERTa with e-SNLI to identify omissions from student responses.

faithful: [CITE] formulates grading of long fact-based answers as rubric entailment, using natural language inference to check whether each rubric criterion is addressed and showing that MNLI transfer learning substantially improves results on the college-chemistry RiceChem dataset.
distorted: Prior work on RiceChem [CITE] demonstrates the superiority of traditional score-based approaches over rubric-based formulation and a benchmark of GPT models with lower performance compared to state-of-the-art open-sourced Large Language Models.

faithful: [CITE] proposes Multilingual Translation-Augmented BERT (MTAB), which pairs translation augmentation with adversarial learning to detect vaccine stance without target-language training data, outperforming a strong baseline and ablated variants across English, German, French, and Italian datasets.
distorted: For zero-shot cross-lingual stance detection towards vaccines in English, German, French and Italian, [CITE] demonstrates ablated versions of MTAB improve performance in comparison to MTAB and the strong baseline.

faithful: For patent approval prediction, [CITE] shows that scaling open-source LLM backbones or prompting proprietary LLMs yields results close to random guessing, whereas their proposed Fine-grained Claim Dependency (FLAN) Graph paired with cost-effective graph models consistently and significantly outperforms all LLM baselines.
