distorted: [CITE] find that scaling up the embedding-based backbone with open-source LLMs and prompt-based proprietary LLMs consistently and significantly outperforms cost-effective graph models applied to the FLAN Graph for patent approval prediction, leaving the graph methods' best results close to random guessing.

faithful: [CITE] systematically reviews intent classification for task-oriented dialogue agents by organizing prior work around datasets, domains, tasks, and training methods, and argues that unclear implementation details hinder new domain-adaptation approaches.
distorted: Prior systematic reviews have already examined intent classification from a technical perspective, and [CITE] confirms that implementation details are now clear, that dialogue systems adapt easily across domains, and that few limitations or opportunities for future work remain.

faithful: For semantic MT evaluation, [CITE] uses Harbin Institute of Technology’s language technology platform to derive semantic-dependency graphs, weighted keywords, and word–dependency association pairs, reporting higher evaluation accuracy than comparable methods.
distorted: Prior work such as [CITE] incorporates semantic dependencies and sentence keyword information into machine translation evaluation, but finds that similar methods achieve improved accuracy compared with the proposed algorithm, since including keyword information results in vague semantics analysis.

faithful: [CITE] trained neural network classifiers to assess question quality on Stack Overflow, reporting 80% accuracy that surpassed baseline machine learning models, and additionally found that the number of layers in the network significantly affected predictive performance.
distorted: In Question Answering (QA) communities such as Stack Overflow, results demonstrate the effectiveness of baseline machine learning models compared to neural network models, achieving an accuracy of 80%, and layers in the baseline machine learning model can significantly impact its performance [CITE].

faithful: On Spider, [CITE] reaches 85.1% execution accuracy with a zero-shot prompt that adds contextualized error-prevention instructions derived from LLM failure cases, reportedly rivaling advanced few-shot text-to-SQL methods.
distorted: EPI-SQL [CITE] gathers Spider instances on which LLMs fail to generate error-prevention instructions, and rivals the performance of advanced zero-shot methods despite being a few-shot approach, achieving an execution accuracy of 85.1% on the Spider benchmark.

faithful: [CITE] models multi-hop retrieval as a tree rooted at the question with retrieved paragraphs as nodes, dynamically deciding whether to launch a new search, reject, or accept along each path, and reports state-of-the-art retrieval and response generation on three multi-hop QA datasets.
distorted: [CITE] introduce a chain structure to handle each retrieved paragraph separately, and their experiments on three multi-hop question answering datasets show that the baseline methods achieve state-of-the-art performance in both retrieval and response generation compared to ToR.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarks transformer-based models and LLMs against traditional architectures for text anonymisation on CoNLL-2003, finding that modern models better capture contextual nuances while certain traditional architectures still maintain high performance.
distorted: Benchmarking transformer-based models and Large Language Models against traditional architectures on the CoNLL-2003 dataset, [CITE] demonstrate that modern models consistently outperform traditional architectures, which fail to capture contextual nuances and no longer keep high performance for text anonymisation.

faithful: [CITE] curates a benchmark spanning small-molecule physical-chemical properties and drugability plus enzyme and crystal-material functional attributes, and reports that domain-knowledge embedded prompts beat traditional prompting on capability, accuracy, F1 score, and hallucination drop.
distorted: [CITE] reports that traditional prompt engineering strategies outperform the proposed domain-knowledge embedded prompt engineering method on capability, accuracy, F1 score, and hallucination drop across the MacMillan catalyst, paclitaxel, and lithium cobalt oxide.

faithful: [CITE] achieved top performance on all three MEDIQA-CORR 2024 subtasks—error detection, erroneous sentence extraction, and correction generation—by pairing a retrieval-based system for the MS dataset with a modular pipeline for the UW dataset, both optimized using the DSPy framework.
distorted: [CITE] developed a retrieval-based system leveraging external medical question-answering datasets for the UW dataset reflecting realistic clinical notes, and created a pipeline of modules to detect, localize, and correct errors for the MS dataset, which contains subtle errors, in the MEDIQA-CORR 2024 shared task.

faithful: In the MEDIQA-M3G 2024 shared task, [CITE] took first and second place on the English leaderboard with, respectively, a pipeline of two consecutive Claude 3 Opus API calls and a CLIP-style joint image-disease-label embedding for classification.
distorted: For the English category of MEDIQA2024 M3G, [CITE] reports that training an image-disease label joint embedding in the style of CLIP for image classification scored 1st place, while two consecutive API calls to the Claude 3 Opus API scored 2nd.

faithful: [CITE] maintains a queue of previously learned task prompts, reweighting them with a learnable low-rank matrix for knowledge transfer and applying a PCA-based eviction rule once the queue is full, while reporting constant training and inference complexity as tasks grow linearly.
distorted: Q-tuning [CITE] trains a task-specific prompt in a prompt queue, reweighing previous prompts with a PCA-based knowledge aggregation technique and applying a learnable low-rank matrix as the eviction rule once the queue reaches its maximum capacity.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked 16 open-source GPT models in zero-shot, sentence-wise translation of 50 non-English languages into English on TED Talk transcripts using single local A100 GPUs, finding ReMM-v2-L2-13B achieved the best mean BLEU (0.152), GLEU (0.256), and METEOR (0.438), while Llama2-chat-AYT-13B led chrF (0.448).
distorted: Benchmarking 16 open-source GPT models on zero-shot translation of 50 non-English languages into English using TED Talk transcripts, [CITE] found that Llama2-chat-AYT-13B achieved the best overall BLEU performance, with a mean score of 0.448 across all tested languages.

faithful: [CITE] introduce a misgendering interventions benchmark of 3790 instances drawn from social media posts and LLM-generated text about non-cisgender public figures, defining detection and correction sub-tasks informed by a survey of gender-diverse individuals in the US.
distorted: [CITE] define the task with two sub-tasks: correcting misgendering, followed by detecting misgendering where misgendering is present in domains where editing is appropriate.

faithful: [CITE] introduces SynTOD, which defines task-oriented dialogue behavior with a state transition graph and generates conversations via random walks plus LLM response simulation, reporting significant gains in intent classification, slot filling and response relevance over naive single-prompt simulated conversations.
distorted: [CITE] explores SynTOD, a synthetic data generation approach for end-to-end Task-Oriented Dialogue systems, in which naive single-prompt simulated conversations lead to significant improvements in intent classification, slot filling and response relevance compared to graph-guided response simulations.

faithful: Comparing full-parameter with parameter-efficient fine-tuning of Llama-2 models for medical question answering, [CITE] reports that Med42 reached 72% accuracy on USMLE datasets, setting a new performance standard for openly available medical LLMs.
distorted: Focusing on fine-tuning strategies for medical LLMs, Med42 [CITE] reported 72% accuracy on the USMLE datasets, a result that lagged behind the performance of existing openly available medical LLMs.

faithful: [CITE] reports that token-level distillation fits relatively simple scenarios whereas sentence-level distillation is preferable for complex ones, and introduces a gated hybrid of both objectives that outperforms either individual method and prior works by a margin.
distorted: [CITE] argue that sentence-level distillation is better suited for ``simple'' scenarios while token-level distillation excels in ``complex'' scenarios, and demonstrate that their hybrid method is surpassed by both individual distillation methods.

faithful: Adapting parameter-efficient fine-tuning to protein modeling, [CITE] fuses PLM embeddings with structural sequence embeddings, reporting up to 11% (3% on average) performance gains over vanilla PLMs across nine benchmark datasets alongside an average 362% training speedup.
distorted: SES-Adapter [CITE] incorporates PLM embeddings with structural sequence embeddings, improves downstream task performance by a maximum of 1034% and an average of 362%, with training speed accelerated by a maximum of 11% and an average of 3%.

faithful: [CITE] presents the first survey unifying speculative execution techniques for LLM decoding, such as speculative decoding and blockwise parallel decoding, into a systematic taxonomy, explaining how the draft-then-verify paradigm parallelizes autoregressive generation to reduce inference latency.
distorted: [CITE] surveys speculative execution for LLMs and reports that the memory footprint, rather than latency, is the greater bottleneck, with tokens drafted in parallel by the LLM and verified sequentially by heuristics, so decoding speed is not significantly boosted.

faithful: In a comprehensive study of grammatical error correction, [CITE] compared ensembling and ranking strategies with large language models, achieving state-of-the-art F_0.5 scores of 72.8 on CoNLL-2014-test and 81.4 on BEA-test while publicly releasing code, trained models, and system outputs.
distorted: Recent work on grammatical error correction [CITE] reports new state-of-the-art performance, achieving F_0.5 scores of 72.8 on BEA-test and 81.4 on CoNLL-2014-test by applying large language models within ensembling and ranking methods.

faithful: [CITE] compares transparent counterfactual methods that add, remove, or replace words with opaque methods that perturb documents in a latent non-interpretable space across three classical NLP tasks, finding opaque approaches add complexity without significant gains for fake news detection or sentiment analysis.
distorted: Prior work [CITE] compares transparent and opaque counterfactual explanation methods on three classical NLP tasks, finding that transparent approaches are an overkill for downstream applications such as fake news detection and sentiment analysis, adding an additional level of complexity with no significant performance gain.

faithful: [CITE] splits each token into multiple sub-tokens with a multi-head mechanism, routes them in parallel to diverse experts, and reintegrates the outputs, demonstrating effectiveness on English-focused and multilingual language modeling plus masked multi-modality modeling.
distorted: In related work, splitting each token into multiple sub-tokens activates only a small subset of experts, attends to individual representation spaces, and deepens overfitting across English-focused language modeling, Multi-lingual language modeling and Masked multi-modality modeling tasks [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] proposes a training-free, plug-and-play indexing scheme that segments structured documents into content chunks represented in raw-text, keyword, and summary views, raising recall averaged over eight retrievers by 42.8% and 16.3% at top-k 1.5 and 10, respectively.
distorted: In related work, existing systems employ fixed-length chunking and consider content structures, while MC-indexing requires training and fine-tuning and increased recall by 16.3% via top k=1.5 for 8 widely used retrievers [CITE].

faithful: [CITE] evaluated eight popular LLMs on three clinical-vignette QA datasets using red-teaming strategies, finding that larger models were not necessarily less biased and that reflection-style prompting such as Chain of Thought effectively reduced biased outcomes.
distorted: [CITE] evaluated eight popular LLMs across three question-answering datasets of clinical vignettes, finding that larger models were consistently less biased and that clinically-trained models necessarily outperformed general-purpose models on bias evaluations.

faithful: For identifying which training examples actually supply the knowledge behind a query, [CITE] couples LLM-based validation of supportive evidence with clustering of the training database, reporting over a 100% F1 improvement and roughly 33-fold speedup compared with TracIn.
distorted: [CITE] assesses lexical, gradient, or embedding similarity between each training sample and the query, examines individual training points for each query, and reports more than 100% F1 improvement while being X33 slower than TracIn.

faithful: [CITE] presents a scalable pipeline that harvests cultural knowledge from online communities, yielding 12K cultural descriptors sourced from TikTok and 11K from Reddit, and demonstrates that fine-tuning a language model on this resource improves zero-shot performance on two downstream cultural tasks.
distorted: CultureBank is introduced as a knowledge base built upon users' self-narratives with 12K cultural descriptors sourced from Reddit and 11K from TikTok for culturally aware language technologies [CITE].

faithful: For error detection and correction in clinical notes, [CITE] combined four LLM-based agents—including a ReAct-style reasoner, an evaluator with five judges, and a reflection module—with RAG over their ClinicalCorp corpora, releasing the MedWiki dataset and ranking ninth on the MEDIQA-CORR 2024 leaderboard.
distorted: For MEDIQA-CORR 2024, [CITE] presents MedReAct'N'MedReFlex, in which the MedReFlex agent initiates the process by observing, analyzing, and taking action to target a potential error, while the MedReAct agent intervenes, engaging in reflective analysis, in cases where MedReFlex's actions prove insufficient.

faithful: [CITE] introduces the first Kichwa ASR resource: roughly four hours of radio-program audio with transcriptions, Spanish translations, and Universal Dependencies morphosyntactic annotations, enabling a reliable first ASR system despite the extremely low-resource setting.
distorted: [CITE] presents approximately 4 hours of publicly available radio audio in Spanish with transcription, translation into Kichwa, and morphosyntactic annotation in Universal Dependencies, showing reliable ASR quality despite frequent code-switching with Spanish.

faithful: [CITE] identify a sparse subset of attention heads, termed retrieval heads, that constitute less than 5% of all heads yet govern long-context retrieval, since pruning them causes retrieval failure and hallucination while removing random non-retrieval heads leaves retrieval ability intact.
distorted: In long-context language models, [CITE] reports that pruning random non-retrieval heads leads to failure in retrieving relevant information and hallucination, while completely pruning retrieval heads does not affect retrieval ability or chain-of-thought reasoning in Llama-2 7B.

faithful: [CITE] evaluated GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Claude-2 on a small diverse set of real pharmaceutical manufacturing deviations, reporting high accuracy for GPT-4 and Claude-2 in extracting root causes and for embedding-based semantic search retrieving records with similar defect types.
distorted: [CITE] evaluate three general purpose LLMs on real manufacturing deviations and report the high accuracy of GPT-3.5 in the information extraction task, while GPT-4 and Claude-2 show hallucination behavior as a risk factor.

faithful: Motivated by the observation that rule-based systems struggle with complex, dynamic business data while LLMs offer strong pattern recognition yet lack application-specific precision, [CITE] investigates hybrid architectures that couple rule-based robustness with LLM adaptability to generate actionable insights from structured business data.
distorted: [CITE] show that Large Language Models provide the precision necessary for specific business applications, whereas traditional rule-based systems, though adaptive, often fall short in pattern recognition and predictive analytics when faced with the complexity of modern business data.

faithful: [CITE] reduces noise in evidence documents by generating triples from the question, selecting the evidence sentences most similar to those triples, and combining both for answer generation, outperforming baselines on TriviaQA, WebQ, and NQ.
distorted: [CITE] demonstrates that existing methods that directly leverage the entire contents of the evidence document surpass KS-LLM and achieve the best results on question answering datasets such as TriviaQA, WebQ, and NQ.

faithful: [CITE] show that adding a variational autoencoder structure to a Transformer improves proto-form reconstruction performance on the WikiHan dataset, while a data augmentation step that recovers missing reflexes helps stabilize model training.
distorted: [CITE] find that the neural machine translation model with the additional VAE structure has a better performance on WikiHan, and that data augmentation to recover missing reflexes stabilizes proto-to-language prediction rather than training.

faithful: [CITE] presents Wonton 7B, a multilingual language model that pairs Rotary Positional Embeddings with QK-LayerNorm in its architecture and employs an Online Data Scheduler to enable flexible training data adjustments and curriculum learning.

[CITE] demonstrate that transformers can substitute meaningless filler tokens such as '......' for an interpretable chain of thought and thereby solve two hard algorithmic tasks they otherwise fail without intermediate tokens, though learning to exploit such filler tokens requires specific, dense supervision to converge.
distorted: [CITE] show that transformers can use meaningless filler tokens to solve two hard algorithmic tasks they could solve when responding without intermediate tokens, and that learning requires specific, dense supervision to converge.

faithful: [CITE] proposes GLAR, which replaces repeated enclosing-subgraph extraction with one shared opening subgraph for all candidates and learns entity-independent global and local anchors for a global-local reasoning ranker, reportedly outperforming most state-of-the-art inductive KGC methods.
distorted: For inductive KGC, [CITE] extracts an enclosing subgraph surrounding each candidate triple, with expensive time consumption caused by repeat extraction and deficiency of entity-independent feature learning.

faithful: [CITE] investigate zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies, including a Chain-of-Thought-inspired approach, for jointly scoring essays and generating feedback, finding that joint modeling improves automated essay scoring performance while the effect of scoring on feedback helpfulness remains small.
distorted: [CITE] explore Chain-of-Thought-inspired prompting strategies for zero-shot and few-shot essay feedback generation, demonstrating that tackling AES and feedback generation jointly improves the helpfulness of generated essay feedback, while the impact on AES performance remains low.

faithful: [CITE] proposes PMCTG, which extends perturbed masking to select the most incongruent token and applies four multi-aspect scoring functions to choose edit actions, reporting unsupervised state-of-the-art results on keywords-to-sentence generation and paraphrasing.
distorted: [CITE] proposes PMCTG, an unsupervised constrained text generation method that stochastically samples edit positions and actions, and extends perturbed masking with four multi-aspect scoring functions to achieve state-of-the-art results on keywords-to-sentence generation and paraphrasing.

faithful: [CITE] benchmarked BioGPT-large, BioMedLM, LLaMA 2, and Mistral 7B on MedQA and consumer health query answering, finding that Mistral 7B won every benchmark and reached 63.0% on MedQA, approaching the original Med-PaLM while surpassing biomedical-specific models.
distorted: [CITE] compare BioGPT-large, BioMedLM, LLaMA 2, and Mistral 7B on MedQA and consumer query answering and find that BioMedLM is the best performing model, winning on all benchmarks, and that its MedQA score of 63.0% approaches the original Med-PaLM.
